First of all, I know I don't have many hours played on the Steam version. Just ignore that, please. I bought this quite some time ago, played it a bit, and forgot all about it. But it was recently released on the Nintendo Switch, so I gave it a second chance there. That's the version I'm currently playing, and the version I will be playing for a long, long time. Put it this way: It's only been a few days since release, but I've played it nearly non-stop ever since. This game is fantastic... sort of.
Alright, let's look at the bad, first. This game isn't flawless by any means. The story is nearly non-existent, and the side quests are short and stupid. My biggest, most interesting side quest so far involved trading with the head cultist. Even that only had me kill some enemies, grab an item, then head to the cultist and talk to him. Simple stuff.
Also, the tutorial is quick and easy to understand, but it fails to tell you a vital thing: How to get more portals. Or to be precise, it tells you how to restore the portal on the first island, but it doesn't say anything about further portals. Maybe I just had a brainfart or something, but I spent a lont time trying to figure out how to make my own portals. Even had to google it, with no luck. Turns out the portals are always on the island, so you need to find them. You can't craft your own. But again, maybe that was just me having a blonde moment. *blush*
As for the good things, there is a lot to love here. While there's absolutely a Minecraft feeling to it, I like the RPG elements (level up your character, get better gear etc), and that and the portals add a simple progression system to the game. Not that it needs one, but it's not to have one anyway. But despite being heavily inspired by Minecraft, it looks gorgeous. We're not living in "block world". We live in a world made out of blocks, but where everything else is "normal". The blocks are also smaller than in Minecraft, making things less... giant blocks. It allows for more details, especially in smaller structures.
All in all, I love this game. Again, I'm on the Switch-version, so ignore the lack of playtime on the Steam version. I easily doubled it in two or three days on Switch, and I've barely started.

Fun co-op gameplay with quests, events, minecraft-style building, and dungeon exploration.  The devs update the game frequently and add fun events with new gear/items for holidays.  Overall, Portal Knights is really fun to play (especially with friends!) and I'd recommend it to anyone who enjoyed games like minecraft/terraria.

If you're a parent looking for a fun alternative to Minecraft, I can highly recommend Portal Knights. I've been playing co-op with my 10-year-old and the both of us have been having a blast. The game has a lot of the crafting and building elements of Minecraft, plus a rather engaging RPG element. Also, lots of character customization and adorable pets. The combat is fun but not too violent.
I've nominated Portal Knights for the "Let's Just All Get Along" award since it's such a family friendly game.

Then the person who invited you says "Oh it is turkey,     except there is no meat. Try it" So being that its someone your familiar with that you like who invited you and served you decide to try it. But from first bite to last, its still not turkey. Doesn't matter how much you eat or what the food was shaped like. Its still not turkey. What it is is 20 lbs of mother f**king lies. And thats what GunZ 2 is. Does the game have swords and daggers? Yes. Can you still run up and along walls? Yes. Is it GunZ? NO!!!

There is an option for the host player to pass the host position to someone else by hitting Esc then clicking change host. However if the host is doing well, they almost never change host. Doesn't even matter if their own teammates are spamming them to change. "Oh but king then you can just quit out of the match then" CAN I REALLY?! I have had to alt tab to get out and then shut the game down. When I relaunch Im forced back into the same f**king lagfest being hosted by the same selfish♥♥♥♥♥who refuses to pass host.
No option for private matches. Even though the only pvp gametypes are Team death match, team elimination, and team assault, you can't even create your own friggen room to practice anything.
You can't rebind your keys outside of a game. Sure you can open up the keyboard functions but thats it. You click on anything and nothing happens. You gotta be in a game to do it.
Ghost lobbies. both teams will fill up but one of the players isn't actually there. Normally people hop in and ready up, maybe vote on the map they want to play before the game auto starts. But if you have a non existant player the game won't start. You don't have the option to unready. And even if you did there is no option to back out of the lobby.
Barebones tutorial. The provided tutorial tells you the basics, movement, how to wall run, and explains the hud. The trouble outside of gameplay is understanding the friggen tesla shop, upgrading gear, armor, and other accessories. I had to find a player created guide to make heads or tails of everything, and that was after I spent the few resources/currency I had. I shouldn't need a guide to understand a menu MAIET.
Weapon variety. For those of us fortunate enough to hit the genetic lottery, there are more fingers on your hands than there are weapon choices in this game. Im not saying that there are 6 rifles or 7 swords. Its like 3 of each class of item.
The Tesla shop. This shop has two tabs. normal and premium which have cool looking and unique gear and weapons. Each tab util.....screw it. The damn thing is random random. You give it your hard earned currency and it takes a sh*t in your face and tells you better luck next time. And the gear that you do get, if it is even equipable by your class is on a time limit that starts when you equip it.
Limited mode options. I could say that there are 7, but I would be stretching the truth. In reality there are only 4. Campaign which I will get into next and the before mentioned Team death match, Team elimination and Team assault. Campaign. What could I say about this mode that I couldn't say about getting robbed at the atm. first let me say that this mode is tough and should not be attempted alone. Anyway so you go through killing♥♥♥♥♥♥left and right hoping not to die. If you die you can only be brought back to life with a revival coin. MAIET has GRACIOUSLY allowed players the option to purchase revival coins for 2 dollars U.S And with the reward for completing a campaign being slighty more xp and gold than a pvp match its SOOOOOOOO totally worth it. South Park: The Fractured But Whole is the sequel to The Stick of Truth and takes place shortly after it. King D-Bag enjoys his time as the leader when he suddenly gets a visit from The Coon who says he's from the future and needs to reunite Coon and Friends in order to find a missing cat and get a $100 reward to start off the Coon and Friends netflix franchise. D-Bag finds himself once again at the bottom as crime takes over in South Park.
One of the biggest changes is the combat system. At first sight it may seem very complicated, but it boils down to basically the same thing but with a grid wherein both you and the enemies will make your moves in. Now the attacks itself are much more complicated. The first game has mana and PP, but superheroes don't need that! Every superhero has 3 normal moves and 1 special move which all vary greatly. Some attacks knockback the enemy, others add burns and bleeding and others will heal and protect. A couple of attacks have a cooldown from 1-3 rounds and the special attack needs to load before it can be used. The normal fights are all about the same, but most boss fights have a special twist about them.
The way clothing affects the combat has also been changed: it doesn't. In this game your appearance is completely superficial and you can create your superhero look without worrying about stats. Everything is now affected by your might, which is added through artifacts. Artifacts help you by f.e. giving you a strength boost or one more move. You start off with one artifact slot, but gain more by leveling up with experience from fights and little tasks.
You get artifacts by crafting them, which is also a newly introduced mechanic. There's really not much that can be said about it though. You collect items all over town pretty easily and then craft them into artifacts, clothing, battle items and mission as well as summon items. South Park still offers a lot of stores, but you can only buy crafting recipes and ingredients. You can only craft one item at once which gets really annoying pretty fast.
While the town still looks the same; the way it does in the show, much more effort has been put into graphics and world design which is highly appreciated. A lot more buildings have been added to reflect the changes made in the show and all houses except for the main kids' ones got an interior renovation. Most non-home buildings got a few extra rooms including toilets, which got a big change as well. Going to the toilet has been turned into an actual minigame with 4 different difficulty settings. They get pretty difficult, but for mastering all 13 toilets you get an achievement and some experience.
One of my personal problems with the first game was the difficulty. It didn't matter which setting you chose: once you have your status effects figured out, you could kill every single enemy without a scratch. This time around status effects are still in the game, but instead of leveling the damage up, you can now only refresh its length. The boss battles themselves can be pretty tricky, but none were impossible on the medium difficulty. But with two different hard settings, I'm sure the battles will become much more challenging for those who dare.
While TFBW greatly improves on a lot of aspects of the first game, there are also still a lot of issues with the game months after it's inital release. Most notable is that the game immediately froze upon starting about half of the time. It usually works the second time around, but it takes a while for the game to even appear when it does.
Loading is really a big issue of this game. During a lot of boss battles, the game froze for a couple of seconds at the start and you'd have to wait a while before you could make your first move. Every time you entered a new area you also got terrible loading times. There's another minor bug where NPCs would load on top of the world and you couldn't interact with them. This is easily fixed by leaving the area and coming back.
Also the game forces you to play through the Uplay client as well as the Steam one and that's really not cool. I guess it's a compromise to make the game fully available on Steam along with achievements and trading cards and to be fair you get free items from the Uplay store so personally I couldn't be too mad about it.
The story heavily relies on the kids as they stumble upon crime after crime trying to find Scrambles. I can't really say much more without spoiling 2/3rd of the game, but the story really goes all over the place and really reminded me of South Park's early days. What surprised me is how little the adults were actually involved, even Randy is too drunk to do anything. For the climax Coon and Friends and Freedom Pals have to work together and it's really great to go on an adventure through South Park while being followed by half or all of the other kids. During certain sequences it almost feels like a Telltale game where you get to talk to every single character before progressing, but sadly their presence only brings some funny jokes at best.
As a longtime South Park fan I feel like this is easily the best season we've gotten in a long time. The multiple storylines all feel like something that could very well work as an episode, while the Stick of Truth just felt like the extension of an already exisiting TV special (which it was meant to be). Obviously the Coon episodes have always been pretty epic, but the show could never pull off an actual fight against an enemy.
The story itself definitely feels drawn-out which is partly due to a lot of intense boss battles that happen at the end of each storyline, though the game doesn't trick you with fake out endings. But the last part of the story feels completely unnecessary and they throw in random battles just to have certain characters appear at least once. Don't get me wrong; the game and story are both super fun, but when you know you're at the end you just want to get on with it or have a real boss battle.
It took me about 31 hours to collect all items, finish the game as well as the side quests and beat every boss including the hidden one. I really don't get how so many people go much quicker through the game unless they only focus on the main story, but where's the fun in that? To me, half of the game's appeal comes from being part of South Park and being able to explore every aspect of it without rushing through a story.
The Fractured But Whole is a fantastic game that still suffers from many small bugs, that however won't affect your enjoyment or break the game in its current state at all. It's what a sequel should be; a great improvement to the old game, the story builds up from and comes back to it and it's clear the developers actually cared about people enjoying the game and listened to complaints about the old one. If you're a South Park fan, especially of the earlier seasons, this is the defintive game for you.

I'm not very good at writing reviews, to make the first note.
I personally enjoy this game very much. It is a classic dungeon crawling RPG, much alike the popular Diablo Series. I prefer, however, this game to Diablo 2. It has the same feel, but many of the flaws of D2 are not present in this game, which also boost much more prefered graphics and art style.
There are a four Classes available: Beserker, Emerbmage, Engineer, and Outlander.
Beserkers are the basic melee standard class you're find in classed dungeon crawls. I love the fact they added twist to the skill trees as this class also has a number of ranged attacks and spititual abilities, like the beserkers and their faiths in history.
Embermages are the typical Caster-Type. Elemental Damages by-and-by. Fire, the Damage Dealer, Ice the Crowd Controller, and Lightning, the Multi-Targeter. Each have their ups and downs, and it's possible to specialize i all three with many of of the embermage's passives, which focus on often lower-level skills, or combinations of spells betwen elements. This is my favorite class, and i often use a Lightning Build with Status Effects. It allows me to take out swaths of enemies, as this game will often pit you against hoards.
Engineers are sort of like a cross beteen the other three classes; part melee, part caster, and part ranged. They focus primarily on having minons and augmenting melee via tech and magic. Makes a great Summoner Class if built with the right items and skillsets, and able to hit like a wrecking ball if a baddie gets through your wall of summons.
Outlanders are a typical Ranged or Archer Class. They have the ability for some minons, being the nature-types they are, and excell in ranged attacks with bows and thrown weapons. Their magics focus on this effect, and you have the ability to sort of enchant your attacks for things such as Elemental and Status Effects. The minons can be focused to be powerful, although i feel the Engineer excells at it more so, if only by a minon margin. In a way, Engineer and Outlander can be seen as the same sort of summoning class, but one focused on melee and the other ranged, respecively as well; focused on different kinds of summons as well: Technological and spiritual/animal, respctively.
All in all, i enjoy many of the games features. The over-all Series's plot and story is pretty good. I cannot honestly say it is all that deep, but it is enjoyable.

The game is fun, and it's core mechanics easy to understand and implement. The story is simple, and I enjoyed the character's knowledge of how ludicrous what they were doing was. It was an interesting take on expected game mechanics (no one questions how 1 man in black ops can accomplish all the tasks he does, it's unrealistic but just accepted by the gamer) but the characters are almost self aware of this without having to do a Deadpool style of 4th wall breaking. An example of this was in the first story mission your briefing tells you that you are to escort a ship and that there will be people trying to attack the escort, and one of the crew members states something to the extent of, "A military mission when we're just explorers and have no idea how to fight? Let's dive in head first!." Subtle humor that I enjoyed. Humor aside you're always just in that believability spectrum, never too far serious or ludicrous. The author knew what kind of experience he wanted to give and he presented it well. This game's story will not lead you into a deeper understanding of humanity or anything like that, but it will give you enough to keep your attention to present to you an enjoyable time.
Visually it's a treat, I don't mean it's NEXT GENERATION GRAPHICS, but it's colorfull vistas and elements of the world backup the style the game is presenting.
I do wish that the way you upgraded your ship/fleet was more progression based, or unlockable I suppose. Not having practically all ship variants right of the start, and getting certain upgrades or new abilities after beating a level would of been nice. Not to say there isn't any progression, but it seems a bit underdeveloped in my humble opinion.
Unfortunately there are some bugs that will hinder your enjoyment of the game. A short gameplay session occurs before what is supposed to be the intro cutscene, and that gameplay segment is a tutorial that you must repeat after the cutscene. The one that caused me the most trouble is the bugged music. While the music itself is great and fitting, you have no ocntrol over the volume. You can try to turn in down using the enraging cursor that is used in menus, using buggy volume sliders, but even if you manage to get the volume to where you want it (which is unlikely since the first slider barley works, the second even less so, and the third is unusable) after a loading screen the volume goes back to max and if you try to change it after that the music will briefly go to the volume you stay and then quickly rise back to max. I point this out because it made it impossible to make a video of this game because the music was always overpowering my voice.
Bugs aside I recommend the game, and look forward to see what come out of the game creator next.

TL:DR, I gave this game a 7.5/10, it feels like Darksiders 2, WoW, TERA and Torchlight 2 had sex. Minus mounts (as far as my knowledge goes) and Jumping.
The game, to me isn't very immersive but addicting, sometiems it feels like one of those games that you need to force yourself to play, like Dota 2, it's not interesting you untill you force yourself to play it.
The game feels like it began as a third-person dungeon crawler RPG similar to Torchlight II turned MMO then reduced to a sandbox RPG that leaves the Dungeon Crawler and MMO elements.
The controls + camera movement gets disorientating sometimes, it's very "woah duuude" if you haven't touched it in a while but it's easy to get use to it.
It's also very easy to get lost doing quests, the main quest and faction quests branch off all over the place leading you to more similar quests and it's easy to get lost in all of these quests, I haven't played long enough to see how rewarding faction quests are, I only have roughly 6 hours on record (I have about 4-5 or so hours in offline mode).
The skill tree system I find is a bit weird and hasn't got alot of variety but it's still good nonetheless.
The video options are a bit limited, I can't find anythign regarding resolutiuon settings so some menus stretch off screen but are still workable.
At the moment there's not a whole lot of armour variety regarding plate armour for brawlers, though i haven't progressed far, Not sure about the other classes though.
The stealth system, I haven't really explored it but from what I know it feels and seems like it's fairly decent, I never really did stealth outside the tutorial level unless I was stealing from chests.
Regarding some other things, the game world is VERY large, it reminds me of World of Warcraft but.. a little larger, a better example of this is, if you've played Darksiders, specifically Darksiders 2 you'd understand what I mean by how open the game is, by this I mean that it takes a fair while to get from place to place and I'm not sure if there's a mount system or not.
With leveling it's kind of? slow but not at the same time, my first 5 levels it felt liek I shoul've been a higher level because of all the crap I did before hand, yeah you can do ALOT between levels so sometimes it feels like you should be a higher level.
Another example of this is, some games, like, you don't normally find yourself killing giant trolls, ettins or whatever like the ones in this game till you're a higher level and it feels so rewarding yet it feels like you shouldn't be killing them in such large numbers. I'm a long term World of Warcraft user and a user of TERA, so, this will sound weird, this next part is a little hard to explain, In the likes of WoW or TERA most of these 'giants', when you kill them in numbers like you do in this game, in other MMO's or RPG's i've played they're usually scaled smaller then the others or placed in very thin numbers, I don't know this is what I mean by it feeling like it was made as an MMORPG then made singleplayer, the game is very unique and strange if you're like me and are use to games like WoW or TERA, A better example would be Darksiders 2 minus the mount and colossal gods, yeah that sounds like a better mechanic example mixed with TERA and WoW.
if you must know, I refer to games like TERA or WoW because of how 'loose' the game looks and feels and the artistic style is similar, it just isn't right to compare it to the likes of Skyrim because Skyrim is a fairly solid feeling game and is impossible to think of WoW while playing Skyrim unlike this particular game.
Another thing I will mention, it feels weird seeing an RPG with this artistic design style that uses Ragdol physics, imagine World of Warcraft with Ragdoll physics... yeah lol.. but it's still good, it's great that made the larger ragdolls interactible as well, like you can push Ettin and troll corpses around, another thing to not, the ragdoll physaics is hilarious sometimes when an NPC has a death animation then snaps to ragdoll, sometimes the ragdolls just freak out.
I can go on longer but the rest is just fiddly stuff, overall I give this game a 7.5/10, If you like open world RPG's similar to WoW, TERA and as open as the likes of Darksiders, I'd recomend you get this game.

This game is a third person RPG that truly resembles RPGs around the Era of Oblivion and to be honest if it had been released then it would of made millions. But the timing was not right.
It seemed unfinished with only one model for each weapon type and barely any difference in armour.
The combat was interesting with different specialised weapons to use with each class. The action bar worked especially well for it. The main mechanic that the combat was all based around was a sort of slow mo that seems to make you do extra damage whilst giving you the ability to do very impressive final hits or death blows. The class systems truly do make a difference and seem to be the biggest decision you will make in the game. The special attacks and weapons were the high point as well as the blends of the difference classes. (I played a Rogue/Mage)
The world reminded me a lot of the original Fable with the same reputation system and choice system. But your decisions didnt really feel like they were making a difference... Except for maybe a few larger points.
The artwork once again reminded me of Fable but the render distance for me was an issue. The world was always fun to explore with secrets hidden everywhere and new towns and houses to explore.
The questing was good and it didnt make you feel like you were grinding like some other RPGs. There are hundreds of side quests to spend your time on until you decide whether you want to buy the DLC or not.
Overall I loved this game even though it had its issues..
If it had a little more time and maybe more funding? It could of been amazing but this is where it was at, I have heard that modding the game can fix a lot of the issues I had with it such as the weapon models.
I rate it a 7/10

Truly an exceptionally good game. After 200 hours in, I decided I should finally get around to writing a review.
I love Spelunky; it's hard, fun, frustrating, and exciting. I play it to take homework breaks. I played it as a couples game with my girlfriend (which was a blast, highly recommend 2+ player at least some of the time). I play it with friends while drinking, which only ups the fun. I play it with the music off and sound effects down low while watching Netflix on the other monitor. If I'm at my computer and not caught up in homework (or Civ), there's an 85% chance that I'm playing Spelunky.
You will laugh, you will cry, and you will swear loudly when you make it all the way to the City of Gold just to be killed by a goddamned Tiki Trap.
Do yourself a favor and buy this game. I got it on sale, but I would pay full price for this game in a heartbeat. I plan on buying a friend or two a copy in the future as a "thank you" to the devs, and to spread the good news of Spelunky a little further.

Hack 'N' Slash.... a genre I don't usually play. However being a fan of the actual animated series I decided to give the game a fair go.
The game is still not fully completed and as such I can't talk about the full story as it's journey has yet to be finished, however the cannon storyline is both interesting and in-depth. However this is contrasted heavily by the chaotic combat, supplied by the online main story mode.
The leveling system is very fair being that when you start any game, you are level one unless you joing a mid-game session in which to are boosted to the average level. Kill monsters, collect experience orbs and artifacts to gain experience. Upon leveling up you can spend one point per level, with the points stacking up. The tree flow design is simple yet effective with various challenges to unlock additional skills. All in all requiring you to play certain characters to unlock unique special abilities or any to unlock generic upgrades such as health or aura.
The only problem with this system is that players are more orientated on experience than team work. I was walking for a box, that could potentially house an experience orb, before a player jumped in front to take my box. This is similar to combat against enemies. I can understand if it's a clustered fight and there is too many for one person but if I'm versing a single monster and I start to go for the last strike to kill it and earn the experience I don't like how people can do a ranged attack, defeat it and earn your experience. A shared pool may be needed?
Realistic point... would I buy the game still knowing what I know? The simple answer, yes. The simplistic combat system is still both fun and engaging. It may be experience orientated but it is still humorous when playing with friends over skype. YES, play with friends. I enourage it to the ends of the earth. It allows better teamwork skills are is more enjoyable.

Comat Update Review
Recently I decided to play this game again because I'm bored from lack of work. To my suprise I found an extensive rework of the combat system. To me it had appeared as if the ranged button had been removed for a heavy attack (right click) and for the first ten minutes I taught myself all the new combos I need and their effects.
I was playing for about ten minutes before a teammate casually asked why I didn't use my barrage ability to which I regrett saying, because I sounded like a noob, "how?". Apparently the 'R' now acts as your ranged attack with 'E' preforming a finishing move and 'F' making your charcter sprint to a enemy like they're offering free money.
The single player option is nice, allowing you to master your skills by yourself before worrying about multiplayer where people judge (as I was without knowing ranged abilities). The graphics and camera additions are implimented flawlessly with the game's appeal and overall its been a great update.
Would I recommend the game, now? Yes, even more so than the previous time. The combat style makes it feel more worthwile and meaningful when an enemy actually dies. Improved enemy AI makes the game harder and more strategical rather than ridicously overpowered. Keep going developers. I'll be here and waiting.

Overall it has a solid foundation for an interesting game.  The combat is both challenging and fast-paced, the abilities are flashy and the game runs well especially with their current optimization.
My only complaint is the character balance is a bit off.  If you are a RWBY fan, you may feel that some of the girls seem lacking in comparsion to the show.  Right now I will tentatively say Weiss and Yang actually feel underpowered, where as Blake and Ruby are in a good place if not boardlining OP in some cases.  Because all of the game (currently) is high mob counts.  Blake and Ruby have naturally AoE in their basic attacks which allow them to damage a large number of mobs very quickly and without much risk, their abilities are also AoEs which makes them ideal for all of the current combat.
Yang and Weiss both have issues in the sense they both do not possess reliable AoEs.  both of their basic attacks have very small high boxes but they don't seem to do any more damage than Blake or Ruby in terms of damage (not enough to be noticable).  Yang at least has a little bit of AoE with her Blast attacks and some of her Abilities are AoEs, so she can keep pace.  Weiss is probably the most underwhelming of the cast.  Her auto attacks feel fast however suffer from the small hit box.  If she uses her Blast attack to end a combo she becomes a sitting duck as the animation has her float back while summoning her Sigil forward, however the sigil blast radius to too small and often doesn't hit enemies, and the push back animation actually leaves her very vulnerable, which becomes a major issue when surrounded.  Out of 3 abilities only 1 is an AoE and one that can be upgraded to be boardline OP (freezes enemies and Heals allies in a very large radius), however because of this ability the other 2 options are practically negliable.
tl;dr - game isn't bad.  Characters need rebalancing, and if you are a fan of the show some of the girls just don't feel as strong as the show makes them out to be.

“Oceanhorn: Monster of Uncharted Seas” is an interesting game in concept. It accurately compares itself to the “Legend of Zelda” titles and is definitely reminiscent of the core gameplay in that series. The interesting part however comes from the game being on mobile devices and PC, whereas Nintendo has so far only released Zelda games on their own consoles. “Oceanhorn” attempts to tap into a niche, and does it fairly well, despite lacking the polish that Nintendo fans have come to expect.
The game is a mostly isometric dungeon crawler game akin to Zelda games. Using a sword and shield, along with various items unlocked through the game, the goal is to progress through various dungeons and reach the boss of each area. At times this is much easier said than done, as the level layouts can be a bit confusing at times. The levels themselves however look fantastic, and generally speaking the game’s graphical quality is up to the standard of the Zelda games, just with a bit less bloom which is very welcome.
In fairness to the game, as of yet I haven’t run into any major issues that have stopped me from progressing or caused me to wonder what exactly the developer was thinking, however my problems with the game arise from a series of small things that are missing. The easiest way to describe it is unfortunately just to reiterate the first paragraph; the game lacks polish in many areas.
The graphics of the game, as previously mentioned are pretty great, the game genuinely looks gorgeous, especially the water used to sail between islands. However some texture glitches and clipping can stand out while trying to solve a puzzle, and the isometric viewpoint can be a bit of a problem at times even with an adjustable camera. The game’s combat is generally solid, however hitbox issues can make fighting a bit unsatisfying, and the music sits comfortably in between being great and defining the landscape as Zelda games use their soundtrack, and being fairly mediocre. I never found reason to complain, but unlike some other games in recent memory, it never left me wanting a soundtrack to slap on my phone.
However, a lot of the issues I’ve raised with this game are present in others like it, and are usually forgivable, however for something that compares itself to a Zelda game, it’s hard to not judge it in the same vein as those titles. That said, this review has been a bit harsh so far -- while the game definitely lacks the polish of Zelda titles, it brings some of its own traits to the table which add to the game.
An experience system and a sprint function without having to wait to unlock the Pegasus Boots is likely the biggest improvement, as being able to zip around places you’ve already been through means hopping right back into a dungeon is always just a couple seconds away. The challenges offer experience as a reward and can add some interesting depth to the game, assuming it’s not a simple one like breaking several pots, something Zelda fans were going to do anyway.
Overall, the game does a decent job at mimicking the Zelda series, but as stated before multiple times, the lack of polish can stand out and may put some people off from the title. That’s unfortunate, because the game is generally enjoyable. It makes some legitimate improvements to the formula of Zelda titles, it’s just hard to not look at some aspects of the game and wish the developers had a bit more experience behind them so they could smooth out the rough bits. That said, it’s an enjoyable experience that at the least attempts to shake things up a bit.

This is a mobile port and it definitely shows. The game is pretty enough, voice acting is decent, but the gameplay itself is dull. The controls feel clunky, especially in combat where your hits do not always register if you attack the enemy too fast. Magic takes too long to be useful most of the time, and even when it is needed it feels underwhelming. An item you get lets you jump across small gaps and dodge roll, both of which are keyed to the same button. The game will let you fall from areas up to a certain height, which means you can be doing a timed puzzle and then inadvertantly (and commonly) dodge roll instead of jumping to the next platform and have to do the entire thing over.
Damage is inconsistent, with bombs doing massive damage to some enemies but barely a scratch to others... and yet those other enemies will take a big chunk of damage from a random pot thrown at them. Speaking of pots, you have to either throw, shoot them, or throw a bomb at them to break them... your sword is evidently the sword of not smashing pots.
Bosses are few and far between, and most are unimpressive. I died a few times to them, not because they were hard, but because of completely unavoidable attacks, the boss freezing (status, not game freezing) the mechanic to damage it and the only way to unfreeze it aside from letting it time out is your magic with the very long windup, or just poorly designed.
Travel between islands is set on pre-set paths, you tell the game to go and it drops you into a little shooting gallery where you spam the attack button to kill anything that gets in the way until you reach the island. On mobile I'm sure it was neat, tap to kill the things, but on pc its just feels like a boring, spam your mouse button and go add-on.
Overall, the game is probably very good on mobile platforms, but not a very good pc game, and comparing it to zelda is like comparing a perfectly cooked steak to a $1 Banquet microwave dinner.

Pros:
- GAMEPLAY. The game has by far improved since the first one.
- COMDEDIC. Honestly there were a ton of moments in the game I found myself bursting out loud and waking people up at 4am. Even though it can get repetitive if you use the same characters and same class the whole game with so much variety and certain classes suiting different battles better (ESPECIALLY on the harder difficulties) it's definitely my recomendation to try lots of different combinations!
- VARIETY. There are a lot of classes and moves to pick from and bonus points for being able to change these at will throughout the game and opening new options very quickly as you progress. Costumes and allies are similarily plentiful and easy to obtain.
- NO CONSEQUENCES. I like games that offer choices that are purely cosmetic, so you can be totally brutal in your choices here and not have to worry about the outcomes- go crazy! You can also dress however you like and it doesn't have an effect on gameplay so I liked that a lot.
- STORY. This game was great and tons of fun to play through! Just like the last game they touched and expanded on lots of things that made it overall a just enjoyable to play through. No spoilers though!
- EASY CRAFTING. Even if you aren't an expert crafter it doesn't take a lot to be able to gather the ingredients to create things you'll need for your fights.
Cons:
- MODERATE LENGTH.
It wasn't extremely short by no means there was enough content in it to keep me playing for several days but after the main story was finished I didn't find a huge drive to play the DLC content. However, the DLC /is/ available for people who want to keep doing challenges in the game.
- MEH SIDE-QUESTS.
All the sidequests in the game that weren't *required* to do to progress the story were basically collecting cats and other less meaningful tasks. One at least you have to do to unlock a new power but I never needed it throughout the game.
- PUZZLES.
Tieing into the last one the puzzles early on are a lot of fun, and as you unlock powers I found myself going back and scoping out the older areas for new stuff to do, but it almost became tedious after a while and you don't really have to do them so it got a bit boring.
- CRASHING. The game for PC it seems is a part, and with that comes a number of crashes and other slightly annoying things but luckily it wasn't a huge deal just a little annoying.

This is a really fun and fast paced game. I really enjoyed the graphics and the music was awesome. The only problem that I had with this game was that it was extremely difficult to play and I was unable to get past the first mission in the story mode. I'm going to be nice to this game. I am in full understanding of that in its current state it is below expectations, however the devs are definitely aware of its issues and are working towards fixing them. This game has some great ideas: The story for it is actually interesting and the idea of a side scrolling shooter in a 3d space is actually quite interesting. However, the enemies are quite hard to hit and the ship building and formation editor are relatively useless when you are constantly under a hellstorm of enemy bullets. I also don't enjoy the soundtrack for this game, I really think that it doesn't fit the 'Hardcore Space Pilot' theme. It sounds like royalty free music from the Musescore website, and it definitely needs an overhaul. I know the devs are working on a difficulty setting option, but I will mention that at the time it is incredibly necessary as the game is over the top difficult right from the start.
If I could make my own suggestion, maybe consider putting in a view option so the player could play in top down rather than a 3rd person? The view is cool and definitely helps to feel the depth of space, but it makes it gosh near impossible to aim.
tl;dr this game needs a lot of work but it has some great potential.

I rate it a 7/10

HIGHLY RECOMMEND  --  LOVE THIS GAME.... It's a Must Have for RPGrs!!!
Honestly... I've never really been much into Graphics or Music... so for that I'm going to assume that both are fine. Personally, I don't see an issue there, but again... not really my thing.
Okay... no game is truly perfect, so I will make one complaint.  Armour-sets, which are available, are a problem to attain before they become obsolete; unless, of course, you use the internet and try to find them early.  I like having a well-dressed adventurer... so that kind of sucks, because I won't use the internet to spoil my game play.
Now with that said....
Game Play... beyond awesome.  This game was created with ME in mind.  I often restart a character several times before completing the game, because I'm curious as to how other builds would do in this game... in short... which would I truly enjoy most.  With this game, you can actually re-set all your stats, for the most part, at any given time.  Thus, if Warrior isn't floating your boat, become a Rogue... just like that; without having to start a new game.
The missions in this game is another point of great excitement.  Besides the fact of being a completely NON-Linear game, there are tons of Faction Missions... Side Missions... and Others which can peak your interest, or even immerse yourself in your own Character's Story.  Admittedly, all missions; Story, Faction, etc., are a bit linear in the sense that you complete the mission Their way or not at all... but if that's the only down side... I can live with that.  As well, I'm finding the various stories of this world fascinating... like a really good book; Very Well Written!!!!
Combat is a whole 'nother story... or more like an Epic Tale.  Besides the many many many diferent attacks that are available, I love the fact that it's not just about point and click.  Timing makes a difference, direction makes a difference, distance makes a difference, reflexes make a difference.  (just as an example.... Boggarts are one of the easy mobs in this game... I got murdered by 4 of them, because I wasn't paying attention and I got cocky; That's a Real Game).
Special Note:  If you get and play the demo for this game, it really doesn't do it justice.  If I recall correctly, it gives you a time limit, and an area limit... this is their mistake.  It should be limited by a certain level... maybe 5 or 6; by then, you'll get a true feel for this game.
I easily give this game 6 thumbs up out of 5...and a Slap on the Hand, to me, for not finding it sooner.

Overall Rating: 7/10
Pros:
* Lots of content with about 100 to 150 hours in the base game alone which isn't too grindy
* Combat and inventory is smooth and intuitive with satisfying action
* Area exploration is pretty fun with smooth not-too-bloomy not-too-brown visuals
* Sound effects and voice acting done very competently with good SKIPPABLE in-game cinematics
Cons:
* Hard level cap of 40 kills the lategame progression (This is probably only game with a leveling guide about SLOWING down.)
* Some abilities and especially item modifiers aren't explained or skew with OP Blacksmithing or Sagecraft skills
* Story is very lacking in depth or characterisation compared to the lore in other RPGs and gets railroady near the end
* Camera will take some getting used to as its dynamic motion can mess up combat (Use an easy hotkey for shoulder camera.)
Ugly:
* Be very careful about quicksaving near spawns as it can corrupt your game.  There are also known issues with loading DLC content.
* Smooth edges shows downside in simplified race, class, spell, and ability selections
* Pure Archmage is pretty overpowered with Rogue probably being the most fun.  Warrior hybrid on Hard may be the best challenge - just avoid XP potions or Reckoning Mode too much.
BOTTOM LINE:
If you want a sure and simple RPG that burns the clock, this is probably the best on Steam without the mod tweaking in TES or the issues in Bioware's stuff.  Definitely worth the value and the bar for a competently made single-player RPG; just a shame that the developer went out of business before really expanding it.

Oceanhorn is shamelessly inspired by the Zelda franchise but unfortunately it doesn't quite hold up to the big "Z" in terms of polish. More specifically, there are just too many inconsistencies with the gameplay and visuals. Some players may ignore these issues considering it’s an indie game but it's apparent that several of them are due to sheer laziness and that's something I can't forgive.
I'll give you an example. The first issue I spotted, even from the trailer, is that the animations are simply stiff. The main character's idle animation is a big offender here. This is because almost all of the animations use a linear transition which creates a really rigid and unnatural feel. This can be solved with easement scaling and a little bit of hand-crafting. Basically the animators were lazy. A minor issue, but the game is FULL of  these minor issues and it's incredibly abrasive after a while.
At one point I fell down a "hole" that I thought was suppose to be the entrance of a cave. My character stopped shortly after falling only few feet, landing on solid ground.  His head bobbed in his rigid little idle animation for a brief moment. I thought that maybe I was mistaken about it being a cave entrance but then the game transitioned into another scene where my character was falling from a cave ceiling. I then realized that the developers simply made the entrance hole too shallow and this broke the illusion of actually falling through it. When I later got back out of the cave the grass that had grown over the entrance when it was undiscovered was there again, floating in mid-air. See what I mean by lazy?
Another huge problem is the absolutely shameless use of invisible walls. Many games use invisible walls but it's pretty hard to forgive in this case. You can only walk off ledges in very specific places and it's not nearly as obvious as it should be. In fact it's almost arbitrary. It just feels weird trying to constantly mime your way off a short ledge.
The allusion to the Zelda series can't just be called inspiration. It's actually a little offensive how much they rely on established Zelda mechanics. For example there are pieces of heart and they work pretty much like you would expect them to. You find them in random chests and you need exactly four of them to create a heart container. I mean, they are literally called "Pieces of Heart". Not convinced? There are crustacean-like enemies that shoot projectiles at you but dig into the ground when you come near them. You defeat them by shielding their projectiles which bounce back at them. I'm not even kidding.
The intent of copying Zelda mechanics are so desperate and obvious that the game should be called "Shoehorn". Exploration is based around the open-ocean feeling of Wind Waker, for instance. That itself isn't a bad thing but they copied the mechanic in the most superficial way possible. Instead of having any sort of interaction with the actual sailing of your ship, you simply click your destination and then watch as your tiny little vessel coasts its way along the featureless ocean at a snail's pace. This may have been somewhat scenic if it weren't for the main character looking around like a dork with his robot movements I feel like any time a game makes me want to get up and make a sandwich instead of actually playing is a huge red flag. I'm sure some players find this relaxing but for the less patient of us, an option to skip this would have been nice.
I think the real thing that bothers me is that I really had high expectations from the game but it feels more like a Zelda cash-in than a love letter. There may be in fact a real gem under here, but I certainly didn't feel the need to find it.

Overall it has a solid foundation for an interesting game.  The combat is both challenging and fast-paced, the abilities are flashy and the game runs well especially with their current optimization.
My only complaint is the character balance is a bit off.  If you are a RWBY fan, you may feel that some of the girls seem lacking in comparsion to the show.  Right now I will tentatively say Weiss and Yang actually feel underpowered, where as Blake and Ruby are in a good place if not boardlining OP in some cases.  Because all of the game (currently) is high mob counts.  Blake and Ruby have naturally AoE in their basic attacks which allow them to damage a large number of mobs very quickly and without much risk, their abilities are also AoEs which makes them ideal for all of the current combat.
Yang and Weiss both have issues in the sense they both do not possess reliable AoEs.  both of their basic attacks have very small high boxes but they don't seem to do any more damage than Blake or Ruby in terms of damage (not enough to be noticable).  Yang at least has a little bit of AoE with her Blast attacks and some of her Abilities are AoEs, so she can keep pace.  Weiss is probably the most underwhelming of the cast.  Her auto attacks feel fast however suffer from the small hit box.  If she uses her Blast attack to end a combo she becomes a sitting duck as the animation has her float back while summoning her Sigil forward, however the sigil blast radius to too small and often doesn't hit enemies, and the push back animation actually leaves her very vulnerable, which becomes a major issue when surrounded.  Out of 3 abilities only 1 is an AoE and one that can be upgraded to be boardline OP (freezes enemies and Heals allies in a very large radius), however because of this ability the other 2 options are practically negliable.
tl;dr - game isn't bad.  Characters need rebalancing, and if you are a fan of the show some of the girls just don't feel as strong as the show makes them out to be.

there is a good flowing storyline for a base of this game. I like the leveling system and the way that the difficulty adjusts itself as you add more of your friends, and I feel like the adaptive difficulty is a great feature. Pros:
-open worlds with beautiful backgrounds just like the original show
-excellent graphics and gameplay
-Characters you do have access to really feel like you are playing as that character so fans of the series will really appreciate the play style
-adaptive difficulty allowing for a more progressing feel to the game
-smooth fight animations and gameplay
Cons: (most of these are extremely nitpicky)

overall this is still a great game that is fun and easy to setup for multiplayer with friends (took me about 5 minutes total to get everyone up and in game) I realize this is early access so likely they are still adding a great number of things that will improve on what they have already created. Its possible that my ain gripes in the Cons section will be taken care of in future updates, and they may not. I was just trying to do my part.

update: Bamco is still working on this game, so I'm going to change review to positive, but most of what written below still applies. Get this game only if you want to compete online.
Game is barebones. Buy it only if you want online.
Negatives:
Story mode is lacklustre, story itself is nonsensical, this mode doesn't teach you anything about the game beyond press LP for left punch. Sometimes it even teaches players wrong things, like attacking into power crush with Mids and Highs. Opponents have moves they don't have in the game, so it's useless for matchups. Can be completed in 3 to 4 hours with all sidestories.
No tutorial, one of the biggest offences, game is complex, but you will have to learn your characters on YouTube and tekken Zaibatsu, not in-game. no frame data, no basic info on your char (punishment tools for example), no challenges, sample combos for chars are extremely hit and miss. Appalling after games like Guilty Gear Xrd.
Online is broken for me and some other players it takes half an hour to find a game. Rage quitters aren't punished properly, some of these hours are wasted on them. Bamco tried to patch PC, but it made things only worse and devs reversed the change.
If you don’t want to go online, there’s nothing to do, like I said story is underwhelming and short, aside from it there are Treasure Battle and Arcade battle, both is just playing vs CPU, sometimes Treasure Battle introduces challenges, like double speed, but that’s it. No Team Battle, no Tekken Ball, no Tekken Street, no nothing.
Positives:
Game runs well and looks nice. Although effects are overdone, reflective costumes + light sources in customize = can’t see anything in game. There are Steam guides how to disable Chromatic Aberration in .ini files.
Gameplay of the main game is rather nice, it might be the best Tekken since T5DR. There are problems, like 8frames of input lag even offline, although annoying and undesired, it doesn’t ruin this game by itself.

Deus Ex Mankind Divided is a good game. Not amazing, but its good. While the length is lacking, I probably could have beaten it much faster if I had just ran through the main quests and got lost a lot less, the story does build up to a fairly climactic final mission. The ending of that mission is lackluster, however, though the cliffhanger is decent.
Before I go more into depth, I want to bring something up immediately. This game is a HOG on your computer. The loading times are a beast and the game itself eats through memory like lava through ice. DO NOT GET THIS GAME IF YOU HAVE A WEAKER PC.
Where the game really shines is the level design and gameplay. Holy♥♥♥♥♥♥ the level design. I can't think of a single augment in this game that isn't helpful in some way, and its all thanks to the multitude of routes available to you, and thats not even bringing up the appearance factor, which is downright gorgeous. Stealth is amazing, I rate it on par with MGSV's stealth. Open Combat wise, this game is a better shooter than most shooters.
The new experimental augments are all incredibly useful, and I found myself using augments I never touched in the first game here, discovering that in Deus Ex Mankind Divided, there are no bad augmentations.
The games weakest link is the story, not because its not good, the story's... adequate. Its not particularly driving or anything, but its adequate. The problem is its short. And the ending is unsatisfying.
And its worth mentioning again, the loading times are atrocious.
Also the store supposedly lets you buy praxis or something but by the end of the game you'll have 70% of the augments, and if you really want to play all out you can go NG+.

Honestly, they really want you to spend money on microtransactions.  They've upped the difficulty so even if you want to play for the story, you might be tempted to pony up some real cash to buy A ONE-TIME use item or game currency.
Beyond the microtransactions, I really hate this dumbed-down second-helping of Deus Ex.  The cover system is again ridiculous as is the switch to 3rd person when, say, you climb something.  It didn't mesh well the first time around.   Popping in and out of 3rd Person is just freaking annoying.   I think thinking about microtransactions has made me judge this game more objectively now.    If the original Deus Ex was remade from scratch with current gen tech, the differences between it and this inferior child would be clear as day.  DE: MD has the ambience nailed down, but that's about it.  The inventory is ridiculous with ammo taking up large chunks of space.
Wait a just a little bit for the price to drop if you must play, BUT play Obduction in the meantime.  Unlike DE: MD, Obduction is not a direct sequel, but it captures the ambience and soul of Myst, of which it is a true spiritual successor.  Unlike SE, Cyan didn't bog down the game with hated DRM, microtransactions, and inflated price tags.

Close Order… What can I say, this game was very eventful, and I don’t mean to put that in a good way. Eventful as in the game constantly crashes and was literally impossible to beat. Now I have a lot of faith in these developers simply based on my judgements of the main menu and the music, but I personally do not think this game is currently in a playable state. It still needs a lot of work. My opinion on this game is based on the game’s current state and I still look forward to seeing how it turns out in the future.
First off, I need to give this game some credit for its main menu. I really liked the music in the background and the fact that you had to actually fly your aircraft to the game mode you wanted to play. Being a musician and slowly getting into sound design and composing music for video games, I must give credit to the music composer because he did a great job. Also the fact that you were able to free roam really helped make the game more enticing to play by holding my attention and making the start of the game less boring.
Now although the main menu looked and ran very well, the following is where my experience goes completely downhill. There was nothing but crashes all the way through even after resetting my computer and changing the settings multiple times.
After the game crashing three times every time I landed in Story Hub 1, I was finally able to click on a mission. Although this got me excited, I was not able to start the mission, I was only able to watch a brief video. Although I was able to watch the video over and over again, I was unable to click on anything else or exit the mission itself. Out of frustration, I started pushing all the buttons on my keyboard until the pause menu came up, which sadly had caused the game to crash again.
Now, this is usually when I would give up and not even attempt to try to play the game again, but like I said above, the menu itself and the music were so enticing I had to try again. This game looks like it has potential and I didn’t want to miss out on anything. I started the game again, but instead of going to Story Hub 1, I flew over to Survival mode, only to have the game crash again the moment I landed in the circle that brings you to the list of levels…
I tried Story Hub 1’s mission, all of the survival modes, only to have the game crash every single time, not allowing me to even experience actual game-play. This is not something you want your game to have a reputation of doing.
After finally realizing I had to click about two inches above what I wanted to actually select, I was finally able to start the first mission in Story Hub 1. This is not an issue with my PC as I have never experienced it before. Everything was fine once the game actually started though, which means that it must just be a simple coding issue that can very easily be fixed.
Man oh man, was that first mission ever difficult. I could even destroy the first tier of enemies! After dying about a dozen times, I gave up with the only mission in Story Hub 1 that I was able to play, and headed back over to survival mode. This game is beyond difficult even when you have minions protecting you! Even in survival mode I wasn’t able to destroy all the ships attacking me after many attempts. It’s so difficult to see the bullets being shot from the enemies, and there’s so many of them that there’s no way to dodge any of them. With little to no progression in the game after around an hour of playing (not including all the time spent actually getting in-game), I decided to stop it there and simply just hope that the game will get fixed in the near future.
This is not my type of game, so maybe I simply am just terrible at it, but I truly do not think that’s the case. This game is not challenging, it’s literally impossible to play. Although the main menu was very intriguing, the constant crashing and the game-play itself made this game completely unappealing to me. I am going to give this game a rating of 2/10. I really hope this game gets fixed. I am looking forward to checking it out again once I come back to it in a month or so!

I purchased this game very soon after its release. It looked from the videos and screenshots like a fun action shooter game. I unfortunatley turned out to be wrong. After booting up the game, I played a quick tutuorial mission, in which I discovered the fidley controls, vague objectives, and confusing camera angles.
Moving around feels floaty, and it is near impossible to have any sort of percession while moving. You can either sit still and take massive amounts of damage while you fire, or spray and pray, missing every shot. The menu is also very fidley and sensetive. Trying to select a new minion to purchase requires you to move your mouse very slowly, and you often fly past the option you want to it just doesn't select when you do eventually reach it.
In the tutorial, I was shown several ships to defeat. I defeated them all (with some effort) and was taken into the first mission. I was then given nearly no direction whatsoever. I floated off into the endless world with no idea where I was going. An "endless" world may sound exciting, but it is just a black background with a few stars permanently sitting in the distance. I eventually doubled back and spoted a hard to see asteroid belt that I needed to follow. This style covers half of the game, and could possibly be a fun challenge, if the other half wasn't just going to white dots on your map, getting some text, and going to a new white dot. Both types of gameplay are extremely tedious, and the battles take up very little of the actual gameplay.
This game looked very promising. But after playing it for a short while I realized it needed a lot of work to become what I would consider a good game. The many glitches (a few of which are gamebreaking), unpolished controls and menus, and the overall fidley gameplay make this game one I would certainly not recommend.

Let's start off with the pros on this review: The game itself is incredibly fun and entertaining for the while you play it. The content constantly has you sit there with a chuckle and looking back at stuff with a smile at least. There are many nodds to the South Park series (obviously) and they are well included in the game itself.
Cons? The game itself is incredibly short. I went up to 98% of the game's achievements with 24h playtime - two very dedicated days of gaming over the christmas vacations. And that was on the highest difficulty for combat, meaning that this game might even take way less if you play on a lower difficulty.
The combat itself is my next point: the combat while feeling fluent and constantly in motion is still a turn based combat game. They improved on the system from Stick of Truth (imo) by adding the grid based combat, leaving you to fight in 2 dimensions, but at the same time they remove one of those dimensions by only giving you attacks/abilities that fire in a straight line left or right. The up/down dimension is entirely diregarded in the game, and thus combat still doesn't feel like it has any depth. Also, it's slightly disappointing to see your choices for class to not have ANY consequence at all to the gameplay, especially towards the lategame, where you can just choose any ability from any class. It's nice in one way, but in another way it makes the whole choice feel incredibly pointless in the first place. Same goes for specific choices on your character sheet (i.e. alignment).
The last big con on my list of cons would probably be the quick times events. EVERYTHING in that game is tied to quicktime events, especially the cooperative powers you unlock with your buddies. Who the hell thought it would be good game design and fun to play with, to have to press F 6 times everytime I want Captain Diabetes use his coop power? Or whenever I want to use Human Kite's ability? Hell, all the coop abilities just feel clunky and the quick time events really feel like they're just in the game to buff up the game length. I'm pretty sure that if you excluded all the quick time events, the game time could easily be cut down by 30 minutes to an hour. It's just tedious, and also (for the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minigame) incredibly hard to pull off on the keyboard at times. Just turn the QTE into a small cutscene that plays whenever I want the buddy power to activate, and then be done. No "player interaction" required. Less frustrating feeling of time being wasted.

This game is fun, but it gets repetetive and the ending is just so, so underwhelming, which is frustrating. Could only recommend if you loved the specific combat style and approach of the first game, but even then, would only buy in a sale, rather than full price. 5/10

I'm a bit torn on this game. The combat is more complex than the first game, but not by much. Different characters have different combat abilities and you can mix and match your team as you progress through the story. The game offers hints and explanations of how to deal with enemies if you use the 'investigation mode' during combat, which helped prevent frustrating fights against powerful enemies.
The game also provides an assortment of little puzzles which are not difficult but at the same time can be a little tricky if you just overlook something. If you spend too much time standing in an area with a puzzle, the game may give you a hint or let you know that you cannot solve that puzzle until you gain a new ability/tool. The game felt like the designers put a fair amount of attention to detail when trying to make sure that players would not get stuck with puzzles or where to go next.
The negative side for me was in regards to the story. Trying to avoid too many comparisons to the first game, but the story in this game just was not as enjoyable for me. The over-the-top jokes and humor are toned down substantially here. I found myself chuckling throughout the game but rarely anything was actually hilarious enough that I wanted to truly laugh out loud. Humor aside, the story itself was pretty boring to work through. The game got better towards the final sequence
, but the ending was really just dumb.
I will recommend this game as the gameplay from a technical perspective is simplistic but good and makes for a solid experience. However the story is not as much fun to work through as it was in Stick of Truth. I did have fun playing through the game and would say that South Park fans should pick this up during a sale.

Also I had some weird audio bug that where some dialog was just omitted or just made this really nasty clipping noise. It was annoying, but only lasted for a second or so and occured infrequently enough that it did not hinder the gameplay.

I've had this game since launch, and despite a rather disapointing launch I would like to take the time to give this game a review it is worthy of. A comprehensive summary of the pro's and con's from about 35 hours of playtime:
Pro's:
- A fully functional, capable fighting system which adds on Mortal Kombat 9's gameplay (which is arguably the most important part)
- A good (for the most part) multiplayer mode, with a mostly good community (with a couple of annoying people)
- Whilst not the greatest looking game in the world it has fairly good graphics (with a good amount of customisability from the menu)
- LOTS OF GORE
- A large amount of features to keep you playing: Factions, Faction Wars, Daily Challenges, Online Matchmaking, A Variety of Gamemodes, Living Towers (towers that change hourly, daily and weekly), Challenge Towers, and a bit more.
- A nice selection of new characters and good returning characters
- A solid story mode which introduces you to the game and into characters that you may have not played if you had not played the story
Con's:
- There seems to be a large amount of lag online, whether that is serverside or problems with peoples' internet and location I don't know
- The DLC is expensive and can seem a bit like a money grab (although that won't change my thoughts on the base game, P.S. Please nerf Jason)
- Towers can sometimes seem a bit repetitive and sometimes just a bit annoying
- Some character's are easily spammable, producing unrealistic win to loss ratios in ranked matchmaking (although there are no cheap characters, only cheap players)
- JESUS CHRIST NETHEREALM, NERF UPPERCUTS
- The story seems a bit shorter than what was found in MK9
- A really bad launch, and apparently there are still some compatability issues. However, despite the fact that my MKX ran horribly for a while (I used a CPU fix in task manager) it now runs perfectly on full settings on my computer (which is just a bit above the recommended settings)
- An option to buy everything in the Krypt for £15 Netherealm? Really?
In all this is a very functional fighter which I enjoy greatly, possibly more than MK9 (judging from my playtime), it suffers from a few issues, the major ones have now been fixed, it looks good and plays well. For those who are judging this game on posts from lauch day, and posts ♥♥♥♥♥ing about DLC I would ask them to only take those into consideration when buying the DLC, the main game itself is very, and I mean very, good.
-Greg Alpacca

A charming action-adventure game with heavy Zelda influence and an inspiring soundtrack. You know the deal. I was pulled in immediately, and blown away by just how much detail was put into Oceanhorn. I actually felt compelled to 100% it and get all the achievements, which took just under 20 hours to do. For CAD16.99, an insane amount of enjoyment an quality was delivered.

It's true: Despite its own graphical style, isometic viewpoint, and some other quirks, Oceanhorn: Monster of Uncharted Seas is essentially a Legend of Zelda style game inside. But why is this a bad thing? As a diehard Zelda fan, I welcome the gaming industry to create their own attempts at Zelda-like games, whether from AAA developers or indies. And Oceanhorn does a fine job of being a fun game, even though almost all of its major elements are pretty much lifted from the Zelda series. But let's be fair here, bows, bombs, swords, shields, and sailing are far from monopolized by Zelda.
Getting into Oceanhorn itself, there's a lot to like about this game. The art style has its own charm, the isometric viewpoint is neat and a nice callback to games like Mario RPG and Landstalker, and the music... sublime. It all comes together in a wonderful presentation package that should delight anyone who can see past the game's obvious inspiration. The controls, for the most part, are pretty fluid, especially considering this is a port of an iOS game, and it felt just right on a controller, although the main character does move just the smallest bit slower than I'd like him to. The sailing atmosphere is gorgeous, and it's fun visiting new islands and charting them out, learning what secrets and people dwell there. The puzzles, while not entirely brainteasers, were the right amount of clever and made the game feel fluid. Dungeons are clever and designed expertly, with creative boss fights I quite enjoyed. In some ways it's a bit on the easy end, but no easier than your typical Zelda game.
The cons with this game are minor. There's the often-cited lack of a map screen, which would have been very handy. I find it odd that you can't dash or roll up steps, which would be nice for speeding up action. And the sailing is even more restrictive than that of Phantom Hourglass; in that game you could at least plot a course, but here, you can only select a destination. I would have liked a little more control, especially in that gorgeous atmosphere, but it's a minor concern.
Also, the game is too short. :(
But that's both a pro and a con; a con, because the game did feel a bit on the shorter side, and a pro, because I only wanted more.
In short, Oceanhorn is worth it if you're a fan of adventure games, especially Zelda obviously, whose only shortcomings are minor. Hopefully the game becomes successful enough to warrant a sequel in the future. Great product, Cornfox & Brothers, and may you see continued success!

Aside from the tragic story behind the creation of this game and leading to its generally buggy state (which generated my only negative opinions about this game), Kingdoms of Amalur is an excellent story. I haven't played many RPGs recently, having experienced more than a few failed starts in the genre. Amalur has made me excited once more to try out a new RPG.
The storytelling is excellent and the depth of the lore is very satisfying. There are even some solid gameplay elements present, with some of the combat experiences feeling quite exhilirating. It doesn't stray too far from the RPG formula, but introduces enough new gameplay elements to be interesting.
Although the story presents the main character as being "fateless," it should be noted there is but one fate available: the one the writers intended. I don't mind, because I rather enjoy experiencing a story in this fashion. Also, this is linearity done correctly: a nuanced, cohesive and satisfying story.
Please be warned: this game is very buggy. Remember to use multiple saves and to save often, especially if you suspect you might be entering a pivotal scene in the game's storyline. More than once, I had to reset and start entire areas over because of game-breaking bugs. Also, of course, if you are looking for a game more than you are looking for a story then you should look elsewhere.
