DISCLAIMER: The game was provided by the publishers. My opinion is based on the current state of the game which is still a really early alpha version.
Close Order is a simple space shooting game. I really tried to test it out but there really isnt more content right now than maybe 20-30 minutes if you try EVERYTHING in it out.
The game mechanics itself look ok. You move with W, A, S, D and aim and shoot with mouse. You get resources from destroying your enemies and can build more ships with them. Sadly it is too filled with unplayable, or rather untestable, content.
The game starts right in the game without any explanation. you just see a timer run out and a ship. Thats kinda ok since the controls are simple (i still found out only much later that i can actually go faster with shift XD) and i dont like handholding much but I still think there should be a little instruction box right under the timer with the controls for the first 5-10 seconds. Once the one minute runs out the intro just rolls in.
The text boxes where too fast for me even though I am a quick reader. The story is overused so i dont think it will become too great, but if the gameplay is fun it doesnt need a super story. That also gets me to the point that there is actually no story in the game yet. There is just that intro and then some random missions that dont connect together as a story. Also the things you had to do in the missions werent really explained. there was just a little marker of where you had to go with a small description and i didnt know what to do most of the time.
The story is way too hard to beat it so you got to play survival first to get more ship slots. The problem is that once you die in the survival mode that no enemies will spawn anymore so you cant really play it. You can try the custom survival since the first wave spawns but after the first wave there are no enemies again forcing you to suicide. I tried to play it for almost two hours and i still got no more slots unlocked so i dont know if i do something wrong or if the game is just bugged.
There was a bug that showed me at first that i would buy a ship with a weak triple shot that spreads randomly but it was the ship with the shield and after a restart it showed me normally the shield ship again. It seems after playing a while I cant buy the shooting ship because the button just cant be clicked anymore even though i have the resources for it. I have to fly arround with 4 shields then but I still end up dieing immediately even if all 4 ships are still full of life.
The resources seem totally broken. The number just hop arround as it likes. Once i have lots of them, then next time i see them i have almost none at all anymore. It also tells me sometimes i dont have enough resources to build a ship even though it shows me that i have more than enough but that has probably to do with the earlier mentioned broken resources counter.
It is annoying to aim with the shots since they are so slow and enemies are so small. It would be good to increase the bullet speed a bit. It is also hard since you cant see exactly how far the enemy is from you. there is no indication and you cant see arround since the camera is in a fixed angle. The camera should be rotatable to see how far the enemies are or  make the whole game use 3 dimensions (like be able to fly up and down and so on) The aiming of the enemies is also really bad. They just shoot exactly where you go. If you dont change your moving dirrection after they shot you will get hit.
The music is ok and fits the game but it gets repetitive quickly since there is no variation. There should be a few background songs at least.
The graphics are kind of good. Yes they arent comparable to those 60€+ games, but they still look enjoyable.
One of the few good things about the game and in my oppinion the best thing about it, are the developer. They seem to care about their game and if they really do, they will probably get everything to work later. I really hope they manage to get everything done and get a game many can enjoy.
All in all i just cant even slightly recommend this game even for a really early alpha acces game. It isnt even really testable. It just has the base mechanics like moving and shooting and absolutely NOTHING else. The developer should at least get a little story for the first 2-3 level or a halfway working survival mode at least before releasing it even as early acces in my oppinion. Yes it can have lots of bugs but, it shouldnt have so many game breaking ones. A little tip from me : The developer should upload this version for the public to play as a demo so that they get the oppinion of many more that dont want to spend 5 euro for an untestable game. I am sure that way they would get much more feedback. And the last thing i have to say is that i hope the developer have fun with their job since they will have a looooot of work to do and wish them good luck with the game :3
I will edit the review some time later too once there is more content in it gladly and give my oppinion about it then again.

Disclaimer: I was provided with a key by the publisher.
I'll start off by saying that the concept of the game is interesting. It really is. Humanity moved to the moon and other parts of space due to a nuclear accident that ended up burning the entire planet. Some time later, you and your crew of three want to go find the remnants of humanity either on Earth or somewhere else in space (didn't really catch which, see "Cons"). You get chased by some ships and have to shoot them. Once you get past the "tutorial," the menu gives you four options. There's a story mode, or Story Hub 1, that has five missions for you to choose from. Survival mode has regular and custom mode, custom being you can choose your own difficulty and enemy frequency. Advanced Minion Management (by the way, you can buy minions (or miniature ships) that fly beside yours and shoot enemies, but they have limited health) just explains ways to improve your minions, you don't really "do" anything. The fourth option, Story Hub 2, is currently unavailable.
-
The soundtrack is actually pretty nice when there's actually music; it's not annoying to listen to at all.
-
As I said before, the concept of the game interests me.
-
There were many times when the speed of the text disappearing on the screen was way too fast. I'm a pretty fast reader, and there were some times I only got about halfway through a blurb before it disappeared. I more or less had to skim through what was being said, so I'm sure I missed a good bit of information. The ability to move through text at our own pace is something that would help the players out.
-
After finishing the "tutorial," I decided to try a story mission. I spawned in, looked around to try and figure out what to do (it said "fight your way to The Emperor") and died three seconds later. Apparently there were ships shooting at me. They were hard to see and very overpowered. About 20-30 of them (a guesstimate, I really don't know how many there were) were all shooting at me at the same time, and their shots never miss unless you dodge them. And that was only the first mission. The other missions are overwhelmingly difficult as well.
-
If you can even call it that. You read through some text explaining the background story of the game, and then you're spawned in space, nothing around you on any side. It says "a ship is chasing you, destroy it." By that time I'd already looked around and lost track of which way was forward, so I flew off in a random direction (I only knew the controls because I read other reviews before downloading the game,
). I heard the ship firing, but couldn't determine where it was, so I stopped and decided to let it catch up to me. After waiting for a couple minutes and still seeing nothing, I flew towards where I thought the noise was coming from. I finally saw the ship and destroyed it. Then you have to do it a second time, and then you're teleported to the menu with the four choices. That's it. That's your tutorial. It doesn't explain how currencies work, or how to buy minions or anything like that.
-
The missions in Story Hub 1 aren't really explained. You're given a briefing, which from what I could tell (the text moved so fast) just gives you the background, not what you're actually supposed to do. I started the second mission, which was about rescuing some people whose ship was mutinied or something. A guide arrow kept pointing me back towards the ship, but it wouldn't let me go in it and I actually got stuck and started glitching out in the wall of the ship. Then I flew far enough away from the ship, looked back, and there was actually text floating above it telling me what I needed to do. But you can't look up or down, so I couldn't see it. That's just an example; the missions need better "briefings" as they're called.
I can't recommend this game in its current state. I just can't. It needs so much improvement; it looks like it was thrown together relatively quickly. There is so little content. Again, the concept is interesting, I just wish it were implemented better. I don't recommend buying it right now, maybe it will be better after an update or two.

Torchlight II is an incredible action RPG in the top-down, point-and-click style of Diablo. Having played both Diablo III and this game, I must say that I found Torchlight II preferable. Many call it "Diablo with guns" but Torchlight II is much more than that. The handy pet system gives you both a battle companion and a courier, carrying your unwanted loot back to town and selling it automatically. The extend of character customization permitted is also much greater than in Diablo. The combat feels much less detached and more engaging, which is a welcome tweak. The greatest advantage of Torchlight II is that you don't have to be constantly connected to the internet to play. You can play solo offline and even play co-op over LAN. In that regard, Torchlight II is much more respectful of you as a customer.

Honestly, I'm not a person too review games in much of any way because when I do, I am very cynical.
However, I personally have found Deus Ex: Mankind Divided to be generally quite pleasing.
(Also note, I didn't follow any hype and just bought it because new game that looked good so all content is a pleasant surprise to me.)
The game as far as I've played it, is interesting though. I personally find that it looks nice, it runs well even though I've got it at basically ultra maxed everything, it's fun, ya know? Nice combat, Nice abilities, great levels with depth, great characters and all around just pleasant to play.
To me this game is just like HR but more updated. On a side note though, it can be a little finicky in menus where it wont register a keystroke and wont close things properly, a few issues with random stutters but it's been rare on my end.
The stealth and non-lethal runs are what I prefer and I'm also a super heavy explorer type and it makes all of that interesting and inticing to do. I've spent probably 5 hours just literally walking around climbing and trying to get places, I mean I only just saved the doctor guy.
It's a little easy even on the hardest difficulty but again, sneaky runs are kind of easier than gun runs. In some aspects, not all.
I bought the deluxe season pass and yes as you may have heard, which I am very dissapointed and feel scammed, that the DLC and content is a single playthrough use. Literal cancer to single player games topped off with a nice hefty dosage of ingame store to make sure you want to cut them wrists open.
(Personally, I wont use the items -which you find in your inventory under "storage"- because I'd rather know I have them and possibly save them for (a) future save(s) if they make it multiple uses due to customer complaints)
It's a dirty tactic to sell and I think if they dont remove it and make it proper content not scum bag one time usage, a lot of people will not bother too buy and will refund and make the game flop, which is deserved of the publishers but the developers I feel bad for.

Deus Ex is a superb RPG shooter. It acheives greatness across all spectrums, story, gameplay, graphics and replay value. Each and every area, quest, and objective has a multitude of possibilites for how to play them. Theres no question its an excellent game, but it has a few glaring defects.
The game feels incomplete, throughout most of the quests. From the main story quests to petty side quests, there is rarely closure or the satisfaction of catharsis. One such quest has you investigate an intriguing story of how Jensen has super high tech experimental augs secretly installed inside him. This "quest" has you go to an apartment room with a corpse, and look around for a moment and thats it. You get no answers and only have more questions, and bam the quest ends. Wtf? I dont understand why they would even initiate a subplot like that to simply kill it immediately after. Squandering a story with such potential is a sin.
Another quest has you look into a murder, analyze evidence and question a witness and suspect. The quest ends with you not finding anything out and the entire story stops in its tracks, unsolved. Then bam quest ends and again, a story with great potential squandered and lost to mediocrity. There is a recurring pattern of plotlines stopping suddenly, never to be heard of again. It seems like either poor writing, or more likely set ups for a sequel. Most people assumed those quests were part of cut content that was to be shoe horned into paid DLC. Since the game is older now, that is not going to happen. So the only logical assumption left is lead ins for a sequel, which is lame. Who is even going to remember let alone care about the half finished plots of side quests years from now when the next one comes out?

I've had this game since launch, and despite a rather disapointing launch I would like to take the time to give this game a review it is worthy of. A comprehensive summary of the pro's and con's from about 35 hours of playtime:
Pro's:
- A fully functional, capable fighting system which adds on Mortal Kombat 9's gameplay (which is arguably the most important part)
- A good (for the most part) multiplayer mode, with a mostly good community (with a couple of annoying people)
- Whilst not the greatest looking game in the world it has fairly good graphics (with a good amount of customisability from the menu)
- LOTS OF GORE
- A large amount of features to keep you playing: Factions, Faction Wars, Daily Challenges, Online Matchmaking, A Variety of Gamemodes, Living Towers (towers that change hourly, daily and weekly), Challenge Towers, and a bit more.
- A nice selection of new characters and good returning characters
- A solid story mode which introduces you to the game and into characters that you may have not played if you had not played the story
Con's:
- There seems to be a large amount of lag online, whether that is serverside or problems with peoples' internet and location I don't know
- The DLC is expensive and can seem a bit like a money grab (although that won't change my thoughts on the base game, P.S. Please nerf Jason)
- Towers can sometimes seem a bit repetitive and sometimes just a bit annoying
- Some character's are easily spammable, producing unrealistic win to loss ratios in ranked matchmaking (although there are no cheap characters, only cheap players)
- JESUS CHRIST NETHEREALM, NERF UPPERCUTS
- The story seems a bit shorter than what was found in MK9
- A really bad launch, and apparently there are still some compatability issues. However, despite the fact that my MKX ran horribly for a while (I used a CPU fix in task manager) it now runs perfectly on full settings on my computer (which is just a bit above the recommended settings)
- An option to buy everything in the Krypt for £15 Netherealm? Really?
In all this is a very functional fighter which I enjoy greatly, possibly more than MK9 (judging from my playtime), it suffers from a few issues, the major ones have now been fixed, it looks good and plays well. For those who are judging this game on posts from lauch day, and posts ♥♥♥♥♥ing about DLC I would ask them to only take those into consideration when buying the DLC, the main game itself is very, and I mean very, good.

This is coming from someone who likes games that are skill base versus item base and I'll share my experience with the game.
This is one of the item base games meaning that you have to use items more than skill, many traps I ran into I had to use items just to throw it or shoot it to win against a target. You run into areas that are unfair meaning you have to save your items, litteraly this means you're force to go around the level collecting enough gold to buy the next items to save you, in fact drops will kill you so your force to use items. It doesn't take much skill to use an item but it does take skill to dodge a trap.
Now some areas I ran into that you're not force to use items, where it's a clear run to the goal, which is fine.
Now the skill base things I do like are shaving the people in trouble because those have a risk and reward factor along with juggling between people versus the only challenge being how much money do you have and did you waste too many items?
Consvering items works as a challenge when you don't have a lot of items, otherwise the game is easy, though at least in those games they encourage you to think like use time and spacing to kill your target versus, "you pressed a button! You win!" When I got an item, it was, press a button and I win against a target. -_- now resident evil 7, you pressed a button! but your going have to think this one through... set back up at choke point or no, push through and hope to find an item to save your life? Versus, "move around a little bit and you'll be fine!" Litteraly, the choices are obivous to make in this game, if your very liberal with your items, your going to die, a lot, hell in a couple seconds I made it to the end of a level all because I saved my items!
Hell this wouldn't be a problem if I had to be skillful with my items at least.

***Disclosure: Key was provided by the developer for review purposes***
It's basically a Zelda-clone. And it really doesn't hide that fact at all. One of the very first things you encounter are pots you can pick up and throw in order to destroy them. There are bushes you can cut down with your sword in order to collect money, bombs and arrows and you have to explore dungeons in order to collect three pieces of a mystical item that helps you defeat the final boss. You also get a new, stronger sword and a new shield over the course of the game. The only thing it doesn't directly lift form Zelda games is the fact that there isn't a princess in this. Otherwise it's an extremely faithful homage to Link's adventures, especially Wind Waker and Phantom Hourglass, since it incorporates a lot of sailing as well.
I think the most interesting aspect about the game is the fact that it actually came out on mobile devices first. Because while playing it on PC, I honestly wouldn't have guessed its origins. The interface is perfectly adapted for PC and it's playable with both controller and mouse and keyboard. And for a mobile game it's definitely quite a lengthy game to play. It took me on PC around 10 hours to get through and I haven't even collected all the hidden secrets in there and even for a proper PC game the length is adequate enough. The only thing it's lacking is good bossfights. There are only really six bossfights and two of those don't involve any strategies beyond holding up your shield and countering when the enemy is exposing himself. Three of the boss fights are the ones where you collect the faux-Triforce shards and then the last one at the very end. Even though you need to employ different tactics to beat them, they're not all that challenging to figure out.
And since there's only three shards to collect, there are only really three big dungeons to explore. The other dungeons are very small and don't contain many puzzles. And speaking of the puzzles, they're mostly very easy block pushing or switch pressing puzzles. Only one of the puzzles was rather hard for me to guess, the rest is fairly straightforward.
Other than that I can say that I'm very pleased with the art style. They really managed to capture the typical whimsical Zelda aesthetic. Though what elevates the experience is definitely the soundtrack. It does take a lot of inspiration from other video game composers, but it's still very enjoyable and very fitting to all your surroundings.
If there's one problem I had, at least with the beta build I got for review purposes, it's the amount of crashes I suffered. The game constantly crashed on me for no apparent reason, and it had tremendous difficulty maintaining 60 FPS on my rig which is saying a lot. Though I did notice that the crashes subsided on the day prior to release, so maybe they've fixed it. Though really, the crashes were only annoying in the sense that I had to restart the game. Because the auto-save function is pretty damn awesome in this game, I barely lost any progress while playing it, so there's that at least.
In the end, it's an obvious Zelda-clone because that's exactly what it wants to be. And for an effort from a small indie studio form Finland it's definitely not a bad one. It obviously can't hold a candle to a proper Zelda-game, but keep in mind that they're created by an army of programmers, artists and composers who basically swim in Nintendo-money.

I have to start by saying I absolutely cannot recommend this game at all even if it was a free game.
YES I know its early access and we'll all get the "Just wait for updates" which is something I always say whenever people criticizes a good early access game, but sadly this is not the case here, this game currently is so horrible I want to forget the experience of playing it and I have a very low standards on what can please me in a game, the entire game feels like a bunch of people got together to make a game and none of them have any experience with video games whatsoever.
There's a small story explaining some parts of the game.
Then you start by controlling this ship not knowing exactly what to do due to serious lack of instructions, left click to attack, wasd for movement and right click to open the "minion" menu to spawn them as you can see in the screenshot, you can also change their formation as you like.
Truth is the story feels like it doesn't hold anything to the game, since its just a video then some dialogues and then just fire at enemies.
I usually start by saying the good parts of a game but since this one almost has none lets do it differently this time.
- The game starts in an open stage with a 60 second timer, I have no idea what was that for, could it possibly be that the items you *retrieved* at that time change the game's story depending on which you got ? Nah cant be that right ?
- Controls are simple but so dull, just moving and shooting which should be fun but somehow isn't.
- Difficulty in video games should be challenging, fun and maybe frustrating, but in this game its absolutely unfair, you get totally overwhelmed by ships of enemies shooting at an insanely fast fire-rate that you cannot possibly avoid it and get destroyed from the start, they tell you if the game is hard try survival mode to increase minion capacity, but ...that is also so unfair its practically impossible to pass, if they could at least reduce their fire-rate it would be reasonable, I think the reason why I got past this is because of the glitch in the parade level that made me slightly overpowered.
- The game is riddled with bugs, if you click on the "simple" survival and lose or quit, next time you try to play the mode the enemies wont respawn so you have to restart the game, there is this parade level that increases the minion count to 40, I think this is a bug because that's a big number considering I didn't do much to get it, you also get this minion that fires these bullets that keeps circling around you and you can't stop it from firing once it starts, if you get a couple more of the same minion the bullets would become too much you would experience frame drops, I did with my gtx 860 build at "Good" graphics option, hell I think even at the lowest one with a high-end system you'd still get serious fps drops because it is a bug eventually, there is also this level that features a button that supposedly shows an intro video story but I click on it and nothing happen, there are so many other bugs but I'll reach the maximum character limit in the review.
- Once you fail a level on warp after finishing, the screen teleports to the beginning of the game, which is 4 portals  -> survival mode -> Hub story -> minion management -> Hub story 2 "coming soon" .
You just use Hub story that features a couple of levels with their own missions or survival mode, I still dislike how it suddenly teleports me back there, the transition looks undone.
- Levels start with a pointer telling you where to go, "Defend this"  " Kill this "  "Stop that" those are the scenarios you should expect, but they're delivered poorly considered they don't really execute in a good manner, also that most of the time when you go to the pointer nothing happens and this is also an annoying bug. Story hub 1 which features about 6 levels is all you get in the game and they all play the same, just move and shoot.
- I am not really a slow reader but the story dialogues moves way too fast for me to actually read it, I think I was able to read about 60% of each before it auto-skipped to next one.
- The method they're using in accessing levels, going into the portal and seeing the list, needs a lot of work, if you have a lot of minions they will block the level you're trying to click on with the cursor and will have to keep moving them around ...
- A couple of levels I wasn't able to finish because of some enemies descending slightly "note that you cannot go up or down in the game" so I wasn't able to kill them and they kept hovering.
- Enemies in are unfair, they come out and keeps shooting at an insane fire-rate, if you managed to survive that, you'll notice that after firing they just sort of drifts of in space and do nothing .. so you can kill them easily, in most levels they get out of the "zone" which you can steer in and you cannot finish the level without killing them.
I think the only good part about this game is the soundtrack.... but judging about how the entire game plays out I have to assume the developers got it from unity assets store... hmm maybe also the fact that its early access and could get improved.
0/10, they released this game way too early, should've at least invested a whole year in it before releasing it on early access, early access means giving something playable and working on it, not giving us something that can be bested by a unity template project.
The concept of the game is nice but its executed horribly.

First 10 hours: 9/10
Completed: Will update
As someone who has logged over 300 (recorded *cough) hours in Skyrim, and rates it as a 10/10, this game is like a slightly less version of it. The combat is a little more awkward than in Skyrim due to a loose camera that kind of spins during battle, but otherwise, this game is comparable and the next-best-thing to it. If you loved Skyrim, you will at least like this game.
COMBAT: General action RPG combat. Comparable to Skyrim with a few more weapon types, at least unique weapon types. As I mentiond above, the camera is not amazing. You will get turned around a bit in battle, but it doesn't ruin the game for most people. There are a few weapons with an animation lock 2-3 attacks in that can be annoying, but they are very powrful weapon types that were probably designed this way on purpose. It's a third person game with no real target locking, you kind of aim in the general direction and it auto-locks that attack onto the monster if it is a spell or bow attack. It's not bad, but it's worth noting.
STORY: The overall story is good so far, the premise is unique and it tells the story (thus far) very well. The voice acting is good, and EVERYONE you talk to is voice acted. The real goodness in this game is the lore though. Surpisingly, I did not read Skyrim lore. I just saw the books and didn't feel like reading them, yet in here, I read every single book I get. There is no explanation for that, because the lore in Skyrim was amazing, but maybe I like the format of the text better. Either way, the lore is rich and it's full of so many notes, journals and books that tell you about the people around them. If you read the books in Skyrim, you will love them here, and if you didn't, you still might like it as I do. There is a lot of humor to be had in the journals that you steal from people.
LEVELING SYSTEM: It's very similar to Skyrim. You have a sizable tree, slightly smaller than Skyrim's. You also do not choose a class. You choose which trees and how deep you go down in them. You can go down the fighter tree, the rogue-like tree or the mage tree, as much or as little as you want and be a hybrid class of your own. I personally love being an assassin mage. This game makes you want to hybrid more though. In Skyrim my characters are pure mage, pure warrior and pure rogue. There are also skill trees for useful things like lockpicking, stealth, blacksmithing etc. The only thing that sets it apart from Skyrim, and only in a small way are the FATEs that you pick. You can have one bonus FATE at any given time. If you have a lot of mage points in the mage tree, you will probably get one of the mage FATEs giving you extreme magic dmg and mana boosts, but there are hybrid cards that give you bonuses to a hybrid mix, or all the bonus types, but in smaller, scaled levels of each.
MAP: It's huge. Not the size of Skyrim of course, but pretty large. It's set up the same way. You can follow the main story, but everywhere you go will have a new side quest you can do which will cause you to go off trail. That is what I loved and hated so much about Skyrim, my OCD makes me want to 100% everything, but I keep getting more quests before I finish the previous ones. This isn't actually a bad thing, there are so many things to do, but if Skyrim made your OCD cry, this game will too.
SUMMARY: It's Skyrim. If you haven't played Skyrim, then go buy it instead; it's actually cheaper. If you have played Skyrim and you are done with it, but looking for more, then this is your game. It won't be the same, it's got its own lore and character to it, but it will bring that feeling of adventure back.

Close Order is a 3rd person space shooter game where you can grow your armada with minions (fleet).
Graphics
This game uses 3d models to give it more of a dark realistic look to it. Some cool planets and big ship type in the play space.
Sound
Close Order has background and sound effects. Nothing really stands out, it needs more gripping music and more different sounds such as your ship just exploded sound.
Controls
Uses keyboard and mouse, I didn’t feel like the controls hindered me but I would like to use a controller.
Gameplay
I’m a sucker for space battle games, so having lots of missions and different ships are great.
Replay value
Seems to have more missions coming soon and a survivor mode which gives good replay value. The dev team seem to be pushing out updates and fixes often so I’m sure more will come.
My Opinion
First off I like this game and understand it’s still an early access game, with that said I would like to see controller support. I like the look of the game using 3d space ships and the feel of space, but giving more sense of “moving” such as the ship leaning to the left, right, up or down would add more to the game. I want to feel more like I’m in space and use those space physics. My first time playing I had a difficult time following the text on the screen, as the characters were too small which made reading the text with no control over the speed of the text difficult. For the gameplay a radar would be nice to have. Also to be able to move faster from some kind of upgrade would be nice and this is an arcade/ bullet type game.

It's basically a Zelda-clone. And it really doesn't hide that fact at all. One of the very first things you encounter are pots you can pick up and throw in order to destroy them. There are bushes you can cut down with your sword in order to collect money, bombs and arrows and you have to explore dungeons in order to collect three pieces of a mystical item that helps you defeat the final boss. You also get a new, stronger sword and a new shield over the course of the game. The only thing it doesn't directly lift form Zelda games is the fact that there isn't a princess in this. Otherwise it's an extremely faithful homage to Link's adventures, especially Wind Waker and Phantom Hourglass, since it incorporates a lot of sailing as well.
I think the most interesting aspect about the game is the fact that it actually came out on mobile devices first. Because while playing it on PC, I honestly wouldn't have guessed its origins. The interface is perfectly adapted for PC and it's playable with both controller and mouse and keyboard. And for a mobile game it's definitely quite a lengthy game to play. It took me on PC around 10 hours to get through and I haven't even collected all the hidden secrets in there and even for a proper PC game the length is adequate enough. The only thing it's lacking is good bossfights. There are only really six bossfights and two of those don't involve any strategies beyond holding up your shield and countering when the enemy is exposing himself. Three of the boss fights are the ones where you collect the faux-Triforce shards and then the last one at the very end. Even though you need to employ different tactics to beat them, they're not all that challenging to figure out.
And since there's only three shards to collect, there are only really three big dungeons to explore. The other dungeons are very small and don't contain many puzzles. And speaking of the puzzles, they're mostly very easy block pushing or switch pressing puzzles. Only one of the puzzles was rather hard for me to guess, the rest is fairly straightforward.
Other than that I can say that I'm very pleased with the art style. They really managed to capture the typical whimsical Zelda aesthetic. Though what elevates the experience is definitely the soundtrack. It does take a lot of inspiration from other video game composers, but it's still very enjoyable and very fitting to all your surroundings.
If there's one problem I had, at least with the beta build I got for review purposes, it's the amount of crashes I suffered. The game constantly crashed on me for no apparent reason, and it had tremendous difficulty maintaining 60 FPS on my rig which is saying a lot. Though I did notice that the crashes subsided on the day prior to release, so maybe they've fixed it. Though really, the crashes were only annoying in the sense that I had to restart the game. Because the auto-save function is pretty damn awesome in this game, I barely lost any progress while playing it, so there's that at least.
In the end, it's an obvious Zelda-clone because that's exactly what it wants to be. And for an effort from a small indie studio form Finland it's definitely not a bad one. It obviously can't hold a candle to a proper Zelda-game, but keep in mind that they're created by an army of programmers, artists and composers who basically swim in Nintendo-money.

Oceanhorn: Monster of Uncharted Seas is a zelda-style RPG Adventure game currently available on Steam. In Oceanhorn you play as a boy who's father has left him a notebook and a mysterious necklace, you read the notebook and follow in your father's footsteps in attempting to slay the legendary Oceanhorn. In order to be able to defeat Oceanhorn you must travel the length and bredth of the Uncharted Seas to find ancient artifacts and powerful magic all while solving puzzles and fighting enemies.
Just to say I have actually played the game longer than Steam says but due to disconnecting it hasn't saved all of my progress.
+Nice graphics which are bright and colourful
+A large map filled with many large islands for you to explore
+The world itself and the stories behind the different locations are quite interesting
+Outstanding soundtrack
+Quite a lot of items to unlock as you progress through the game
+The three biomes as well as the islands that make them up are very different to the others
+The game's puzzles are challenging without being painfully difficult
+Nice variety of enemies
+Simple combat system which for the most part is good (I'll come back to this later)
+Very relaxing to play
+Appropriate for all ages
+Full controller support and I suggest you do play with a controller
+/-Voice acting is very hit and miss in Oceanhorn, some of the time I thought it was quite good other times it just falls flat
-The story isn't particularly interesting
-I experienced a lot of framerate slow downs to pretty much single digits, judging from other reviews this is a problem for more than just me
-Sailing between islands is pretty dull as you can't steer your ship, only shoot objects with a gun you unlock and these sections cannot be skipped
Worth a mention:
-Oceanhorn was originally an iOS game which has now been ported to PC which could explain some of the performance issues
Verdict:
8
A fun and relaxing RPG, Adventure game with nice graphics and an outstanding soundtrack that helps to prove that not all iOS ports are bad.

I'm about half way through the game.
You can tell it took a lot of influence from the Zelda series, but it lacks that feeling of true adventure.
I'm enjoying the game, and I think it's worth a try. It's not terribly expensive, but I would probably wait for a sale.
Each area is fairly linear with only a few secrets on each island.
The travel method is automatic, so don't expect to explore the ocean. I haven't hit a fast travel option yet, which would be nice.
The difficulty is like a rollercoaster. Minions are very easy and have a simple AI, while bosses are extremely powerful and use cheap tricks to destroy you.
The story is good enough to keep me interested, but I'm not burning through the game to find out what's going to happen.
While my laptop is older now, the game isn't optimized well for Windows. The framerate drops often. It's most likely using OpenGL instead of Directx (especially that using DX would require severe amounts of recoding)
Overall, I enjoy the game, so I recommend it. I just wish they gave us a bit more to explore.

And play Mortal Kombat X! Scorpion says it best, and should entice both newcomers to fighting games and MK veterans. As someone who played the previous Mortal Kombat game, I can testify that the fighting system and feel of the moves is much more robust and improved. This is a game that has been well-worked on and refined to allow for precise and feel-good execution of moves. I cannot recommend it enough.
COMPLAINTS ABOUT MULTIPLAYER SLOWNESS CANNOT BE APPLIED TO ALL USERS. It is incredibly variable and mostly dependent on individual internet capabilities, and widespread lag has been greatly reduced since the first few weeks.
In addition to gameplay mechanics, MKX features a wide variety of specializable characters that allow for a new fight every time. All 25-odd Non-DLC characters feature 3 different variations, essentially giving the game 100 different play-styles if all DLC is acquired. Each character has unique dialogue, and if Scorpion is fighting Mileena, he will refer to her by name or trait in one of several intros. It is remarkable that a game with such exceptional gameplay has such strong characters as well, but you can believe that you will find at lease 6 characters unbelievably bad♥♥♥♥♥in some way.
I play Liu Kang almost exclusively. He has three variations, each giving him different special moves and essentially redefining his playstyle. Each variation also gives him a slightly new skins. He also has a number of skins purchasable or obtainable through gameplay. He has hundreds of lines of dialogue and his character model looks and behaves great. I only play one character and still have a blast with MKX.
If you can afford it or catch it on sale, MKX is fun for all and replayable for hours, online or offline. If you are not very good, playing against easy bots offline is still fun and will refine your reflexes and skills quickly. The revolutionary practice mode is difficult to explain but impressive and remarkably useful. If you have any doubts, check out the Mortal Kombat Community channel on YouTube for some cool trailers and character breakdowns.
3 TIPS FOR AN MK BEGINNER
1. Pick an easy character to start with. Scorpion is great, as is Sub-Zero
2. Some projectiles will hit you if you crouch-duck but not if you simply duck
3. Don't button-mash, don't projectile-spam, and BLOCK

The Hat Man: Shadow Ward is a horror game that sends you off in a hospital hell to collect journal pages and overcome obstacles in an attempt to bring your daughter home. Using a simple search-and-find-the-pages mechanic used in other very famous horror games, The Hat Man also adds the twist of having a changing maze inside the asylum so that one hallway isn't always the one you just came from. You're fleeing The Hat Man, a paranormal anomaly called a shadow person, who feeds upon the sick and weak. Did I mention he can teleport? He does that.
A lot.
God I'm gonna steal that stupid hat and throw it down the hall and see if that'll distract him. I digress.
The game isn't difficult. Notes are shrouded in whispers so as you find yourself outside a room containing one, the whispers within your head becoming maddening (they might even drive you...insane? RIMSHOT.) Your foe moves slowly enough that you can out run him or you can hide if you find a perfect method of how to do it. Rooms are spacious that if you plan things, you can loop around to bypass the hovering spectre. That is, if you're quick about it. I didn't have so much luck with this. I ended up rushing into walls and getting caught just by that last second and ended up starting over. Sigh.
As this is a horror game, you're probably asking just how scary is it. Shadow people, as we know them, tend to be these looming types that are said to stand there and make you feel uncomfortable. The Hat Man is designed well enough that he gives you a you a nice shock when he teleports right into your face in a very literal way. One second you've left him five hallways away and POOF, there he is! You can also see him coming from a good distance off so you're feeling pretty free to give him the finger. He's not gruesome, but just unsettling enough that he reinforces the stories of shadow people being vague, smoky, and shadowy outlines of people who are unable to take proper forms. He's a bit menacing so that was good enough for me. Good enough for me to swear every time he tried to tickle me with those ugly hands.
As for the feel of the game, I mentioned it's a good hospital hell. You've got rotting bodies, the sound of people crisping against defibs (I jumped a foot), the traditional falling ceiling tiles, loud noises to freak you out as you turn corners, and the much appreciated radio playing assorted music. I loved the pieces that made me feel like it was a Twilight Zone episode. The radio is a nice touch. It's something a lot of games do, but not many use them so nicely as this, I believe.
You can play as the father or mother. This has no bearing on the story. Your child's sarcasm and dull humor as noted in the diary OBVIOUSLY comes from your commentary. You are a parent on a mission and somehow you even make some off-color comments at the start of this adventure. (Father calls the asylum a funhouse. Mother says homemaker turned homewrecker.) Upon reading the journal, even your daughter has found time to make off-color comments about her own situation. The apple has not fallen far from the tree. This amused me greatly. I didn't find it out of character at all. It seems like a perfect defense mechanism in a horrible time like that. (Referring to her attempts as a "been there, done that" light heartedly in group therapy which horrifies everyone who has never attempted? Yes as someone who has been there, I find this very funny.)
Overall, the game is one that's simple in premise and offers gameplay that a majority can enjoy. However, I noticed a few things that did make my gameplay a little less enjoyable.
Upon playing, the save function that was hinted to was not obvious to me. There was no button or indication of an autosave. Even after accomplishing a set of actions where the Hat Man was unable to get me (and I kept mercilessly taunting him until I got stuck in another maze ahaha don't do this.), there was no save function that appeared. Unfortunately, I'm a handicapped gamer and I do need breaks after hitting buttons for a while. I'm just confused if I'm missing something. I did search the forums and I wonder if only I'm missing it. This made the game entirely difficult for me and made me lose interest greatly.
The mother's subtitles have a few typos. I noticed. It didn't really kill the game for me but I spotted them.
The journal's audio seems a bit off. Is that audio that was placed there that we're not supposed to hear? That doesn't sound like the daughter's normal voice-over. Nothing game killing here, either.
Notes for the handicapped gamers like myself: You're going to get tired while navigating. Pause frequently. Take breaks. I'm paused right now, matter of fact. There are flickering lights and flashes. If you are triggered by flashing lights at all, I would exercise extreme caution with this game. I would go as far to say this is not a good idea and play at your own risk.
The story is rather unique and I'm happy to see someone use shadow people as a source of horror fuel as they're one of the most common paranormal occurrences in the world. It's a little bare bones and maybe even cliched, but it does well enough. The world of the "limbo asylum" is rough yet rather beautiful. You're not getting AAA graphics because after all, it's an indie horror, but it's pretty enough to know that even if the world you're traversing in does repeat in a maze of horror, there was some time taken to make sure that everything looked properly decrepit and set out. Though large hospital rooms seem more for gameplay benefit rather than realism. You will be kissing the ground for those large rooms.
This game reaches a wide audience. There are those who like medical horror in their video games, those who enjoy the collect-and-boo type horror games, those who enjoy chase-type games, and those who are constantly in the need of challenging themselves to beat their time. Trust me. You'll want to tackle the achievements to beat Hat Boy in record time.

Brutal Legend was a curious experiment by Double Fine that delivered on a lot of fronts, but also kind of bit itself in the tuckus. In its attempt to blend action adventure and RTS gameplay elements, Brutal Legend surprised a good number of players who came looking for the former, and left some feeling as much as betrayed by the presence of the latter. Personally, I'd seen enough going into things to not feel like any deception was going on, but marketing could have been a bit clearer.
That being said, Brutal Legend is still a loving tribute to metal music through and through, no matter what you think of the gameplay. The way it draws upon multiple core threads of metal and offshoot musical genres for both its soundtrack and its aesthetic is fantastic, providing a yin and yang of visuals and audio that accompany one another perfectly. Even with many elements traditionally clashing with one another, Brutal Legend knits together all its source material into a unique yet familiar world that many a music fan has only dreamed of.
However, even with how well everything's tied together, Brutal Legend does often feel like there might be a bit too much. The dragon statues hidden throughout the world as a collectable unlock feel a bit too numerous. The variety of upgrades for your ride, the Druid Plow, feel excessive and unnecessary after a while. That is, unless you're chasing the racing mini-games, which also feel like they could have done without at least one. I could just be bitter on that last front, as the last one was so exacting, it's one of the few things that have ever made me throw a controller in rage. Overall, the game suffers from a case of quantity being thrown on top of quality, instead of reining things in a bit once the quality is already there.
As for the RTS combat, I enjoyed most of it after getting the hang of things and getting better at intervening directly. Bringing your own axe and power chords into the fight is essential, especially during some of the more difficult battles later on. A couple of the setups for battles felt unfair, and I distinctly recall one of the last engagements with the goth army taking several attempts that were very, very long and arduous. If anything, just make absolutely sure you know what your units are good at, and you'll be able to economize your production a bit better to deal with that sort of thing.
I loved all the performances in the game, both musical and vocal, despite not really being a Jack Black fan. Lemmy (RIP) delivers what could be considered the flattest performance as the Killmeister, but his character is pretty much written as being indifferent, so it works.
Sure, there's nay-saying about a lot of things, including the way Brutal Legend was handled on the marketing front, but it's still got that Double Fine magic. I'm all about seeing other people give this a chance, and hoping we do eventually see a follow-up way down the line.

I see a lot of promise in this game, and it really does seem like a fun concept. While I say that, there does seem to be a lot of work that still needs to be done on it. It is as alpha as a game can get, and at the moment it seems really messy and not straightforwards. The story line did not seem to be interesting enough to keep me reading and instead I just skipped right through the briefings. I still have yet to play this game more, but at the moment my first thoughts are that I am going to wait for a bit for things to get a little more finesse'd.
I like the crossroads idea, and the idea of flying from mission/fleet formation editor/etc, but right now I don't see why I have this 'hub' of options in the first place. I also think that right off the bat, you're overpowered, you can immediately fill up 40 slots with drones, and just take out wave after wave of enemies.
On the note of enemies, I loaded up the parade mission and it was just stuck on 'enjoy the parade' and nothing else happened. So i quit. Then I went to the one where the Tsar bomb explodes, and I didn't even know that I wasn't supposed to get near the bomb carrier? Or something happened and I just immediately died. There isn't a lot of clarity of what I should be doing in the missions, and an objectives log, for example, in the top right corner or something would be really helpful of keeping track what you're supposed to be doing. Briefings should also be readable, so that way you can just skim through if you want to and still be up to date on what the mission is about. This game also needs a bit more backstory of who you are where you came from and why you're doing these missions in the first place. First time play through you shouldn't be able to skip the first cutscene (I did by accident) and I missed the intro.
I'd like to see something like a tech tree, or unlockables for your armada, so that you get new ships, and all of them aren't available to you yet.
All in all, this really seems like a solid game, but as of right now, I would not recommend buying it for 7.79. Perhaps if it goes on sale or if it is given out for free, try it for sure. But the state of the game makes me want to wait until there are more patches and the game is smoothed out a little more. I may edit my review later on as well.

The developers have shown true commitment to their customers and their own vision. The game has grown and now shines. It's not for everyone and the core concept might be alien to casual gamers but for those who are looking for something original and challenging will find warm & fuzzy feelings with Close Order. As an indie developer and a proponent of innovation in gaming I fully support this team. For $5 I think this is a great deal.
ORIGINAL REVIEW BELOW:
I am recommending to purchase the game only for those with patience and an interest in actually contributing to the development of a game. This game needs a lot of help from the community as the developer is capable but apparently inexperienced with game design.  NOTED IMPROVEMENTS: tutorial is great now, the UI is improved and polished, the few bugs I encountered originally are all gone, the difficulty curve seems to have been smoothed out as well. Exceptional improvement IMHO. Well done Raconteur Games!
There are core design decisions in place that are interesting and could prove to be really fun with a lot of polish and refinement. Missions are currently disjointed and transitions are abrupt and break the fourth wall. Your "minions"(fleet) disappear suddenly and without reason or even explosive effect in one mission. If you skipped the conversation, as many shooter fans do, it is confusing. I kept spending my amassed fortune replacing those ships only to have them suddenly dissapear again. 3 times I did this until broke and finally understood that this mission forces you to go alone. Unfortunately this is the sort of unrefined gameplay I was mentioning. An experienced developer would know to remove player's ability to spend on new ships and when they attempt to do so, place an explanatory message on screen. It takes 10 minutes to code but without user feedback and direction, it will never happen.
The game is less than $5 and has tons of potential but don't buy it expecting others to fix it for you. It has a small user population and the forum is empty right now. Buy it and help out or stay clear until reviews at "final release".

Tekken 7 is my first fighting game that I've decided to take seriously.
The graphics are great, the customisation allowed for each character is fairly large and overall the gameplay itself is fantastic. The movement in this game feels great and the combat itself is quite intense, along with some slow motion moments that pump you with adrenaline!
Outside of gameplay, the game runs completely fine without any hiccups (i5-4670k, GTX 1060 6GB) and the load times are very short.
The only noticeable issue, for new players to Tekken, is the lack of tutorials. Some could argue that the story mode is the tutorial, but that's unacceptable. The story mode misses out a huge portion of mechanics hidden within the game, such as all of your recovery options when you're slammed onto the ground.
The only real way to learn how to play Tekken 7, outside of learning by yourself through practice mode or online matches, is to research tutorials and mechanics online.

My favorite Genre is the Rogue Like.  They are tough, fast (sometimes) and they rarely get old and stale.  Of all the rogue likes I have played, Spelunky is by far my favorite.  The mechanics are pretty simple and easy to understand, yet very hard to master, making it a game almost anyone can enjoy at any skill level.  I feel other Rogue likes often try to use some sort of gimmick to enhance the experience, such as Enter the Gungeon fusing the bullet hell genre or Rogue Legacy, allowing you to chose from a variety of heroes, based on the traits of former heroes on your run. Spelunky on the other hand feels like a pure Rogue Like, right to its core and as such doesn't need flashy gimmicks to stand out from the crowd.  Highly recommend this game, especially with the low cost.  If this is on sale, buy it.

It's got all the pieces that made Human Revolution a really fun game, but it has put them together all wrong.
You can see a lot of hate for the in-game microtransactions in other reviews; while I understand the dislike, it really is purely optional.  It shouldn't bother you or affect your game if I'm so bad at it that I have to pay to get extra help.  Certainly doesn't bother me if I only finish the game on easy but you want to finish on "real life" mode.  The microtransactions are a strange choice, and I think a bad one, but not worth hating.
But the way everything fits together might be worth your scorn.  Maybe the painfully bad writing will be what drives you away.  Maybe the dull, unbelievable voice acting will do that.  Perhaps it'll be the insultingly blatant fencing used to make small and unimaginative world maps take more time to get through.  Or all that might be fine to you but you won't be happy with the clunky controls while in stealth. What is safe to say, is that something will drive you away from this game.  Because everything is so close to good that not only is it not good, but it'll build up your hope in the intro/tutorial and then just dash all those hopes with no care at all.
Wait a bit.  Let it get patched up, maybe get some things smoothed out.  It's close to a good enough game to recommend.  Just not yet.

I wanted to like this game....I really did, but the mechanics are just broken compared to the last game. I don't know why they changed it so much. Some parts of the game are just stupidly difficult on easy. The jokes are a bit lame and there is no skip in some parts for when you have to replay a part. Stick of Truth was soooo much better of a game.

If you're a south park fan this game is fantastic, but if you aren't a lot of the humor probably won't appeal to you and some references will go over your head. The gameplay can possibly make up for it if you enjoy turn based RPG combat, but if you aren't into either of those things I'd skip it.

The game improves on Stick of Truth in many good ways, but these are overshadowed by the unbelievable number of stupid button-mashing QTEs and pointless minigames that are otherwise impossible to fail. The 20 hours or so of content could probably be done in about 4 hours if the "puzzles" involving QTEs were removed.
The puzzles that need to be solved may as well not be there, as the game hands you everything on a platter every step of the way. The very few choices you are given play absolutely no role in the story and don't at all affect the outcome. While Stick of Truth had some interesting back and forth scenarios and mixed it up with the storyline, Fractured But Whole is largely predictable and actually mostly frustrating to get through. There is an unusually large amount of time walking around town and fiddling around with railroaded puzzles rather than unravelling the story.
Somehow, /somehow/, I was having framerate problems in the game(!). There were also many, many, many small but non-breaking bugs in the game related to skipping, glitching, and sounds playing multiple times. The default keybinds for PC are also an absolute dumpster fire. There is absolutely no way this was not designed for consoles first.
That being said, this 20 hour fart joke was moderately enjoyable and if you enjoy South Park and pointless button mashing,  this game will entertain you, otherwise give it a miss or wait for the price to drop.

One of the things that kept Stick of Truth moving despite basically being a very simple game was the wild variations in the environments from section to section. You're in a town, but wait -- now you're on a space ship! Now you're in an RPG! Now you're 4 inches tall! What's gonna happen next?!
This game doesn't take those sorts of big swings, so it really feels like you're just spending hours running back and forth across the same map, not accomplishing much, waiting for the animations to play through in the hopes that something new will happen. It's a grind with very little to distract from the fact that you're repeating the same actions and seeing the same character animations over and over again. For $60, it's kind of a bummer. Your time is worth more.

is clearly inspired by the games in the

because it takes place on a series of islands, but it's really more similar to

. You don't have free reign of your boat like in
, but instead select an island from your map and a path is automatically charted. During the trip, you must shoot down attacking octopi and mines, but everything is on-rails. Most of the map is locked away at the game's start, but additional islands appear when you learn about them from NPC's or other sources.
The main game takes place on an isometric grid. One thing to keep in mind which is very important for puzzle-solving and finding hidden secrets is that you can only drop down from above by a distance of one "block". If this isn't possible, then you will simply walk to a cliff's edge and stop. Combat is simple and a bit loose, but it works okay. You have access to items such as bombs and arrows which help out in combat. In particular, I found bombs to be very potent against stronger enemies.
Block puzzles are featured fairly often, though they never become too complex. Most of the other puzzles are more of the navigational variety, and you'll really only find a challenge if you look for optional collectables.
features "Challenges" similar to what you see in many mobile games. Each island you visit brings with it three new challenges, some that are general goals (i.e. "Defeat 50 skeletons") and some that are specific to that island. Completing these challenges rewards you with a large amount of experience points. You can also gain experience by defeating enemies, but it can be a bit of a grind. When you level up your abilities become more efficient (require less stamina), you can hold more consumable items, or other various bonuses.
There are also optional items to collect called Bloodstones, which eventually unlock a powerful spell. I noticed these items early on, but I thought I had to get some sort of shovel or something to dig them out. It turns out, you just have to whack them with your sword like twenty times to collect them. I don't think the game ever mentioned this, so I was kind of annoyed when I realized this after I passed by so many during the first few dungeons.

is mute. In most Zelda games, however, some sort of proxy character is present to give some sort of voice to Link. The nameless main character of
lacks this, and coupled with an always emotionless face, you really don't get a feeling of any personality for him at all. The other characters in the game fared a bit better, though none of them were too memorable. In addition to other humans, the world of Arcadia features bird-like Owrus and fish-like Gillfolk. While a bit clichéd, the emerging backstory was interesting enough to keep me playing, and had a slight twist that I didn't expect.
Overall, I enjoyed my time with
. It's not perfect, but it's a decent substitution for a Zelda game on PC. It's much shorter than recent Zelda titles and isn't padded with a lot of filler. It may be a Zelda clone, but it's certainly a competent one so I'm not going to complain.

The camera is locked, you're kind of weak (I haven't gotten the Coral Sabre yet, however), the stamina system stinks (although it does make sense, it just hampers the game, it doesn't add anything), your ammunition is super low until you hit the max level (where you can hold 99 bombs and 99 arrows), the monsters drop far too little money and experience, the items lack originality, the puzzles aren't that creative.
The one thing I think the developers did well is the drop rate, which is very high, so your low amount of maximum ammunition doesn't severely hamper you as it's pretty easy to fill your bomb bag and quiver up. The ship travels quickly from island to island as well, so that's another good point. So yeah, if you've never played a Zelda game and you want to get into the Zelda series, then do play this. If you HAVE played Zelda, don't play this, as it's worse than pretty much any Zelda game ever released.

Oceanhorn is an adventure game heavily inspired by the legend of zelda series, namely The Wind Waker to be exact but even though it resembles a lot of that series, it in it's own way has it's unique flavor and gameplay to it making it just different enough from the series it's paying homage to.
There are some things the game does that is a bit more seamless, like the ability to swap your sub-weapons on the fly without needing to go into the menu by just pressing the d-pad in that direction, the boat sections seam to be more straight forward that resembles Phantom Hourglass and a level up system that grants things like more bombs, faster boat traveling, money and such that takes the hassle of having to find some of the upgrades yourself.
Some of the things that could have been better, would include the puzzles which while simple and fun were a bit too simple and pretty straight forward, majority of the boss battles a tad on the easy side,  the graphic options can be taxing on the best of PCs, and the storyline.
The problem with the story is that while once again seams to resemble the ideology of TLoZ series, it seams rushed in some parts, and dis-jointed in others with some of the ambiance it tries to convey lost due to odd timing in cutscenes and dialog, which seam out of place with some characters.
The Graphic problem on Pcs stems from graphic options that cause slow-down and need some optimization for PCs, which isn't all too bad on custom settings or medium settings as the game itself looks fantastic visually.

However with those problems, it doesn't take away from the enjoyment of the game nor the fun you have in this game which is presented with a nice looking isometric view.
If your a fan of TLoZ series and want to try something simular on the PC. This 8 to 14 hour game is worth checking out.

This game was marketed as a Zelda clone.  However, it is not even close.  The only similarities are, bows, bombs, and swinging a sword.  It ends there.  There are no original gadgets, no compelling storyline, no challenging boss fights, and no challenging puzzles.  The entire game feels extremely limited.  There is no real mystery to character development and the storyline is petty.  All of the mobs require the same logic to defeat and there are very few variations of them.
If this were to be a clone, then where are all of the extra gadgets and related puzzles?  The only extra "gadget" you get is the ability to jump over 1 block.  There are a total of ~10 types of creature to defeat, but really only 4 different types: flyers, biters, sword swingers, and archers.  All of them are weak against everything.  So there is no real need to mixup your playstyle.  Bosses show a little bit of variety, but are too simplistic.
The competition offers variance between mobs.  Some mobs can only be killed with bombs, others with the bow.  You could use a boomerang to stun them or grab what they dropped.  The puzzles in the competition actually required thinking.  This game blatently points out what exactly needs to be done to solve just about all of the puzzles.
So, if you want an incredibly easy and boring ripoff, this is your game.  Otherwise, I'd only consider purchasing this during summer sale at the price it is worth - ~$3.

The Hat Man: Shadow Ward
Survival horror
Game Mechanics
Game Mechanics
is a first-person survival horror game set in an asylum developed and published by Game Mechanics.
You play as either the father or mother of Virginia Berry, who disappeared from the asylum where she was being treated for attempting suicide. As you go and investigate her disappearance, you find no one in the asylum and you start looking for pages from your daughter's journal while being chased by a shadowy figure.
Unlike most horror games of this nature, reading the notes and discovering what your daughter was living through is more interesting than simply looking at doodles and drawings of the monster. Unfortunately, the plot really goes nowhere and is disposable at best for the game.
As far as Unity games go, this doesn't stand out from the crowd. The environments are polished and I didn't encounter a single bug, but the rooms all look the same and it becomes really hard to navigate the environment. The design of the titular villain and the shadow people isn't really scary, and once you see them the built-up scariness disappears.
Similarly to Slenderman: The Eight Pages, you must move through the environment looking for pages while avoiding being caught by the Hat Man. You will also need to find some objects to open new areas and further explore the asylum. The pages are really easy to find since they make a noise when you are near them, and the shadow people can be "defeated" by hitting'em with your flashlight "Alan Wake style".
The game is really easy to beat, and the antagonist showed up rarely and was really slow and easy to avoid.
The voice acting for both the father and mother is hilariously bad, and that alone is worth playing the game. There is only one piece of music, and is the relaxing one that plays at the radio. There are also some ambient noises, and luckily no screamers or loud jumpscares.
After having beaten the game, you can replay it to unlock the 11 achievements that require you to beat the game as fast as possible and find and listen to all the diary pages.
The game is creepy most of the times, but the boring level design, poorly developed ghosts and short length make the game feel more boring than it needed to be. However, I recommend this game for the voice acting and really cheap price to support the developers to create a better product.

We live in an awesome time where small teams (and in many cases, one person) can create indie games and share them with the world. I
indie games.
is obviously a labor of love for senpai studios, and I highly encourage them to keep doing what they are doing. There is alot of promise in this work, but unfortunately, I cannot recommend this game. What I can offer is some constructive critiscm.
1. While there are minute differences, it shares all too much with the
series. I fault that series for the same things found here - the mechanic it is built on is too simple, and the gimmick wears off quickly. That game concept works best as phone or tablet games. To explain further - finding book pages while avoiding a ghost is boring. Maybe if you added RPG-like elements and extended gameplay? Criticism should always be supported with possible options for a fix, IMO.
2. Graphics are bland, at best. If you cannot make it hyper-realistic, I would try to go for a retro look. What you have here is something that falls in the middle, and ultimately just looks like every other basic FPS game. I would bet this was made in some GML or game making program (I don't believe senpai studios actually built those wheelchairs sprite by sprite). Once again, I am just trying to seed ideas.
3. Maybe get rid of the voice acting, and just add captions.
4. Make the Hat Man scarier, and much faster. Maybe make his 'darkness' totally creep and cover your entire view. As-is, he feels like a polygon on a rail.
5. I would do something risky - everything that is currently in this game has been done before. In many cases, it has been done
before. Maybe add split-screen co-op where the second player plays as the Hat Man. Might make for a good couch co-op romp. Who knows?
Thank you for reading the above ideas, and thank you again to senpai studios for the free copy. I seriously commend you for seeing the complete developemental process to finish. Not many can actually do that. Keep up the hard work. For my Steam friends - pass on this one.
Peace,
-Ryan

Well the dev added me and gave me this for free so I feel like I should be nice and give him a good review on this but I also want to be honest because this is one of the worst games I have played in a long time. Before I say anything else I can definitely say that I fully appreciate the time and talent of the people who make games, good or bad, because it isn't easy. To the game's credit it had no technical issues and controlled and performed very smoothly. There is no in-game vsync so I had to force it through Nvidia control panel, but no biggie. Unless I missed it, there is also no mouse sensitivity option so I had to lower it in my razer synapse but also no big deal. Although I am not a fan of adventure games I felt like I owed it to this guy to try his game and give it my honest opinion. The game lacks heavily in detail (basically none) and overall production value. The graphics are a major turn off. The game was very, very bland and very boring. The graphics look like pre Half-Life 1 and the environment is almost empty, only adorned with a few tables and a radio, a few beds in some rooms, sinks and toilets, a few things on the walls, and nothing else. It is very plain and mostly empty. I think the game repeats on itself, meaning there was no end as I moved in a direction through doors and hallways and the environment kept repeating. A piece of ceiling fell down with a scary music que eventually so I guess if you wander enough more things happen. Really though I'm not sure. Three times I encountered a black ghost (Bill Cosby from Ghost Dad I think) with a BOO! cartoon halloween style face and the game just popped up the dead menu, showing restart and quit. Nothing happened, just dead and menu screen. I do not know how the black figure is triggered, or why, or how to avoid him if I see him, or what the point of the game is or what exactly I am supposed to be doing, and overall don't care to see the answer to any of those inquiries. Note: I read that you just go around and collect journal pages and avoid the black figure and the game can be beat in like 30 minutes. That could have saved me a lot of words in my review.
Out of 50+ installed games, this game just can't hold an audience with me anymore. 20 minutes was more than enough time spent on this. Although I dislike adventure games, I have played a few out there that are similarly priced (when on sale which is often if you know where to look) that are far superior in every aspect. Namely Outlast. Where this game would be a 3/10 Outlast would be a 8/10, easily trumping this game in every possible aspect.

It's got all the pieces that made Human Revolution a really fun game, but it has put them together all wrong.
You can see a lot of hate for the in-game microtransactions in other reviews; while I understand the dislike, it really is purely optional.  It shouldn't bother you or affect your game if I'm so bad at it that I have to pay to get extra help.  Certainly doesn't bother me if I only finish the game on easy but you want to finish on "real life" mode.  The microtransactions are a strange choice, and I think a bad one, but not worth hating.
But the way everything fits together might be worth your scorn.  Maybe the painfully bad writing will be what drives you away.  Maybe the dull, unbelievable voice acting will do that.  Perhaps it'll be the insultingly blatant fencing used to make small and unimaginative world maps take more time to get through.  Or all that might be fine to you but you won't be happy with the clunky controls while in stealth. What is safe to say, is that something will drive you away from this game.  Because everything is so close to good that not only is it not good, but it'll build up your hope in the intro/tutorial and then just dash all those hopes with no care at all.
Wait a bit.  Let it get patched up, maybe get some things smoothed out.  It's close to a good enough game to recommend.  Just not yet.
