+ Tekken finally has a PC-port and it's fantastic!
The entire version is objectively the best with fantastic graphics, short load-times and tons of peripheral support. This is a perfect example of a series transitioning to PC! If you like fighting-games, this is an absolute must-buy!
+Fantastic mechanics that are fun for all
Tekken has a low barrier to entry, but a massive skill-ceiling. You can buy this game and have a fantastic time even if you have never played a fighting game before. For the serious player the game features insane depth and a lot to enjoy. Tekken 7 has changed things such as throw-breaking and made things generally more streamlined, but maintained it's complexety and depth. This really is the best Tekken has ever been.
+Optimized roster
While not perfect, the roster is tightened up. Your favorite is most likely still in the game and the newcomers are generally good. Each character feels unique and I feel Namco has made good decisions on which characters to keep.
+Hype as ♥♥♥♥ final boss
Just play the story and see for yourself.
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
-Lack of content in general
I would like to underline that this game has already been out for 2 years in arcades. While not the FR-version, the game has techinally been complete. This begs the question of what in the ♥♥♥♥ Namco has been doing for 2 years. Customization is a joke compared to Tekken 6 and there are very few modes. There is also no replay-mode or anything outside the basic ranked online.
The story-mode is very short and the scenarios for other characters are just abysmal. These scenarios are basically a random fight with an in-engine cutcene that does the bare minimum of fan-service. Every Tekken-game before this has had far more fleshed out content story-wise in general. Also, the customization is especially sadening considering that there are so few characters and one would assume this means more options for each one.
-Mediocre story-mode
The story-mode is short and nothing to really brag about. It has some cool moments (and Akuma), but it's basically a bunch of CG-cutcenes tied together with a terrible narrator and a hamfisted plot. The story makes no sense, but I can't really fault the game for it. Tekken has always been bonkers. However, compared to many other fighters it really falls flat and it has to be pointed out considering that the game offers very little other content.
-No tutorials or help for newcomers
The game has absolutely no tutorial and it's honestly baffling. Tekken is not an easy game to get into. Sure you can mash buttons as Eddy, but there is only a question of time until someone bodies you. It's easy to feel lost in this game, yet the game makes very little effort to teach you anything. You are going to end up on YouTube and other sites to figure out combos, frame-data etc. and that isn't good. There should at least be something here to teach new players the basics.
-Online has flaws
As of writing this there are several big problems with online that will hopefully be fixed soon. First of all, rage-quitting is a SERIOUS problem. There is basically no punishment for quitting and if a player disconnects on you, you don't get the win. This becomes an even bigger problem in Tekkens tournament-mode. If the host gets mad he can kick you immediately or outright leave to shut down the entire lobby. As a result, playing Tournament-mode is rather difficult.
Connecting to other players is also very difficult as of right now. Connecting through the match-list is almost hopeless and filled with error messages. The best option is using warm-up and wait for a match to be suggested by the matchmaking system. However, this is also frustratingly difficult. It can take 3-4 requests before you can accept a request to fight that actually works. As a result you will often end up in games with 3-bar connections because the game has not been able to connect to the players that fit the criteria you searched for. Most of the time you will be told that "the connection to the opponent has been lost". You might think that this is your potential opponent declining your request, but in the majority of times it is in fact the game struggling to connect. However, this will most likely be fixed and when it happens I will remove this from the review.

I don't normally write game reviews but I felt compelled to gush about Tekken 7.  I'm completely sucked in.  It's so much fun.  I write as someone who has 500+ hours in SFV, and I think Tekken 7 blows it out of the water in almost every way.  First of all, the singleplayer offering of Tekken 7 is actually worth playing, unlike SFV's awful and frustrating Survival mode.  I'm not a fan of either game's story mode (not an anime fan and long cutscenes with terrible voiceover is just not my thing), but Tekken 7's treasure battle is very addictive, with a similar reward loop of unlocking cosmetics as Overwatch.  My hope is they will continue to add to the game's Tresure Battle unlocks as the game's lifespan continues, as I've unlocked almost everything at 90 hours.  However the real meat of the game of course is multiplayer, and the fighting system itself.  I'll say that although I got pretty far in SFV, that game's reliance on frame traps, 50/50s, and unreactable attacks made the neutral very dissatisfying and losses were often more frustrating than educational.  Not so in Tekken.  With each character's huge move lists and the plethora of movement options, I feel like every L I earn is deserved since I could always have made dozens of different decisions before I got there, every time.  I'm having fun learning the game and it seems like there's nearly infinite depth to go.   The one thing I really miss about SFV is the CFN social features unlocked in the most recent patch, the automatic replay recording, and the deep tracking of every match, per-character stats, and global rankings.  It made every ranked battle feel more consequential and less random.  I hope Tekken 7 gets those features eventually.  As far as this PC port, I can't speak to the quality of the console version since I don't own a console but I'm running this game buttery smooth at 60 FPS 1440p on a GTX 1070, it looks fantastic.   There's full button remaping, and my Madcatz fightstick worked right out of the gate with no need to fiddle with drivers or  settings.  Matchmaking has been solid and I'm told a lot better than the console version.  Lag has been less noticable than with SFV too.  What can I say, I'm hooked!  Get this game.  It's real good.

Main reason why this game is not recommendable is this game isn't remotely playable until whoever is playing it has sunk dozens of hours into it.
The game only becomes playable after absurd amounts of trial and error. There are so many things that will damage or outright kill players if they do not already understand and remember exactly how that thing works. How far will that enemy jump, how high can it jump, how long is its aggravation range, how far can it throw, how far can it see, how does this trap work, how does that trap work, so on. It goes beyond just learning through playing, because there are numerous of these things; each is only a small aspect to the game and many are localized to different parts of the game, each works in very specific ways, and the player will potentially die or get hurt if they do not understand exactly how it works. It's like trying to navigate through a room full of dishware where if you step out of line once it all suddenly breaks, this game requires complete and exact knowledge of every single inch of it for the player to have a good chance at winning at all.
Normal Rogue-likes involve trial and error, like most difficult games in general. But with this game it is the entire system. Everything requires precise knowledge in order for the player to be able to respond to it properly. Everything, every single thing. After that, after you have played dozens and dozens of hours; then you can actually begin playing the game and potentially lose out of bad luck or lack of dexterity instead. Only then does the obligatory learning through death grinding experience end and the real game begins.
Some objects in the game that are harmless can become hazardous when the player interacts with them; if the player forgets there is an unlikely chance of this happening when they interact with the thing they will likely get hurt. Players can get knocked around and or stun locked by attacks, leading to them taking huge damage or an instant death from only getting hit by one normal hazard. The ridiculously powerful shopkeeper can get triggered by boulders, stray explosions or stray bombs. Traps can spawn in areas where players have no resources to counter that trap. Players can run out of vital resources needed to traverse the map at all. The players attack is awkwardly slow for absolutely no reason other then to make it harder to react quickly to threats. Enemies have inconsistent aggravation ranges and some can be triggered through solid surfaces. Enemies which drop down on the player can be hidden off screen and thus come out of nowhere at rapid speeds to hit the player. Spider webs serve to pointlessly slow the player down and there is no default way to destroy them quickly. Enemies can get jammed in awkward places which make them extremely hard to fight or even to get through that place anymore. Multiple enemies can attack from above yet the player can only attack to the sides except sometimes when their attack can hit above them but not always. Explosions can fling objects around to hit the player at ridiculous angles or distances. Objects can ricochet off surfaces to hit the player at ridiculous angles or distances. Enemies with inconsistent hit boxes for hitting them on the head. Enemies which are immune to being hit on the head normally, yet have massive amounts of health and speed and thus just camp ontop of the player until they are dead. Explosives with inconsistent sensitivity. Traps spawning adjacent to shop entrances so if you go inside you will likely die trying to come out. Enemies with line of sights turn with no warning animation. Some enemies can throw projectiles instantly. Various enemies have ridiculous leaping patterns which make them extremely dangerous and extremely hard to avoid and predict. Half the significant threats in the game are instant kills, so why bother getting health when no matter how good you are doing you can die instantly anyways. Boons or significant future progress elements in a map can be randomly generated to cancel themselves out or be in places that make going after them overly tedious. There is no sense of progression or progression based mechanics to make players feel like they are making progress over their numerous deaths, and no real mechanics to make the game easier for players the more they play it save for the shortcuts which aren't even canon to use if you want a complete run. Hired help is useless and can potentially get the player killed, as help also comes during that playthrough any time the player unlocks a new character so unlocking new characters can get you killed. There are no achievements for finding the side maps in the game, even though there are multiple of them and the game gives achievements for completing the normal maps; again a lack of feeling for accomplishment. Water physics do not apply to enemies. Enemies are inconsistently able or unable to run off their current platform in pursuit of the player.The controls make precise ledge grabbing and landing awkward yet the map generates obstacles which require precise ledge grabbing and landing. Players can run in mid air in order to speed up their jumps, which only serves to make platforming more inconsistent and awkward. There is not even any special animation for the player holding or carrying objects, they just float infront of them. The game does not explain the system of dynamically throwing objects at all, even though this mechanic is extremely important for the gameplay. Traps can spawn off screen or near the edge of the screen to shoot players who are not examining the environment every second. Some traps trigger preemptively when the player gets close, which is counter intuitive to how a normal trap works which thus requires players to adapt to unintuitive dangers which only apply to one hazard in the whole game. After the player has picked up a damsel if they drop them the damsel runs around anytime they are set down, so they can get themselves killed especially if the game generates a map where the player has to set the damsel down to do something. Dark maps can get the player killed by hiding spikes are large drops in the darkness if the player loses their single torch at any point. The game has a limited amount of useable items in it at all and half of them are situational utility benefits at best, otherwise there are no unique modifiers or perks to the players equipment or build. And the ghost is an exclusively poor feature, forcing new players to leave levels early and experienced players to grind tediously if they want to get maximum currency for the run.
This game is fraught with short sighted and poor design decisions which massively spike the difficulty artificially. Requiring the player to memorize the counter and response for every single bad design element before they can actually begin playing with a tolerable chance to win. And even then the player can still lose to many of these design problems because some of them are still not countered by trial and error. It is just a permanent unfair danger that can show up to screw the player over whenever the game feels like it. It is why even experienced players who know much of the game and have beaten it; still struggle to beat this game consistently. Because the game can screw the player over by complete chance or the game can screw the player over just because they stepped out of line once.
The base of the game itself is fine but the artificial difficulty makes it obnoxious, arbitrary and completely asinine to even attempt to beat. Most other Rogue-likes, even many bad Rogue-likes, do not depend this heavily on trial and error for the player to be able to win; and they also have a sense of progress and accomplishment along the way which this game has absolutely none of.

I personally love this game. It has given me many opportunities to make many friends with similar interests as my own and I have thoroughly enjoyed it.
For those reading this before purchasing allow me to explain the game for you at the current date of Dec 15th 2015.
RWBY: Grimm Eclipse at the current date is a hack and slash game with one campaign and four characters to play. Team RWBY. It is a very simple game with simple hack and slash combat. The game is not a very complicated game to play but that is what makes it a lot of fun with friends. It has a very quirky style just like the anime and its a nice refresher from some of the other games I play.
I have mastered all four characters skill trees and I will share my personal opinion on each character.
- I feel as if Ruby is the most polished character in the game. With a very fluent movement style and a very flashy but controlled combo, she is easily my favorite to play. Her dodges and movements are designed very well where she disappears with rose petals into a roll just like enemy. Her three abilities are Crescendo, Reap and Dust Blast.
I feel as if Reap is a more useless skill compared the raw power coming from the Crescendo and Dust Blast skills.

Ruby has a glitch that makes her 360 cover the strongest cover in the game in my opinion. After she uses it once, using it again allows her to move while charging.
is, in my personal opinion, Ruby's useless move. Cleaving Reap is a very good mastery move. It does what I'd expect from a mastered move. It takes its weakness and capitalizes on it. It greatly increases the range of the move with the rocks that get thrown out as she crashes into the ground.
is a shot of dust power. It's kinda like shooting an explosion, you have the normal dust blast, electric, ice and fire. My personal favorite is the Electric due to the massive amount of range you get with it due to the chain lightning. It can kill up to 3 people in what shot and if you hit one, two enemies will get shocked with chain lightning. A very neat and unique effect.
Ruby's two passive abilities are Armor Piercing and Hyperballistic. Armor Piercing allows your ranged attacks to hit armored enemies like the pigs. Hyperballistic decreases how much of a combo you need to achieve a block of special towards using your abilities.
- Weiss is a very solid and powerful character. I personally like her movement the most because she has a very graceful and smooth movement style. Her dodge is a quick transition that you barely see and it's just overall a very smooth experience when playing as Snow Angel. Her three skills are Nova, Pierce and Barrage.
is my favorite move with Weiss. Its a very powerful move that, when mastered, is a lot of fun to use. Supernova is the mastery of Nova and it draws in opponents as you charge the move. Unlike Ruby, you cannot move after using it, still giving Ruby the edge in this category of move.
is a pretty powerful move with a bit more viability than Ruby's Reap. It has more range and can one shot Beowolves at level 2. The negative draw back is what i call the universal range. You can only kill opponents if they are all right next to each other making the move not very viable in a lot of situations.
Yeah.. I didn't really like this move until the mastered Ice Bolt. Ice Bolt is immensely powerful and has a very long straight AoE path. It's a really good move fitting for Weiss along with Supernova.
Weiss' passive abilities are Ice Queen and Perfect Form. Ice Queen makes her blast attacks freeze opponents. Perfect Form makes her combo meter fill 2 special bars instead of one. A very useful ability.

She does a really really good ranged attack just by the simple shot she does. Her three abilities are Shadow Clone, Shadow Strike and Blade Beam.

Dash dancing is when you are attacking and dodging at the same time, kinda looks like you are dashing so I call it dash dancing. Her three abilities are Quake, Sunbreaker and Blast Wave.

The gameplay and comedic values are south-park esq, which I'm a big fan of, and you'll get hilarious south park moments and south park soundtracks/characters that's all inclusive in this game, as opposed to the previous one, where most of them were in the game, but you couldn't really interact. But this one, you can interact, and you can do mini side missions with everybody. Also, the phone system is ingenious, and the game introduces all these complex elements so well and smoothly, that you don't really have to worry about it at all. There's a few bugs in the game and some weird puzzles that just didn't work imo, but aside from those and some repeated gimmicks of puzzles and using your buddies, the rest is just fantastic. TL;DR - This game is sort of like a 50:50 Minecraft and Terraria mashup with updated graphics. So if you liked those, I would recommend checking this game out, especially if there's a sale going on.
It has the 3D building of Minecraft with the boss fights of terraria. The devs are frequently putting out updates and gameplay additions including new items, mechanics, worlds, visual effects, etc. Since the game is so new, there might be a little bit less content than some people would like, but at the rate they are upgrading the game it has only been getting better and will continue to get better. Speaking of which, I think this new update (V1.2) has brought some amazing changes to the game, and it's really starting to feel like a fleshed out, polished game. But yes, there is room for improvement.
There are 3 bosses currently, each with a set of worlds leading up to it. Each boss also has a hard mode later in the game. There are the standard 3 character classes (warrior, archer, mage), and you can make like 5 different characters at one time. There is a max level of 30 with new perk options every 5 levels or so, but the game can be a little bit grindy once you get to the upper 20's. But again, with the latest update I think this will be partially addressed by the update with the addition of more level variety (low gravity worlds) later on in the game, quest and dungeon updates, and the unique and more epic boss-specific portal gate visuals.

A lot of it was stuff fans/players have suggested in their forums, and I think its's great that the devs routinely read/comment on/listen to their player base and make their updates reflect that.
I think Terraria was one of the best bang-for-my-buck games that I've ever bought, but Portal Knights may very well rival that in the future.

I just do not like this franchise at all. Hell’s highway’s story is competent and in my opinion it is the best story in the franchise but that’s not saying much. I did like the increase in production value, it’s nothing impressive but it gets the job done and the presentation overall is much better than the previous two. The gameplay however is so generic that it’s sad. Even though I didn’t like the gameplay in the first two they removed pretty much everything that made the gameplay somewhat unique. They added a very bland cover system and regenerating health. The shots you take from cover are on point now so you never have to use your squad because you are a one man army, even on the higher difficulties. Peek from cover, kill about 2 enemies with headshots then get back into cover and regen your health, that’s the game in a nutshell. This honestly would have been fine though if the shooting was actually satisfying but it’s just not. In the first two games they made the gameplay so you couldn’t hit anything with your gun so the game forced you to use your squad to help take out the enemies. In this game you see all the enemies with the third person cover and you are practically a sniper when you peek out from cover killing anything In your way so your squad is practically useless. This game is just a very bad experience and it’s a very boring one too. The decent story and budget increase is pretty much the only redeeming qualities of this game.

Mortal Kombat X is the latest edition in the ever popular Mortal Kombat series. The game has been in development since April 2012, and was released early this year in time for the latest Mortal Kombat series due to be released in September.
Having played a lot of Mortal Kombat as a child, this is the first I have played since then.
Firstly, I really enjoy the newer aspects of gameplay here; an energy bar which I believe was introduced in the previous Mortal Kombat game (2011), which allows players to perform special techniques such as an X-Ray. This is also included in another one of NetherRealm's titles (the developers), Injustice: Gods Among Us (which was one of my games of the year in 2014). Fighters are also able to interact with much of the fighting environment, such as burning your opponent in a trough of fiery coal, or smashing them around the head with an old woman (you heard that right).  In addition to these, each fighter has three different variations, each featuring a different set of moves they can use during the fight.
The gameplay modes on show here, are the story mode, 1 vs 1 Ranked King of the Hill, Survivor and Test Your Luck. Another new addition this time around is a mode called "Living Towers", the play conditions in this mode changes every hour. There is also a "Faction War", where each player has to choose from five factions, to align with and join an online cross-platform competition. Winning points for their faction to contribute in the competition.
Mortal Kombat X is one of the best looking games to date, you will need a really beefed up rig to play this on high settings, but it is seriously worth it. Not one fault with the graphics.
The story mode uses the same format as Injustice: Gods Among Us, a lot of cut scenes and QTEs, which isn't always a bad thing, since I thoroughly enjoyed the story mode, and is the mode I enjoyed the most. This mode only took me four hours to complete, which I thought was a little short, but I suppose devs were thinking most people would buy this for the multiplayer.
The game is hard, and you really have to learn the combos, you can get buy with button bashing, but you will struggle at points; I had to play a few stages more than two or three times before I managed to progress.
I have only noticed one technical issue while playing; the initial loading time from launching it in Steam can sometimes take one or two minutes. It will be sat on the mini splash screen, and you'll think it has frozen, but it is in fact still loading.
The multiplayer has been known to have a few issues, I experienced a little lag, but that may of been my internet connection, however others constantly report lag online.
I would recommend buying MKX, however not for full price, keep your eyes out for it to drop down to £20 and then pick it up.

I have to say, if you remove technical issues with the port (most of which have at last been solved), this is one of the best fighting games ever. Amazing depth, style, content, innovation. I recently have hopped back online, hoping that the netcode would be improved, and to my delight and--it must be said--surprise, I found a vastly improved online experience. I played for almost 10 hours the other day and every single match I played didn't lag in a damaging way. The interface for finding people to fight with could be improved ( in ways which it is outside the scope of this review to write about), but in general the experience was exemplary.  There is also a decent base of PC players, despite the outrageous prophecies of doom that followed the game even on day 1; PC players shoot themselves in the foot by making such cynical predictions, because then prospective buyers look at the forum and don't get the game, which hurts the whole community!
There are certainly cumbersome aspects to this game: make sure you have enough space for it's battery of oversized patches, make sure your computer can run it, and make sure you have a decent connection before you buy. Looking at the larger picture, though, this game--the actual GAME--is incredible and you would be doing yourself and the whole MKX community on PC a huge favor by picking it up and come joining us in a room to play! The amount of content and care put into that content is just staggering, and the depth and feel of all the fighters is getting to the level of SFIV technicality while retaining it's distinctive MK style and flow. Ignore the overpriced DLC's if you want, but don't let them deter you from one of the best fighthing games of this generation.

We've all had those games in our lifetime that reflected our favorite movies or TV shows.  These games have always been hit or miss. One notable exception to this very specific catagory are the Matrix games.  Path of Neo as well as Enter the Matrix were both fabulous games. However, even they lacked the thing we all wish we could have in a TV/Movie based game.  That "thing" being the simulated feeling of what we are playing is true to what we watch.  Despite my love for the Matrix games, it was still computer generated graphics mimicing live action which hampers the immersion slightly.  RWBY:GE breaks this mold.  The show itself is made with the same graphics style as the game.  RWBY:GE provides a level of immersion into a favorite show of mine that is unrivaled, and anyone who slightly enjoys the show at all MUST play this game.
Pros:
-It's freaking team RWBY
-It's early access and RoosterTeeth is well known for satisfying their audiences desires.
-Graphically identical to the show, and the use of the actual voice actors (another perk to Rooster Teeth production, all    the cast is on stand by pretty much) provides immersion into a game like none other.
The combat is simplisitc yet addicting (for Hearthstone players, you'll really understand what simple yet addicting feels like)
-Only one level currently available during early access and after nearly 2 dozen play throughs I still do not feel the bored at all.
-Yang is punny.  RT Fans understand... that if Dunkleman is making a pun, it's a good day.
Cons:
-Many people have been harsh on the sound levels.  I don't quite understand that since anyone who has used TS3 or Vent while gaming should already be use to having to adjust sound levels to personal preferences.  However, all the gun fire sounds exactly the same, which can become tedious on the ear drums.
-The game is most fun when all four girls are present, having duplicates in the same group negates some of the joy
-No target lock.  Nothing is more aggravating than being swarmed as Ruby, firing your dust blast, and rather than it exploding and decimating the swarm... it launches over them all to a random grimm far away.
Juice's Hopes and Dreams for this Game:
The following is just my personal opinion on ways to improve game play.  I know very little about coding, and difficulty of implenting these ideas.... but this is what I fall asleep at night day dreaming about here lately.
1. I feel one way to encourage the selection of each individual characters would be to implement a team combo system.  One of the things that makes the show so great is Ruby leads the team in "plays" during combat where they all work together to vanquish their foe.  For those of you reading this who have already played.. imagine how awesome it would be for someone to press lets say 4, to call for a combo and R W B Y appears across the screen, and as each person also presses four their corresponding letter lights up in their color, and once they're all lit there's a short cinematic of a bad♥♥♥♥♥combo as the team annihilates the tough grimm. Am I right? Legit day dream you just had there wasnt it?
2.  Of course another way to encourage not having duplicates is to include more characters, which hopefully is already a plan.  I'm hopeful to see Team RWBY and Team JNPR for sure.  Playing as Pyrrha Nikos would be amazing.  Playing as the team that Qrow was a part of with RWBY's mom would also be great.
3. There has to be a way to work Zwei into this game some how.
TL;DR:
Fans of the show, you wont regret the purchase.  Those who have not seen RWBY.. Take 2 hours and watch volume 1 on netflix.  Be prepared to spend 2 more hours watching volume 2, then downloading the RoosterTeeth app to your mobile devices to watch Volume 3 as it airs weekly (we're up to chapter 6) and then.. you'll be inspired to purchase, and will not regret the decision.

Spelunky easily classifies as THE MOST frustrating game I have ever played and the one I will never touch again after its completion. This flaming garbage of annoying and deadly enemies, unpredictable traps, overly-too-long stun locks, difficult health recovery options, slippery controls that are unfit to a game requiring precision and care, pitch-black levels, useless items that are situational at best, Shotgun + Jetpack + Kapala combo that tries to overcompensate for all the other trash items with them being near requirement to win, limited resources, events out of your control that screw you up every time, lack of invincibility frames, multitude of instakill situations, unreliable throwing mechanics, shopkeepers that turn against you without your fault, annoying ghost that makes a careful exploration of levels non-viable, limited range of your own weapon, every single snake, bat, spider, caveman, monkey, yeti, temple guard and everything in between that tries to make your life miserable…
It’s a rouge-lite game gone completely wrong. The sheer masochism and/or skill ceiling required to force yourself into this is a complete misunderstanding of basic qualities that makes a game fun. Where is the fun in a game where in every possible situation the odds are stacked against you, the dice are cheated and the luck makes fun out of you? This isn’t a problem with me or the genre, since I personally can endure quite a lot or pain and there are many rouge-lites that actively fix all of Spelunky’s problems with easy solutions. Games like FTL, Crypt of the Necrodancer or Risk of Rain are no walk in the park by any stretch of imagination, but still offer much better experience. They present themselves as more fair, complex and much more open to players' different play styles and tactics. They offer higher predictability of enemy actions, bigger, more useful range of items where every combination can be a winner and still allow success with small mistakes on the player’s part - not penalizing with sudden death for every stray from perfection.
Spelunky with its clumsiness and absolute lack of regard to simple and fair rules of play, effectively broke my respect to the rouge-lite genre for a while. If it wasn’t for the aforementioned, great games, I would never touch this type of the permadeath, procedurally generated style of games. While other rouge-lite games are now save from (admittedly a little bit unfair) hatred towards them, Spelunky
get away with it.

After 94 hours of gameplay, I finished my first run. Yeah, I took my sweet time exploring, and searching everywhere for anything I could find. Took my time putting every enemy to sleep without alarms or hostile combat. So yes, it took a long time. That being said, there's some other negatives...
- Long loading times. SERIOUSLY LONG, and for Prague, this is annoying. Seriously, they could have found a way around it or put in something better than a stupid subway cutscene. Makes me miss the elevator conversations of Mass Effect.
- The story isn't nearly as strong as Human Revolution. I felt HR told a story of what could happen. Mankind Divided however is just a story, and a bit of a weak one. I don't want to ruin anything, but it's just not interesting.
- Choices feel meaningless. If there was ever a game I played where the choices I made felt like they were pointless, this game nailed it. I know there are different endings, and I've only seen the one I got so far, but it felt empty. Completely empty. Sort of in the same way Mass Effect 3 gave you a rainbow, this gives you a *spoilers* warningwarningwarningapicusnewsstoryontvwarningwarningwarning
Now, I put in 94 hours, so obviously it wasn't a BAD game. No, it wasn't bad, it didn't suck. There was a lot to explore and some missions have you running around all over the place. I also reloading previous saves a lot to redo things or to try again. I wanted the first playthrough to be as flawless as possible. Somehow, I failed the NO ALARMS achievement, which is bs, because I never triggered any alarms, and when I had, I reloaded a save before it happened.
Now, another worthy note is NEW GAME +. You carry over everything you previous have in your inventory, money, and praxis kits... Now this effectively means you carry over anything of actual in game value... However, there's still the issue with some DLC content being a one time use per account. So if you remove those items, do so at the start of the game and save. And don't overwrite that save. Though if you lose it, you're out a few bonus items you technically paid for. Really slick there SquareEnix.
I expected more. I expected a better story. I expected a better game.
Human Revolution was easily in my top 10 games for the previous generation, and honestly, one of my all time favorites. Yes, it's a science fiction story, but also a very real future we're racing into. Human augmentation is likely to become a thing before the 22nd century. In a world where medicine and healthcare are big business, one has to wonder where these human enhancements will go. Who will be able to afford them? How will it impact society? These are things Human Revolution poked at. Mankind Divided though doesn't. It tries to poke at racism, but it turns into a linear terrorist story with little value and no real plot.
I can't really recommend Mankind Divided, especially if you're lacking solid pc hardware. It's kind of a monster, and for no good reason. On sale at 50% off, it's probably a good deal. DLC has yet to roll out, but the DLC in Human Revolution was nothing special, so I don't expect any of this to me either.

After reading the reviews it is sad to see how many people have given this game a negative review due to the microtransactions or preformance issues. Honestly I didn't even know about the microtransactions until reading the reviews... why? Well because I was too excited to jump into the game and see what it has to offer! I saw the shop option in the menu but didn't pay attention to it. They aren't forcing us to buy anything and if they never do then what is the problem? Like another player said, don't buy the microtransactions and get over it. Unless they impede my ability to continue with the story I won't give a damn about microtransactions.
Yes it is a little sad that the dlc is a one time use but that just means you have to think about when to use them. Oh no, thinking! How dare they make us do that. I bought the season and have yet to use any of the dlc that came with it. Once I found out it was a one time deal I figured it would be best to save for a later use. In a way it adds to the game by making you have to decide when to use the extra items you bought. Do you want to use them on the first play through or wait for a second play through? If you never use them... well I'm sure we've all wasted more money on pointless things or things we barely use.
For performance issues I have yet to have any. I didn't change a single thing in the settings and the game runs smoothing for me. I can understand people being upset due to the game crashing, bugging out, not loading, or whatever else but I don't see why that is cause for a negative review. How can you say the game is bad just because you can't play it? I've done my fair share of troubleshooting games and not being able to play them due to crashing, not loading, or lack of hardware. I understand the frustration but I would never tell someone not to get a game just because I couldn't play it.
With all that said I love this game. It is an improved Human Revolution and all the imrovements have been for the better... well aside from one... Why couldn't they get the same voice actor for David Sarif?! That is the only disappointment I have for now. Still have much more of this game to experience since I only have 3 hours logged but I wanted to let others know that it is worth the buy!

This is a quick preliminary review after just under 6 hours of play.
This is Deus Ex; closest to the original I've seen yet. So far, this game actually has the same feel as the original. As much as I liked Human Revolution, it wasn't able to quite achieve that.
Cons:
Yes, Square is unabashedly making a money grab with the store. But in no way does it impact the game, nothing is available to you exclusively through the store. It's really not a big deal. Only downside is that the preorder items are treated like store purchases, so you won't be able to use them on a second playthrough.
Lipsyncing is a little off, and occassionally the enemies are a little jerky, which can make combat feel a bit... twitchy at times.
Software takes up inventory space. Uh, in a cyborg?
Yes, mouse sensitivity is jacked up to 11. Turn it down in the options. Another tip mentioned in a guide is that turning it to 0% effectively turns off mouse accelerations, suggesting it might have been better labeled in the settings.
Pros:
So far the characters are well written and presented. Prague feels fairly open and there is definitely plenty of flexibility in how you approach things. As it should be with Deus Ex, you get a lot more of the story if you take the time to read things. A lot is true to the original game. I found myself cursing not being able to carry every gun around - even after upgrading my inventory - but then remembered that choosing what to carry with you is a standard trope of the series.
If you're wondering, stealth is totally a viable option.
And the game is quite pretty to look at.
Ugly:
Edit: Have to say the interface - it's clunky. While better than many other ports, it's obvious the interface was built around consoles. You have to reach for the Esc key way too often to navigate menus - and sometimes (depending on context) instead of backing out it just jumps to the menu screen. I'd recommend mapping Esc to a spare mouse button if you have one. Might have made sense to actually use RMB to back out of menus, since I believe it is only used for ironsights. Long-pressing the Y key to bring up the weapon menu is another example - no reason long-pressing should be necessary on a keyboard. As a final example, you should be able to mouse over an item in your inventory to see what it is, but instead you have to click on it which brings up a menu and blocks many other items.
Anything that involves item manipulation (throwing, grabbing and moving) is overexagerrated. Trying to stack objects to reach a vent is a pain when each item want to slide all over the place. Throwing an item can send it ricocheting off walls. Why is this not listed under cons? Because it feels exactly like the original Deus Ex.
The really ugly: the ridiculous number of people that are not recommending this game because of one issue (the one issue varies by individual) is absolutely absurd. Also, take the comments about terrible performance with a pile of salt. I've seen very few AAA titles truly optimized at launch. If you expect all the drivers to work perfectly and no need for patching on launch day... go fire up your console. If you're running a 970 or 980, be sure to adjust your settings as widely recommended (disable MSAA and turn volumetric and contact hardening shadows to On instead of Ultra). As to people reporting 30-40 fps on GTX 1080 SLI or other such beastly rig: They likely need to adjust something (game settings, drivers, OS, etc.).
Yesterday I took my aging rig (i7-3820, ROG Formula X79 MB, 16GB) and replaced 680 SLI with a new MSI Gaming GTX 1070. I also went ahead and updated to the latest Win 10 Anniversary patch and updated all my drivers. I am using the default OC mode in the MSI app (not manually OCing). At 1080p, no MSAA, volumetric and contact shadows to On, and everything else using the Ultra settings, I am getting 100fps and my GPU temp isn't even clearing 70°. Not even close to stressing this card, and everything is running great.
I have heard that Afterburner sometimes misreports GPU memory usage, but for those running older cards I will mention that my numbers are showing the game using 6GB of VRAM. If accurate, that might explain why some are having issues.
remember kids to update your video drivers and check graphic settings to adjust to your systems capabilities!

Although I've played through pretty well the whole game (minus a little bit of DLC) I can't recommend this game.
While others say that all the side quests are great and add value to the game, all they were for me was make busy time to make the game feel long.  For example, towards the middle/end of the game there is a gnome city where to get the side quest you go to the very back corner of a house and then to finish the fetch quest you have to go the very back of another house and then of course go back to the quest giver to finish the quest.  There doesn't appear to be any sort of design choice for that other than making the quest take longer.  The amount of side quests also showed just how forgetable the main story quest was.  I don't recall much if any of the main quest because there would sometimes be hours and hours between times you did something related to the main story quest.
As 'big' as this game is.  It feels empty.  Almost every area you go to is super similar.  You go to a new area, there will be one town or a larger city to get quests from, then there is a bunch of caves/tombs/ruins to fulfil those quests.  A lot of those caves/tombs/ruins all feel the same because you do the same thing in each.  You enter the side quest area at one end, go to the end of the area, finish your quest and then a new path opens up to send you back to the beginning.  As well each of these areas feel like copies of each other with different colour pallets.  Half of these areas could  have been removed and more time/focus spent on bigger and better side quests that actually felt rewarding.
As well there is a serious problem with enemies in this game, as in, there is not near enough of them.  There appears to be a set of them and then a bunch of recolours or with a different weapon or something.  There was hardly an variety in the enemies making each area again feel like copies of previous areas.
The one positive I'm going to give this game is the amount of lore they've packed into it.  If you complete all the side quests/faction quests and main quest you will have a lore overload and if thas your thing this game has it.

I really enjoyed this game, I think it is great. You play as Sgt. Matt Baker in command of the 101st Airbourne in France during operation Market Garden. Being in command of your squad is really fun and engaging and makes you think about your approach to each situation, especially on the higher difficulty of Authentic. You use surpressing fire from your MG and Base of Fire teams to cover and move your Assault Team up and flank the enemy which is really satisfying when it works. The story is the best part of the game in my opinion. It would be best to play Road to Hill 30 and Bound in Blood prior to this to get a background to the story and be fully engaged in it. For a 2008 title it looks really nice on the Unreal 3 engine and the attention to detail in the uniforms and weapons is really cool. Of course it looks a bit dated by today's graphics but it's not all about the graphics anyway. It still holds up after 8 years.
However I think the ending is a bit abrupt and leaves you on a cliffhanger, and we haven't even had any news of a sequel since the game was released!! There are also some tank sections that seemed a bit too easy in my opinion. In addition I had to restart the game one time because the teams weren't firing upon enemies when I told them to but I only ran into this bug once.
I played the game with an Xbox controller and it felt like it controlled quite well. Also, the K98 is MUCH more accurate than the Garand (and probably anything else apart from the snipers) in this game.

This game is a total 10/10 for me! TONS OF FUN to be had with friends, a MUST HAVE for fans of the show! I have to say, the smoothe combat and the great characters REALLY take the cake for me!! The voice acting, animation, and soundtrack make it feel so much like the RWBY show--fans will defs enjoy. I can tell the developers paid a lot of attention to detail; each character has its own unique way of moving that looks just like the characters from the show! Sometimes it's hard to believe I'm playing and not watching ;) And when I do go back to watch RWBY, I suddenly have a new-found respect for the characters and their unique fighting abilities. That, in my opinion, is how a show-based game is DONE! **insert standing ovation***
A note to the developers though...I know this game is meant to be enjoyed with the 4 main characters of team RWBY, but sometimes when I'm playing, I miss the other characters from the show!! I feel like that's part of what makes RWBY what it is; the richness of the characters! I understand that games have their limitations, and you guys are after all developers and not gods lol... but is there any way you could add even more amazing characters from the show? Specifically speaking, I would be ECSTATIC for some team SSSN (who doesn't love Sun and Neptune?), or even team JNPR of course! Especially team SSSN would be an incredible addition I think, because they would add even more variety of combat styles! Sun's unique style of hand to hand combat, or Neptune's lazer-shooting spear lol.
Anyway, just a hopeful plea... otherwise, this is an amazing job! And of course, I'd never want to say that the characters present aren't already wonderful. There's no comparing anyone to the amazing Yang Xiao Long, in my opinion... And the combat styles are already satisfyingly varied and really enjoyable!
Still, if you found a way to add even just Sun and Neptune to this game... I would legitimately worship you! Then I would give you an automatic 20/10!!! ;)

Let me start off by saying, don't expect much from this game. I feel like it is a game that could be victim to overhype.
I went in merely with the intention of clearing some dreaded Steam backlog and hadn't seen anything about the game in over a year, forgetting how nice the screenshots looked.
Therefore, going in with no expectations whatsoever, I came away having played one of, if not my favourite, game of all time.
This game gets better and better as it goes on, so don't expect to be blown away from the start. It is the grand sense that I really had been on an adventure that was left with me at the end, and being 3-4 hours long it feels like I had taken part in an interactive movie (having played it in one sitting).
But it is definitely a game, and the gameplay was just the right amount of fun. A lot of clever design choices means the game continually flows, adding to that sense of adventure. The puzzles aren't particularly difficult, but never did I feel like I was having my intelligence insulted either.  There were times when I anticpated having to do something again, or something similar to what I had just done and had a feeling of tedium, only to be pleasantly surprised that the developers recognised that, and changed it up completely.  I wish more developers would recognise that a game doesn't have to be long and filled with fluff to make it good. Three hours of quality is plenty for someone with limited time to play games.
The story isn't complex but it will leave an impression on most people. And how they go about conveying that story was also a clever touch. The game has no understandable dialogue, using only an invented language with no subtitles to get it's message across and I'm surprised at how well it does this when, in my opinion, the character models are the worst part of the game. They look out of place against the fantastic backdrops that make you stop and sit on a bench to look at the vistas, even when you were planning on rushing through a game to get it off your checklist. So at first, I wasn't struck. However, despite this, the sense of emotion you get from the characters is really rather deep and by the end you're completely invested. Most of the game is spent in third person and you won't be up close enough to see the poor character details anyway.
The other thing most people will comment on are the controls. You control both brothers, from different sides of the keyboard and I can see why a lot of people will mark them down negatively. It is often difficult to get them both running in merely a straight line. I argue though that the controls are perfect for the type of game it is and add a layer of complexity to it that stops the game feeling too easy. Like I said, the puzzles aren't difficult at all, but the controls make you have to think about what you're doing, and I have to say, the times when you simultaneously have both brothers doing something complex, or even just running down a path and crossing over each other and turning at slightly different times, but doing so accurately, feels really good.
There are a few negative points to the game, a couple of which rear their head almost straight away. As mentioned, the character details aren't great. Then, you come to the first puzzle.  You have to raise a platform, and it's immensely tedious, especially if you let go, and you have to start again. This platform raising happens once more in the game, and if  anything is even more tedious. Maybe I did it wrong. But it's over in a couple of minutes and overall doesn't affect the game. Lastly, texture glitches. In two cutscenes, some textures didn't load. It was only a rug and a chest of drawers, so not game breaking, but noticable. Also in one part, a shadow didn't load that was part of the mechanics of the situation, and I died. I didn't realise why until I started again and saw the shadow now loaded.
Overall, I can't believe I had this game sitting in my library for so long being unappreciated. I also feel bad for spending so little on it. I can't quite remember what I paid, but it probably wasn't enough.
Play this game, don't expect much and you're sure to have a good time.

From a longtime, I had  heard good things about Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons.  The main selling point was the amazing story that the game had.
Without seeing any trailers or screenshots, I bought the game, this was cool since I didn't know what kind of game was in front of me, so everything was new to me while playing the game.
In a brief summary, Brothers is Adventure game where you had to guide 2 brothers in their quest to retrieve a medicine to heal their dying father. The first thing that I had to say is that this game could be a little frustrating at times, since you had to control the 2 brothers at the same time, for this reason a dual stick controller is required since you had to use them to move both brothers separetely, so you will need some good coordination at times. Also If you separate them too much, they will not move until they get closer, so this could be a drag.
The main mechanic of this game is to solve puzzles and do some plataforming. This puzzles are SUPER easy to he point that it will be almost impossible for you to take more than 3 hours to beat the game on your first playtrough. The only challenge in this game could be the coordination required to solve some puzzles, but after a while that will not be a problem.
With those 2 points in consideration, one could said that this game is average at best, so, why is so well regarded? Well, for everything else.
The narrative in this game is very good, without shouting a tangible word in the whole game,  you could understand the whole point of the game through good animations and storytelling. The easy puzzles start to get a point since they help you to tell the story, and also to enjoy it without getting stressed. The atmosphere of the world and the music is also top notch, helping with the narrative in a way that isn't very common in this genre.
And also, the most important thing in the game, the ending, which is so powerful that you could never forget it, and that once you can see it, you will  want to start the game again to analyze the whole game in retrospective, and start to appreciate way more the narrative of the game, even in some moments that could seem very trivial at the beginning of he game. The second playtrough is more relaxed since the game is shorter when you know what to do
So in resume, if you want a challenging game, Brothers isn't for you, if you want to play and interactive movie with great graphics and music, buy it.

Brutal Legend is more about aesthetic show than a gameplay. Yes, it is a proper game with a intricate gameplay of many interwoven genres, with switch changes from third person slasher through arcade race to tactical battle for tower dominance. Still, the main part of the game is kitsсh and forgotten childish dream about coolness. It visualise glory and vivid brutality of the golden age of hard rock, binding together all archetypal memes of the time. And it is glazed with nostalgy about  good old times, with a bit of self-irony - for forty year old boys, who just remembered the youth.
Story is bloody, setting is epic, heroes are brutal and girls are hot. To make it more spicy for oldies, it glimmering with few noir-ish strokes of bitterness of burn-out mid-age man, who sees time passing and new generation replacing his achievements with own new ideas he rejects.
Nevertheless, the main theme is a fun and child dreams about something cool to rapture.
You want to see mountains made of giant blades piercing clouds? You have it! You want to see how sound of burning electric guitar trembling the earth and knocking out the foes? You got it! How about Big Metallic Spiders spewing web of hand-thick steel wires? Or giant dam maid of subwoofers capable to scatter rocks? Or hellish creatures raised by your guitar solo? Enemy crowd turning to your side by crazy cool rock music you play to lead them? Yes, yes, and you can ask for extra.
Brutal Legend keeps high standards of Double Fine games - rich and expressive grotesque heroes, original and amusing  visual metaphors, perfectly suited voice actors together with a tiny bit of social satire, sufficient to cause snicker but not enough to become gloomy serious.

If you like singleplayer RPG's this game is a must buy.
The game is quite easy to get into and easy to play as well. You have a choice between the classic 3 classes; Mage, Rogue or Warrior. Which you can change between throughout the game by respeccing if you want.
The story is overall pretty bad, and i didn't really care about it that much. i mostly skipped all dialogue and just went on with bashing stuff and getting loot.
The leveling is fun, with levels being gained pretty quick, and new fun abilities being unlocked. You can stack up different types of damage to become rather overpowered in the end, which for me is fun.
The loot is great, and every pack of mobs tend to drop an item or two. But there is a problem of carrying it all. Some items are bugged so you can't remove them from your bags etc. so you end up with less space than you want all the time. You start out with room for 60 items i believe, and can buy bags so you can carry 110 or so by the end.
The loot you don't use can be sold or salvaged for materials to craft new items.
The crafting is fun, you can combine professions to create really overpowered armor by the end if you find the correct materials. These crafted armors are much better than what you can find even as rare or 'epic' items in the game. depending on level of course.
Overall: Get the game if you want a fun RPG with many hours of dungeon crawling, looting, leveling etc.

If you decide to play this, make sure you skip most (if not all) side quests. Otherwise, the story is too drawn out and the game becomes unchallenging from over-leveling.

Quick note on frame data and new players:
I find this game to be one of the best fighting games for new players to get into. One of the main frustrations for new players trying out fighting games is the fact they don't know when it is their turn to press buttons in a fight. This is due to the mechanic of frame data.
Games like Injustice 2 or Street Fighter 5 heavily rely on frame data and provide little defensive mechanics(sf5 more so than I2). You need to know when it is your turn to press buttons because otherwise you're stuck getting smacked in the face, and if you press a button when you shouldn't, you're now you're eating a combo for breakfast, lunch or dinner.
So what does Tekken do about this? It has many defensive options besides relying on frame data or meter bar. This smooths your transition learning the game. The defensive options are as follow:
-More high attacks and less mid attacks as compared to games like I2 and SF5. This means that ducking or doing a low attack(which ducks your character) is a more viable option.
-You can side step thanks to the 3 dimentional field. Your opponent could be throwing their best string, it is completely inefective is he is hitting the air.
-A lot of high crush, low crush attacks. You want to defend and attack at the same time? NO PROBLEM.
-Universal low parry. Tired of somebody stepping on your sneakers?
-Less knockdown advantage. Less 50% 50% set ups and vortex. Big boys play standing. Unless you're a filthy Capoiera player.
This is not to say that frame data is not an integral part of the game, but it is not such a steep hill for new players to climb due to other game mechanics.

PROS
-Massive roster of varied fighters
-Satisfying combat with loads of depth
-Robust online mode with decent netcode
CONS
-Doesn’t do enough to teach newcomers

I abused the summer sale to finaly purchase the Brothers In Arms Series over Steam as I already own the DVD versions of it. I did it in order to review it for you guys, not to mention the fact I am tired of the discs. This series is the most authentic World War 2 video game you can find in the video games market. Unlike any other kinds of games, you are really leading your men during battles and their faith in the battlefield is in your hands.
Now, to the point,
review.
In Brothers In Arms: Hell's Highway you are playing as Staff Sergeant Matthew Baker also known as Matt.
You are leading your men through Holland during
, an Operation that had the idea of punching through the German lines in order to open a highway to give a quick end to the war and be home by Christmass.
After Normandy (First 2 BiA games), Baker's platoon is folded into a brand new Reconnaissance platoon. The recon platoon relies on their jeeps for fast movement through the battlefields to recon and harass enemy positions. The squad is broken up to two teams assigned into jeeps.
Unlike the first two games, this game has taken the cutscenes to the next level. Almost feels like you are watching a movie and you are the lead actor.
The game has great writing. The cutscenes are adding alot to the game and to the emotions you feel while playing it. Almost feels like you are there and not Baker.
The dialouges during Battles are amusing and it feels real. Unlike in other games where when your teammates die you don't feel anything because they were 'Badass', here
you are connected to the chararcters emotionaly, you care for them and you are conecered about them during battles. When a fellow team mate gets killed, it feels like
someone has just kicked you in the stomach and it brings up feelings, almost to tears at some points. In addition to what I said, in this game Baker suffers from guilt as a result of the deaths of his friends during the battles in Normandy and you can see its affect on him through out the game. The locations of fights in the game are re-created real battles that took place in the real world, they were worked on by the developers team and historians to make the game more authentic and realistic.
The game has amazing graphics. The areas that sorround you in the game are just beautiful and mind blowing at the same time.
The uniforms of the Allied and of the Wermacht are just beautiful to look at, the weapons look way more authentic and more. There are beautiful locations in alot of occassions in the game.
In my opinion the Brothers In Arms Series is the best World War 2 series to exist. Its the most authentic world war 2 series and most realstic. It has great gameplay and storyline and brings
alot of features that other games don't. No other game made me care for my team like Brothers In Arms did. I replayed every and each one of the games for so many times, I just can't get enough of it.
I am still waiting for Brothers In Arms: Battle Of The Bulge, or what ever the name of the next Brothers In Arms is going to be. The Brothers In Arms Series needs to have a closure.
I suggest to you to buy the game, but also consider playing the first 2 games first to get a better idea of whats going on with Baker in this game and understand the game more deeply.

1)Play the game without supression bars or any other kind of miscs on your screen;
While playing with a clean screen you can enjoy the game way more than you thought you could.
Playing with a clean screen gives you the feeling you are really there in the battlefield, ordering your men.
*You will need to remember where you placed each squad and what's the role of each firing team when you order them to move because it won't tell you which firing team you chose on the screen. You might wanna know who are the soldiers of each team before you order them around so in the battlefield you will remember by that which squad is located where and move them around correctly.
*You will need to keep an eye on your fire, yeah I know hammering the enemy is fun but when you don't know how much bullets you have left in the magazine or if you have extra bullets if at all you might run into some trouble in a battle - yeah running out of bullets infornt of a german firing squad is not a great idea nor fun.
2) Play the game on authentic. Playing the Brothers In Arms series on Authentic gives you the real feeling of the battlefield. It gives you the best out of this game. Every small move, decision or order can be critical in a battle. It also disables all I said above(miscs, etc) on default because of the extact same reasons I pointed out earlier. You need to be super strategic and careful when you move your men and yourself. Stay in the open for to long and you might find yourself dead, injured or losing men.

Arguably the true successor to Diablo II, Torchlight is exactly what you want from an action RPG: loot, and lots of it. I've actually spent the majority of my time just playing through the game by myself, but you could easily jump into a server with some other people (or link up with friends) and tackle dungeons together. While there are certain items blocked to certain classes, you don't necessarily feel like you need to specialize with your character. It's entirely up to you what weapon you want your character to use, or what skill tree(s) you want to invest your points in. Torchlight doesn't use a "branching" skill system, meaning you don't have to have lower abilities skilled to achieve the more powerful abilities in that particular skill tree. As such, you are choose freely from your favorite abilities from each of the three skill trees your class has.  Another thing that I like about Torchlight is that you level up fairly quickly. I'm glad that it doesn't feel like you need  to grind so hard before you go to the next area / dungeon, because the game makes grinding fun, with frequent leveling and the promise of loot.

Overall: very worth if you have any interest at all in this kind of game.

Love, love, LOVE this game! I'm so addicted! I only got it 2 days ago, but I've played through it like 8 times now!! It's a LOT of fun, and the replay value is DEFINITELY there! Even though you're facing the same enemies, it never feels boring or repetitive to go through and tackle them again, finding new areas and unlocking new abilities along the way!
I've been reading through the comments and reviews, however, and I feel there are a couple of criticisms out there that aren't completely valid. At least for the sake of the developers potentially reading through this, I wanted to correct some of them and point out that we don't all feel that way; and maybe revision in those areas isn't actually necessary.
My biggest beef is people complaining that the "bosses aren't hard enough". I think the reason this bothers me so much is because I LOVE the flow of the game--I think it's been perfectly executed! It's always clear when one area moves onto the next, when some enemies are harder to kill than others, requiring more of your character's skill and special abilities. It feels like a story that way--it feels like RWBY!! Any fan of the show will truly appreciate the immersiveness of it all. But I think people complaining about the boss difficulty are wanting it to be a different game than what it is.... as a hack and slash game, and especially as a RWBY game, I think it's valuable that the characters feel strong... that the pace is constantly moving forward, and the fight scenes are immersive! I would be really sad if the developers felt the need to change this, if the game became all about beating the hardest bosses, and then some of that atmosphere was lost...
Some constructive feedback that I do agree with however are:
--the XP sharing thing; there is currently no real XP sharing. I don't have so much of an issue with the potential kill stealing, because I think there's usually more than enough grimm for all the players to have their chance. I think it would be nice though if breaking crates could always give XP to all the team members! In my experience it sometimes does, and sometimes doesn't--maybe I'm doing it wrong? But either way, I think that might be a nice touch! :)
--The subtitles don't follow the voices all the way, and I think they even contain different dialogue sometimes from what's being spoken! So I might recommend a look at that.
--It is kind of sad that you only get like 10 points to spend on your skill trees, especially when you've unlocked most of your skills!
Otherwise, I have a million more positive remarks:
Graphics are GORGEOUS
Characters are SO well animated, and feel so much like the characters from the real show! I love the little details, like Yang lighting on fire (and the awesome sound of her crackling), and their spot-on sprinting animations.
Combat is loads of fun, rewarding, and perfectly perfectly balanced (seriously, it was never too easy, never too challenging, always so well executed)
The soundtrack is so great!!! I especially love when you're in a fight with a big boss and the RWBY fighting soundtrack kicks in--the first time it happened I could almost swear I was in the actual show! ;) Great touch, guys!
Plot seems very good so far! Even the occasional cutscenes are great!
A really well done hack and slash multiplayer game! Mad props to the developers, you guys are AMAZING! Keep up the wonderful, wonderful work, and please don't change the great RWBY-worthy atmosphere of hack and slash fun! :)

Yes, these are things that the dev should improve upon, but I also begin to feel like everyone is really overreacting and I was one of the people overreacting and I feel no problem with admitting that I was wrong.
Breach Review:
An absolute waste of time. I'm sure most of you haven't even touched that thing, and for a good reason, so i'll explain what the gameplay is: you enter a network, each network is an overworld, kinda like in Mario games, where you can choose a level to enter. Each level is a small map that will take you around 5-8 minutes. After you finish the level, you get XP based on your performance and a bonus if you did better than the developer set time/score then you get a bonus of some sort. Problem is that this gameplay loop wrapped around some Squeenix exec saying "We need microtransactions in Deus Ex", so the gamemode is obviously balanced around that. For around 70% of the game you can do well without any microtransactions or unnecessary grind but then you hit the 3rd darknet file (darknet files are quests that revolve around you beating specific levels) and you can feel someone's hand reaching for your wallet. If you bought all the DLC then that's unnecessary, they give you so much money and so many items that you don't even know what to do with all of it. I will admit that I had SOME fun playing this gamemode but it's not even remotely worth it, let's just say that MD can't carry itself on gameplay alone.

First thing to say. This game is loooong. I played for 36 hours till now and I only completed first part of the really massive map. I'm not sure if I finish this game because of that, but whatever. What I've played yet made me staisfied.
What really stands out here is dynamic and fluid comat system. There are lot of ways to wreak havoc among your enemies which makes this game really enjoyable and keeps you playing over and over.
The other nice touch is the possibility to completely rewrite your character on the fly. Bored with your rougish, sneaky archer? Spend little money and make yourself a tankish, badass hammer-wielding paladin. You can make all sorts of builds but the game focuses on versatility. You can play as standard RPG mono build but You can also excell with a character based on every class available.
The game engine is more than competent. I experienced no hang-ups, glitches, stuttering or framedrops which is really something that makes this game stand-out in comparsion to some recent big game releases.
Graphic style is inspired by the works of Todd McFarlane and if You have seen his comics and figures,  You know what to expect. I really dig this set-up and it really helps to enjoy the fairy tale fantasy world that was created here.
What I don't like about this game is the writing. Dialogues are rather boring and I skip them most of the times. I'm not sure what is wrong about them but they seem pretty generic. All the lore that consists of books, lorestones and ballads are really forgetable. The main plot is pretty generic either. Your standard nameless-hero-saving-the-world kind of thing. That's probably the reason why this games didn't receive that much of attention since it release.
Anyway this game is more than decent and if you have abundance of time to waste, this game is more than capable to make you satisfied,

It really is a shame that 38 Studios went under and won't be able to bring anymore Amalur content or a sequel of some kind.  This game had the vast open world of The Elder Scrolls, along with the deep lore, and the satisfying hack n' slash combat of God of War.  While the combat did feel repetitive at times, I found that mixing up the three main skill trees (Might, Sorcery, Finesse) helped negate that feeling.  This game also provided TONS of voice acted dialogue, with some pretty decent voice acting to boot.  In short, if you're a fan of open world RPGs, definitely try this one out.  This game, in my honest opinion, is a prime example that even good games can flop, whether the reason be for being severely overlooked, or for coming out at the wrong time.  Despite its flaws, it really could've gone places, assuming they would have added more polish and tweaks here and there in the right areas.  Maybe one day, a company will pick up the Amalur name and jumpstart it back up.  We can only dream for now.

So, I missed some things in my previous review. I'm going to break this into parts: Presentation, Story, and Gameplay.
Graphically and artistically the game is fine. Nothing about the monsters stand out, but nothing seems phoned in. There are no slow downs. Sound design is fine and the voice acting isn't too bad but....
....The cutscenes have that dreaded eagle-eye stare. It's like Oblivion except worse. Additionally, the music is fine until you start fighting people. The combat music is exactly the same for every encounter, even the nobody stuff that you can one hit. The only two times I've seen the music change is when you are fighting the Tuatha or a boss. The two other songs are better and actually have some love put into them.
The biggest and most glaring problem is the camera. I'll discuss it below with gameplay.
The story is about.. um... The elves-I mean Fae! The Fae are broken up into factions and they are timeless, ageless.. yadda yadda. One group, the Winter Fae, has broken off into a new group, the Tuatha, who believe they are bringing a new god into the world. You, the player, are killed and brought back to live by the Well of Souls.
Here's where the game gets interesting story wise: Since you were brought back to life, you are no longer tied to the shackels of fate. You can choose your own destiny and change the fate of the... Wait a second, this sounds a lot like Raziel from the Legacy of Kain series. In fact, the concept is exactly the same. With real free will, your character is supposed to change the world. This works really well in the world, and it plays nice.
However, the gameplay is flawed. This game was clearly rushed out because a lot of it has zero consideration. Polish wise, everything functions, but there are a lot of things that are out of place. It's really, really easy to gain gold, to the point that you can respect everything into crafting abilities to make new gear, then respec back to your combat stuff. Don't bother with the warrior or mage trees at all, just make a finese character because the dual weapons + bow and arrows are literally the best weapons in the game. By 10 hours in, you'll have so much gold you can easily respect to fit your builds.
Now, developers, I have a question for you: Does making the game world bigger make it better? Lemme answer for you.. NO!!!! Reckoning has a low run speed.. But so did Skyrim! But here's the thing... Every time you enter a new area, there are 3~5 new quests to do and they are all the same. Unlike Skyrim, there's no reason to explore areas UNLESS you have a quest. Since everything gives you XP (literally, everything does), you'll run into a problem where everything gets too easy too quickly. I highly recommend playing the game on hard, otherwise it will be too easy. You'll also encounter a problem where you discover an entirely new area that has more quests in it but... everyuthing in the area has a gray name because you were over leveled by the previous area.
The big areas are worse with the mini-map and the camera. The Minimap has that problem Final Fantasy XIV had where the only areas you can run are drawn or emphasises. Since there are invisible walls around the edges, the big massive world turns into whatever is pictured on the minimap. The camera only makes this worse because you have to manually aim up to see how vast everything is. It auto-levels to a downward angle of the player whenever you move.
Technically speaking, Reckoning is also a Fable clone for combat. You can hit stuff, shoot stuff. It works just fine. But as I have stated above, there's only one real viable option: The finese route. You can mix and choose, like I did for my original 30hours on Origin, but you will HAVE to use the finese armor and skills because they simply do so much output.
If you can withstand, avoiding some quests so you can focus on the main quests, the game isn't that bad. Combat can be fun when it isn't insulting easy; and the MAIN story quests and the FACTION quests are worth the time. Just only pay $10~15. Be sure to get the DLC for the quests; but not those extra weapons because they will be replaced within your first two hours of play.

Ok.  So.  The game itself is everything you hoped it would be.  It's more Deus Ex, it's more Adam Jensen, it keeps the atmosphere of the previous game without being a carbon copy of it.  It improves on several areas and makes a plethora of little quality of life changes.  The new abilities are glorious and fun and intuitive, and it just rocks.  If you liked Human Revolution, you'll like Mankind Divided.
Now to the cons.  The DLC is a complete scam.  If you preordered the Season Pass, I'm so very sorry.  All DLC is one-time use only, on one save.  Want to replay the game?  No more DLC equipment packs.  The in game shop is used to repurchase the crap you already purchased.  This is such a cheap money-grap it's insulting.  Do not buy any DLC.  Period.
As to the performance issues, there are a few things you can do to improve it.  Turn off MSAA, and make sure Volumetric Lighting and Contact Hardening Shadows are set to off.  Bam, now things run smoothly unless you're near the bottom of the system specs for the game.  As for any other bugs, this review was written the day of the release.  I'll give Square Enix a bit to patch them, but they're not really that intrusive even now.
Buy the base game.  Enjoy the base game.  Don't give Square Enix another dime after that.
