While this game obviously has it flaws, especially the imprecision of the ranged combat, it's a very good game. I'm a huge fan of the Warriors franchaise, so this feels like it's a more frantic version of that, with a nice little system that you figure out as you go along. It can be played with KM just as well as Controller, so that's pretty damn good.
It looks like a very promising game, and the drop in and drop out gameplay style online means that if you have something come up during the campaign you don't have to worry about screwing over the rest of the group, as it also scales difficulty with people.
As I said, ranged combat is a bit bizarre. It shoots exactly the way your character is facing. This may not seem like much, but given that the camera needs to be manually controlled, it means that you might think you can hit an enemy to finish it off, but you instead hit another enemy accidentally.
Rooster Teeth you bloody amazing people, I can't wait to see where the game goes from here.

Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning is a great action RPG. The combat is smooth and entertaining and the attention to detail in the world is enough to keep you interested during the 35 or so hour gamelength. While there are hundreds of quests, and the game could probably be played for 70-80 hours, I recommend playing this as a story driven RPG. Focus on the main quest and the extremely entertaining faction quests, and the game never skips a beat. However, if you decide to tackle the 100 or so side quests, you will open a pandora's box of issues. For one, most of the side quests are generic. Thats not to say they are not well made, just that they are not anything beyond "go here, kill this/find that, return". On top of this, you can quickly over-level. There are ways to avoid over-leveling, but the easiest is to simply limit the number of side quests you do. If you take all of this into account, you'll find that Kingdoms of Amalur is a fun, well made RPG that has plenty of story and gameplay content.

The best way I could describe this game is World of Warcraft meets Skyrim.
Amalur has a lot going for it in the way of efficient dialogue, skilled voice actors, spectacular combat animations, and masterful music.
Amalur falters, however, in inheriting the problems of WoW and Skyrim: frustrating inventory system (at the beginning of the game when you don't have a Stash yet), tedious quests, repetitive fights, very long travel distances, and not the most engaging plotline I've followed.  The game kind of feels like it's trying to be too much for too many people; the way instructions are worded makes one think this were an introductory RPG (as compared to much more detail-oriented games like Divinity).  This irked me, strangely.
I still recommend the game.  It's not "bad" per se, but falls short on too many levels to keep it from holding more profound players.  It's a 60-hour hack'n'slash with some great role-playing bits (not in terms of the story, ironically, but in how you want to approach combat) that you might like in spite of the amount of running you do.  Suggest picking it up on a sale.

Have you ever played an MMORPG and felt, "oh gosh, I wish there was no once else but me and the NPC's around here"? Then this game is right up your alley.  This game is right down to the core an offline MMORPG. You get tons of trash armor, there's something that reminds of dungeons, kill and fetch quests everywhere and as much action in the gameplay as you would expect of an MMORPG. While the overworld have some pretty places to look at, you rarely get much of a chance to do so since you spend most of your time inside somewhere.
Positive:
+ Combat is responsive when dodging and there's nice hit detection when hitting an enemy
+ The armor is the game looks good
+ Overworld is pretty and there's a lot to look at
+ If you dig deep there's can be some fun character builds
Negative:
- Using shields in combat is absolutely unresponive and awful
- The amount of trash equipment you get makes it a chore to find anything. You spend more time going through trash than you do comparing which weapon to use
- Questing is VERY overwhelming in this game. You get quest, on quest, on quest, on quest.
- Questing is completely uninspired. If you've ever played an MMORPG you probably have experience with the kinds of quest you get in this game.
- They don't put much effort into getting you interested in the story, which is needed in this game since you get so many story side-quests. Sometimes you end up doing a quest and out nowhere find out it was apparently a huge part to the main story, but unless you're really reading and listening to every single NPC on the way you won't get anything from it.
- I played over 10 hours and not a single hint of a mount of any kind. Wouldn't even be a little surprised if at least 5 hours of my gameplay time has been just running from dungeon to dungeon and city to city just to get filled with quests. Some cities only exists to give you quests.
- Overworld, while pretty, feels very empty. You get the feeling of playing a dead MMORPG everywhere and it just stops the world from feeling alive at all.
With all of this said, you might find some enjoyment if you really enjoy making original character builds and mess around with that. But if you're anything like me and just enjoy some classic warrior action this game is going to bore you to tears and you're better off with Guild Wars 2, which actually is an MMORPG with an alive world and have fluid combat as well.
Only buy this game if you're starving for some wRPG action.

Spelunky is a 2D action platformer, and an HD remake of a freeware title I used to play all the time. It's a simple concept: You play as one of a handful of cute little explorer people reminiscent of the Indiana Jones film series, and you attempt to guide them through a series of 15 Randomly generated stages across 4 landscapes, with optional side landscapes and optional bosses to discover, Players must fight their way through the game in one continuous run to complete the game, as the entire game world is randomly generated every death. The game also offers alternate game modes to mix it up a little, such as (up to) 4 player co-op, 4 player VS mode, and a Daily Challenge.
This is one of my favorite games, and I highly recommend it to any fan of Rougelikes or 2D platformers, you'll get hours of entertainment from this game!

At this point, anyway. I'm sorry, but $15 is just too much to ask for what you get.
There's just not much here. Two fairly short missions, combat that still needs a lot of tweaking, and the beginnings of a story. I played through all the content the game has so far in 1.2 hours, and unlike the original fangame demo, it's no longer something you can keep playing until you get bored. The whole game is very rough around the edges and clearly a long way from completion.
I have some reservations about what's there, too. While revisiting locations from the show with established characters has an appeal in and of itself, I would have preferred to see different parts of the world and play new characters. Combat becomes repetitive and pacing is lousy, although this is something that can and hopefully will be tweaked. And there are a lot of standard tropes and stock elements- the game just doesn't really distinguish itself much.
With all that being said, it's not all bad. The graphics and animation, barring a few glitches, match the style of the show well, and the sound design is surprisingly good for a game in this stage. Despite being unbalanced, combat is pretty fun- the problem is that it gets tedious because of pacing, not that it's inherently flawed.
If you're a die hard RWBY fan, you probably bought this the second it came out anyway, but if you're on the fence, I'd wait a bit before taking the plunge. I have faith that someday this game will be something great. But that day is not today.

Howdy guys, I have read alot of different and varying reviews on here about Gunz 2.
However here is my take(from in game experience)
This game considered to be in a *Early Access* Phase, which means that there will be many bugs, and server crowding issues. This is a result from the hype of everyone wanting to play the game at once. Now I have read forum posts about how they have servers in other countries, they have had a year at least to get them perfected, I am very sure that the Korean Servers were working as smoothly as they were when it first was released. So please dont turn away fromt he game because you cant enter. Be patient guys, you will be able to enter and have fun, just give the developers time to work out the server kinks.
Anyway, MY take on the game is this
There are 4 different chracters to choose from
Ivan- The marksman, he uses precision rifles to snipe from range, and he has a nice SMG to back him up in CQC.
Max- He is basically a tank, he runs around with a shield to bash people with and blocks incoming attacks, He also carries a minigun and flamethrower
Elena- She is kinda  mixture of power and versatility. She carries a Assault Rifle, and Grenade Launcher
Reva- She is an assassin, and I personally think she is OP right now but she uses daggers and SMGs, along with shadows to kill enemies with
There isnt much customization in these characters right now because it is Early Access, but there are 3 types of gear sets for each, as well as 3 different weapons to choose from in each character category.
The servers can only hold 4500 people right now, but that is going to change here very soon.
The combat system has verred away from any K-style, BF, DBF and such and is focused more on a Run and Gun mentality.
Wall Dashing and running is a little more complex than in Gunz 1 but they changed the mechanic to make sure people werent reloading and firing while bouncing off the walls all the time, making the game more balanced for less agile players.
There are typos, and DC"s but overall I recommend this game for those willing to wait and see it. It is very fun, and intense at times and for what they released it is a fun game.

First and foremost, this game is MASSIVE. The main questline itself is somewhat on the short side, but when you combine it with the sheer number of side stories and quests that are available, well... I think looking at the number of hours I've spent playing it speaks for itself. It's worth noting that though this is a strictly single-player game, it has a very MMO-like feel to it.
Gameplay-wise, there's a LOT going on here. Firstly, you have a massive number of weapons that all offer unique styles of gameplay. Then you have a multitude of classes you can choose from, from warrior, to rogue, to mage, to any combination therof, and you can respect yourself as often as you like. One minute you can be cutting down your foes with a broadsword while hurling fireballs into their face, to sneaking up from behind and stealth-killing everyone in your path. There's so much variety and versitility offered that it's pretty much impossible to get bored. You're also offered a crafting system that is in-depth but easy to master.
Story-wise, the main story is somewhat interesting but pretty generic. You play a chosen one - a hero killed from the start and brought back to life, are now unbound from fate, and has the powers of a god who can break the fates of those around them and fight against a bunch of fae who've been courrupted by demons. While the main storyline is somewhat bland, that isn't to say there isn't a lot of depth to be found.  Along the way you'll be able to take part in many optional side stories, from from becoming a member of a court of fae and learning about their culture, to unraveling the secrets of a school of magic. There's a lot of additional lore too for those who wish to dig deeper; in-game books to read, and many NPCs offer their individual thoughts and opinions on a variety of subjects.
Graphics-wise, everything is beautifully rendered. Unfortunately  the world itself, while gorgeous at first, is pretty generic and gets old fast. Forests, dessert, plains, etc. Dungeons especially become visually boring and repetative. As for the audio, the voice acting is very well done and the music is very nice.
If you're a fan of action RPGs and MMOs, I highly recommend this game. If you choose to pick it up, be sure to grab its DLC as well. It's just as worth it as the main game.

This is a really great game. Of my 16 hours playing this game, I have probably only done 2 of the main quests, because of the fact that there are so many fun side quests and side story lines to do. That includes the time I spent to beat the DLC, which I would say is worth the money spent on them.
The game allows you to chose your fate as you go. You earn skill points, which you can put into Might, Finesse, or Sorcery. After putting a certain amount of skill points into those skill trees, you unlock fate cards, which grant you bonus perks that will help you with the skills you unlocked in the Might, FInesse, or Sorcery skill tree. The best thing is that they have 6 fate cards for each skill tree, that you unlock as you put more skill points into your respective tree, but you don't have to only put your points into one tree. They also have 6 fate cards for each of the hybrid classes: Might/Finesse, Might/Sorcery, and Sorcery/Finesse.
For certain quests, you will also obtain Twists of Fate, which grant you permanent bonuses which could include extra XP, more health, more physical damage, etc. As you progress through the game, you get more of these, which all stack, so you become more and more powerful as you do quests.
The actual gameplay is great as well. It is a Hack 'n Slash sort of game where you can string together different combos that you unlock from the skill trees. It is also a Button Masher, but I like that about games, so no complaints from me.
The Story is interesting so far, but from what I said, I haven't played too much of the main story, just because of the sheer vastness of the side quests. I mentioned that I played the DLC, but there are so many other side quests and factions excluding the DLC. The game allows you to venture off as soon as you finish the tutorial area, and you are free to explore and do any side quests you want before playing the story.
The graphics are pretty good, but not amazing, and the voice syncing is kinda iffy, but the voice acting itself is really great.
The game is also somewhat easy to play, so I would suggest playing it on the hardest difficulty in order to have a decent challenge.
Overall, I would rate this game a 8.5/10, a must get for any RPG and Hack 'n Slash fan alike.

Numerous times through the game I couldn't help but think that the producers, having probably spent a large portion of the budget to bring in McFarlane for concept art; Salvatore for story writing; and voice actors for all of the dialog, were demanding unrealistic publish dates that forced the developers into a tough position.  The world wasn't immersive enough, the combat encounters were way too repetative due to painfully small monster variety, the itemization was awful... during the last quarter of the game I stopped openning chests and looting bodies completely because I never found upgrades anyway, and the level design felt unnecessarily drawn out or repetative in many ways.
Ultimately, this game shows that a lot of quality work went into conceiving a game that would have been amazing to play, deeply immersive, and with many novel concepts, but somewhere in the process of development a line was drawn and deep concessions were made. Evidence that the games' potential was never realized is staring you in the face from start to finish. It is a shame really.

I was in the mood for a world war 2 shooter, since nowadays those are surprisingly rare. I read reviews on Steam and Metacritic to see what was popular and Hell's Highway came up.
After beating the game I am still not entirely sure if the game deserves a recommendation or not.
For starters, the game has some glaring errors in historical accuracy, such as German 88's firing at Sherman tanks at point blank range and failing to penetrate or a single such Sherman tank rolling through hundreds of men, tanks and 88's (for some reason there are no other antitank guns in this game, just the 88 anti-air -guns) with ease.
The graphics (originally designed for the Xbox 360) are obviously dated, with character models warping and distorting uncomfortably and facial animation all but missing entirely. The voice acting is lackluster to say the least, ambients sounds are often missing, weapons sound muted and dull and even the music seems to be oddly off-key in few points (though this part might just be my lack of knowledge showing through). All in all, the game's audiovisual presentation is pretty terrible. Even the ragdoll physics are glitchy as heck (I shot a german soldier in the head and he jumped 50 meters in the air as he died)!
So far, then, this seems like a no-brainer: an ugly game with bad audiovisual design through and through.
And then we get to the gameplay, and here I find myself intrigued. You are acting as a squad leader for most of the game, and that means you cannot just charge the enemy Call of Duty -style, but have to order around your fireteams (up to three at a time, ranging from machine gun team to base of fire team to bazooka team to assault team), setting them up in cover, assigning them targets to suppress and maneuvering them to outflank the enemy. The levels offer a sometimes surprising amount of freedom in how much you can maneuver and the system feels surprisingly good most of the time. I especially enjoyed the frantic tension of emerging into a new area only to observe a german squad marching across a field, ordering my men into position and then watching the enemy spread out into cover as the shooting starts. The enemy AI is also surprisingly good, acting surprised where appropriate, falling back and regrouping into better positions as they are overrun our outflanked and generally putting up a good fight.
And then the game shoots itself in the foot again. Several times I had the AI completely glitch out, with my machinegun team or bazooka team simply freezing in place and refusing to move, getting stuck in walls or cover and such. The game hands you a sniper rifle on a few occasions, which immediately results in you, single handedly, gunning down literally dozens of germans within a minute or two, utterly breaking any immersion the game might have had so far. The tone of the game is all over the place, and then, in the end credits, comes the final straw. The story ends on a minor cliffhanger with "To Be Continued" -emblazoned on the screen. This game came out in 2008. I played it in 2016. There are no sequels, and likely never will be.

Spelunky is a 2D action platformer, and an HD remake of a freeware title I used to play all the time. It's a simple concept: You play as one of a handful of cute little explorer people reminiscent of the Indiana Jones film series, and you attempt to guide them through a series of 15 Randomly generated stages across 4 landscapes, with optional side landscapes and optional bosses to discover, Players must fight their way through the game in one continuous run to complete the game, as the entire game world is randomly generated every death. The game also offers alternate game modes to mix it up a little, such as (up to) 4 player co-op, 4 player VS mode, and a Daily Challenge.
This is one of my favorite games, and I highly recommend it to any fan of Rougelikes or 2D platformers, you'll get hours of entertainment from this game!

First: This is not a terrible game, but in my opinion there is no point in playing it.

Problem is the controls are not fun to use, and to make the player become attached to the charachter requires challenge so he can feel what these 2 kids are going through, but there was no challenge. The Journey these 2 kids went through was sometimes ridiculous and they should be dead million times but because the game was so goddamn easy it never really felt like a dangerous journey.
However from a narrative perspektive this also doesnt make sense in my opinion. These 2 kids do this journey to find this cure for their father who will die (maybe?), however it should be very obvious that this is the most dangerous journey ever but it isnt because this is a story and not real life and the thing is I would be okay with that, but the ending ruined it.
The ending, oh boy, what a terrible and cheap way to "shock" people. No spoilers here, I have a spoiler part at the end of the review.

Not only does it look very awkward how the people talk (so the player knows what they are talking about) but the language itself sounds extremely fake and also funny which took me out of the experience many times. Oh, the game was also♥♥♥♥♥♥♥full of cliches ... think of any cliche from old disney movies, all of them are in this game, the most obvious being the characters of the two brothers. The older brother is of course the clever and brave and the younger brother was fooling around most of the time.
Did I mention the game is only 2-4 hours long?
I know the game has very good reviews and some people love it to death, so you also might like it.
One positive thing is that the game had some beautiful locations, however the graphics are bad from a technical standpoint and some animations are terrible, this isnt a big problem though because of the perspective you are playing from.
"what a terrible and cheap way to "shock" people" what I mean by this is the death of the older brother which was stupid. First of all it was so obvious that the girl is evil, another cliche (pretty girl turns out to be evil ugly monster or witch), the boss fight against her was boring and extremely easy. The thing is while you were controlling the younger brother she was attacking the older brother, but did NOTHING to him. I know this is a game but the thing is after you rip out all of her legs she just picks the older brother and kills him like it was nothing. When she is half dead and cant even move somehow she learnt to attack all of a sudden, but before when she was extremely fast she did nothing. This is the cheap narrative. The writers want you to think "yes we made it! That was a close one!" and at the last moment "♥♥♥♥, it wasnt over yet! Brutal Legend is more about aesthetic show than a gameplay. Yes, it is a proper game with a intricate gameplay of many interwoven genres, with switch changes from third person slasher through arcade race to tactical battle for tower dominance. Still, the main part of the game is kitsсh and forgotten childish dream about coolness. It visualise glory and vivid brutality of the golden age of hard rock, binding together all archetypal memes of the time. And it is glazed with nostalgy about  good old times, with a bit of self-irony - for forty year old boys, who just remembered the youth.
Story is bloody, setting is epic, heroes are brutal and girls are hot. To make it more spicy for oldies, it glimmering with few noir-ish strokes of bitterness of burn-out mid-age man, who sees time passing and new generation replacing his achievements with own new ideas he rejects.
Nevertheless, the main theme is a fun and child dreams about something cool to rapture.
You want to see mountains made of giant blades piercing clouds? You have it! You want to see how sound of burning electric guitar trembling the earth and knocking out the foes? You got it! How about Big Metallic Spiders spewing web of hand-thick steel wires? Or giant dam maid of subwoofers capable to scatter rocks? Or hellish creatures raised by your guitar solo? Enemy crowd turning to your side by crazy cool rock music you play to lead them? Yes, yes, and you can ask for extra.
Brutal Legend keeps high standards of Double Fine games - rich and expressive grotesque heroes, original and amusing  visual metaphors, perfectly suited voice actors together with a tiny bit of social satire, sufficient to cause snicker but not enough to become gloomy serious.

Now, don't get me wrong. Despite the negative rating, I honestly do enjoy GTA V, or at least the singleplayer part. It's a fun and charming game with a lot to do, great writing, and a lot of hours to spend. The multiplayer, however, not as much. With rampant hackers, a play-to-win model, and microtransactions everywhere, it leaves a lot to be desired.
In the years since GTA V's PC release, Rockstar and Take Two have constantly been making decisions which have been incredibly consumer-unfriendly. Whether it's the neglect of the singleplayer mode in favor of the broken online which just happens to make them more money (seriously, where is the singleplayer DLC? No, let's just keep having more MP microtransactions instead), or the time where they manipulated Steam sales by adding one of their virtual currency cards in a bundle to avoid actually going on sale, or most recently, the debacle where Take Two has gone against the modding community, by sending a C&D to the OpenIV team.
Mods have been an important part of PC gaming for a long time, and the Grand Theft Auto series is no exception. In the singleplayer campaigns, people have the right to do whatever the hell they like with a game that they have purchased, as long as it has no bearing on other players. But no, apparently that's bad now, according to Take Two. Never mind the epidemics of hackers on MP, it's the singleplayer modding community which is the problem.
But as long as these issues still stand, there is a definite problem, and it needs to be addressed.

The game is alright, but the company is garbage with p2w features allowing you to basically buy anything you want, and Take 2 trying to destroy the singleplayer community by issuing cease and desists to anyone modding them game. I've been playing this game since Early Access, and back then it showed promise. There were plenty of issues, but those are to be expected in an EA game. So I tolerated them, waiting for the developers to work out the bugs and add missing features.
Now, however, that they've gone into full release... I can no longer show any leniency with it. And seeing the positive reception, I feel the need to make my thoughts on the game known.
Behind each game, there is a motivation. A thought that caused it to form. Sometimes it's "I want to make people think", sometimes it's "I want people to get together and have fun", sometimes it's the infinitely less desirable "I want to make money."
For this game... It's pretty obvious that the thought was "I want to make something pretty." The game does look nice. Pretty bland and kind of mobile-y if you ask me, but artstyle is a much more subjective issue. The real problem is that the people behind the game strike me as graphics designers, not game developers. Because while the game looks nice, it is littered with beginner mistakes gameplay-wise. Allow me to list a few.
- The game is an INSANE grindfest. Resources are divided into tiers (portal blocks, ores, gems, etc. all follow this model), like copper to iron to gold as you might be used to if you play any game like this. But here's the catch... Each tier requires more resources. You need more ore to craft a bar, more bars to craft certain items, more portal shards to craft a portal block, and so on. This means that each new tier requires you to spend more time grinding and effectively makes them feel gradually less valuable. You only need to spend a little time gathering copper, but gathering titanium takes forever. And if you play with friends, don't expect to stop whacking those ores with your pickaxe any time soon.
- Random crashing. Sometimes, for no apparent reason (only when playing online as far as I have experienced), your character glitches out entirely after which the game shuts down, sometimes with permanent in-game effects like a loss of money. I remember seeing other varieties of crashing, but that's the only one I distinctly recall. What's worse, sometimes after crashing the game won't even start and you have to reinstall it. This is not acceptable for a "full release".
- Unbalanced classes. The ranger is garbage. Objectively. The mage gets spells, the warrior gets "shouts" that are really just "warrior spells", and the ranger gets... what? In a similar sense, its equipment appears to be worse, it overall underperforms when put next to a warrior or mage, and perhaps worst of all... resin. Because the game wasn't grindy enough. At one point in development, the terrible decision to add resin to the game happened. And now, rangers need to run around chopping down a ton of trees in order to craft most of their equipment. Meanwhile, the equipment of both warriors and mages requires much easier-to-get resources for the most part. Still requires excessive grinding at higher levels though.
- Awful GUI. Look at something like Minecraft. How smooth its inventory management is thanks to a handful of easy-to-use options. Now look at Portal Knights. Its inventory management is terrible. For the longest time there was no way of separating a stack of items, and the best they've done at this point is add a "split stack" option. That's not enough. What if you just want a single item from a stack? You'll have to split it over and over. Why not do it almost exactly like Minecraft? Well, one reason is that right-clicking a stack in this game brings up a menu of options. However I'd argue this menu isn't necessary. It has options like "drop", which already has a special slot for you to put items in. And even if they wanna keep the menu, at least add more useful options. Like the ability to type in the number of items you want to withdraw from the stack. Also, your inventory as well as storages are WAY TOO SMALL for the abundance of items in the game. Prepare to make a ton of chests. And forget where things are constantly.
- A painful lack of variety. The game consists of you moving from island to island, biome to biome, collecting what you need to upgrade your equipment and move on to the next island. However the islands are not distinct enough to make this worth it. The most prevalent reason for this is the enemies. There's only a handful of them, as well as biome-specific varieties. After a handful of islands, you'll barely ever encounter another brand new enemy save for the three bosses. Only cheap reskins with different elements and maaaybe a slightly different attack. And since the game relies so heavily on this exploration, this "journey", this gets monotone very quickly. If there were more side activities, perhaps some that tied into each biome to make them more worthwhile, then this might be more forgivable. As is, the worst part of every new save is having to unlock all the islands. Which is a problem, because it's the main goal of the game.
- Mediocre combat at best. Click a lot. Click nearby if you're a warrior, click far away otherwise. Step to the side when the enemies do their thing, maybe sometimes step backwards or run around a little. That is basically all there is to the combat. Save for the bosses, however they instead all rely on the same tactic. Do a thing, and attack them while they're stunned. For the first and third boss, the thing is to attack something other than the boss. For the second boss, the thing is attacking it in a slightly different yet obvious way that makes it extremely easy.
This level of combat might be acceptable in a game not focused on combat, but well... this one is. And I think the biggest problem isn't what I described here, but the fact that enemies have a huge amount of health, even if your level and equipment is appropriate for the area. The chore of having to wait for each one to die only adds to the grindy feeling of the game. The aforementioned lack of variety also makes it worse, especially in the dungeons which circulate between only a handful of enemies. Of course, another big issue is something that I felt the need to make its own point...
- Plain stupid enemy abilities. This is one of the more evident signs of the developers' lack of understanding of video games. Let's start with blocking. Some enemies have the ability to block. When they do this, they become invulnerable to all attacks. The problem? They randomly do this for several seconds. Which means that once they do it, you just have to stand and wait for them to stop. Blocking should be something very brief, when an attack is expected. The way it's done in this game, it only disrupts the flow of the fight. A more extreme example is the Kupongo enemy (renamed "Alp-Utan" for some inexplicable reason, even though I personally like "Kupongo" way more), which at half health freeze themselves in ice and become invulnerable in the same fashion, for waaay too long. It's a pointless, annoying mechanic that only makes combat even worse.
I think the worst offender however is probably the Fallen Wizard. When these guys die, their resurrect themselves. Not once, not twice, but INDEFINITELY. The only way to permanently kill them is with a weapon that deals Light damage. And here's the thing... There's no in-game indicator that this is the case, and I imagine a lot of players won't bother with Light weapons either because of roleplaying reasons or more likely because there are better alternatives.
I could go on with more examples, I could elaborate on the intolerable lack of swimming in water, other balancing issues, the pointless forced class-specific nature of equipment that prevent multiclassing (which was added in an update, a big mistake like the resin if you ask me), etc. but the character limit is fast approaching... Prepare to be frustrated. Prepare to be mercilessly beaten by better players over and over again. Prepare to constantly think, "No way! That's totally broken!" Prepare to have an open mind and realize that while, yes, the balance between classes is a little skewed, it all boils down to player skill. Prepare to stay mobile, for a stationary player is quickly killed. Prepare to spam your directional keys, yell at your screen, and sometimes even win. Prepare to have a lot of fun... if you're willing to learn and get better.
For those familiar with Gunz 1, the sequal is essentially the same, but with the removal of animation cancelling, and everyone has about a third as much health. In addition, everyone has a melee weapon, a short range weapon (usually smg of some sort), and a long range weapon (sniper/mortar/etc.). Combat is still frantic, and even moreso frantic now that deaths happen so quickly due to low hp. Also, successful execution of a melee chain usually results in death.
The campaign mode is back, and is much more robust than before. However, the reduction of player health pools makes it... well, a little different than before. If you try to just jump in and melee, you will die. Quickly. However, it's still fun, and even has a story connected to it.
While the game does have a slight pay-to-win aspect to it, the advantages you gain are minor, and mobility and aim are so important that a better player will beat a worse one regardless of the gear/class equipped. Either way, the game is free-to-play, so go ahead and give it a shot.

Overall, I can't say I'm in love with this revision of the Tekken series.  But if you're looking for a good 3D fighter to play, especially if you're able to have local matches with friends, it'll get the job done.
+ Seems well optimized, I think it can run on a lot of the hardware that's out there in the wild.  No problems whatsoever on my i5 3570k with a gtx 970.
+ When I could find matches for online, the connection seemed alright.
+ Akuma is a really interesting addition to the cast and is a great representation of the Capcom character.
+ Rage Drives -- a technically complex mechanic that allows for some great (and impressive looking) combos if you can manage to find the execution necessary to pull them off.
- Rage arts.  Tekken did not need the equivalent of super/ultra moves from other fighting games.  It tries to add a comeback mechanic that wasn't really needed for some reason and doesn't really add anything or help casuals pick the game up.
- Not in love with the character redesigns either (for the most part); at least Bandai Namco gave alternates that could be used that were more like the Nostalgia costumes Cacpom charges for.
- Surprisingly, it was possible to somehow pre-order and not receive Eliza.  Not only this, but she is apparently not available in the Season Pass or as part of the Deluxe Edition overall. However, she appears in game during the Treasure Mode as AI.
- Online already seems dead.  If you don't have friends to play against, you may have trouble finding a match.
Arguably the best 3D fighter on Steam, but it leaves me longing for a port of TTT2 or Tekken 5/6.

Okay so first of all this isnt a full review its more of an early thoughts review. I will try to be spoiler free :) also I will update this when i complete the game. I also wanna point out I bought this on greenman gaming for 45 USD. That aside I would like to say that i've never played a Deus Ex game before. I am Currently at 6 hours and so far im impressed before I go any further here are my specs.
Windows 10 home premium
Amd Fx-4130 overclocked to 4.2 hz
Msi Gtx 960 2gb (reference not twin frozr)
125 gb ssd(as boot drive)
500 gb saegate harddrive
8gb ddr3 ram
Let me talk about performance. My rig isnt the best by any means but the game is definately playable for me on release day. It took me around 30 minutes to tweak my settings but I managed to get from 35-55 fps. That being said there is parts where its not so smooth the framerate could go from 50 to the mid thirties when you do things like fall from a height and do the icarus fist groundpound move. Of course these problems could just be from my older cpu and only 2gb vram on the 960. I know I can just turn down the texture quality and volumetric lighting but this game is so beautiful I wouldn't dare. Do I think there should be a patch that fixes the choppy frame rate yes. Once they make some optimazation tweaks and add dx12 support I believe I can get a constant 50 fps. Here are my settings.
I have msaa on 2x, Texture quality is on very high, Shadow quailty is on high, and I have everything else as high as it can go including volumetric lighting.
If you have never played a deus ex game(like me) there is a great 12 min cgi you can watch when starting a new game that gets you caught up on the lore. I wasnt aware that deus ex is an rpg I like games where you lvl up your character. As for the game play I choose the lethal route (I Love Shooters). I love the cover system and the gunplay. Takedowns get repetitive and they take awhile to recharge. So far the augment abilites are really cool. The hacking mini game is a little confusing at first so make sure to press help if your like me and get a little confused. The cutscenes are awesome as is the fact that you can pick up many in game objects and stack them to climb up to places or throw them to distract enemies. Alot of people are complaining about in game purchases but so far that hasnt affected my game in any way. You can just as easily find weapons and ammo if you search for them.
So at this present moment I would recommend this game. The graphics are awesome. The controls are great(I use an xbox one gamepad). The music and sound are amazing. A few parts reminded me of the witcher 3 soundtrack. But the important part is that im having so much fun and isn't that what video games are for :) I can't wait to finish this game. Then Again who knows I might finish the game and change this to a negative review.
Hope this help interested buyers with their decision :)

so, first impressions after playing an hour: for an early access game, this seems pretty polished! everything ran smoothly, no lag, even when someone would jump in/out of the game! graphics are great like the show, soundtrack makes great use of the show's background soundtracks (could've used maybe 1-2 instances of some of the sung songs?). voice acting is decent, few lines got a bit repetitive (looking at you yang) but overall on par with the show. gameplay is where things start to get a little...eh, with room for improvement. right now, all 4 characters are very similar in how they play; same combos, same sort of attacks, but they do have some difference to them. Ruby's attacks hit very wide, weiss feels very sharp and precise, blake has a sort of jumpey floaty feel to her, and yang feels heavy and weighty with her attacks. personally, i think as the level caps grow, more skills could be added that would defferentiate them better.
overall, this is a pretty solid core game, and the only thing really lacking right now is content. more campaign chapters, characters, and skills would bring this game up. one thing i did find odd to be missing is any kind of tutorial though. nothing about control mapping, or explenation of the controls. that being said, they are pretty basic, so a few minutes of button mashing and you'll figure it out! for now, i'd reccomend this game to fans of the show who wanna support it's continued development. for 17$ CDN, i feel this was a worthwhile purchase

I have to say that for an early access game, this is really good. I believe that it has huge potential in the future, and I can't wait to see where they go with it. That being said, there are a few things that I do take issue with. First, the auto target is crap. A game like this is definitely in need of some kind of lock on system for long range attacks. The second thing, as some others have mentioned, is that the combat can get incredibly repetitive and dull the longer you play the game. Most games like this use the standard "heavy attack, light attack, gun" and it tends to work very well. A combo system of some kind would also be nice.
However, the biggest issue I have with this game is the fact that it's online multiplayer only. I hate online multiplayer, and I always will. Now they do have a "play with friends" option, but I don't have any other friends that use steam. They all play consoles and I don't like to play with just random people. When they said it was similar to Left 4 Dead, I was hoping they would also include a single player mode in which the AI could control the other three characters. Sadly, this isn't an option and it kind of dissapoints me. I won't say the game is bad because of this. Most people don't mind it, and there isn't anyting wrong with it. For what it is, this is looking like it could be a really decent game and I would definitely recommend it, but be aware that it is online only.

-Every character has an individual skill tree with three specials and two unlockable upgrades.

-Of the two individual upgrades, one usually requires a certain amount of special attack kills and the other is only unlocked when you reach level 10, but it stays unlocked for future playthroughs.
-Other upgrades include: increased health, increased aura (pretty much shields), decreased aura recharge time/delay, decreased revive time (requires 5 revives to unlock), and increased amount of special attack points.
-Only has one champaign but will have a total of three
Recommendations:
-keyboard is fine but prolonged playing hurts your fingers. USE A CONTROLLER
-Always get the Lvl 10 upgrade on your first lvl up (assuming youve made it lvl 10 in a previous playthrough)

OK, time has come to write a review about the game. For starters, I 'll apologize for my bad english, and state that the game has far more problems that I 'll write of; I am only gonna say the ones that is worst in my opinion:
The game, sometimes (really sometimes), is fun, it can get pretty fun WHEN is balanced. You still gonna keep playing, and getting angry and frustrated to stumble at these rares battles.
Before someone tell me that Reto-Moto is a small company and all that, I can say that the game is already old (three years is a long time, a large amount of money gathered from players) and they should have been less greedy and fixed this game at soon it got popular; so, people like me, who fell in love with the game don't feel robbed from spending a lot of cash paying the 90 days veteran bonus (it's the first and only F2P game I have done that in all my life, and boy, how I regret it now).
The community is more toxic than Team Fortress 2 (a game that I loved so much ultil valve broke it, but hey, the community was toxic even back then):
I don't know how that was possible! I mean, the game doesn't have a chatlink between teams, I absolutely loved that; that means less tension and sport-play, right? No! You get killed a lot by guys nicknamed "noob hunter", his soldier name is "noob raper", and his weapon's name is "back to spawn, b."; lovely... There are tons and tons of insulting names for weapons, soldiers, and nicknames (the majority of these guys are hackers, what a surprise...). And since your team can't chat rage them, they let their hatred and frustration on their teammates; so the real fight is on team itself most of the time.
The unberable grinding:
"Heroes and Generals", yes, that sorta reminds "D & D" for a catch title, but is also for the fact that  you that you 'll need some "heroes" (soldiers) and some generals to effectively play the game. HOWEVER, is not SOME soldiers, you gonna need A LOT!
Put this way: the game doesn't allow you to change your equip. when in respawn in battle. "Oh, OK, they just want you to balance your stats and focus on a role at a time", WRONG; you cannot change equip and badges (badges are the most RPG part of the game, they are unique bonuses for a soldier to equip at a time, pretty fun and neat they are), but you can change soldiers in any f. respawn, or even a soldier of another class (provided your squads have "seats" available). And it gets worst the controversy, you need to achieve everything to every soldier from ZERO. You don't even have a bonus fto "speed" achievements that you already got in another soldier; so, the "don't change equip. setting" is a blatant trap to make players grind themselves insanely, and ultimost, spend their cash. That makes most of people play a insane amount of time just farming credits and ribbons (gameplay achievements); that's right, only a very few are really in a battle, a large number of players are "working" their account, just like they do work in a office or for their school.
The matchmaker, hackshield, and report feedback (inexistent, to say the least) are a gigantic bad joke:
There, there is the worst part of all for me, this is the sole reason (even having so many) that I am giving this game up.
Is so, so difficult to find a fair match, most of the time, or you and your team massacrates the other(s), or, you and your team is massacrated. You can see that in the very beggining of a match most of times. And before people come around saying that "war is not far" and all that, I 'll tell that resources are NOT the issue, is the inexistent balance matchmaker between players. Even if teams HAVE that same resources, generally just one side have players that are available to USE IT. In short terms: in a match, a team have five players playing tanker, three aviators, five snipers (most of the times, the game could be named Snipers and Generals), and a few inf., while the other team consist maily in inf. that 'll be a target party for the other; that solo tanker, fighter, or sniper in that unfortunate team will or be camping, or beeing a target pratice as their inf. mates (to make things worst, that sistematicatly dieing you cost you, much more than you make in the match in these matches).
Have a fighter-pilot, or a tanker that can help your team from being slaughtered? Good for you, rarely you gonna be assigned in squad that can afford that class change.
Are you playing in a short time like me? Ha, you gonna play with those guys that have every equip., and tons of in-game experience as well.
Hacks users, cheaters, wow, just, WOW! The only game I saw these much hack users in a game was that infame crap Combat Arms back in the day. I mean, there you be a time that will be commom to see three grenades explode in the foot of a player (even in your team, in everywhere), and he gets only "wounded", that said player, not surprisely died very few times, has super-human reflexes (aim-bot), and kill everyone with only one bullet of ANY gun (even pistols), in the torso (super-bullet); it gets better, you can get headshotted, over and over, 700M aways in a foggy map, by that same guy that doesn't even have a scope or in a MG of a tank. Combine this by a lot of insults in their weapon's, soldier's name and thats that. Then, you ask yourself why keep modding your weapons, charaters and all, just to be killed with people with no skill, only programs; why keep playing at all?
That brings me the last topic, the report feedback: Is very easy and intuitive to report players in this game, the bad news are: you are only wasting your time doing that. This game is pretty fun and not as much of a b-list game, as I expected for the price.  This is a fairly linear, old-school WW2 shooter, with a cool squad factor.  Beware of have far away you are and the path a squad might take though.  I've had them basically commit suicide by running through enemy lines, rather than behind something.
You are part of a glider team that lands in Holland sometime after D-day, and basically have to move forward and  clear out a lot of Nazis.  There is also an interesting back-story that unfolds, involving the main character's engraved .45 pistol.
As far as the game mechanics they are pretty much what you would expect with standard motions, weapons and shooting.  Strangely, there is no jumping, except for valting over a cover item.  If the game  recognizes an item as cover you can also vault it.
As far as the cover,  pressing Q benind a solid wall or other solid item like vehicles will put you in  in a temporary 3rd person cover mode, and you are crouched behind the cover item.  Using the arrows allows you to  move behind the cover or lean out to shoot.  This mode also give you a a much finer cross-hair for aiming, and a much steadier aim.   This is kind of  cool, but also has a  drawback, as you can' t control how far you lean out (or up if behind a wall).  So when shooting from cover you have to expose yourself to multiple enemies.   The method is to take fire until the view is starting to get pretty red, then go back into cover before dying-- and hopefully killing a Nazi or two in the process.  This is a little lame and would be much better if you could lean just enough to sight in on a single enemy, depending on the positioning.
Another really lame thing is that when sprinting you can't change direction very much with the mouse.  You can use A and D keys to kind of swerve--, but you basically have to stop sprinting to make a normal turn.  This is very weird to get used to, and I can't imagine what the  developers were thinking. Another weirdness is that while in cover and being flanked it is easy to get "stuck" to the cover.  The only way to get off is to move directly backwards, and that is easy to  forget when under fire.
Still, in spite of these negatives, this is a pretty fun game, especially for the price.
If you think you would like an old-school, ww2, squad shooter with a decent story then skip a fast-food lunch and you'll have the cash for this game.  Bon Appetit.

Spelunky is a great blend of the platforming and roguelike genres-- hell, I'd even say it's in the top 10 influencial games in the last 10 years. Even The Binding of Isaac, one of the most iconic roguelikes currently out there was inspired by Spelunky. So let me just be blunt here: this game will kick your♥♥♥♥♥ especially when you first begin. If you have ever played Isaac before, that game has a focus on quantity. Some items are amazing and some items are bad. However, in Spelunky, pretty much every item can help you out. With 2 notable exceptions, all of the items in the game are not direct upgrades to each other (the exceptions being Udjat Eye > Spectacles and Vlad's Cape > Cape). Also, some items have hidden features, like how Spike Shoes not only deal extra damage when stomping on enemies, but you have more traction on slippery surfaces or how the Spectacles can increase your vision in darker levels. The items are all balanced with each other and there isn't an apparent disadvantage to any them. Unlike Isaac, the items all increase your utility more than anything. When it comes to stats, the items you get don't directly increase a broad stat. Instead, they help you reach higher platforms or see where the exit is located, which in turn can help resource efficiency and prevent unnecessary damage. One important thing to know about Spelunky is that you can easily die at any point in the game. I've lost 7 hearts in one level to one small screw-up. There are very few times where you would blame the game rather than yourself. One more thing I want to talk about: the worlds. There are 4 main worlds in Spelunky, but there are also a few secret stages as well. The first world is the Mines. The space isn't very open and Arrow Traps appear, which do 2 damage on hit, but you can easily disarm them by throwing something in front of them. The enemies that appear will also do low amounts of damage and move slowly. After 4 stages in the Mines, you enter the Jungle. The Jungle is widely considered to be the hardest level of the four. The Jungle generally follows the same structure of the Mines, but with completely new obstacles, like Tiki Traps which can single-handedly end a run if you are not careful. You will have to progress through the Jungle slowly and methodically, because the game has a lot of opportunities to end your run immediately if you are not careful and observant. The Ice Caves are a pushover. There is a lot of space, but there's also an abyss at the bottom of the levels, so if you take knockback and get stunned, you can be done for. Ice Cave levels are very short and sweet. The Temple is the final main world of Spelunky. It brings back all of the old traps and also introduces new and very dangerous Crushing Traps that play like Thwomps in Mario that can attack from all of the cardinal directions. The enemies in this level can move quickly and do a lot of damage. After the third stage in the Temple, you fight the final boss and win the run. However, that is not the only ending to the game. I don't want to spoil it because some people are sensitive about that, but the second ending that I speak of is very, very difficult to obtain. Think you have what it takes? Buy Spelunky!
Tip: The game goes on sale for a very small price tag on major Steam sales.

An imporvement on the Stick of Truth in almost every way, although it's very apparent that this game was made with the Xbox and PlayStation in mind since the mouse support in the game is kind of glitchy.   Instead of just being able to easily click on a menu option or select an enemy in combat, the mouse kind of snaps to different items and the cursor doesn't even initially start moving for a while.   It's clear the developers would prefer you just use a D-pad to select things, for no good reason.
On a related note, the inventory menu is overall more difficult to navigate and everything is designed to be more compact and stylish, which makes it difficult to read and analyze.
However, I liked the improved and more interative combat, the random encounters and special boss battles. And I like that they made the random scraps that you find around South Park useful for crafting instead of literally doing nothing like in the Stick of Truth.
I also like that they separated costumes from stats so that you can design your character however you want.  Although, the artifacts system is a little cryptic as to what they actually do and I usually ended up just choosing stuff with higher numbers.
The story and the humor also stood out more in this game.  I especially liked the stuff related to your identity with the rednecks and Mr. Mackay, the blend of social inclusion and satirism in this area felt just like an episode of the show.  And all of the time travel callbacks to Stick of Truth were really cool.
In conclusion, the game offers about 10 more hours of gameplay that Stick of Truth and buying it actually includes a copy of Stick of Truth, which I didn't expect.  Definitely recommended.

I remember the day when I had bought this game when it was on a Steam sale. I had a couple of dollars left and I wanted to spend the money on something that interested me. I had bought Torchlight II and haven't touched it for quite some time, since I was not an active Steam user back then. When I first played it, I immediately regretted not playing this sooner.
Torchlight II is, to put in the simplest words, an amazing game. The product is a highly polished game with many surprises hidden around every corner.  The world is randomly generated every time you start a new character/start New Game+ on an existing character so every experience will be a highly unique one. The game really gets to the point; you can immediately delve into the fun of clicking on monsters and annihilating them with your weapons/skills.
As is said in many other reviews, the story is definitely lacking. I had attempted to follow the story when I first started playing but ended up not caring for the story at all. If you are into an RPG with a rich story, this game is not for you.
Gameplay-wise, this game tops it all. You'll be mashing your number hotkeys and your mouse trying to rid of the monsters trying to swarm you. There are many random traps and surprises lurking in every dungeon and area you face. The skills for each character are also special and will leave you wanting to upgrade all your skills. As said before, each dungeon and area is randomly generated, providing a unique experience everytime you play. You will feel a great sense of accomplishment as you finally knock out the final boss of the game. This then leads to the Mapworks, which you can buy with your in-game currency and play special dungeons. Or you can start up NG+ and start your whole adventure again, keep all your character stats but buffing all item drops and monsters.
All in all, Torchlight II is definitely a game that anyone should check out, even if you do not like RPGs. This game is a must-have on anyone's game list.

I can recommend buying this game whole heartedly, I have thoroughly enjoyed it.  It goes so far beyond any other game of its genre in depth and scope that there is just nothing like that I have ever even heard of, not when you really get down to meat over everything this game covers--manual combat, strategic battle, significant RPG elements, kingdom simulation, trade simulation, political drama. . .  there is so much here.
The game is not without its flaws however.
1--The thing it does better than everything else can be its greatest weakness.  This is at its core a game of mounted combat, and it can have a bit of learning curve to figure out how do step up and be a real mounted warrior.  I am not the most coordinated guy and I struggled mightily getting a handle on the combat in this game.  My soldiers rode circles around me, it was embarassing.  I can see some folks just giving up--don't, it's worth it to learn and enjoy the depth of the system.
2--There are many other different elements besides the battles/combat they are all good/nice but not great/thrilling.  They are very stylized, formulaic, and obviously randomized and proceduraly generated.  This can hamper the immersion for an RPG guy like me.
3-- Your companions have a basic I like A, I hate B, I have this background and that is about it.  There is not really much development.  In a game with this much going on I can totally understand it, but I'm an RPG guy and in any game with companions I want development.  This kind of goes along with #2 they did a little companion work but not so much as to make you really care about your companions.
4--Once you get land and investments things can get pretty tedious.  There is not really any way to set things up to manage themselves although I'll admit that I have not played a large amount of time at "Endgame Content" so I might have missed something.

In M&B:W, you play the part of a foreigner in a new land, hopeful to break into the world of Nobility.  How you go about this is almost completely up to you. You will start out as an independent operator, scraping by fighting rabble and engaging in trade, eventually (if you choose) becoming a vassal of one of the kings, managing your own villages, castles and towns and, perhaps, even becoming a king yourself.
Gameplay consists of a combination of RPG, strategy, economic simulation, resource management, and, most importantly, 1st/3rd person battles.
Pros
----
- Sandbox experience, several ways to approach the game.
- Grand scale and replayability, lots of gameplay hours.

I believe I have enough hours on this game to write a decent review. (But you can never have enough)
First of all Mount & Blade: Warband is definitely not the prettiest game out there, but don't let that stop you from buying it.
In warband's singleplayer the main goal is to take over Calradia, you can achieve this any way you like because you are basically free to do whatever you want. You could join one of the factions (The Nords, Swadians, Rhodoks, Khergits and the Sarranids) and help them conquer Calradia. You could also create your own faction and capture every city there is by waging wars againts the other factions.
You build up your army by recruiting soldiers from villages, after some battles you will have the option to upgrade them. Every faction has certain troops that are superior compared to the other factions for example The Nords have huscarls, and they are without doubt the best infantry in the game.
The combat, I've read alot of mixed opinions about the combat system. Some say it's way too difficult while others say it's just a matter of blocking and slashing. In my opinion it just has a very steep learning curve, which is hard to master. There are 4 attack/block directions and plenty of weapons to chose from. (there are throwing weapons, bows, crossbows, lances etc.)
Another feature is the fact that you can earn reputation through completing quests for certain lords, this can come in handy late game when you have to convince lords to do certain thing for you.  There are many more factors like right to rule, renown etc.
The singleplayer also offers the options to marry, siege, recruit companions and gear them up, tournaments and much more.
In my opinion what makes the singleplayer so amazing is the fact that you can control your army while also fighting yourself, it's a mix of Total War with Chivalry basically. Also the many mods keep it interesting to play.
When you first play the multiplayer you will get absolutely destroyed, this is because the game is old and most of the players have already played it for a long while.
The multiplayer offers:
The community is amazing, if you have the Napoleonic Wars DLC there are regiments you could join. These regiments have trainings and events that are a ton of fun.
I would give it a solid 9/10, old but gold!

Okay i love this series but i need to do this in a neutral way,
So first characters
Lets start with Ruby Rose. She is the AoE huntress of the group clearly. Her basic combo and specials are all AoE expect for her 3:d ability. She is the most stable of the group not many bugs that have happened with her.
Next Weiss Schnee. Shes the single target character who excels in taking single grimm out really fast. Shes also kind of the medic of the group with her nova capable of healing with upgrades. She has a single bug with pierce that ive encountered that it does no dmg.
Blake Belladonna. Blake is kind of in between with everyone else. She has the highest basic combo on attacks so shes capable of getting her specials back fast. Blake has also been stable expect for dmg bugs with her specials.
Last but not least Yang Xiao Long. Yang is the tank of the group taking dmg can help her to be able to do some amazing combos with her specials. Specials are balanced really well. Only negative side with her is that she has the most bugs. Every single ability has a chance to do 0 dmg and her blastwave can throw you to the other side of the area.
Next gameplay itself. Its a Hack and Slash what do you expect? Combat gets repeative pretty fast but its still extremely fun to do. Grimms AI:s are somewhat good but they bug out every now and then and make sudden turns randomly. Every1 of the group is special in its own way so picking your huntress is really something that changes the deck a lot.
Graphics are decent but i dont personally care about them. Its a + if good graphics but it dosnt make a game good in my opinion.
Perfomance is decent too. I had to play myself on Potato quality (Nice job on naming it :D) but i didnt see to much difference between Potato and Ultra.
Voice acting is great! Every character feels the same way as they do in the series. Ive had a single bug where Doctor Oobleck didnt start his dialogue in mountain glen.

Ive had a bug where a player joined the match but he/she had to go the other way for some reason. Last bug ive encountered is that a Weiss in my game got stuck (spoiler alert) in the bomb at the last part she got out of it but it was really strange.
My hopes for the future are that there would be more groups heres a few characters that i would like to see and play as Oobleck, Goodwitch, Ozpin and of course get JNPR in there ;)
Overall the game has an amazing potential, fun gameplay, great taste of unique between characters and a great dialogue and im really looking forward for more.

The world is made up of blocks and you can mine them and use them to build or craft things. It's like Minecraft in that way. If you like Minecraft, this game will feel very similar at times. What got me hooked on this game, though, is that it compelled me to progress. The first set of islands you visit contain resources that help you prepare for the first boss fight. The second set provides resources for the second boss fight, and the third set provides everything for the third and hard mode boss fights.
Progression feels decently balanced. I didn't have to go out and grind tons of XP to get to the level cap. Mining/farming for resources starts out easy early on, gets a little more time consuming mid-game, and starts to seem daunting as you approach end-game. It levels off at that point though. Mining for Titanium for instance, seemed to take ages at one point, and now I have so much of it I'll likely never use it all. Alternatively, you don't really have to mine most resources because mobs drop most of them. It's nice to switch from mining to fighting and back to break up the monotony.
Potions you might want to use for end-game content are also dropped by mobs, but I tend to enjoy setting up large farms to grow my own resources and craft them myself. If you like building/maintaining farms, it's pretty easy and satisfying in this game.
You can play as one of three different classes: Warrior, Mage, and Ranger. I guess you can technically play each class a variety of ways, but for me, it seems like every boss fight is just using Poison Rain and attacking with whatever weapon I have equipped. In this way, combat is pretty simple, and maybe a little repetitive. I tend to enjoy it though.
You have multiple options for gear. My wand-wielding mage is currently wearing two light armor pieces, two heavy armor pieces, and a medium armor cape. It has decent damage mitigation, decent self-heals, and decent damage. You could also gear for a pure damage build and be a glass cannon, or a pure damage mitigation build and be a tank (although it seems like being a tank only has situation-specific uses at this point... maybe the hard mode dragon boss).
My only major complaint about the game involves the camera/targeting system. Particularly noticeable in the Worm boss fights. Every time I do one of those fights, I find myself constantly targeting the boss while I'm trying to target the worm tails. My reticle will be directly over the tail, but I'll lock on to the boss for some reason. Happens a bit in the Hollow King fight with the crystals as well. You can switch targets using the Tab key, or whatever you bind it to, but it seems to me the "lock on" feature should prioritize whatever your reticle is over. Sometimes feels like I'm fighting with the camera, but it isn't enough to be a deal-breaker for me.
Other than that, I'd just like to see more content. A wider variety of loot and craftables would be nice. More bosses and more zones would be awesome. I'd love to see more of this game in general.
Edit: They finally added DLC content that previously was only available to pre-orders or early access or something. So that's cool.

Easily my all time favorite rogue-like platformer.
This game is very challenging and might seem unforgiving at first but it is not, when you start, you are just going to stumble upon every single lethal traps and possible combinations of bad actions that will lead to your instant harsh death.
So you might hate it at first, however once you start to learn from your mistakes and how to avoid or fight enemies,obstacles and traps, you will get to access deeper parts of the game, grab better gear and it will feel extremely rewarding because this game isn't about memorizing the layout but anticipating possible pitfalls from previous experience and from your ability to made quick and smart decisions but also long term decisions such as managing your bombs and ropes.
As you improve your spelunking skills you will realize how much more depth the game has than you previously thought and how well designed it is.
The levels are procedurally generated, so while the themes of the levels and enemies have a general structure, the paths, positions, quantity of items and enemies do change every time you restart, this makes the game a lot more interesting as it challenges your ability to improvise and anticipate.
The game also offers optional paths and shortcuts, different endings and overall just varied play styles.
Sometimes you will be given a layout with many resources, tools and weapons and in other cases a layout might have very little resources or weapons, so you will have to adapt and be more careful with your starting resources (bombs/ropes).
While sometimes a layout can seem bad, it may become better if you keep progressing and it might surprise you with a special opportunity or item.
The game does have a slight bit of gambling but your experience, choices, actions and determination are what will ultimately define if you'll be able to "beat" the game or not.
If you're really having a hard time making any progress, reading some guides helps but don't spoil yourself the deepers parts of the mines you haven't gotten to yet.
I wouldn't consider it cheating to get some help from guides as you still need to remember all the traps, enemy behavior etc and make the proper choices in the moment on your own as the layout is always unique.
This game is full of surprises, accidental chains of events that happen with items bouncing around triggering traps or hitting an enemy leading to hilarious deaths or events, which again, you can avoid if you anticipate.
This is one of the things that make the game so great, the interaction between the player, items and enemies with its physics often creates new situations and you will always see something new happening even have hundreds of hours of play.
It took me a lot of hours to beat the game, but the feeling of satisfaction and completion is unlike any other game, this game takes "work" to beat, you have to outsmart the game and top yourself every time you make a new run, its a game that requires you to think, no hand holding but that's why its so rewarding, if you beat it, you sure as hell earned that victory.
The game also has collectibles, with a diary that records every item you found during your adventures, enemies you killed etc for the fans of collecting items and achievements, this game is probably one of the most challenging, if you manage to get them all, props to you :)
Finally the visuals and character design is great, music is fantastic, catchy and there's even some rare special tracks which are even better, will you find them?

Now, don't get me wrong. Despite the negative rating, I honestly do enjoy GTA V, or at least the singleplayer part. It's a fun and charming game with a lot to do, great writing, and a lot of hours to spend. The multiplayer, however, not as much. With rampant hackers, a play-to-win model, and microtransactions everywhere, it leaves a lot to be desired.
In the years since GTA V's PC release, Rockstar and Take Two have constantly been making decisions which have been incredibly consumer-unfriendly. Whether it's the neglect of the singleplayer mode in favor of the broken online which just happens to make them more money (seriously, where is the singleplayer DLC? No, let's just keep having more MP microtransactions instead), or the time where they manipulated Steam sales by adding one of their virtual currency cards in a bundle to avoid actually going on sale, or most recently, the debacle where Take Two has gone against the modding community, by sending a C&D to the OpenIV team.
Mods have been an important part of PC gaming for a long time, and the Grand Theft Auto series is no exception. In the singleplayer campaigns, people have the right to do whatever the hell they like with a game that they have purchased, as long as it has no bearing on other players. But no, apparently that's bad now, according to Take Two. Never mind the epidemics of hackers on MP, it's the singleplayer modding community which is the problem.
But as long as these issues still stand, there is a definite problem, and it needs to be addressed.

The good:
- Great combat system for an RPG
- Great graphics and animation for its time; ran very light on my relatively weak system
The bad:
- A blind chimpanzee can beat this game's "hard mode"
- Without any challenge, there's no incentive to take advantage of the game's combat system
- Very poor zone scaling mechanics hurt the "open world" aspect
I should begin my review by saying that as far as RPG's go, I tend to be on the "power player" side of things which means that I'm more interested in combat mechanics than immersion and storyline.  KoAR is a game that had so much potential because the developers put so much effort into the combat system, yet all of it was thrown out the window because of the game's pathetically easy difficulty.
The list of things that makes this game too easy is vast.  Your character gains exp too quickly.  Crafting and gathering grant you obscenely powerful items.  One single piece of equipment with HP regen renders you nearly invincinble for 99% of the game.  Some spells are incredibly overtuned.  The list goes on and on.  What makes this so frustrating is that "Hard" mode is actually quite challenging for the first hour or so.  In fact, approaching one of the first bosses at the wrong time can make for a very brutal fight.  But once your character begins to develop, any semblance of challenge is thrown out the window.  Side quests are a detriment to the player's enjoyment, because the character begins to gain too much exp and will eventually overlevel his surrounds by a wide margin.
The combat system is one of the best seen in an open world RPG.  The game offers a lot of Devil May Cry-like mechanics which allow the player to dodge blows and juggle mooks, but why overcomplicate things when the monsters don't even hurt me to begin with?  I can try to juggle this kobold across the map with an insane looking combo, but in the end i could have closed my eyes and mashed left click to win the fight anyway.  It's just a mess of lost potential.  And this is on "hard" mode.
The game has other flaws including a very poor level scaling system in which monsters in a zone are "locked" to the level which your character first entered the zone and some poor balance mechanics with the talent trees and side professions offered to the character.
I understand people playing "unarmed Dark Souls" challenges or whatnot, but for this game it is a requirement to play with no side quests, no side professions, no potions, and use of only starting gear to even begin to feel like it had any difficulty.  I understand that Dark Souls and Devil May Cry aren't for anyone, but at least try to make "hard" mode... hard.
