It's a good game - a strong example of a squad-based shooter. You control the position and focus of 1-3 fireteams, edging your way through battlefields to flank enemies and progress through linear levels. It encourages you to leverage your fireteams because your own weapons are unreliable to the extreme - on par with Counter-strike accuracy. Bullets spray for no particular reason, shots that are dead-on don't always register, and enemies take many shots to take down. While that's frustrating, it highlights that you are not a pure badass. Sure you may mow down hundreds of enemies in a playthrough, but ultimately it tries to knock you down to size with it's iffy gun mechanics - you need to use your squad to succeed. And while it is frustrating to not be rewarded for your own skill, i can understand that sloppy controls make you rely on your squad more.
It also seems to want to be Band of Brothers, the TV show. The game spends an enormous amount of time showing wooden characters (some of which are obviously derived from Band of Brothers characters, one of which even shares a voice actor) talking to each other about the war and each other. It spins narratives about cursed guns and lost loves which have exactly nothing to do with the game. The first ten minutes (not an exaggeration) is a series of unskippable cutscenes that awkwardly introduce a set of characters which it clearly wants you to be invested in. It keeps introducing new characters who have small quirks and different voice actors, but whom you really don't care about. When it kills off or maims a character, you're clearly expected to care, but there's no *reason* to care; the gameplay (controlling the position and focus of 1-3 fireteams) is identical no matter which characters are involved, and you're aways given replacements who are exactly as capable. Cutscene after cutscene is used, even with "shaky-cam" effects and close-ups of expressionless faces. It's all the more frustrating because this came out a year after Bioshock, a game which is almost purely story-driven, uses the same engine, and yet falls into none of the gameplay or storytelling pitfalls that this game does.
Ultimately, it's a fun game that executes a squad shooter very well, despite the flaws. I'd recommend it if you're certain you want a squad shooter, and wouldn't recommend it for any other reason.

If you want to play Brothers in Arms just play this. Unless they rerelease the older ones and fix some mechanical issues with the games and flesh them out more this is pretty much the best BIA game. Its basically a cheap bargain bin WW2 game that. Thats BIA. I feel like for the BIA games they just copied mechanics of other better games and especially when they were popular. When Socom/Freedom Fighters and COD were popular they made the first two games, when Gears of War and shoulder high walls became popular they put that into the game. But honestly the cover mechanics make this game better, one of the issues in earlier games was that you couldn't go third person and get a feel for whats going on very quickly, so you could either look at a wall then pop out or risk being shot and just stand there.
The damage system is ♥♥♥♥ing terrible. I don't think you need to get shot to get hurt, but its so terrible I can't describe it. You regen health though but its not like that makes it better. You have to hit the enemies and work to get shots to hit their mark but they can just spray all over the place and still hit you.
AI is terrible, especially friendly AI. They either path in the way of fire or they decide to run around like headless chickens even though you gave the order to stay where they were. Its about on level with Road to Hill 30 give or take.
I would say the game as a whole objectively and as a game is better than Road to Hill 30. Its atleast easy to shoot people once you learn the system, and its otherwise given a bit more polish. Unfortunately its still not a polished game and is only a bit better in general than the older ones but its that extra bit that makes it a playable and enjoyable video game.
BIA is a bargain bin series, which is unfortunate as there are points that you can see a gleam of something great shine through in production or writing, but then it falls apart when a character is looking at you with a look that makes you think hes holding back maniacal laughter right after a character died.  Its this kind of stuff that makes it impossible to care about anything in this game aside from the base combat. Also your squad can die, but they respawn at the next check point, which also makes you not give a♥♥♥♥♥♥about characters since they die over and over and over until they die in the story.
They also tried some weird F.E.A.R. like situations where its supposed to be spooky but its just stupid and the enemy AI and gun play show themselves as terrible when compared to FEAR (which is one of the best FPS in terms of gunplay and especially AI).
Man,  I don't recommend this game, but if you want to play a BIA game this is the one you ought to. Its still pretty below average though but its not as terrible as the older ones.
If they remade the games they could easily make them great though. Add some more polish and make the existing systems make logical sense. It wouldn't take a terribly large amount of work to make Hill 30 into a great game but it would take money. Which is fairly obvious with these games they didn't want to spend money, they wanted to put out something quick that would make a profit off current trends then move on.
For what its worth I kinda like it. Not enough games let you command units whilst directly controlling your own character. But its certaintly not a objectively and mechanicly good game. Its okay at best.

Beautiful game. I have to say, I originally was put off by what seemed like clunky mechanics, and wondered why there was no support for a second player. I wondered about the simplicity of the game, the lack of instructions, and the seemingly cliched task of going to find a cure for a sick father. I wondered about the slightly odd meshing of textures that the game presented; the contrast of a stylized background with semi-rough looking foreground. But all of that became something that was so much more than it initially seemed to be. It became what is an incredibly emotional, poignant, and immersive experience. The clunky graphics prove to be a product of two brothers working together on a difficult journey. The lack of instructions speak to the experience that the two brothers face, a sort of unknown journey that they must puzzle their way through. The seemingly boring outset of the game ends up being a wonderful checkpoint for the story to come full circle to.
The game is mechanically simple, you use just a single controller with a joystick and trigger controlling each brother. There are never in game instructions, and all that you finally get through is done by experimentation. Some of the tasks seem pointless, and I will admit that initially I was struck with the lack of any driving reason to continue in first 1/10 or so of the game. However, as the story develops, you become more and more excited to continue on in the journey and learn more about the world that the game takes place in. The narrative travels through several different areas which tell a story in their own right. Several times, the brothers come across opportunities to help others, and to discover a little bit about the place that they inhabit. The game does a great job of giving you a little sliver of story that you then can infer about, and use your imagination to embellish.
The game is graphically quite beautiful, and it does a remarkable job conveying the atmosphere through the use of lighting and really well done models. The water is gorgeous.
The game has several themes that run through the course of its story, which I will not spoil because really what you should be doing is picking this up right now and playing it through.

This review is mainly for the co-op mode. I make this distinction early because, surprisingly, it is very different to the single-player. Gameplay-wise it's more or less the same, but it feels very, very different.
This game supports co-op but I believe it's best played single player. This is because the screen (assuming you are playing same-screen local co-op) follows the leader. The screen doesn't accomodate two players very well, as the screen will MOVE WITH the leader as the leader runs and jumps around, thus making it very difficult to control and keep track of your character if you're not the leader. Not only this, but if you're not the leader, you can literally disappear from the screen, at which point it gives you a few seconds before you DIE. This is incredibly frustrating as the name of the game is platforming, and PRECISE controls are ESSENTIAL in the genre.
It doesn't feel like two player co-op, but more like the second person is tagging along. If you've played the likes of "Enter The Gungeon", you'll know what I mean. The second player is at quite a huge disadvantage, and yes they can contribute, but they're considerably weaker and more often than not actually hinder your movement and progress. Friendly fire is also ALWAYS ON (this is not necessarily a good or bad thing, as it can be hilarious but also very annoying) and in a game where you're jumping around and dodging spikes that can kill you in one hit (yes the spikes are insta death) and chucking bombs that fling you across the screen it's definitely something to consider (I personally like this, as it adds a level of challenge and teamwork). Also, you can't save the game (this is important) and if you want to complete a full playthrough you're going to have to start from level 1 ALL THE WAY THROUGH to the end (Lost Castle, Enter The Gungeon). You can find the "tunnel man" who will let you skip levels, but this actually puts you at a huge disadvantage because going through the levels allows you to stock up on necessary items such as climbing ropes and bombs, so ultimately you have to start from level 1 if you want any chance at beating the game.
I may be a little too harsh on this game, and feel free to comment if you believe it to be so. It is a good game, with precise controls and simple to learn but hard to master mechanics. There are also a variety of items that change the way you approach a level, and you must be meticulate and methodic when running around to collect as much money as possible to buy items. You'll be stacked with gold if you're quick and smart, but it's not easy or generous by any means.
I think it's unfair for me to give this a bad review because I thoroughly enjoyed this game, so for the sake of this review (I review games for couples, so naturally the co-op mode is what I'm here to review) I will give two different verdicts.
Single Player: 83/100
Cooperative Mode: 73/100

what makes the game so difficult; but that more interesting and fun

I purchased the game on recommendation from a friend. I finally downloaded it several months later but once I started playing, I didn't stop for almost three months. EA, 38 Studios and Big Huge Games collaborate to create one the most creative, immersive and playable open-world RPGS I have encountered. Heralded as surpassing Elder Scrolls: Skyrim in depth of character, plot and combat dynamics from several sources, Kingdoms of Amalur was an absolute joy to work through. The world draws you in with all its vibrant textures and colors, begging you to explore more as you discover literature, warring factions,  strange creatures and races, exotic locations and an enormous list of armor, weapons, and accessories. The fantasy world that you enter in to is overflowing with side quests and locations to explore in its massive scape. Gameplay is unique and intuitive enough that it never became old.  Each weapons handles differently and takes time and experience to fully master. Colors and textures pop from the screen giving this  RPG unique and warm feel as the environment comes alive in front of you. Side quests are diverse; allowing you to grasp the expanse of Amalur as you explore hillsides, desert, forrest, islands or plunder caves, dungeons and castles in search of better equipment. You become attached to your character, the weapons you forge for him/her and gradually become invested in their success as the story deepens and eventually unfolds into a fantastic tale set in a magical world. After logging over a hundred hours  in this game and working my through every section and sidequest; I can say that I was left feeling extremely satisfied and pleased with this work as a whole. The story is masterfully written and gameplay is fun and intuitive. I would recommend this game to anyone looking for a fantasy rpg with a intricate story that they would like to sink a considerable amount of time into, experiencing all that Amalur has to offer.

The online portion of the game (which is being pushed heavily right now), is horrible. There are long loading screens everywhere, trolls who want to do nothing but kill you repeatedly are the main players in lobbies, and hackers are rampant. All of the interesting things they've added in the online mode aren't made available in singleplayer either. The final nail in the coffin for online is that the grind is insane. For example, to gain access to CEO jobs, you need about 3 million dollars. To get that much, you can do heists or jobs which net you very little money and often rely on the good nature of other players for you to succeed. It's a simple case where those who've played more and have better equipment can just stop you from progressing at any sort of meaningful pace. Of course you can just pay huge amounts in the form of microtransactions in order to skip some of the grind.
Something that I bought this game for, which I had hoped would massively improve the quality of the game, was modding. However, with Take Two's current stance on any sort of modding this isn't likely at all. If you want a fun open-world game, I'd recommend any of the Saints Row series or even Watch_Dogs instead. This falls far short of what I'd consider a well made game.

Portal Knights is a fun combat oriented builder game that is made much more enjoyable playing with a friend.
The Combat
Each of the three classes gives players the freedom to create their character around their play style and mix classes somewhat. I really enjoyed this, as creating a knight who can throw lightning bolts is right up my alley. Additionally, being able to dodge and roll out of the way of enemy attacks makes the combat feel engaging and skilled. I will however note that the challenge of the game can quickly escalate or become dull depending on where you are fighting and what your goals are.
The Building
As of now the game feels fairly limited in the furniture that it offers, there are four sets and many other items are dungeon specific, meaning you’ll have to pull some of your decoration from dungeon instead of being able to craft them yourself. There are however a lot of cool blocks to build with. The variation of blocks keeps me wanting to build something new, using different styles and using different worlds for the backdrops, it’s a little limited but still rewarding.
The Late Game
If you aren’t someone who’s good at setting goals for your character than this part is where the game can lose its charm. The late game aspects don’t offer much more than farming bosses for all the best gear to add to your collection. However if you enjoy building this is the best time to get to it, since by the late game you will have unlocked all the worlds and gained access to much of the cartable furniture items.
In short I felt the game made for a fun builder and decent action with friends. And I should stress that here, the game is built to be played with friends. So team up, explore and beat down some monsters.

So I have spent a few weeks in the lovely world of Portal Knights. I have always loved the concept of a world connected in such a way as you find in Portal Knights. You can build all kinds of things in Portal Knights, Buildings, furniture, armor and weapons etc. it is a rather expansive list. Each world that you travel to has a robust and distinct environment with events, boss fights and questing. Overall, very enjoyable experience. The only drawback is a limited number of class choices. You start with the basic RPG  standards: warrior, wizard and ranger. Although there are stacks and stacks of fun things to do with each type,it would be nice to see the class choice expand. overall amazing game. would definitely encourage you to pick it up.

Tekken 7, hmm what can i say
pros:
- new characters, + large roster of characters, each is unique and feels different
- the new additional mechanic, Rage drive & Rage Art are a welcome addition and add alot to change the game and make it more tactical and even gives a struggling player the chance to come back
- plenty of unlockable content such as, cinamatics, art and customization pieces for the characters and player information screen
- the game has a splendid online functionality as far as ive experienced regarding the quick and ranked plays
- a decent story (quite short i finished it on 3 hours 27 minutes, on mid difficulty)
- excellent level design, with a fairly large amount of maps for a fighting game boasting 23 different maps
cons:
-the tournament mode is barely playable ive had several sessions in which 8/10 or 12/15 tournaments were bugged out and did not proceed the winners to their next match, or start the next match, or WORSE refused to proceed to the victory screen, after the last match
- the character customization (in my opinion) lacks alot when compared to tekken 6, characters like Kuma and panda barely have ANY customization at all,
- character customization items and pieces can ONLY be unlocked in annoying chests which must be grinded through either tournaments, or treasure mode
- the conenction of blows can sometimes seem very odd, hits that should never have touched you, still connects and you take the full dmg, or characters with skeletons too large for certain combos to properly chain off of(example, katarina's 10 hit combo, vs kuma/panda/gigas/jack7, only goes to 7th hit before she just misses)
- BIGGEST CON, controllers, keyboards w/e you might be using has a tendency to just disconnect and this has a very varied rate of happens, ive had matches with this error 6 times within the 3 rounds, and then played for 6 hours with it not happening, HOWEVER this is the most frustrating thing a player can experience. losing a match due to controller disconnect and its on the games part, ive consulted with other players and they seem to also experience this, even on a brand new controller this will still happen (You have been WARNED!)
however how does the game play out overall,
well its ♥♥♥♥ing awesome, getting into a match with an equal really makes you feel the adrenaline pumping, the level design, with its breakable balconies and floors and walls are so much fun to experience, combos are more fluent than ever and the character seem to react much better to the buttons, with several characters i found myself unleaching a hell of unending blows & kicks.
the tournament mode ( when it works without issues) is a splendid mode that allows for single or double elimination fights which has a prize pool that adds up the higher the amount of players participate, this mode is also the most efficient at grinding the rare loot chests for the customization items.
The amount of unlockable content from previous games such as art and cinmatics is great, its such a funny nostalgia trip to go back to Tekken 3 and watching Yoshimitsus ending xD or art from tekken tag tournament
the achievements are, quite easy to aquire 42 (pre dlc) with all ranking achievements available in offline mode with no pressure to visit ranked, though there are still a couple of online achievements.
I found this game quite alot of fun with new characters to master, great level design, amazing flow of combat and combos it really is quite an excellent fighting game, if not some character currently being a bit overpowered due to certain combos being chainable midair permanently, though its quite few and rare
highly recommand the game and rate it 8/10

Take2 sent a cease and desist letter to OpenIV, the backbone of all singleplayer mods for GTA, under the guise of "protecting multiplayer", saying that there was a mod for OpenIV that affected the multiplayer gamemode. This multiplayer-affecting mod does not exist; the real reason Take 2 wants OpenIV gone is that mods played through OpenIV are the only way to get otherwise multiplayer-exclusive vehicles and other content, and Take 2 wants people to play the multiplayer instead so that they can get more microtransaction revenue. This review stays negative until Take 2 reverses their decision and releases an apology.
I guess, the fact that they've decided to focus on microtransactions instead of single player expansions alone deserves a negative review.

Many great developers and publishers know the value of the modding community to keep games alive and support sales. Steam as a platform was built on this concept. Unfortunately, Take Two Interactive Software Inc. has shown they do not understand this, despite it being the de facto standard in the market for decades.
As such, I would strongly advise against supporting them in any way, and recommend you do not purchase this game.

I started Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons with no expectations in particular and woah was I blown away. Despite it being a fairly short game (about 3 hours) it was a very memorable and unique experience. The story is a simple one: you play as two brothers going on a journey to find medicine for their sick father. Their adventure takes them exploring through Scandinavian style landscapes, through forests, caves and snowy lands, and you will meet creatures and animals of all sorts, both friendly and not so friendly. The emotion and atmosphere in the game is superb.
You can play with both keyboard and game controller, I played using the latter one. In the gameplay itself you take control of both brothers at once using the joysticks and right and left trigger buttons (to interact), and the game has made good use of these mechanics for puzzle- and task solving. It may take some time getting used to, but the learning curve is fair and in most cases you know what you must to do to make progress.
If I were to pick on anything it would be the non-real language they speak. In the beginning it put me off a bit and made some moments seem almost unintentionally comical, but as I played I got used to it. In hindsight I admire that they have conveyed the story of the game so well without a "real" language, and maybe because of it more people can relate to it.
Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons is an amazing game and it kept me excited all the way to the end. If you enjoyed Journey on PS3 you will enjoy this.

I'm conflicted, because this new version of Spelunky is honestly worse than the old one. But that still makes it a damn good game.
A smart and funny roguelike platformer, Spelunky really offers the best in it's class. And in my opinion, it's because of how transparent the game is; you will immediately understand how something works after you see it work. Now, that may mean it just killed you, but no matter. You can try again. Trust me, it wouldn't have been long before you had to, anyway.
It's just a pity to me that this version (Spelunky HD as it was known when in development) has let a few minor flaws slip in. The controls are a little "slidey"-er, without the crisp responses of the original. But only a little! Likewise, some of it's mechanics are a little less clean, with climbing gloves becoming a way to stick yourself to a wall in the midst of danger just a fraction too easily. These are minor weaknesses, but in a game where a tiny mistake can mean instant death, they feel painful.
And, this is just personal opinion, but the art just... Lacks soul. The pixels of the original gave it an 8-bit feel that immediately evoked the legendary platformer about a couple of plumber brothers, then quickly unfolded into Wonder Boy in Monster Land. It was aware of it's primogeniture, but also it's own game. Now, it feels a little sterile. But maybe that's my own nostalgia.
Buy it. You'll love it. I just wish I could say it was as utterly flawless as it used to be.

This is probably the best WW2 game out with a story to tell. BIA HH continues where BIA:EiB left off. This is part 3 of 3
So you have Brothers in Arms Road to Hill 30, Brothers in Arms: Earned in Blood, and Brothers in Arms Hell's Highway. Apparently there is a supposed to be a sequel but It got cancelled or something.
Onto gameplay
The game is a FPS with squad control mechanics. If you played the other BiA you know what Im talking about. You setup your squad behind cover and try to flank the enemy. Only in this game they removed the Health system from the player, instead you have in place a sort of Aggro where when you start to build aggro your screen will turn red and then you will die when it turns too red. The AI do not try to flank you, as you are the one always trying to flank them.
Every now and then the game will zoom into an enemy you killed and show their deaths. eg grenade ripping them apart or a bullet ripping just a corner of the backside of their head. (Note I never saw anything like this in unreal I only ever saw head parts come off or heads explode in other games. Seeing parts of the head get removed instead of the entire thing makes this game unique. UBISOFT really put time and effort into this game.)
The weapons in this game are solid. You get Iron sights when you are not in cover and sadly Over the Shoulder sights when in cover. You can carry only 3 weapons with 1 always being the Colt 45 pistol. The weapons in the game are the MG42(You want to lay the most suppression? This is the gun for you) The M1 carbine, M1 Garand, M1 Thompson, M1928A1  Thompson, Kar43, Kar98, MP40, STG44, Panzerschreck, BAR, and the M3A1 Submachine gun.
On some of the levels you get to control a Sherman Firefly that has an MG and a 75mm cannon.
I just finished this game, I will admit I cried for some of the characters. War is a terrible thing, but this shows what it does to some of the people in it.
I definitely recommend this game.

EARLY ACCESS REVIEW: So, other than optimization issues and bugs (which as anyone on Steam will say always come with early access games), the foundation Rooster Teeth is putting out right now is incredibly solid. Pretty much feels like a complete game so far, that just needs some more content in the long run.
The currently available gamemode is a nice mix of MOBA elements with the typical campaign/story mode system of levels with progressing difficulty, which (at least personally) I haven't really ever seen before in a multiplayer game.
That being said, I have do an issue with the design choice of allowing players to all pick the same character as each other in a game. Forcing players to each pick a different character and switch up their playstyle couldn't be that harsh of a restriction, and honestly could lead to more interesting sessions instead of four Ruby's with dust nukes.
However, if Rooster Teeth does decide to add more characters, I think it would be amazing to not restrict four player teams to only the four characters of a team. Allowing players to mix and match different characters from different teams would create some incredible synergy with all of the combinations people come up with. However, I imagine the work load would be a lot more than just restricting players to a single team for a session, because it would require literally balancing everyone with everyone.
Of course these ideas come from someone who has never actually made a videogame, and are really just things that one person would like to see come along in the game. I could also just be repeating what's already known, so yeah.

This game seems pretty lackluster and I can't recommend it for full price. Maybe at $20 but that's still pushing it.
Pros:
+ fairly well built world
+ good number of little details for world building
+ large open world
+ decent story and characters
Neutral:
- little detail in the world
- most weapons feel extremely similar
- most vehicles feel very similar
- physics aren't very good
Negative:
- progression is slow
- very little depth to characters or world (similar reactions from everyone, AI is pretty bad)
- the grind is fairly bad
- loading times are absolutely horrible, even loading from an SSD
- ONLINE
The online portion of the game (which is being pushed heavily right now), is horrible. There are long loading screens everywhere, trolls who want to do nothing but kill you repeatedly are the main players in lobbies, and hackers are rampant. All of the interesting things they've added in the online mode aren't made available in singleplayer either. The final nail in the coffin for online is that the grind is insane. For example, to gain access to CEO jobs, you need about 3 million dollars. To get that much, you can do heists or jobs which net you very little money and often rely on the good nature of other players for you to succeed. It's a simple case where those who've played more and have better equipment can just stop you from progressing at any sort of meaningful pace. Of course you can just pay huge amounts in the form of microtransactions in order to skip some of the grind.
Something that I bought this game for, which I had hoped would massively improve the quality of the game, was modding. However, with Take Two's current stance on any sort of modding this isn't likely at all. If you want a fun open-world game, I'd recommend any of the Saints Row series or even Watch_Dogs instead. This falls far short of what I'd consider a well made game.

THIS IS A FIRST IMPRESSIONS REVIEW, I MIGHT CHANGE MY MIND
Deus Ex: Mankind Divided is, in my opinion, everything 'next gen' gaming should be. It's dense, detailed, rich and beautiful, with the traditional branching missions and RPG elements of every Deus Ex game. I'm only a couple of hours in, but as soon as I got through the (fairly linear) Dubai tutorial level, I was in Prague, the first hub. This city and its contents is so richly detailed that I spent a sizable chunk of time just exploring Adam Jensen's apartment.
As I'm not far in, I can't comment on the story in detail, but so far, it's been the traditional Deus Ex mix of choice, sidequests, lore text and background conversations/broadcasts making a richly detailed story to be explored. I'm hoping to learn more about how Adam and Sarif survived the events of the last story, and to see if Bob Page is the big bad in this one.
There are issues, though. There's some really weird mouse acceleration shenannigans which I eventually ajusted to (ish) but could quite easily be game-breaking for others, so I hope that's patched ASAP. Also, this sequel adds additional functions, like weapon management and so on, which can lead to keybinds being quite cramped, but a rebind to my DX:HR control scheme fixed that. In addition to this, there are irritating bugs like when fallen enemies clip into objects and can't be moved, or textures on certain items flicker in the inventory, but these are never gamebreaking.
And since it's apparently a big issue, I better mention the microtransactions situation. Basically, you can buy ingame items as overpriced, one time use DLC. Why you'd do that, I don't fhucking know. There's also a 'Shop' button in-game, but that doesn't seem to work for me, it's fairly obvious what it does though. Also, the superfluous Breach challenge maps have Tech Chips or whatever to get upgrades and new weapons, these can be exchanged for real money, again, I don't know why.
It's a real shame this was put in a Deus Ex game, but it remains a choice. The microtransactions are, however, a faster route to items and upgrades which are easily gained in-game. My advice is to not buy them, but don't bother not buying the whole game for that reason. That said, I'd strongly advise SE and Eidos to remove this from the game, or at the very least not put it in any other games.

Kingdoms of Amalur is an interesting game. It seems like the developers of this game wanted to make their own Elder Scrolls game and built it from there. Rudimentary, shallowly implemented elements are present: theft, crime with the bounty system, personal homes you can upgrade and the like. However when it comes down to it the game focuses more on the combat and it does it pretty well.
Considering how much combat makes up these open world types of RPGs that's enough to buoy it to a tentative recommend. Much of the shortcoming of Skyrim and the like is the lackluster combat and this game certainly delivers. Everything else is just good enough to keep the game engaging. It's a fun game, although you can quickly grow overpowered. Worth a look when it's on sale, but I can see why it didn't meet its sales goal by a longshot.

You can also join all the different factions in the game, and even buy titles in some cities.
- Every story and quest is voice acted, and they are fairly good acted as well.
- If you like cartoon-ish graphics, this will be something for you.
- Fast travel between cities and dungeons.
- Maxed level at 40, wich I find good as this will keep the game balanced.
- 3 modes -Casual, Normal and Hard.
- Cool looking weapons and armors.
- You can alter your fate (specs) at any time in this game, just find a fateweaver (icon looks like a deck of cards)
Cons:
- Main quests are done too fast, in my oppinion.
- Sound is/can be buggy during battles and in areas with too many sounds at the same time.
- After a few fights with the different enemies in this game, you quickly learn the way they fight, so they become quite
quite easy to kill.
- Some of the side quest can be repeated, sadly this can be quite annoying as you can´t remove them from your list.
- Only one quest at the time can be marked, shows a yellow ring on the map. The white rings are the other quests.
- The 2 DLC´s are way too easy to complete. A max of 2 hours each.
- Game does not seem to be supported no more.
All in all, this game is a really good single player RPG, and without a doubt worth trying.

There you are, a lowly nobody in the land of Calradia, trying to make a name in one of the capitols of the six kingdoms. Finally you find your path: a merchant who braves the roads, woods and mountains filled with quite the lovely fellows who comment the pleasure of seeing your face (that's a nice head you have on your shoulders).
After many days of abusive fellow travelers, you snap. You decide to become the raider king and surround yourself with fellow men who are very inquisitive about traveler's purses. It goes amazing, robbing peasants and merchants alike, filling your coffers with gold, spices and silks, wine and cabbages. Until they catch up with you. The swadian flatlands were a mistake to raid upon and after charge after charge of swadian knights preceded by the rain of swadian arrows fired from longbows, you are thrown in a cell.
Finally you get out. You change your life and join a king with a small force of peasants. You fight in battles in the name of a true monarch. Your force grows, finally reaching the point where no lord is an actual danger anymore. Finally the recognition you deserve: a title, a fief a wife. Glory, Gold and Power. The next step is becoming the kingdom's marshal. After much lobbying, bribing and plotting, the army is yours to command. The capitols of your kings' enemies will fall.
What now? No reward? No thank you, no fief, no lordship over the grand cities you conquered? You start your own path, you retire from service and declare war on the smallest kingdom left. After taking over a castle, you declare yourself independant and your fellow disgruntled lords flock to your banner. One by one the kingdoms fall, until you stand over the armoured king who once commanded you. Fallen and defeated, he relinquishes his throne to you, all monarchs flee, never to return. The Empire of Calradia has returned and the few obstacles left are no match for the diverse army you now field.
But sometimes, your remember what you used to be. Sometimes you are reminded in a subtle way. Just sometimes you ride around in the most regal armour ever created, with a personal guard of over 200 knights, only to hear that one sentence:
AWAY WITH YOU, VILE BEGGAR!

I'm really enjoying this game so far.
I got this game after watching some gameplay of it, and it plays as well as it looks. I beat the storymode on normal and then I went to practice mode to test each of the characters to find my favourite.
From my testing I feel confident enough to say that this is a fighter that is easy to pick up and relatively quick to master, depending which character you choose to have as your "main" of course. Unlike other fighters it relies less on multi-button presses to execute complicated moves, and focuses more on execution of combos. Of course you can do 10-hit-or-so combos here as well, but they're not as difficult to pull off as in (for example) Guilty Gear. At least in my opinion.
Either way to win in a match you don't necessarily need to be able to remember how to do a 10-hit combo, sometimes a well placed hit or a grab here and there is enough to do the job. I imagine the better you get and the higher rank you obtain the more the game asks of you. I'm not great at this game either, but I can already deliver a good butt-whooping every now and then, and even when I lose it feels fair.
The roster is massive, lots of different playstyles are presented. You can be aggressive, heavy hitting, combo reliant or defensive "poker" - its all there. I'm sure anyone planning on picking up this game will find their favourite character soon after starting, and then its just a matter of time and practice until you git gud.
(I prefer the quick poke or combo reliant characters myself for some odd reason. My brain should starting thinking about maybe liking the heavy hitting not-so-combo-reliant characters more, thank you very much!)
Game's good, and this is a good place to start if you haven't played fighting games before, or it has been a while since you last played one. I will definitely keep playing more myself!

I like this game a lot, you really get the most out of it playing with friends with VOIP though. The developers have been doing some great updates and optimisations lately and I would recommend anyone who likes tactical FPSs to give it a go. If you join one of the public teamspeak servers you should be able to find plenty of friendly clan players to play with and show you the ropes.
H&G has always attracted a lot of complainers, but the fact that the majority of them are still playing the game should tell you all you need to know about that side of the story. The game has asymmetrical balance between factions and this brings about a lot of misunderstanding where people are convinced that one side is OP/unbalanced 'blah blah blah' but I don't think this is the case and the global stats seem to back me up on that. The asymmetrical balance is one of the best things about this game from my perspective; different factions have to employ different strategies and tactics to get the most out of their equipment and assault teams and adjust depending on which other faction they are playing against.
That being said, it takes a bit of investment of time before most people learn the basics and don't feel overwhelmed by more experienced players, though Reto have done a lot to make it a bit less punishing for beginners. I have been playing since alpha as well, so I might have a skewed view of how grindy it is but I have recently levelled up two new characters and didn't find it particularly tedious, now I have an LMG infantryman and a second paratrooper and I have found the time it took to be well worth the payoff, in fact it was probably more rewarding because it took a bit of commitement.
Anyway, it's free, so have a go and see for yourself. I promise to be nice... Mwahahaha >:).

After Angering GTA 5 Fans, Rockstar Releases New Statement On PC Mods [UPDATE]
Rockstar and Take-Two won't take action against single-player mods, but it's not quite that simple.
Update: A new update for OpenIV has now been released, seemingly with Rockstar's blessing. It's unclear what exactly about it has changed to abide by the rules outlined by Rockstar and Take-Two below, but this appears to be a positive move for the modding community.
Original Story: The recent legal shutdown of Grand Theft Auto V mod tool OpenIV angered fans, to say the least. Developer Rockstar Games has now released a new statement addressing its stance on mods, and while there is some good news, it still likely isn't what many people are hoping for.
In a post on its website, Rockstar reveals that it's spoken with its parent company, Take-Two, and convinced it to avoid pursuing legal action against certain types of mods. "Rockstar Games believes in reasonable fan creativity, and, in particular, wants creators to showcase their passion for our games," the statement reads. "After discussions with Take-Two, Take-Two has agreed that it generally will not take legal action against third-party projects involving Rockstar's PC games that are single-player, non-commercial, and respect the intellectual property (IP) rights of third parties."
No Caption Provided
There are, of course, other restrictions as well: "This does not apply to (i) multiplayer or online services; (ii) tools, files, libraries, or functions that could be used to impact multiplayer or online services, or (iii) use or importation of other IP (including other Rockstar IP) in the project," the statement continues. "This is not a license, and it does not constitute endorsement, approval, or authorization of any third-party project. Take-Two reserves the right to object to any third-party project, or to revise, revoke and/or withdraw this statement at any time in their own discretion. This statement does not constitute a waiver of any rights that Take-Two may have with respect to third-party projects."
All of this started when Take-Two issued a cease-and-desist to the developers of OpenIV, which is a tool that is used to power numerous GTA V mods. Take-Two and Rockstar subsequently explained that this wasn't intended to specifically target single-player mods and that "malicious mods that allow harassment of players and interfere with the GTA Online experience for everybody" were the real problem. The companies also said they were investigating how to "continue to support the creative community without negatively impacting our players." Despite this, there was an outcry from fans, who sunk the game's average user review score on Steam. Additionally, a petition calling for OpenIV to be left alone has attracted nearly 77,000 signatures as of this writing.
Today's statement doesn't totally clarify what the future of GTA V mods looks like. OpenIV would seemingly still be disallowed by these rules, despite not directly targeting GTA Online. Rockstar told Motherboard that it's spoken with OpenIV's developer about allowing it to continue, but at this point, it remains unclear where things go from here.
-Gamespot

KoA: TR is a classic action / RPG in the style of Dungeon Seige III.  As such, its appeal is mostly for fans of the console based RPG who enjoy the simplistic interface and sophisticated button mashing combat.  I come strictly from the PC world so I tend to prefer things like Skyrim, Baldur's Gate, and the like.  However this game managed to keep my attention because of its "charm" and great combat.
I assume that you are familiar with the basics of an ARPG title, so I'll skip right to the pros:
> The world is absolutely huge.  I have 40 hours logged so far and have completed about half the game in terms of exploring the map.
> The number of quests and side quests is equally enormous.  Given this, the means for managing them all works quite well... any quest can be designated "primary" and tracked easily through the kingdom.  Secondary quests appear only on the detailed map which shows the immediate area.
> The voice acting is excellent, and ALL NPC dialog is spoken.  I recognized one of the voice actors from Skyrim!  I wouldn't be surprised if there are others from the school of Bethesda.
>  The combat, which is the meat and potatoes of the game really, is fantastic.  This is the primary reason to play this game.  The controls are easy to learn (I recommend an XBOX controller) and the unlocks as you progress are interesting and powerful.
> Although there are basic classes (ranged/mage/tank) the level of customization available allows you to combine classes in interesting ways or focus on a specific branch within the class.
> Crafting is available (create gems/blacksmithing/alchemy)... and exploring any one of those paths yeilds GREAT rewards mid-late game.
> The pacing is excellent, and largely under your control.
> AWESOME support for 3D Vision... you will want to patch the game using helixmods.  Google it.
> Great weapon effects, such as flame, electricity, ice etc.
> The story is interesting.
> The camera is generally well managed by the game, particularly in combat.
> It is possible to completely "respec" your character at any time!
And the CONS:
> Graphically the game reminds me of world of warcraft... rather cartoonish.  Not necessarily a deal killer but I prefer a more realistic look.
> The character animations are limited, in particular when speaking dialog.  You will see the same animations repeated hundreds of times, to the point where you begin to notice them... a bit distracting.
> Occasionally there are some wild camera glitches.
> The difficulty can be uneven, especially early in the game.  You will be sailing along beating up baddies with abandon and then be unable to complete a boss fight without reducing the difficulty.  That seems to be less of a problem by mid-game if you have been managing your build well.
> The loot drops are generally not that interesting... mostly junk, at least by mid-game... although by that time you have a specific build in mind and you are looking for specific loot.  I find that merchants are a better source of loot than drops.
Overall I heartily recommend this game

After Angering GTA 5 Fans, Rockstar Releases New Statement On PC Mods [UPDATE]
Rockstar and Take-Two won't take action against single-player mods, but it's not quite that simple.
Update: A new update for OpenIV has now been released, seemingly with Rockstar's blessing. It's unclear what exactly about it has changed to abide by the rules outlined by Rockstar and Take-Two below, but this appears to be a positive move for the modding community.
Original Story: The recent legal shutdown of Grand Theft Auto V mod tool OpenIV angered fans, to say the least. Developer Rockstar Games has now released a new statement addressing its stance on mods, and while there is some good news, it still likely isn't what many people are hoping for.
In a post on its website, Rockstar reveals that it's spoken with its parent company, Take-Two, and convinced it to avoid pursuing legal action against certain types of mods. "Rockstar Games believes in reasonable fan creativity, and, in particular, wants creators to showcase their passion for our games," the statement reads. "After discussions with Take-Two, Take-Two has agreed that it generally will not take legal action against third-party projects involving Rockstar's PC games that are single-player, non-commercial, and respect the intellectual property (IP) rights of third parties."
No Caption Provided
There are, of course, other restrictions as well: "This does not apply to (i) multiplayer or online services; (ii) tools, files, libraries, or functions that could be used to impact multiplayer or online services, or (iii) use or importation of other IP (including other Rockstar IP) in the project," the statement continues. "This is not a license, and it does not constitute endorsement, approval, or authorization of any third-party project. Take-Two reserves the right to object to any third-party project, or to revise, revoke and/or withdraw this statement at any time in their own discretion. This statement does not constitute a waiver of any rights that Take-Two may have with respect to third-party projects."
All of this started when Take-Two issued a cease-and-desist to the developers of OpenIV, which is a tool that is used to power numerous GTA V mods. Take-Two and Rockstar subsequently explained that this wasn't intended to specifically target single-player mods and that "malicious mods that allow harassment of players and interfere with the GTA Online experience for everybody" were the real problem. The companies also said they were investigating how to "continue to support the creative community without negatively impacting our players." Despite this, there was an outcry from fans, who sunk the game's average user review score on Steam. Additionally, a petition calling for OpenIV to be left alone has attracted nearly 77,000 signatures as of this writing.
Today's statement doesn't totally clarify what the future of GTA V mods looks like. OpenIV would seemingly still be disallowed by these rules, despite not directly targeting GTA Online. Rockstar told Motherboard that it's spoken with OpenIV's developer about allowing it to continue, but at this point, it remains unclear where things go from here.
-Gamespot

The first thing I'll say is, you do not have to be a veteran tekken player to enjoy this game. Whether you are new to Tekken or not, this is certainly a fighting game you will enjoy.  I've played Tekken for years, but was never near that of a professional, however,  I can play Tekken 7 competitively decently. This is now amongst one of my favorite games. The music is amazing, and so are the visuals. The gameplay is highly solid. Some may argue that the game is "broken" due to the strength and fighting style of certain characters, but if you play strategically and study how these characters fight, you will most likely crack their code. So far I find Eddy the hardest to fight. This game introduces the Rage Art mechanic which i have mixed feelings about, but love. I feel Tekken 7 is the most complex fighting game to play. If you're new, don't be overwhealmed. You'll be surprised just how fluid the gameplay is once you play.
Also, the game runs wonderfully. I can't go fullscreen for some reason, but I'm not using the best PC. I'm using a Dell Inspiron 5759. This laptop wasn't necessarily meant for intense gaming. However, on mid to low settings, the game runs beautifully at 720p.
The customization in the game has been dumbed down, though. I feel like that specific part of the game was rushed. There are barely any decent hairstyles.
Also, if you have a PS4, I'd reccomend using that version of the game instead. There's been exclusive content made just for that console. You get it for free, including a jukebox mode which includes all music from the Tekken series.

The main problem here is that, if you're new to the game, you have a monumental ladder to climb to be competitive with existing players. Rockstar, in their infinite wisdom, has put everything behind exorbitantly high pay walls. This is to compel people to buy Shark Cards. Further, they've taken away just about every substantial money making method at low to mid player levels. Yeah, if you're well equipped, you can do Pacific Standard levels, but what if you aren't?
For the last three updates, Rockstar has done about 0 innovation, and instead released new content at gouging in-game prices and playable content can only be done in public sessions with hackers and people geared to the teeth. There's no such thing as ranked matchmaking, so if you're in your teens, be prepared to go up against players with a full arsenal and maxed stats.
So let's say you make the foolish mistake of plunking down $100 for 8 million in-game dollars. What does that get you? Gameplay: there is none. You just read a story. Now that that's out of the way...
"ChuSingura46+1 S" tells the story of a modern-time-boy (naturally, he doesn't have a girlfriend and isn't exactly popular at school) who due to a curse finds himself in Japan during the Edo-era and surrounded by beautiful female samurais. Now he has to find a way back to his time, but the question is - does he really want to?
This VN is fully voiced in Japanese and has English subtitles. The soundtrack is pleasant and the artwork is quite pretty.
However, music and visuals felt a bit redundant at times. Also, whenever there was a close-up of a scene, the picture would be blurry from the zoom. In this regard, ChuSingura lacks a bit in quality.
I still enjoyed every bit of it :D
Initially, I had two reasons for downloading it: 1) it was free and 2) it was tagged as "erotic." But even though I came for the boobies, I stayed for the exciting and touching story, that often had me on the edge of my seat or on the brink of tears. Also, this is the most cinematic VN I've ever read. Most VN could have just been published as images or print as graphic novels and no one would care, but ChuSingura brought out the best of its medium.
Plus the characters are lovely! <3 Hard to pick only one Samuraifu...
Now let's talk about the tag "erotic." In my opinion, there is absolutely nothing erotic about this VN. It's just full of Fan Service. Cleavage, nipples trying to pierce through the clothing and the occassional side bewb. There should be a tag for that certain kind of adult content, because it left the hentai-fans disappointed and just felt like bad advertising.
Then there's the sheer quantity ChuSingura: it took me nearly 12 hours to finish this thing, and I skipped a lot of voice acting because I'm a quick reader (and a horrible listener.)
12 hours of VN.
Does this justify the price? Perhaps.
Do I recommend this VN? Definitely.
But will I really buy the other parts? Totally. But not in the near future ^^' I need a break, mate...

Alright, time to edit ye old review. The first time I did this, I was pretty upset. The game had a disasterous launch on PC if anyone remembers. Since then, some time has passed and, more importantly, some critical patches have come out. Here goes...
First off, I am a fan of the MK series, been playing em since MK3. I think that MKX is a pretty good fighting game. The characters and variations are diverse and interesting. The game, in my opinion, is balanced well. The graphics are great especially in regards to character models and backgrounds. The fighting is fluid and has good animations. The story is serviceable. Its no Mass Effect, but I found it interesting(minus the stupid QTE). People who haven't played MK before should have no trouble understanding whats going on. Besides the story, you got stuff like klassic towers, test your might, etc. The Krypt also makes a comeback if you are into that kinda thing. They made it sorta like a minigame which I found to be ♥♥♥♥ing annoying. You have to run around and solve little puzzles to unlock regions with chests. Summing up, I would give this game an 8/10.
So why do I not recommend it then? ONLINE MULTIPLAYER. Yes ladies and gentlemen, even after all the ♥♥♥♥♥ing and the patching, it still doesn't work properly. The lag simply makes online play impossible. This isn't some 3-5 frame lag like in USF4, your character behaves as if he/she injected 100cc of morphine and is struggling to stay awake. Simple combos that I can pull off with my eyes closed in practice cannot be performed online due to the lag. Multiplayer is such an important thing to get right in a fighting game. If you look at my "time played", 90% of that time I spent in practice/story/towers. The other 10% I was trying my best to play online. This usually defaulted to: play a couple of matches, get♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥at the lag, toss my controller across the room and turn the ♥♥♥♥ing game off. Matches are starting to take longer and longer to find. The rooms are pretty much empty most of the time except for Brazil for some reason.
So basically, unless you want to play against the computer, don't buy this game. As for me, its a little late to get a refund xD. I'm definately not buying anything from Neatherealm on PC again though and same thing goes for those ♥♥♥♥ers at High Voltage.

Kingdoms of Amalur is a single player RPG developed by Big Huge Games with 38 Studios for both Console and the PC. One of the notable personalities involved in its development is former Major League Baseball player and known avid World of Warcraft subscriber Curt Schilling, the founder of 38 Studios.
The game places you in the role of the “Fateless One”, a mysterious character who was recently resurrected back from the dead and discovers a new found power to change destiny itself. Travel the land of Amalur in search of answers on why you were recalled back into the land of the living and at the same time, learn more about a great war in the east against an immortal race called the Tuatha Deohn and why they want you dead...again.
+ Beautiful Graphics, models, animation and special effects
+ Stunning scenery, levels and environment
+ Healthy game time that doesn't get too boring
+ Expansive world which rewards exploration with...
+ Good loot, item and weapon variety
+ Fun combat regardless of the class you're playing
+ Crafting system is deep but easy to understand
+ Class System is VERY extensive (want to make a warhammer wielding wizard that's good with stealth? Then why not? This game lets your cross-class as much as you want.)
+ Good enemy design and variety
+ Lots of fun side quests (Also a CON)
+ Fun and relatively long DLC story (Legend of Dead Kel was fun for me)
+ Nice, straight forward story that is complicated enough to not get boring, but simple enough to follow.
- Way too EASY, even on the hardest difficulty. This is possibly the BIGGEST CON of the game (There is a mod to fix this and I have provided it in the comment section below)
- Player customization is very limited
- Some forgettable npc characters
- Too many side quest (Also a PRO) that levels you up too quickly even before you reach the end of the game, this results in...
- Boredom will set in after max level, specially if you max out before the final stage
- Money becomes irrelevant really quickly
- Generic world and story
- Massive map with NO MOUNT (Jogging Simulator 2011)
It's a NICE RPG game that provides several hours of entertainment. If you have an itch for an MMORPG but can't be bothered with the complications of playing with other people, then this game is right up your alley.
The game boast a very beautiful and colorful art style, enjoyable levels and scenery with a fun combat mechanic. The game play gets boring at times because the difficulty curve is too easy and provides no challenge. It has a big expansive map with lots of places to explore, but gets tedious because of the lack of mount. Still, all in all, I can easily RECOMMEND this game while on sale.  If MMORPG games are Cigarettes, then Kingdoms of Amalur is the Nicotine Patch.

These controls are very much masterable and once you get used to them you can perform all kinds of stuff. It's like saying Toribash has bad controls; it doesn't, it just has unusual controls with a high learning curve. Get past that learning curve and you can do goddamn ninja flips and advanced wrestling moves.
If you're desperately looking at a "simulator" game that will actually keep you entertained for more than five minutes, Surgeon Sim is definitely for you. Unlike a legion of other games in its genre, your actions have consequences on your environment, it doesn't solely rely on the "haha funny physics and dumb controls" joke to carry the humour, and above all else Surgeon Sim has an actual game buried under the madness.

CONS:
[07 / 10] BELIEVABILITY: hit and miss; plenty of absurdity.
[05 / 10] ROMANCE: cut content impacts relationships, IMO.
[02 / 10] TRANSLATION: chapters 4 & 5 were especially bad.
[02 / 10] QC: inconsistencies & typos abound.
[06 / 10] PACING: long bouts of filler at times.
[07 / 10] AUDIO IMBALANCE: you'll be playing w/ options.
[01 / 10] PLAYER INPUT: practically no player choice.
CHAPTER RATINGS:
[10 / 10] CH.1: historical explanations = initially confusing.
[10 / 10] CH.2: super long; battles & plot twists galore!
[09 / 10] CH.3: slow pacing, but awesome climax.
[07 / 10] CH.4: relatively short; excessive history lessons.
[07 / 10] CH.5: slow pacing; weak climax, IMO.
CONCLUSION:
ChuSingura46+1 is a classic masterpiece that will elicit a wide gamut of emotions due to its compelling storytelling and cast. Some of the more significant moments are sometimes expected, but there are many sponateously profound events that will rend even the coldest of hearts, seemingly out of nowhere.
Overall, the overwhelming positives outweigh the negatives, but the subpar translation and cut content is a huge letdown. Regarding the former, the last two chapters especially were negatively impacted by the bad translation to the point that it was intrusive. Regarding the latter, I honestly feel that the sex scenes would have helped cement the romantic relationships as they felt underdeveloped and superficial, IMO. Either way, this game deserved better treatment by the developers, so I am left wondering what this magnificent game could have been in the right hands.
In the end, ChuSingura is a rough ride, but despite its flaws, you'll definitely get your money's worth and enjoyment with the DLC. If you can forgive the translation and bouts of absurdity, I suspect that this game will leave a positively lasting impression for fans of the genre.

There you are, a lowly nobody in the land of Calradia, trying to make a name in one of the capitols of the six kingdoms. Finally you find your path: a merchant who braves the roads, woods and mountains filled with quite the lovely fellows who comment the pleasure of seeing your face (that's a nice head you have on your shoulders).
After many days of abusive fellow travelers, you snap. You decide to become the raider king and surround yourself with fellow men who are very inquisitive about traveler's purses. It goes amazing, robbing peasants and merchants alike, filling your coffers with gold, spices and silks, wine and cabbages. Until they catch up with you. The swadian flatlands were a mistake to raid upon and after charge after charge of swadian knights preceded by the rain of swadian arrows fired from longbows, you are thrown in a cell.
Finally you get out. You change your life and join a king with a small force of peasants. You fight in battles in the name of a true monarch. Your force grows, finally reaching the point where no lord is an actual danger anymore. Finally the recognition you deserve: a title, a fief a wife. Glory, Gold and Power. The next step is becoming the kingdom's marshal. After much lobbying, bribing and plotting, the army is yours to command. The capitols of your kings' enemies will fall.
What now? No reward? No thank you, no fief, no lordship over the grand cities you conquered? You start your own path, you retire from service and declare war on the smallest kingdom left. After taking over a castle, you declare yourself independant and your fellow disgruntled lords flock to your banner. One by one the kingdoms fall, until you stand over the armoured king who once commanded you. Fallen and defeated, he relinquishes his throne to you, all monarchs flee, never to return. The Empire of Calradia has returned and the few obstacles left are no match for the diverse army you now field.
But sometimes, your remember what you used to be. Sometimes you are reminded in a subtle way. Just sometimes you ride around in the most regal armour ever created, with a personal guard of over 200 knights, only to hear that one sentence:
AWAY WITH YOU, VILE BEGGAR!

I love this game. Even though I bought it on special I would have been satisfied had I paid the full price. The South Park humour is awesome. It may be less enjoyable for people who are not familiar with the recent seasons, but I really enjoyed seeing my favorite new characters like PC Principal and Classi.
It's debatable whether the 1st game was more fun, but I seriously don't understand why the user reviews are so mixed. To me this game was even more enjoyable and shows better replay value. There is less variety in the locations to explore and less time spent on side quest, but the main story felt longer and more satisfying  (25h of play for me vs about 18h for the 1st game).
The super-hero theme is well adapted and makes for interesting character building as well as combat. There are more companions to pick with very different personas and sets of skills. The combat is still pretty simple but more strategic with movements and position-specific attacks. The wide variety of combat skills makes for very different gameplays depending on your choices. You eventually learn all the skills, but can only memorize 4 at a time. I especially enjoyed the way you get to pick your gender/race/religion as you progress. These moments are hilarious social satire, but they also give you the opportunity to really create a persona.
South Park games are just fun af. Any small complaints are trumped by the overwhelming fun and hilarity.

At it's current state I cannot recommend the game. It's fun, but has too many issues, a lot of which revolve around it feeling like a bad console port.
My biggest problems:
1. Mouse lag in aiming and menus. It takes a swift movement of the mouse or clicking once or twice to get the mouse moving, which in-game is a problem as enemies will often run up to you before you even get the mouse working. I have tried disabling controller settings and such without any effect, so it's probably a remnant of console porting. PC players prefer the mouse (to keyboard aiming) and they prefer that it works.
2. The map. Dragging on the map to move it should be a thing, edge scrolling seems so very clumsy and since we have a mouse why don't A and D move the view and not the cursor? Console port issue again.
3. Crafting menu/inventory scrolling. Putting the mouse to the bottom or top part scrolls the menu/inventory up or down, most PC mice have an amazing feature for this, it's not exactly revolutionary: the scroll wheel. (The scroll wheel works, but the top/bottom scrolling is also enabled and switching is clunky.) Once more feels like a bad console port.
So clunkiness of UIs and aiming are my biggest issues, I haven't seen many bugs yet.
I can't remember any of these issues in The Stick of Truth.
Personally I don't mind Uplay, but I do understand why it may be an issue to some people, so be aware of that before buying.
(I haven't yet beaten the game, more issues may turn up as I get further.)
This game has potential, if it is made to feel like an actual PC game.

Manos: The Hands of Fate, was a 1966 horror film with a measly budget of 19,000 dollars. The movie bombed at the box office, and was panned by critics (With an average score of an amazing 1.9 out of 10 on IMDB). It is often said that while it is one of the worst horror movies of all time, it is also one of the most famous "B Movies" ever too, along with movies like Plan 9 From Outer Space. Anyways, this game is based on that cult film. In the game, you control a man named Mikey and you go into a spooky mansion named Valley Lodge where weird and strange things occur, leaving your'e family behind. It's a platform game, and while it has some good points, there are some noticible negatives that push this game down quite a bit. Like I said earlier, you control Mikey, platforming through the terrifying 8 stages of horror. But don't you worry! Because Mikey here is prepared with a handgun! This gun is your primary weapon throughout the game, but you can upgrade it to a shotgun to get a triple shot. It's useful, but it goes away if you get hit once, (I hate it when games do that stupid stuff!). You can also optionally collect secret hands throughout the game, this will permanantly increase your health, which is very helpful. The controls for this game are very good, Mikey walks at a brisk pace, stops on a dime when you stop, the jump feels good, and the gun fires as soon as you press the button, or key. The graphics are also pretty good. I like pixelated games, and the graphics are bright and colorful. However, while I like the presentation for the most part, the gameplay is where the game starts to fall apart. The game is of the most simplistic, basic platformers I've ever played, the level design is too basic for my liking, and it's the same basic platforming too. Really, it's either just jump from small block to small block to me, or a stage where there is literally just a single level with maybe some stairs to go up. There is a shooter stage, but I'll get to that in just a second. The music, oh god is it forgettable! It's super quiet and extremely boring too. After playing, I couldn't remember a SINGLE tune in my head, nor would I want too. And finally, the game is super short and ridiculously easy. You want to know how long my playthrough of this game was on the normal setting? 34 minutes, I'm not kidding. The stages go by so quickly and there is literally no challenge in the game. In fact the only difficult thing in this game is when enemies just come out of nowhere, knock you back off a tiny platform, and die. That's not challenge, that's just being annoying and cheap. Remember when I said about the shooting stage? That's also too easy! Just fly in one corner and press the buttion as fast as you can. NOT. CHALLENGING! Keep in mind, there is nothing wrong with making a game easy, but this? This is just too easy, enemies have extremely predictible patterns, and very VERY rarely take two shots to kill. Bosses? Got nothing to say, too easy as well with super easy patterns too. Well, after all that, do I recommend this game? Well, can't you tell? It's a super basic, super easy, and also a super boring game in my opinion. I do know it is on mobile devices, and in that case, it isn't the worst ever, especially considering the quality of some apps out there. But as a PC game? No, this game isn't all that great. I know that it's cheap to buy, but paying 2 dollars for a game that's easy, basic, and super short for PC? There are better games on PC for the same price. If it's 50 cents (like how much it was when I bought it,) That's a complete maybe, but only that. Again, this is my opinion and I will completely respect other's, but in my case. I didn't have much fun with this one, and at it's best, it's mediocre.
Rating: 5/10

In my opinion, Brutal Legend is one of the best video games of all time.  I'd rank it up there alongside Star Control 2: The Ur-Quan Masters.  Similar to Star Control 2, Brutal Legend doesn't really fit into any single genre.  It's not a classic adventure game, although it has some elements of that.  It's not a third-person shooter, although you play in third person.  It's not an open-world game, although you do have the freedom to explore and play side missions.  It's not an RTS, although the big battles involve an RTS-like experience played in third person.
What it IS, however, is AWESOME.
First, if you are at all a fan of heavy metal music, BUY THIS GAME.  The in-game soundtrack features an imperial crapload of awesome metal tunes, all of which you can play (or you can customize your own playlist) while you cruise around the world.  The in-game guitar solos you play are also played by none other than KK Downing and Glenn Tipton (the guitarists for Judas Priest).
The story itself can be played through fairly quickly if you just do nothing but play story missions...but where's the fun in that?  You miss the fun of exploring the world, listening to cool tunes (and finding new ones to listen to within the game world), improving your abilities and gear, etc.  That said, the story is, well, honestly pretty damn good.  Jack Black's voice is oddly appropriate for the character of Eddie, and the game kind of feels like an interactive movie almost.  Not in the sense of cheesy "Full Motion Video!" interactive movie games from the 90s, but rather like you're living inside a world that could be a movie developed by Pixar's metal-head older cousin, who is also steeped in old-school D&D.
The gameplay, on the whole, is a lot of fun.  There are some weak points, though, especially the RTS battles.  They aren't bad, but they feel more like an experiment that turned out "ok."  You command on the ground, rather than the more traditional top-down view.  This makes commanding your troops a bit more hands-on.  You can get in the mix yourself, too, using your combat abilities and guitar solos (which act like powerful spells, basically), but you're also vulnerable to enemy units and your death costs your team resources (you do come back).  It's not a bad part, it's just "ok" and doesn't measure up to the fun of the open world segments.  The side missions can also get repetitive after a while, but if you enjoy them, that's not as big  a deal.  And, of course, if you're not a Jack Black fan...avoid this game like the plague.
Honestly, though, I cannot recommend this game enough.  At $15, the game is well worth it.  If you get it on sale for less, it's even better.  I bought the game originally on Xbox (it plays well with a controller, by the way), and loved it so much I bought it on PC again, and picked up an extra copy to gift to a friend.
10/10 Jack Black

Manos: The Hands of Fate is a game made by the same people who did Angry Video Game Nerd Adventures and it's based on what is regarded as the worst movie of all time.
Manos takes place in a creepy mansion where a family of three meet up with a crazy man named Torgo who is the protector of the mansion and he advises them to stay away, cause the Master will kill them.
The movie in itself is a marvelous joke and it's really funny and I highly suggest getting friends together, getting absolutely wasted and watching it, cause it's a delight.
But enough about the movie and let's get into the game.
The game in itself is alright for the most part. I had a lot of fun revisiting scenes from the movie and the music is a spot on 8 Bit rendition of the music from the film which I though was incredibly impressive.
The game has great graphics and the art style is similar to other games in the 8 Bit genre, it's also really similar to the follow up game by FreakZone which of course is the AVGN game.
Gameplay wise it's a simple platformer where you run and gun enemies, but the fun thing is that you run into other bad movies like Plan 9 from Outer Space and The Giant Claw.
The game is pretty hard, but never impossible, keep playing and you will complete it. Some sections are difficult, but with enough tries you can easily finish the game in an hour, but this game has some replay value like a Hardcore mode and you can play the game again as Torgo after you finish the game with Michael.
The game has a few negatives. The game is really short, as stated before you can finish the game easily in an hour maybe even faster. Also the controls are incredibly slippery and take some time getting used to, but after you find your footing it get's easier.
Overall I enjoyed Manos: The Hands of Fate Director's Cut, but I still suggest watching the movie first (which will be the greatest challenge of all), but since the game is so cheap you can get a pretty decent game on your hands.
Pros:
+ Nails everything about the movie
+ Fun
Cons:
- Short
- Slippery Controls
Final Rating:
7/10

This one's pretty much on the cusp of being recommended.  Two things push it into negative territory: an anti-virus conflict that prevented me from playing for months, and being designed to be annoying.
"MANOS" is both designed as a callback platformer shooter to movie licence NES titles, as well as an homage to the infamous MST3k episode featuring the "film".  The production values and controls are much better than the games it's based on and it's thankfully briefer than the movie.
Unfortunately, the horrible film-grain shadow obstructing your view, the airplane hand of fate, certain checkpoints (namely the nigh-unescapable pentultimate one on the last level) and generally uninteresting bosses aren't enjoyable or even funny, even with a few drinks in you.  Most of the MST3k references and the game in general will sail over most potential buyers' heads, and only the torgo theme stands out amongst the soundtrack.
In short, this is too niche and annoying to recommend.  It's pretty short and easy, but ends up being too similar to what it's mimicking.

Final score: 10/10 "The master would approve!"
