Forged by the former Blizzard developers who brought you Diablo games (none of the former Blizzard North employees worked on Diablo 3, btw) it's hard to not compare the two, especially when you hear that nice and atmospheric soundtrack from Matt Uelmen (who, of course, wrote the soundtracks for the first 2 Diablo games) which will certainly bring back some memories of Sanctuary. Since they are just an indie dev studio now, without WoW-milking Blizzard budget, there's no more shiny things like super-duper CGI cutscenes, but that doesn't take away from its charm.
Besides those mentioned reasons there are some others with Diablo vibe. Former hero who got corrupted, and now poses a threat to the world, while he is traveling across the wooden-snowy/dusty desert/jungly regions (sounds familiar, doesn't it?) in an attempt to free an ancient evil. Of course, you are always behind him, while you are trying to fix things which he messed up, until the final showdown at the end.
Each region has a town which serves as your safe heaven/hub area. There you can trade, use enchanters to boost your equipment, certain specialist who can recover your gems by destroying the equpment or vice versa - destroying gems and freeing the slot to insert better gems to give better stats to your equpment. And there you will get majority of your story related quests. In the town, and in the areas around it, there are folks who can give you bunch of optional quests. You can ignore them completely if you want, but without the experience from their quests it will just be harder for you the further you travel into the game.
You can chose between four classes: Embermage, Engineer, Outlander, and Berserker. Personally, I've found Engineer to be the most versatile, as through investements in his skill tree you can turn it easily into close combat fighting machine or into ranged fighter. Sure, you can do with other classes whatever you want, but Berserker is obviously close combat class, which you can't say for Outlander.
You can also chose a pet, including iconic Half-Life headcrab. Your pet is your shadow, it fights beside you, and also serves as a secondary inventory. You can send it into town to sell whatever you don't need, and also to get the potions/scrolls from your shop list, and in this way you don't have to bother using town portal scrolls or to travel back to do it yourself. Pet can be fed with various kinds of fishes (yes, you can also fish in this game), temporary transforming it into different kind of a beast. And, just as yourself, it can learn spells, making it even more usefull in combat.
There's multiplayer co-op, which requires creating 3rd party Runic account.  Group can contain up to 6 players, although I've never played in a group this large, but more players will certainly help in the hardest modes, especially when you create an hardcore character who's death is permanent (at least pet's death isn't permanent, even in this mode). Speaking of which, you can also share your equipement between your own characters over shared stash in towns, but you can't share between hardcore - non-hardcore characters. As gold and loot flies everywhere just grab anything without any pardon, since every player sees his own loot. Then you can trade with each other, which is usefull for getting rid of certain class exclusive pieces which your current class may not use (unless you are planning to share it with yourself for another character of yours, over previously mentioned shared stash option).
Once you complete the game, you can start the New Game + mode, and continue developing your character. By finishing the game you are also unlocking Mapworks area (also available in NG+), where you can buy dungeon maps with various buffs or nerfs for either yourself or your enemies, and spend the time killing and looting in them to your liking.
If I have to nitpick about something... Those goddamn 4 broken achievements! UARGH, this achievement-hunting junky rash in my hand... Its really lame when you've spent so much time completing everything, including some annoying grindy achivements, and devs are still saying it will be dealth with, even after an year since they originally promissed it will be solved... As you can see, the support of this game is dead, as they are just a small studio which moved all of its manpower to the next big thing. But there's Steam Workshop support, and no lack of quality mods for this game. EDIT: After several years of whining at Runic Steam forums those broken achieves have been finally removed. It was totally worth it...
But if you don't care for such things, the game itself is worth the cost (even with some free quality titles such as Path of Exile, but T2 doesn't have microtransactions like PoE has), especially on the sale, as you can easily squizee at least 20-30 hours of fun from it. Friend of mine who said he got sick of the game has over 20 hours.

If you like RWBY (the show) and you like beat 'em ups, you will probably like this (it's basically a love letter to fans).  If you have no idea what RWBY is, go to YouTube, look up "RWBY Season 1 Episode 1 : Ruby Rose" and start watching
Remember Haloid? Dead Fantasy? Red vs. Blue? The creator(s) of all three of those are behind this series.  It basically runs on the TV Trope "Rule of Cool."  (Yeah, you're now going to spend the rest of your day on TV Tropes.  You're welcome.)
Visuals and Sound:
Gameplay: "FUN BUT BUGGY."  To be expected from a title which has literally been in Early Access for less than two weeks as of this writing.  That being said I'd be remiss in not critiquing this, as that's the point of Early Access -- feedback.
* Lots of invisible walls are frustrating, especially when it's not immediately apparent why you can jump off one ledge, but not off of another ledge which visually looks exactly the same.  @Devs: If you're going to do this, please add some visual aid like a fence to explain why we can't jump off something.  Current invisible wall placements feel arbitrary, especially in The Emerald Forest.
* Left-click combos tend to automatically go into the air after the first couple of clicks, which can be annoying if you intentionally do not want to go into the air and want to stay on the ground and keep slashing.  @Devs: Need more control over combo attack directions.  I mean I wasn't going into this expecting a Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance level of combat complexity but you may want to look at that game for ideas!
* Aiming gun modes (right click) is frustrating as you have seemingly little to no control over where you're aiming and have to have faith in ye gods of autoaim to hit the right target.  Devs: Please, please look at Dark Souls and Metal Gear Rising and Phantasy Star Online for examples on how to do auto-lock-on targeting well.
As this is an Early Access title, this review will be updated after my next RWBY:GE session (especially with the next version).
If you read through all this, please leave a comment! :)

RWBY: Grimm Eclipse turned a week old recently, and I fell in love with the game. Ruby, Weiss, Blake, and Yang are unique from each other, and I love to play as all four huntresses. The soundtrack that plays when playing the game is really good, and the controls are not stiff. I love the gameplay as well, and the teammates you play with are supportive (after all, working as a team is crucial when playing multiplayer). I may love the game, but there are two flaws that makes me cringe a bit. First comes from the lag that may occur if too many things are going around. I am only referring to certain enemy attacks or the loads of enemies that appear when battling, but the rest of the game runs smoothly which I like. Secondly and possibly the most important is the experience players receive when playing online. Artifacts, exp orbs, and wave clearances are fine, but getting exp from Grimm becomes an issue. The exp is given ONLY to the player who finished off the Grimm, and that can be frustrating, especially those who took so long to weaken the enemy and all of that is ruin when someone else takes it out. So why not instead have assist exp for those who help out fighting Grimm a player is having issues with. The person who took it out will get the most experience, but players who helped out can also get experience so it can be fair for everyone. Overall, the game is enjoyable especially with people online, and I bet the team is still creating some new features and fixing bugs and hiccups for the game. I reccomend this game to anyone who loves RWBY and/or hack-and-slash games.

Host method will be the undoing of this game.
What will inevitably cause this game to flop will be the single host method of connectivity. What's the problem with it and what are the alternatives? As most GunZ 1 players know, GunZ was a P2P method of gameplay but it didn't for a long time get anti-lead measures.
As of now, whoever the host is gets extreme priority on hits, and whoever lives closer to the host is the runner up. Meaning that competition will always be tilted in the favor of the host & closer players, aka coast to coast competitions will always be unbalanced.
Futhermore, rather than just having every player connect to one another P2P (not quite sure why not opt for this if you're just going to use a worse and more biased form of this), which would result in equal gameplay between all players, i.e., everyone gets equal priority in games.
Or simply consider measures for setting up dedicated servers & the ability for players to purchase dedicated servers of their own if MAIET doesn't have the money to fund such an endeavor.
While there are some other glaring issues, I believe that the current method of networking will inevitably turn players off from the game, even if its other issues are fixed.
P.S. Have been through T Gunz 2, Eu Gunz 2 and some private servers in between. MAIET has been aware for a while about the inefficiency of the system but has not yet decided to re-work the networking. As the team says their focuses are:
* More new character classes  -- should focus on balance and quality rather than abundance
* More language support (Spanish, Portuguese, and etc..)  -- don't know why this is one of the main focuses...
* More game modes -- could be fun
* More levels (maps) -- this one is a given
* More character customization items (cosmetics) -- don't know why this is a focus right now
* Enhancement on UX (user experience) features -- better late than never
* Stabilizing compatibility and optimization -- too bad fixing the networking isn't part of this

This... is a bit of a complicated title to review on...
Okay, let's start with the mechanics of the series:
-You assume the role of a U.S. Army sergeant
-You have to lead your squad (MG team, assault team, whatever...) through trenches and waves of enemies
-USE TACTICS AND FLANKING POSITIONS (applies mostly to the first two installments of the series)
The mechanics work SIGNIFICANTLY better in this title than its predecessors... the other two, when I played them a few years back, I recall having painfully repetitive, boring, difficult, and frustrating gameplay mechanics.
BUT! that doesn't mean that this installment is none of those things:
-The levels do feel recycled
-Even on the game's hardest difficulty, the game doesn't challenge you at all. In fact, it can be quite boring. There were times where I was hoping for a real challenge, such as playing a level where I would have to use stealth efficiently
-The game restricts gameplay to cover and squad-based FPS mechanics, and tank levels (these I enjoyed, but they don't last long and there are only three).
There is no justification for these main issues, it's simply rushed and poorly managed game design.
The visuals are... well, they vary. There were moments where the game made excellent use of the Unreal Engine's lighting, shadow, and occlusion effects (really really impressive for a 2008 game). However, the textures feel so flat and grainy, and vegetation barely looks passable. Then again, the character models are amazing, the development team really outdid themselves with the main character models.
The story, granted, is really, REALLY slow (boring) and broken at first. But as you further progress, it unfolds into a powerful and emotional story, with quite a few unexpected twists and turns. It's damn near a masterpiece. Hell, it even felt like I was playing scenes from Saving Private Ryan.
Most of the bore from the story came from the questionable voice acting at the beginning of the game... I'm not going to hide this... it was bad. The narrator (protagonist) at first sounded like he was shouting his story at you, and the rest of the characters sounded like really cheesy 90s video game sidekicks. Oh yeah, it's pretty bad. But for some reason, not even an hour after the game, the voice acting and scripting improved incredibly fast.
After that one PAINFUL hour, I really got into learning more about the main character, Matthew Baker, and the challenges he must face on the battlefield. And I have to give the developers credit for a really important aspect of the story's progression: character interaction. For once, in a really long time, I cared about the characters. This one particular scene in the game was so emotional, I actually started tearing up. Damn good job, THAT is proof that the developers cared about their characters. Games need to attribute human feelings to them, and this game is exemplary in that sense.
Overall, the experience I had with playing the game was OK...
Pretty much the only thing that kept me going was the story's progression, I always wanted to know what would happen next. And I genuinely cared about the game's characters.
Had this game not been rushed or simplified, it would've been a fantastic title.
Conclusion:
6.5/10

In my opinion, Brutal Legend is one of the best video games of all time.  I'd rank it up there alongside Star Control 2: The Ur-Quan Masters.  Similar to Star Control 2, Brutal Legend doesn't really fit into any single genre.  It's not a classic adventure game, although it has some elements of that.  It's not a third-person shooter, although you play in third person.  It's not an open-world game, although you do have the freedom to explore and play side missions.  It's not an RTS, although the big battles involve an RTS-like experience played in third person.
What it IS, however, is AWESOME.
First, if you are at all a fan of heavy metal music, BUY THIS GAME.  The in-game soundtrack features an imperial crapload of awesome metal tunes, all of which you can play (or you can customize your own playlist) while you cruise around the world.  The in-game guitar solos you play are also played by none other than KK Downing and Glenn Tipton (the guitarists for Judas Priest).
The story itself can be played through fairly quickly if you just do nothing but play story missions...but where's the fun in that?  You miss the fun of exploring the world, listening to cool tunes (and finding new ones to listen to within the game world), improving your abilities and gear, etc.  That said, the story is, well, honestly pretty damn good.  Jack Black's voice is oddly appropriate for the character of Eddie, and the game kind of feels like an interactive movie almost.  Not in the sense of cheesy "Full Motion Video!" interactive movie games from the 90s, but rather like you're living inside a world that could be a movie developed by Pixar's metal-head older cousin, who is also steeped in old-school D&D.
The gameplay, on the whole, is a lot of fun.  There are some weak points, though, especially the RTS battles.  They aren't bad, but they feel more like an experiment that turned out "ok."  You command on the ground, rather than the more traditional top-down view.  This makes commanding your troops a bit more hands-on.  You can get in the mix yourself, too, using your combat abilities and guitar solos (which act like powerful spells, basically), but you're also vulnerable to enemy units and your death costs your team resources (you do come back).  It's not a bad part, it's just "ok" and doesn't measure up to the fun of the open world segments.  The side missions can also get repetitive after a while, but if you enjoy them, that's not as big  a deal.  And, of course, if you're not a Jack Black fan...avoid this game like the plague.
Honestly, though, I cannot recommend this game enough.  At $15, the game is well worth it.  If you get it on sale for less, it's even better.  I bought the game originally on Xbox (it plays well with a controller, by the way), and loved it so much I bought it on PC again, and picked up an extra copy to gift to a friend.

I will write down this review as accurate and specific as possible, will quote spoilers where applicable.
To give you context as to why I purchased this game, let me tell you that I came across its existence thanks to Mass Effect 3. I purchased the collector's edition and got the Reckoner Knight Armor, this brought me down to downloading the demo for Xbox 360 just about when Mass Effect 3 came out. I played the demo for 1.5 hours. I enjoyed it just as much as I enjoyed playing TES IV: Oblivion for the first time. But I had to play ME3, so I left the demo untouched forever, and said to myself; I will buy this game whenever I get the chance; whenever I have the money, and time to play it.
To make the long story short, I just recently (about 5 months back) became a Steam player, and added the game to my wishlist. It wasn’t until about last week that I bought it. Now let me talk about the game itself.
Oblivion; that was the experience I lived the first 6 hours of gameplay, a vast, open world to explore. There are rich characters, good graphics, gorgeous music, and killer combat and leveling systems. At first it took me some time to adapt to the enemy variety; particularly Boggarts, those slippery things are everywhere. Next was the weapon variety, just like in Oblivion; I found a 'Rusty Iron Longsword' and I won't lie to you, I felt like a god. Feeling that vanished the moment I ran across my first Troll. That fight took me a well invested 10 minutes to finish, I died 4 times before I could put the monster down (normal difficulty). Which brings me to the difficulty system; in normal, this game has its toll, it's not hard, but it certainly isn't easy.
Like I said before, the graphics are average at best for a game that came in 2012, but overall, the world is beautiful. The design is just exquisite, it has a Fable-like yet LOTR-like feel to it. I have been playing for almost 20 hours, and I haven’t even paid attention to the main quest.
I can go on, paragraph after paragraph, but I know that you don’t want to read all that. My final verdict for this game is a well-deserved 8/10. This game gave me the same experience Oblivion did when I first played it. It surely isn’t better than Skyrim in many aspects, but Bethesda wishes they had come up with a leveling and combat system as rich and powerful as Kingdoms of Amalur. The game has its appeal, and in terms of gameplay, it is a strong attempt. This franchise has a bright future, I hope someone with the resources and influence will someday give it a chance.

Spelunky is a hard, unforgiving 2d platformer. It is NOTHING more than that. Don't be fooled by the gameplay videos, like I was. To call this game "rogue-like" is being awfully fu cking generous. Sure, it has perma-death. Is that all that's required to be considered a rogue-like nowadays?
Oh, well it has altars, you might say. Yeah, you have like, 2 minutes to try and use them while you're racing through a level, and the rewards generally are NOT worth the effort.
I was expecting Spelunky to be more of a strategic, adventure game with heavy RPG elements. Spelunky is none of those things. Yes, obviously, skill is required to navigate through each level, but not as much as you might think. Generally you just have to slow down, and meticulously make your way through. That's it. I quickly found myself getting so bored that I started racing through the levels faster and faster, and (obviously) dying more.
More than anything else, Spelunky feels like an arcade platformer, pushing you through the game with its forced time limits. Yes, the ghost that enforces these time limits can be dodged, and is not instantly lethal by any means, but it still forces you along. And there's no reason to linger anyway; yeah, you can "ghost" a level to convert gems into more profitable valuables, but you gather so much gold in the early levels anyway that this is hardly necessary.
There's just not much else here. The extra "characters" are just superficial skins. The "death match" PvP is a frenetic, no-skill, laughable waste of time. Do your homework on this one. Make sure you like the gameplay because this game is basically just a platformer with perma-death.
TL;DR: To call this game "roguelike" is being generous. This is an unforgiving 2d platformer with timed levels that gradually increase in difficulty. That's all.

RWBY: Grimm Eclipse turned a week old recently, and I fell in love with the game. Ruby, Weiss, Blake, and Yang are unique from each other, and I love to play as all four huntresses. The soundtrack that plays when playing the game is really good, and the controls are not stiff. I love the gameplay as well, and the teammates you play with are supportive (after all, working as a team is crucial when playing multiplayer). I may love the game, but there are two flaws that makes me cringe a bit. First comes from the lag that may occur if too many things are going around. I am only referring to certain enemy attacks or the loads of enemies that appear when battling, but the rest of the game runs smoothly which I like. Secondly and possibly the most important is the experience players receive when playing online. Artifacts, exp orbs, and wave clearances are fine, but getting exp from Grimm becomes an issue. The exp is given ONLY to the player who finished off the Grimm, and that can be frustrating, especially those who took so long to weaken the enemy and all of that is ruin when someone else takes it out. So why not instead have assist exp for those who help out fighting Grimm a player is having issues with. The person who took it out will get the most experience, but players who helped out can also get experience so it can be fair for everyone. Overall, the game is enjoyable especially with people online, and I bet the team is still creating some new features and fixing bugs and hiccups for the game. I reccomend this game to anyone who loves RWBY and/or hack-and-slash games.

So I haven't quite finished the game.  It freezes constantly on the second to last mission, and now I've got to go and see if anybody else is having the issue and debug.  In my playtime (you'll get about 15-20 hours of playtime depending on what side-quests you do):
* Multiple crashes
* Bad syncing of the video and audio on some cutscenes
* Maybe 1-2 failures (supposedly the last two missions are much tougher, so I may have died more and this isn't terrible given the game is really for the story)
To start with I loved the stick of truth, and was excited for this game despite the mixed reviews.  Coming from that stance, I am very disappointed.  Even ignoring the multiple problems the game was disappointing.
If I had to pick one word to describe the game it would be repetitive.  You're going to hear the same quips many times, you'll have to do the same QTE many times to solve puzzles,  you'll get to hear quips that make no sense (cartman yelling at call girl that it's coon and friends when this no longer makes sense), the exact same ultimates, and you'll spend a lot of time walking between the fast travel locations.  Some of this existed in the prior game, but it was much less pronounced.  A lot of the jokes fall flat, probably because a lot of the same jokes were done in the first game better (the story of getting your powers was done before in the first game, but instead of telling it showed).
The gameplay was also more repetitive than the first, there's much less different gameplay than SoT.  The battles are fine (ignoring the repetition), and the tactical turn-based combat is acceptable.   It's definitely not deep, but it is a change from the first one.  I'm not sure it really added anything over the original...there's not enough depth for the positioning to matter much (save a couple of special battles)--this leads it to feel different but not necessarily better.
Even to a long-time fan of South Park I have to admit I didn't enjoy the experience here very much.  It neither went crazy enough, nor deep enough to make it sustaining.  Without the zaniness and twists from the first game, it just feels lacking in comparison.

Torchlight II: An amazing ARPG that has made significant improvements over the first, and comes along with strong exploration elements. Also, it has multiplayer, which is great.
If you ever were a fan of the FATE series or the first Torchlight, this is a must. It's overall gameplay is much better than the first Torchlight, but it still keeps the theme.
Combat has been drastically improved. The classes are generally more fun, but a little more unbalanced; the ranged class does very little compared to the berserker, unless you're with a group.
Exploration is the strongest point of this game. The visuals are breathtaking for an overhead ARPG. The environments are huge, and the dungeons are menacing.
The only noticable downside I see in this game is that the first few hours seemed rather dull to me. When I got later into the game, though, it became very interesting.
Also, the environments are static, meaning they aren't procedurally generated. This isn't really a bad thing, it allows for much more detail in the levels, and detail I saw. It just means there isn't as much replay value. So once you beat the game, you might hesitate starting over again.

Man...
I mean there's a lot this game does SO RIGHT...
The controls are better in every way compared to Human Revolution.
There are SO MANY side missions, it's insane, and they're all nicely executed.
The visuals. especially the textures, are simply incredible.
The updated color scheme does fit this title pretty well, though I did prefer HR's.
Hacking is more compelling.
You don't feel punished for either choice of combat (stealth VS direct, lethal VS non-lethal)
The voice acting is superb.
The animations suit the game.
I feel more compelled to fully read emails, ebooks, etc...
Atmosphere is definitely solid, music and all...
Very compelling and difficult choices to make in the main missions.
And of course, the weapon design is fantastic.
HOWEVER, this game suffers from a LOT of issues, and they're not restricted to technical hiccups. Simply put, definitely does not have the charm nor the "OOMF" Human Revolution had.
1)The engine used here, just... blows on PC. Yes, the lighting is fantastic. Yes, the textures are crisp and detailed. But let it be known that this engine just hates Nvidia cards. DX12 is simply an afterthought here. Stutter galore baby. The in-menu benchmark is unreliable. Switched back to DX11 and all of my stuttering was gone,  I only lost 1-2 frames MAX and saw no difference in the visuals. FURTHERMORE, SSS, Chromatic Ab., DOF, and Tesselation effects only seem to apply a disgusting vaseline filter to everything, in addition to making the game run like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. A friend of mine brought over his RX 480 for testing and lo and behold, less problems and stuttering under DX12.
2) The waypoints are unreliable. I activated them for the "Give Me Deus Ex" difficulty and half the time they kept jumping all over the place. Ex: oh gotta head down to my apartme- WAIT why is it pointing me towards a random building? BLEH.
3) AI is both dumb and eagle-eyed.
4) There is ZERO incentive to use any of the extra augments Jensen gets early on throughout the entire game. ZERO.
5) Micro-transactions. Don't care if I didn't use any of the bonuses. They have no business here.
6) To me it felt like there was a serious lack of diversity in locations. I dunno... Prague was the only "HUB" city througout the main game.
7) Buggy all-around. Hell, I know for a fact that a lot of the locked achievements should've been completed. Nope, still locked, don't know why. But the worst of it is when you load a level and a bunch of distorted shapes pop out of nowhere and cover everything but your HUD. This has only happened to me occasionally but enough for me to reload the level.
8) Finally... the ending... I won't spoil anything but what a disappointment. Yes I know Human Revolution cheaped out on that too but this was just... BAD. Simply rushed and unimaginative.
Welp, guess I'll try out the DLCs now.
I have to give this game some tough love.
7.5/10, still fun, does take a few leaps ahead of Human Revolution, but a real disappointment near the end compared to its predecessor.

TLDR – Brutal Legend is a third person hack / slash game with some simple rhythm elements and a sprawling single player campaign. There’s a lot of humor to be found, probably due to the lead character being played by comedian Jack Black. It’s also got a lot of foul language, so be warned if that kind of thing offends your sensibilities (you get the option to add censors).
In the story, you play Eddie Riggs, a heavy metal music “roadie” whose job it is to follow rock stars around fixing things and setting everything up to make the band look awesome while staying out of the spotlight himself. Through a mystical event, you are cast into the distant past (The Age of Metal) ruled by a demon named Doviculus, and inhabited mostly by monstrous creatures. The whole game has a heavy metal music theme, including rock concert battles, playing music to cast spells (kind of like songs in Ocarina of Time), and a lot of cameo appearances by famous rock musicians.
Most of the gameplay is straightforward third person hack slash where you use your trusty axe and just swing until the enemy is dead (you can buy more special attacks later on). You also have a magic guitar to play songs for special effects, and as the story progresses you learn more and more songs to play. You also spend a lot of time driving around the open world in a car that you can summon (one of the first songs you learn). Like with most open world games, this means that the map is filled with optional missions and racing minigames, as well as artifacts that you can find for “fire tributes.” Fire tributes are the “money” of the game, and despite the game playing like an RPG, you don’t level up or get experience when fighting. You acquire the fire tributes and spend them on power ups and cosmetics for your character. One note that I’ll make is that a lot of the purchasable items are unlocked as the main story progresses, so don’t bother doing all the missions and hunting down collectibles too early in the game, since you won’t be able to buy much anyways until later on.
Pros:
+Despite not having the greatest graphics, it is clear that the game developers spent a lot of time on the scenery and overall game world. The main characters may look cartoony, but the otherworldly environment is great. If you’ve played Just Cause 2, you should know what that’s like (gameplay graphics better than cutscene graphics). If you enjoy rock music, you’ll be in for a treat as well. Driving along with the soundtrack is pretty fun.
+The game’s story is engaging and well written. Since the game world is so different from our own, the writers were free to come up with some interesting villains and history. Maybe you don’t like Jack Black’s style of comedy, but I thought it worked well with this particular game. He’s probably better known for childish humor/movies, but Brutal Legend has some mature themes.
Cons:
-As with many games of this type (open-world) there are a huge number of collectibles to be found and if you’re like me you probably don’t want to go out of your way searching for them after the game’s story is over. It turns out that you won’t have enough money to buy all the upgrades unless you hunt down most of the collectibles. There’s no easy way to do it either, even with an online guide because the game’s world map is kind of weak.
-One weird thing I noticed is that the game never actually tells you how to unlock some of these collectibles (using fire spells or thunder clap skills). I had to look it up online. This is a minor gripe though, since most collectibles just give you some fire tributes to spend. I was able to beat the game my first playthrough without buying much. The majority of purchasable items are cosmetic.
Overall, if you liked action adventure games such as Darksiders, but thought they would be better with more humor and less hardcore fighting, you may enjoy Brutal Legend. The game doesn’t take itself seriously, and the silly ways that rock music is woven into the story/gameplay will likely bring an occasional smile to your face.

This is a pretty enjoyable, albeit simple, puzzle platformer.  You control two brothers simultaneously in order to get through the game; the older brother uses WASD + Space bar, the younger uses directional arrows + Right Ctrl. An odd side-effect I noticed of this system was I found myself actually trying to keep both brothers relatively close together throughout most of the game, and I felt generally more connected with both characters at once.
The story is simple but solidly delivered despite the lack of intelligible dialogue.  The characters use hand gestures and a SIm-esque language to describe scenes and lay out the puzzle.  It's pretty effective and doesn't feel cheap or overly obvious.
Overall, this game about brothers adventuring to save their dying father is touching, easy to pick up and put down, and pretty to look at (especially the snowy/icy areas).  Hats off, devs! :)

"Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons" is a great experience with some interesting puzzle mechanics and a touching story.
The games mechanics are based around the idea of "singleplayer coop", meaning that you control two characters (The titular brothers) at the same time in order to solve puzzles. This game does require a controller due to these mechanics.
The controls themselves are quite simple, with each brother using an analog stick for movement and a trigger for interacting with the world. The left and right bumpers are used to rotate the camera.
The games puzzles are not incredible difficult, most of them are quite straight forward, but several of them required me to stop and think for a while. This was in part due to the lack of clarity in regards to what the brothers could or couldn't interact with.
Visually, the game isn't incredible, but it does feature a great art style, which really fits the tone of the game. You will venture to several different environments, each with a unique atmosphere.
"Brothers" has a simple, yet touching story about two brothers going on a journey to help their father. I won't spoil anything, but the story takes you through some really well designed landscapes. While it is quite short, it is a great experience with a lot of emotion bottled up in the 3 hours it took to finish.
"Brothers" does a good job of conveying emotion and story despite all the characters speaking gibberish. While you can't understand the words the characters are saying, their tone of voice and body language make it easy to understand what they mean.
Speaking of body language, the animation work is great. While the animations are quite simple, they do a great job of conveying emotion and intent when the characters speak.
In conclusion, I highly recommend this game if you want to experience a touching story with some interesting mechanics and great environmental design. If you're looking for something action-packed, this may not be the game for you.

I spent the first ten minutes feeling that Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons was too game-y, that the mechanics were blatant enough to ruin any attempt at atmosphere. That faded about twenty minutes in, by which point the lil' Simlish-speaking brothers were growing near and dear to me, and I felt invested in seeing them through on their adventure. An hour in and the world was charming, kind of like the immersive Scandinavian fantasy realm Skyrim wishes it could offer. An hour and a half, and the charm was struck through with bits and pieces of horror and concern. By the time I finished I was pretty much a screaming, teary-eyed emotional wreck.
Bear in mind that the game's content struck very close to home for me, and I imagine that fact is magnifying the impact tremendously, but even so I adore everything that's been put together here. I've been a fan of Thatgamecompany's work for years, and Starbreeze Studios' Brothers manages to evoke everything Flower or Journey pulled off, but in a dark and haunted way that feels just right for the Scandinavian indie game scene. Do yourself a favor and set aside a good 3-4 hour block so you can enjoy Brothers all in one go.

Tekken never fails to impress and Tekken 7 is no exception! I've been a fan of Tekken since I played Tekken 3 in arcades back in 96'. Tekken 7 continues to build on the various fighters' styles/attacks and the overall evolution of Tekken gameplay. There's nothing in this game that stands out as "Amazing" compared to previous Tekken games but, who cares--we have Tekken on PC now and the net code is great (compared to other fighting games on Steam).
Tekken 7 provides a smooth fighting experience. Like all Tekken games, it’s easy to get started but, difficult to master. As with each new Tekken release, the controls feel smoother and more responsive than the previous title. Tekken 7 has a HUGE roster and grinding to unlock fighters was done away with so you can use every fighter from the start!
The Tekken 7 story-mode is a bit over-the-top but, it did have its amusing moments. Some reviewers have down-voted Tekken 7 because the story-mode is "Too Short." My advice is to increase the game's difficulty if you want more out of story-mode--this is a fighting game not an RPG. Besides, in comparison to other Tekken games' story-modes, Tekken 7 offers a HUGE improvement with an expanded story that takes advantage of modern hardware/software by building in entire scenes/in-game mini-movies instead of the still pictures with text we had in the previous titles.
Positives:
-Excellent graphics
-Smooth Gameplay
-Huge Roster
-Great Net Code
-No Grinding to Unlock Fighters
-Bigger/Better Story-Mode
-Next Evolution of Tekken Gameplay
-Works perfect w/ mainstream controllers, fight-pads and fight-sticks
-Tekken on PC!
The only 3 detractors I've come across are:
-Rage Art
-Online Cheaters
-Long Loads
Rage Art abilities are extremely punishing dealing roughly 30% of your opponent’s HP! Rage Art becomes available on characters when they fall to about 10% HP. Executing Rage Art is easy--press R1. Rage Art can also be used in conjunction with other combos; plug it in wherever you like. Although Rage Art may be easy to execute, a proper execution is difficult. An experienced player can interrupt or side step Rage Art and it can be shut down completely by juggling an opponent or suppressing him/her against a wall until HP is at ZERO. Even so, Rage Art can be frustrating for returning Tekken players until they get the hang of shutting it down. It may also be frustrating for new Tekken players but, probably less so because new players shouldn't have the same preconceived ideas of gameplay as Tekken vets.
The MP cheaters are annoying. Some cheaters are using a mod that displays character hitboxes  and others simply don't take any damage or have endless health pools. I get around this by NOT playing online MP--I mostly play against my buddies IRL. Besides, it's more fun to kick your buddy's♥♥♥♥♥when he/she is sitting next to you on the couch than it is to win an online battle against some random person. Also, keep in mind that the majority of players ARE NOT cheating. You can play dozens of games before you run into someone who lands every attack and takes ZERO damage (even from attacks they didn’t block). However, when you do run into that person it really breaks the game’s immersion (at least for me).
Long loads are super annoying in general but even worse when playing online MP. I have Tekken 7 on 2 SSD in RAID 0 and even I think the load times are disgusting. However, there’s a faster load mod and EVERYONE who plays Tekken 7 online MP should download it. You can also see the hitbox hack in this video:
That’s my Tekken 7 review (for now). If you have any questions feel free to ask in the comments section. Oh… and don’t worry about my time played. I’ve been playing mostly with my next door neighbor doing versus battles together on his Big Screen (and his Steam account) which, is far superior to my little 25” 1080p screen.
ALSO, check out my profile for instructions on how to play Tekken 1-6 on PC (includes Tekken Tag Tournament). This means you'll be able to play every Tekken (aside from TTT2) on PC!

Do you love MST3K? Of course you do, that's why you're here. Let's be honest for a minute; there is nothing groundbreaking about this game. It is a standard sidescrolling platform shooter. But ya see, that's the very thing that makes it beautiful. If you yearn for the good-ole-days of gaming where all you needed was a glass of sweet tea, your faithful NES Advantage controller, and a weekend to play your newest rental from Blockbuster... then you should really do yourself a favor and pick up this game. There are plenty of in-jokes from the MST3K series to make you chuckle, the gameplay is solid and straight to the point, the music is beautifully rendered, and the achievements will keep you playing. The game is a bit short, but many were from the era that this game faithfully emulates. It does, however, have replay value. If you liked the Manos episode of MST3K, or NES era sidescrollers, then you will enjoy this game.

Not only is it a good game for fans of the legendary (For all the wrong reasons) Manos:The Hands Of Fate. But also, of all the games that try to be old school NES games... this is the closest one come to actually feeling like you're legit playing an old school Nintendo game as opposed to a mindless meme fest with levels ripped from Mega Man and Castlevania.

MANOS: The Hands of Fate - Director's Cut is a very short and frustrating game. Set in a retro horror world with an NES homage, you control Mike and play through the game Super Mario style. Be prepared for some anger-inducing, blood-pressure-raising moments, especially on higher levels of difficulty.
I've played my fair share of difficult indie platformers so i'm trying my best to separate the justified and unjustified rage-quits. Of course there will be times when you see that flying UFO, but forget that it was coming and reacted too late. Or the times when the swinging spikes just happen to clip you mid-jump. This is all normal in a challenging platformer. The issue comes with respawn locations, poor enemy placement, or poor design choices. For example, one respawn left me on the last (elevator) level on a single-block ledge with two flying eyeballs almost instantly bumping me off seconds upon revival. Another time, a creature bugged out on the stairs leading downwards, getting stuck in my path. Not able to kill him, i tried to jump over him which ended up killing me because i was not in direct contact with the stairs, causing me to touch the bottom frame of the game.....Dying too many times will reset your score and force you to replay the entire level, reliving through the terrible situations previously dealt with.
I actually like MANOS for the most part as it was more fun than aggravating; however, due to a couple bugs and really poor design choices, i really can't advise getting this game at the moment. If patched or fixed, I would definitely recommend this game as the retro style adaptation added a nice flair setting it apart from the common crowd of indie platformers out there.

This is one of those games that you either love or hate.  Gameplay-wise, it's quite reminiscent of the Elder Scrolls series with a Fable style feel to the graphics.  Yeah, the landscapes and denizens are remarkably clean for an agrarian based society and it's a pig to mod but there's something inherently fun about running around a huge, open landscape weilding weapons that, in many cases, are bigger than you are.
As a lower level character there are plenty of loot drops to enable you to afford the healing, training and equipment that you're going to need to progress through the game and the merchants have unlimited funds to buy the plethora of weapons, armour and potions that are simply beneath you to use.  The real challenge is in levelling your character to the point where the abilities and skills you choose complement your gameplay style rather than feel like an adjunct.  The ability to visit a fateweaver and pay them to be able to reset all your skill & ability points is a plus...if you're unhappy with the skill trees you've chosen or if they're just not working for you...change 'em.  It's all about experimenting to find the style of combat (might, finesse, sorcery or a mixture of two or all three) that provides you with the most enjoyable playing experience.
There are plenty of dialogue options that allow you to choose the essential nature of your character...good, evil or indifferent although the opportunites to be a really nasty Dark Lord style world destroyer are too few and far between for my liking...what's the point of making a pact with a Niskaru Lord when it doesn't give you any visible benefits other than having Warsworn mercenaries trying to kill you at every turn?
The world itself is open - always a plus - and the addition of the two DLCs will allow you to run around like a headless chicken for weeks, slaughtering anything you come across that's weaker than you and getting squashed like a bug by trolls and niskaru...at least until you've got to level 20 or above at which point, you'll want to move to hard difficulty if you haven't already because it starts to get a little too easy.
Side quests are plentiful and, in many cases, are more fun than the main mission.  Plenty of faction quests too, most of which are advanced tutorials in the different styles of gameplay and the careful choice of abilities & skills which is where a visit to the fateweaver to change your point allocations is a must.
All in all this game is fun to play and is one you can happily drop for a couple of weeks and then come back to without having to remember how to play it again.  It's challenging enough to keep you engrossed yet not difficult enough to be frustrating and the control and combat systems are simple to understand and use.  Voice acting is good, graphics are bright, colourful and well rendered and, despite some truly ugly or stupid looking armour sets there's not really anything negative to say about this game.  Buy it, play it, enjoy it...but tackle the DLCs
you finish the main game - you'll need a higher level character to stay alive.

TL;DR
I would not buy this game if I hadn't already.  But I would advise people playing it.  Make of that what you will.  Simply because of the creators who actually put their heart into aspects of this game and because of modders who really make it shine; this is a fun game to play and worth the time.  It is NOT worth ANY money.
"But why?"  You might ask.  The extremely long rant to follow are *some* (not all, I am just tired of writing) my reasons:
This is a love hate thing with the Sims 3.  I was so addicted to Sims 2 I lost whole days sitting in front of my computer planning out their day to day routines and hoping that they actually did well.  (I know a lot of simmers just want the absolutely worst outcomes and love either killing and/or torturing their poor Sims)
But this game changed that a little.  I still don't have a bunch of murder, sex or terror mods that make their lives truly miserable, but I don't care near as much for the characters I make or choose to play, I don't have much of a connection to them and sometimes I just stop caring and walk away leaving them to do their own thing until I just save and exit.  Sims 3 lost a lot of charm Sims 2 had and honestly, I blame this entirely on EA's way of thinking which seriously tanked in the customer help department about the same time.  It also began to be called the worst company every year and so on and so on.  The game is pushed more and more for microtransations and not much else now.  Especially with the upcoming Sims 4.
Microtransactions are a good thing, do not get me wrong please.  These are very small purchases someone can make with real money online to pay for all different types of digital goodies to use in game.  For most things this is a term MMORPGs use and they sell cosmetic things.  Outfits, pets, mounts, hair, etc. etc.
With games like Team Fortress 2 this has not only kept the game alive, but brought forth an entirely new type of community where artists and creators come together to make outstanding creations which the community can then vote on and the original creators can make real money from their serious effort and hard work; hand in hand with the original game's creators to make something entirely new.  This idea has even started to be embraced by MMORPGs such as EQ2 which now has their own type of workshop where players can now create things for that game.  It goes on and on and on how awesome microtransactions can be for a game, bring it back to life and keep it ticking with new content and eye candy for everyone.   It's even been how some companies now fund the next expansion, start new servers or how they are able to further polish their games.
Sims 3 though went and tore this concept apart (as far as I am concerned) and with Sim Points introduced a new low in this field.  Sim points are nothing new, the way they are handled in Sims 3 though is.  If you want to buy a certain type of object that has new animations and/or has an actual use in the game that would change it at all; then you cannot just buy that item but actually have to spend more money than you would just buying a stuff pack alone.  These things are usually leaning towards harassing the player even in their game to buy the items.  Everything with Sims 3 is an add to buy something else in Sims 3 and it never stops even when the player is playing.  You can turn these options off but let's look at the key point for EA: Sell items to little girls playing.  Mostly these little girls do not understand the value of a dollar, do not understand what EA is about or how little they could care.  I'm not saying a lot of companis are bleeding hearts but it's more than obvious that EA takes the cake when it comes to giving their customers the finger.
On top of all of this, there are the bug and game stopping glitches.  I want to state first of all, ALL GAMES WILL HAVE BUGS AND GLITCHES ALL OF THE TIME ON ANY CONSOLE OR PC NO MATTER WHAT.  Even Mario still has glitches!  It doesn't matter, games cannot be 100% polished at all times, it is not possible.  But game breaking glitches that either force the player to stop playing, do not allow the player to continue to play or break the game entirely, ruin the save or even break itself; are out of the question!  Especially for such a large company!  Every time a Stuff or Expansion pac has come out, there is always a game breaking glitch that does one or more of these things.
Late Night is a great example.  Mysteriously players suddenly had a horrible time trying to please or even sometimes control their Sims.  Sims would be unhappy no matter what the players did.  They would stay bright red day and night, become incresibly ticked off at all times, divorce one another without the player being able to stop it, kids would be taken away.  No one knew what was happening or how to stop it.  As it turns out, it was the beds.  For some unknown reason beds weren't working correctly in games.  They would cause the characters to become more and more upset until someone finally made a mod fixing this glitch.  The game breaking glitch was fixed well *after* Christmas, months after the game came out and the glitch was made aware by players on the forums of Sims 3.  Simply because the game wasn't tested enough nor were the customers heard.
Game breaking glitches and huge annoyances adding to lag and unplayable situations are still in the game today even though Sims 4 has been announced and you can even pre-order it though they only have a handful of screenshots and a video that they have also stated will change.
They make it so obvious that everything is only about money that they forgot the simple truth.  This is a game for kids and adults alike.  This is a learning machine for everyone and a fun experience to boot.  I would suggest playing the game.  With the right mods (Google NRAA Sims 3) this game is really fun.  It is very time consuming and if you are willing to face a serious challenge, (unless you don't want that you can always mod it too!) at least with your time, than I would suggest this.  It is a LOT easier than Sims 2, make of that what you will (if you played).  You do not need to know anything at all about Sims 2 to play this either which is another plus.  Although the cow plant is brought back and I adored that as well.  Yes it still eats Simmies.  Sims 2 was a huge challenge money and happiness wise, this is more of a "how much time are you willing to sit and grab achievements online, skill up, etc." type of thing.

The game looks great (very cute), the combat/exploration is OK (quite fun) but the design is nonexistant.
This is where Portal Knights fails hard. A game needs to engage the player so that they want to keep discovering new things, craft new powerful items and found mighty spells. However, Portal Knights does nothing of the sort.
To give you an idea, let's talk about itemization: extremely simple. All swords are the same with a different damage value. Just upgrade your tier, keep farming, get the next tier, and keep repeating for hours. Weapon/armor modifiers are irrelevant. What about enemies? "Slow-moving turrets" with a single easy spell or melee, except that some may one-hit you and others will be harmless. To top it off, some of the midly interesting mechanics are irrelevant if you have a ranged attack. Worlds are beautifully themed, but there is no real motivation to come back or fight a boss again. Drops are always predictable and uninteresting, even from secret chests!
The game could be interesting with some heavy redesign of its gameplay systems, keeping the graphics, but right now it is 4 hours of content and then repetition without no goals nor rewards. It feels like a showcase game for an engine, rather than a game in itself.
On the technical side, the game works fine (including multiplayer, no major bugs found). However, note that the performance is not great (even in Small worlds), so many people (like kids with low-end laptops) will have to disable most of the effects/details.

Oh boy. I've owned Portal Knights since it's Early Access days, and let me tell you about this game and it's wonderful developers. This is probably the only EA title where I don't feel like I wasted my money, the devs have always done a great job of smashing the few bugs that existed, and they've also kept the community informed throughout the entire process. The game's quirky art style is also a lot of fun, and the game has just enough a story to make you understand why you're in this world, but gives you enough free-reign that you can really do whatever you like with the game. I do have a few qualms with the game, for instance because the game doesn't have a matchmaker, if you don't have any friends who play the game you have to solo it (which isn't bad, but sometimes you just want to play with other people) and also, the worlds that are often prime base-building worlds don't have NPCs, so it's just you and maybe some friends in this giant castle by yourselves. That being said, this games pros heavily outweigh the cons. It's got a cute, quirky art-style, the game is neither too hard nor too easy, and I can definitely see it going somewhere in the future, and developing a good fanbase :) I can't really say 'if you've played this game before, you'll like portal knights' because well, the game isn't really like one game. It's got the freedom and base-building of minecraft, the quirkiness of games like animal crossing, and an art style that looks like a modern wind-waker. If you do enjoy base-building games, give this one a try :)

Im a realist plain and simple. You can do anything you want with this review, even wipe your♥♥♥♥♥with it for all I care.
The game is free to play (awesome) the graphics are pretty damn good for a F2P game.
The game introduces all types of troops to play (Infantry, Recon, Paratrooper, Tankman, Fighter Pilots) (Stated in the game description)
The game has three factions (US, Soviet Union, Germany) with varying guns, equipment, and vehicles for each side. Sides have their weaknesses and strengths in areas...it evens out for the most part though!
Equipment modifications (ammo type, trigger hairs, barrels, springs, sights) that can increase a weapons effectiveness such as accuracy, damage, and range.
Tankman details: There are 4 armor classes in this game; Light Armor, Medium Armor, Heavy Armor, Tank Destroyers. Each group has seemingly cool tanks with varying side gunner seats with MG's or even secondary cannons.
The maps...the maps are incredibly huge (I mean it) that consist of buildings scattered along paths, with a big town in the center of the map (mostly).
The realistics of the game: Bullet drop/travel, Stamina bar, Grenades seem a bit more realistic to me (big radius), Weak and strong points of armor on the tanks, Fighter planes seem realistic (HE bomb dropping & geometry), For the most part it can take 1-3 (maybe 4) rounds to drop a guy. There are RESOURCES, meaning that everyone has a limited supply of tanks, fighter planes, paraplanes, and infantry (lives really). The game can be won either by capturing key points or lines OR by destroying the enemy completely. It just depends on how long the game goes.
For some negative reviews that I see about 'campers'. Its a realistic game, this isn't really a game for 'COD Warriors'. Running in the same direction that you previously got sniped in is the definition of insanity...doing the same thing and expecting different results. It's a game that requires a little bit of tactics and/or even communicating with your team. Rambos don't get far.
For the reviews saying its a pay to win game. Everything is available to you by earning credits. Everything. You can even buy the 'Veteran Membership' with credits. People can buy stuff with real money, but they must unlock the items first (paying for each little ribbon completion is expensive as hell). This game is nowhere near pay to win.
For the reviews saying it takes forever to purchase things. It really doesn't take forever. You are paid on an hourly salary(not including getting paid for your score after the game). The more you level up your soldier, the higher his salary is which means more money rolling in quicker. If you are looking to make credits extremely quick. Buy a fighter pilot, learn to fly and shoot well. You will be leaving with a lot of credits as your score will always be in the thousands every game. 262 hours when I wrote this review. I have all US type soldiers. Infantry with ALL weaps. I have a paratrooper, Recon with fully upgraded sniper rifle (most expensive class AND weapon), Tankman with best Light Armor, and a Major level pilot.
That is my review. Do with it what you please. Beyond amazing game for a F2P.
P.S. If you plan on playing. Do your TEAM a favor and get on the objective points to capture or defend, every body counts. Dont slap on a red headband. Dont wander through the forest. :)

When I started this game, I figured it would be a nice little platformer. Sure, the knock back was beyond even what Castlevania made you work with, but hey, I could deal with it. That is, of course, until I reached the auto-scroller that obscured your vision... then the knock back became a major issue.
Speaking of auto-scrolling, I assumed that the first one would also be the last; you know, just toss in that old convention of the platformer needing at least one of them. I could deal again, I personally don't like them, but I assumed I had gotten the worst out the way, or at least half of it, since sometimes they toss in a second one just to remind you that this is an NES style platformer. Boy was I wrong, as the last half of the game is almost nothing BUT vision obscured auto-scrollers!
So now that the fun had been completely sucked out of the game, I reached the vertical auto-scroller pulled straight out of Castlevania III... except, again, with obscured vision, because that never gets old, right? Only it came complete with checkpoints that were designed in such a way that enemy spawns could kill you within two seconds of your own spawn for that authentic controller snapping frustration of losing your last life by getting knocked off a small platform by a giant eyeball within a second of respawning.
This game falls under Nintendo hard to be sure, but such a thing is divided into two camps; cheap and an actual, well constructed challenge. When I die, I feel like it's not because I lack skill but because I was cheated: the knock back, the fact that I cannot see anything while the screen pushes me along, the blunt and forced memorization in order to get anywhere in half of the game, all of the slam head into brick wall until it gives tactics are in full force in this game. While this may appeal to some, or perhaps many, it doesn't do a thing for me.

Different, but not bad.
The original Gunz was one of my favorite games of all time. One of the only reasons I quit playing it was due to some pretty bad carpal tunnel. I remember making myself learn to K-Style and D-Style. I remember going naked so I could carry 2 rocket launchers and lol spam rockets in death matches while flying off the walls. Gunz was a great time with an extremely high skillcap. So how does Gunz 2 match up?
The first thing I noticed was the movement. Although individual character movement seems slowed down the feel of combat is still extremely fast paced. You can no longer keep dashing into a wall to keep yourself afloat and dashing is much slower in this game with more time in between each dash. I remember being to dash 2-3 times in a single jump in Gunz 1, where in this I might get 2 sometimes.
The most obvious and controversal thing is the removal of K-Style. People who couldnt learn K-Style complained about it being a glitch and not suppose to be in the game. People that did learn found it to be a fundamental aspect of what made Gunz, Gunz. While K-Style is gone the overall idea of it still exists. K-Style was used because it was the ultimate offensive and defensive playstyle. You basically were a constant moving target that could not only defend but also attack very quickly with your sword. It essentially covered all your bases.
You can still block and move in Gunz 2 but not at the speed you used to. Also attacks are now comboed so you can not constantly butterfly to attack.
I will now explain the 2 main gameplay changes that seem to seperate it from Gunz 1.
First is that in Gunz 1, the sword was the main weapon. It did everything except attack at range. I've done and seen people kill multiple people just by butterflying even when they used guns. In Gunz 2 there is an increase movement to using ranged weapons. Your melee weapon is great when the enemy gets close, but anything outside sweep range you are basically wanting to stick to your guns.
Second is the more emphasis on team play. Gunz 1 was more about who had the best player. A single elite player could take on a team of 4 by himself in Gunz 1. This is no longer as easy in Gunz 2. The class system also further emphasizes it. I found the class system to be interesting and similar to TF2 in that basically every class has a counter.
Classes:
The Silent Avenger is basically your extreme range and extreme close range specialist. Their weapons are swords, SMG's, and Sniper Rifles. They are great at really far range sniping and when they get in close their SMG's and swords make quick work of enemies. They are not great at medium range or groups and their counter is the Gunslinger because she can basically defeat him at any range outside extreme close and extreme range.
The Shadow Dancer reminds me of the closest thing to Gunz other than the Silent Avenger. Quick and fast, she specializes on killing enemies that don't see her and is amazing against 1v1. A good tactical Shadow Dancer can take on multiple enemies quite easily with her decoy skill however. Her counter is the Silent Avenger. Better at ranged combat and having just as good melee, she has a hard time against SA's.
The Gunslinger is your ranged class obviously. Her Assault Rifle does great damage at medium range and her grenade launcher is the only current indirect weapon, meaning you can lob it around corners and other places too set up traps. She excels at ranged combat and against groups however she is poor 1v1 and at close range the high rate of fire of the SD and SA's weapons makes mincemeat of her. Her counter is the Shadow Dancer because she can easily get within the GS's range and jungle her to her doom.
Finally is the Shield Trooper. He is like the Heavy from TF2. He is amazing at close/medium range thanks to her Minigun and Flamer. He also excels at fighting groups. Where the gunslinger is better at medium/long-indirect fire, the Shield Trooper is better at Close-Medium range gun damage. He is kind of a wild card in terms of counters. He can easily get beat medium range against Gunslingers, but if he gets in range, youre boned. SD's can dash around him all they want but his health and no juggle make him hard to kill. SA's can snipe him, but if he gets close,, again, its a bad thing. Basically all classes counter him and he counters all classes.
Overall the gameplay reminds me of Gunz 1 with just a different feeling. It is without a doubt extremely fun. There wasn't a moment in the couple hours I've played so far that I was bored. The best way I can explain it is like Resident Evil series going from 3 to 4. 4 turned the game into more action oriented, but it wasn't a bad thing, it was quite good. It didn't feel like Resident Evil, but it was a fun game in it's own right. Gunz 2 doesn't quite feel like Gunz 1, but I think it will be a great game and I can already see people coming up with new techniques for it.

First off, yes, the in-game store is completely un-needed and the fact that the DLC is only usable per one save each is a little sketchy. Personally, however, I do not have an issue with any of this in the grand scheme of things. No, I do not like the store, but why should I worry about that when I am not even going to use it? And yes, the one save DLC is annoying, but am I planning on playing the game twice? Personally, no I am not.
So, looking past the store and DLC issue, the game is amazing. I have no graphics or optimization issues, which I know is not the same for everyone else. However, the story so far is amazing, obviously I do not have a ton of playtime, but I am already wrapped into the story. It is complex, overcasting, and provides an amazing backdrop for the gameplay.
Other than the fact that the mouse seems to be a little fast, even when changing the mouse sensitivity, the gameplay is great. The shooting mechanics are nice, the cover system is intuitive and helps to maneuver the maps, and the stealth parts of the gameplay I feel are realistic in terms of how fast and from how far enemies notice you.
All in all, I love the game. Once again, the DLC and store issues are annoying, but I am not going to let that ruin my game. I bought the game for the story and gameplay, I could not care less if the people who made the game put in a store or made the DLC usable for one save, because apart from the first time I noticed these issues, I will probably never look at them or remember them again after playing the game more.
In conclusion, I recommend the game. The story is great, the gameplay is fun, and the issues with the DLC and store that people are mentioning are not IN YOUR FACE issues. If you do not want to notice them, you do not have to.

This game needs some more development before the 20 euro price tag is justified. Let me sum up the positives and the negatives i've experienced in my 10 hours of gameplay. (I know it's a pretty short amount of time)
pros:
-terraria-esque character and world system where you can use a character across multiple worlds
-lots of building materials (more would still be nice)
-unique world system where you hop through portals to different biomes
-dungeon system with loot (crafting recipes being among the best loot)
-lots of crafting materials that require you to farm various blocks/creatures/recources
-there seems to be a decent levelling and skill system
cons:
-tediously long time in order to change biomes (we're talking about 30 seconds on an ssd as the host)
-in coop multiplayer you can't have 2 players in 2 different biomes (huge con for me)
-the biome loading time is even longer for the non-host player (we're talking close to a minute)
-repetitive enemies across higher level biomes
-armor level requirements don't really match the biome level you need to reach in order to gather recources for the armor
(you need to mine iron in level 11 biome to make level 7 armor?)
general conclusion:
You'll enjoy this game if you were/are a fan of minecraft and/or terraria, and there's a pretty good farming/looting system for people who are into that kind of game. except that I miss some optimisation (loading times), features(end game and being in different biomes) and diversity(creatures).
Give this game a shot, especially if you can find it at a lower price.

EARLY IMPRESSIONS REVIEW
Tekken is FINALLY on PC and it's pretty damn awesome.
I've played every game in the series (even including Tekken Advance on GBA) so I'm a long time fan of the series. Tekken 3 is probably my all time favorite but there hasn't really ever been a bad Tekken game and Tekken 7 is no exception to that rule. The gameplay is tight and responsive (most importantly it has that special Tekken feeling) and the addition of rage arts is pretty cool. I see some people are complaining about lack of content but I can't really agree. There are enough offline and online gaming modes to keep you busy for a long time and the unlockable content is mostly goofy but still kind of fun. The game looks and runs great (my FX8320 + R9 290X combo pushes the game in 1080p 60FPS on ultra settings). The online modes mostly work fine but there are some connection issues here and there.
For me it doesn't get better than this on PC. I just love Tekken more than any other fighting series out there (don't get me wrong, there are other great fighting games on PC, too, like the MK series, for example). I couldn't be happier this game is available on Steam and I can wholeheartedly recommend it to any fan of fighting games.

This is a more streamlined Tekken game than usual in the way you can assign buttons to press a few at once to any spare buttons on your controller. Combos are much easier to pull off, you can do it almost accidentally doing a few. They don't explain certain types of moves well in the command list. You should approach the game learning moves that work for you than all of it.
The movesets have changed a little bit more transitioning from Tekken 6 to 7 to make the combos easier to pull off, but it still has that Tekken feel.
If you came here from a NetherRealm fighting game, don't expect the story to blow you away. It doesn't take itself seriously. If you're a Tekken fan, then you would most likely enjoy this like I did. The online was very good, but there wasn't enough players sometimes and the wait time was a bit bad. There were only like a few matches where it was unbelievably laggy, it paused every few frames.
Customisation is not very expansive as say, Tekken Tag Tournament 2, at least from what I felt. As for modes, there's basically these: STORY, TREASURE BATTLE, VERSUS, ONLINE, TRAINING
Nothing much more other than CUSTOMISING your character and player tag.
The boss is pretty rough and unfair feeling, even worse than NetherRealms old days, but you can set it to easy mode to combo everything in spamming one button which isn't that fun.
tl;dr: as a tekken fan, get it. it's more streamlined with same tekken feel, meh customisation. very enjoyable, despite meh story. if you're new to tekken, expect to invest time learning to play. don't play if you don't have time

Well, where to start?
I can say in all honesty, that this game is probably ONE of the best dungeon crawlers I've played. A lot of people are either saying "it's better than Diablo 3!" or "This is crappy compared to Diablo 3."  This is both right and wrong (although I wouldn't ever call this game "crappy") What I mean is, they both have their own pros and cons, but regardless they are both great for the things that they offer. I am playing Diablo 3 alongside Torchlight 2, and enjoying them both equally.
I would say that I would compare Torchlight 2 more to Diablo 2 though, it makes me think of it with the town portal scrolls and identification scrolls, skill trees/points etc. I have played Diablo since the first one was released and have been a fan ever since. But, this is about TL2 so I'll get on to that;
TL2 is a really fun, fast-paced, beautiful looking game. I love the features it has, and I think one of my favourites is the fact you get a pet that follows you around and protects you and picks up your loot for you. You can also tell your pet to go back to town and sell your unwanted items and buy you potions/scrolls, which comes in REALLY handy. I love the combat on this game, like someone said before, it doesn't feel like a grind killing the monsters - because it's actually fun doing so. It's fast and fluid and I can see this being a game you'd want to replay just to use the other classes.
If you're an achievement hunter, this game is great for that too, you get achievments for pretty much everything and that's a nice thing, it makes you feel like you've acomplished something - even just by doing something small and receiving an achievement for it.
OVERALL, this game is a must buy, it's great for the price - and honestly, could be sold at the same price as Blizzard is selling Diablo 3 for. If you like dungeon crawlers, pick this one up! And even if you're new to the genre - I'd definitely suggest buying this as your first, it is a guaranteed winner in my books.
TL;DR - 10/10 just buy it now.

Brothers in Arms: Hell's Highway was an amazing experience and an example on what modern military shooters should do nowadays, yes, looking at you, Call of Duty and Battlefield. At thing which bugs me about modern shooters is that every single one of them has its focus on the repetitive multiplayer where as today most of them play essentially the same, just as the campaign.
We need more games like Hell's Highway which are not glorifying war but show the human side the soldiers have instead of how many times they can yell "♥♥♥♥ YEAH, AMERICA!" while pulling out the flamethrower to "burn them, burn them all!!!"
The men you fight along in Hell's Highway feel human and just as in the older Brother's in Arms games, the main focus lies in the single player. If you want to buy this game for a killstreak loaded multi player to "pwn scrubs", you are wrong here.
A roughly about 10 hours long campaign (I played on Veteran difficulty)  will keep you motivated with a nice tactical component to command different squads such as the MG squad or the assault team as Matthew Baker, to surpress the enemy and use the element of surprise to flank clueless and somtimes dumb acting enemy soldiers. The commanding barely gets old and as you hop around different hubs of the hot areas during the war. Those range from wide fields to close battles in troubled cities and villages as well as asylums and collapsed buildings.
The thing which does get a little repetitive are the objectives you have to achieve using those methods of commanding. Most of the time you find yourself having to destroy 88 cannons and sometimes drive a tank around in which you are mostly safe even on the higher difficulties. Really annoying did those things only become in the end to me, as the game finally came to a closing, during the last hour of gameplay. The story itself kept motivating as protagonist Matthew Baker's mind started to crumble and he realized more and more and war is insanity.
The "To Be Continued" in the end was a huge bummer to me though, especially because Ubisoft doesn't seem to care at all about this amazing series which could definetly standout amongst "Call of Boredom" or the recent development of the"Battlefail" games.
It doesn't need amazing graphics to make a good game. While Brothers in Arms may looked fine back in the day it is quite outdated for the modern standards. Second to none facial animations, horrible lip-synching at times but nice destructability of cover and physical correctness of the debris look damn fine as well as gore and ragdoll of fallen enemy soldiers.
Also the sound design is great and as the bullets fly over your head  in cover and the enemies speaking correct German, which is a rare thing to see to be honest. The atmosphere is really great and makes you feel as if this was an episode of the critically acclaimed "Band of Brothers"-TV show. The developers really did a great job in capturing an unique and equally terrifying experience.
Overall Brothers in Arms: Hell's Highway is a technically and gameplay wise far from flawless but also an unique and tactical game which definetly gets a recommendation for me, even if solely for the atmosphere and the long campaign.
Grab this game if you are sick of modern shooters and/or glorification of war.
