Alrighty then, here's my first review. Ever. Abyways, I always thought this game seemed a bit childish and rubbish compared to the games I usually play (Shadow of Mordor, Skyrim...etc), and was not going to buy it at all for its original price. Then Christmas came, and with it, the sales. My girlfriend saw this and thought it was something she'd like (she's not that into games, but anyway) so at 4 euro I figured, why not? I have to say, this game is nothing like I expected it to be.
First of all, the single player co-op (wut?) is awesome. Personally, I've never played a game that had that kind of playstyle, so it was something new and it worked suprisingly well. It'll test your ability to multitask and you just might end up ambidextrous.
While the riddles and gameplay weren't completely challenging, it still felt like you achieved something when you figured out the puzzle.
The graphics are absolutely stunning, especially the water textures and there are a few benches scattered around which show you a better view of the enviroment surrounding your journey, which are well worth seeing if you're not in a rush.
The story is also superb. While I couldn't understand a single word (not sure if it's in another language, or something made up like the teletubbies use) I pretty much got the jist of what was going on most of the time. And the ending? Man, was definitely not expecting that.
I know it's rated 16+, but I was mislead by the graphics. It started off like a kid's game, but certain scenes were rather... Mature. Every now and again the game would remind you that this wasn't intended for children (there's a few nooses found throughout the game, to avoid spoiling it for you).
The downs? Well, there aren't many. Would've been nice to understand what they were saying, but I can't complain much about that. Also, while great, the story was rather short, and there's no replayability UNLESS you want to try and unlock the achievements. Those things are hard to find. I only managed to spot 5/12 during the first playthrough, so who knows where the other ones are. You need a keen eye for those.
In short;
PROS:

I'll tell you this now. I am a huge fan of RWBY, probably one of the biggest, but this game in all honestly is really underwhelming. I know this game is still in early access, and I know the game will definitely improve over the next couple updates and become an amazing game, but for now, it's really bad. This game as of now is not worth 15 dollars, so don't buy it unless you're a diehard RWBY fan such as myself.
I'll start with the cons first of this game.
Cons:
-The Animations for this game is very choppy. When I see the characters walk, I sorta cringe a little because of how bad it was.
-This game gets VERYYYYYY laggy at times. When you hit big waves, which you're going to often encounter, the game can't handle all the mobs and gets super laggy.
-Your character progress does not save once you exit the game. This is very frustrating at times because I would get my character to a pretty high level and it doesn't even save.
-Very Limited move pool. I know this is going to expand further as the game updates and such, but each character only has 3 special moves and then the normal slash combo. Pretty underwhelming because if you compare it to other Dynasty warrior ripoff games, they have this aspect correct.
-Subtitles are pretty bad/can't keep up if they speak very long sentences.
Now onto the Pros:
Pros:
-It's a ♥♥♥♥ing RWBY game. I've been waiting for this for so long. Once I heard it was on Steam greenlight, I immediately upvoted it because more RWBY stuff = More RWBY love and popularity.
-Voice Acting is very good. They got the Voice Actors for each of the RWBY characters in this game and it's really awesome hearing them speak in the game.

-Character designs are awesome. Besides the choppy animation, them character designs are to die for.
-It's a New story, new enemies we've never encountered, it's pretty awesome if you want to see that.
-The ♥♥♥♥ing music is beautiful. let me spell it out for you. B-E-A-U-T-I-F-U-L.

This game is a little rough around the edges, especially with regard to documentation and introducing new players but after a really rough few games you can begin to see the potential of this game.
Unlike first person shooters like heroes and generals, or RTSes like company of heroes, in this game you control a single squad with no respawns. You move them around with the mouse or keyboard (in this game, learning hotkeys is a must or there's no way you can respond in time to changes in the field of battle). The objective of the game is to either capture victory points (VPs) or to eliminate the other team.
You move your units between cover and you try to minimize the percentage hit chance the enemy has on you. The game has mechanics of suppression, including for grenades, and also fog of war (though, it's not indicated as fog on the map, your units have a limited field of view in a cone in front of them).
The game moves very quickly, and falling behind can quickly lead to being flanked. However, with good team work and communication you and  your team can also move individual soldiers so optimal positions to snipe, suppress, or kill the enemy and win the game.
I reccomend this for anyone who wants a tactical game based on soldier positioning and teamwork.

Sadly, the tutorial is nearly non-existant, there's no single player game mode (just a very basic "training" game mode where you can play solo or against other players) and a bunch of content is still to be released: more sides (Russians, partisans, British),

You might want to hold to your money and wait for further development, but it's quite addictive and enjoyable as it is, and the devs are responsive and fixing bugs.

Despite contending with ridiculous unlock delays and pre-load issues I eventually entered Mankind Divided with high hopes. Unfortunately those first two hours have not been a pleasant experience
[System: 4770K/16gb/980Ti - Nvidia Driver: 372.54]
- The mouse acceleration is unbearable, configuration files are not user accessible.
- The maximum FOV is uncomfortably narrow.
- Changing LOD settings in-game causes basic objects to disappear resulting in floating objects. You can also enter 'restricted' areas as the collision detection is mapped to many of these surfaces.
- Increasing screen resolution causes severe frame rate issues. At 1440p I can play with most settings on high/max at 60fps+. At 2160p I can barely maintain 30fps with all settings on low.
- Visuals are distinctly soft and low resolution at a moderate distance, despite disabling effects such as motion blur, depth of field and temporal AA. There appears to be further post-processing effects which cannot be disabled.
- The mouse and keyboard controls are not very intuitive, Jensen frequently jumps when attempting to move between cover. I will have to explore this further via custom key bindings.
- Excessive and unskippable splash screens, plus the usual nonsense regarding the game's auto-save 'feature'.
Many of these issues should be an easy fix but the tyranical approach to the file system means we will be left waiting for patches or perhaps a savy programmer to release tools to modify the files.
There are currently too many issues to even consider recommending this game, if I had purchased direct from the Steam Store I would strongly consider a refund. Bitterly disappointed.

Okay, here we go. This game is still in its early stages, so naturally, it's going to have flaws. But, despite being in early alpha, it has already managed to impress me. So, let's go through what this game does well, first.
RWBY: Grimm Eclipse does a fantastic job of making it feel like you're 'playing the show'. The animation is great, and every once and a while you get a little quote from one of the characters, which, just like the show itself, is fantastically voice acted. The graphics are great, and the game holds up well enough performance-wise.
Perhaps the thing that was focused on the most in the development of this early access game was the combat. Fighting in this game is so satisfying, especially when you land a huge hit on an enemy and they go flying back, melting away slowly. The attacks and fighting styles are fluent and beautiful, and it just feels right when you hit something. The four playable characters each have three special attacks that, through leveling up, increase in power. Every character has a fairly in-depth skill tree that you can put points into, to make your character more powerful. Keep in mind that this game features  MOBA-style leveling, so each time you play, you will be set back to level one. This may sound like a drag, but it is a very good concept. When you start a game with friends, you can place your points according to how you want to either support your team, or just be a full blown killing machine.
As far as story goes, there really isn't much in the realm of story as much as there is just slaying hordes of monsters, with an objective here and there. So far, there are only four stages, which can all be completed in a matter of 45 minutes. Obviously there are more to come, but at the moment, we have only four stages. Surprisingly, playing these levels over again does not get boring. With the ability to make a different character build every game, the seemingly repititive gameplay continues to be exciting and fun.
As stated earlier, of course this game is going to have flaws. There are a few, not many, but only two stand out to me.
Firstly, I found that the four playable characters are very unbalanced. Yang and Weiss are fairly versitile, but it seems like Ruby is too overpowered, and Blake is too underpowered. I've played as both of them, and playing as Ruby was so easy, while playing as Blake put me through the ringer. Some more balance would be nice.
Lastly, the lack of a main story makes it very difficult for someone with a limited knowledge of RWBY to know what's going on, or know who anyone is. There really isn't much more to say. Hopefully the full game will have a cutscene at the beginning or something like that to introduce tha characters, and the plot.
Overall, so far this game is well done. There's still plenty more updates to come, though. Perhaps we'll get new characters, new abilities, the possibilities are endless. This game is an easy buy for big RWBY fans, but for others who are either new to the series or never heard of it, I'd wait for the full game to be released.
Overall Rating: 6.5-7/10

I cannot explain how bad this game is. If you are looking for a short review here it is:
DO NOT BUY THIS.
If you want a real review here is mine:
If you enjoy games that do not tell you how (or even allow in many cases) you to do anything then you will enjoy this game. I am a huge fan of grand strategy. I have something like 900 hours logged in CK2. I am perfectly fine with a substantial learning curve. I am equally ok with having to put in a large number of hours to learn how to fully enjoy a game. This game simply provides no useful information at any time. The tutorial is clumsily thrown together scenario set in pre-WWII China that provides only the most basic of information, e.g. how to build units and how to queue up research projects. Anything from a strategic level such as managing your economy, forming useful diplomatic bonds and controlling your incomprehensibly complex military is not provided.
Unfortunatly this is not where the game's problems stop. On top of the fact that even figuring out what to do is near impossible, the game is riddled with glitches/bugs. On several occasions (once during a Japan 1939 campaign and another time during an Italy 1939 campaign) while "invading" -- I use sarcastic double quotes because this game practically demands that you not directly control your military -- the south Pacific, I gained control of Indonesia. When prompted to annex, colonize, or liberate the nation I was asked if I wanted to annex colonize or liberate myself. As a result I ended up playing the rest of the campaign as "Japanese Japan" (or Italian Italy in the Italy campaign). Similarly the minister controls used to influence your nations policies seem to do essentially nothing. Once when playing as the Soviet Union in the 1949 I found myself in a fair amount of debt. How this happened in the first place I don't know. That said, I gave my minister the "reduce regional debt" command. This policy remained in place for several years with absolutely no effect. This was not for a lack of money, I was actually running a rather large surplus. My minister simply would not pay off my regions debt. Being the astute gamer I was I decided to attempt to just manually pay off my debt with money from my treasury. Guess what? You literally cannot do that.
Now a few bugs is understandable. All software is a work in progress. The community for this game, both players and the developers, is the antithesis of helpful. Most posts related to not understanding this game are met with answers that essentially boil down to 1) Did you play the tutorial? 2) You can't do that. 3) Why would you even want to do that?
If I could get back the 100 some hours I put into this game I could easily have played all the way through a game that isn't really unfun. Do you self a favor and take a pass on this one. Yes even you grand strategy enthusiast.

This is the ultimate game for Grand Strategy game lovers. A lot of micromanagment, a lot of indicators and things to consider, but still game-like enough to let you follow your dreams. There are a lot of people that critisize the AI. Some people like to be constantly frustrated and have a sadist opponent that whips them continously. I dont. The game is difficult enough as it is because it has a long learning curve. It introduces you to indicators like inflation or taxation to the pensioners and you have to learn to connect the dots.
You can get any nation you want, at any period you want and try to make something out of it. Would you do the same choices as France in WW2? Is it possible to do anything else?
The only thing i dont like about this title is that although you can mode a lot of things, you cannot do population distribution corrections across the map or assign different royalties (or multiple) in hexes. Or at least have an in game way to affect royalty. Which renders conquest a bit useless, unless you want certain resources.
Other than that it is a pretty fascinating game which will guarantee you hundreds of hours of entertainment.
Almost as addicting as coffee, candy or cocaine, yet slightly enraging, like cocaine. This game is cocaine.

Continuação do jogo GunZ: The Duel produzido pela MAIET Entertainement. Houve uma melhoria consideravel na parte artística do game, que o torna mais agradável aos olhos. Modelos bem trabalhados com um level design interativo são encontrados tanto no modo PvP quanto no modo PvE(missões contra a AI). Foi implementada uma ideia interessante onde se aplica aos personagens uma árvore de habilidades distribuidas em ofensivas e defensivas. Pode-se notar uma melhoria na mecânica de interação personagem-mapa que permite não só andar por paredes, como antigamente, como agora é possível controlar a direção durante a corrida pela mesma.
Um jogo bem produzido mas que deixa os antigos jogadores a desejar quando se trata de mecânica de combate, nesse novo GunZ não é possível realizar ações dos bons e velhos D/E/K-Style. Atrevo-me a dizer que são possíveis as realizações de Flash Step, Butterfly e Wind Step, assim como suas variações segurando armas.
Foi uma boa tentativa de reviver um ótimo jogo que marcou alguns anos de minha vida e de muitas outras pessoas, mas creio sob meu ponto de vista que não foi de muito agrado, ao menos durante esse primeiro contato com o jogo. Há ainda a possibilidade de alterações serem feitas no jogo tornando o gameplay mais parecido como o encontrado na versão anterior da série. Vamos aguardar que seja feito.

If you are reading this don’t purchase the game, if you didn’t immediately buy this because “South Park” you want to wait until this is on heavy discount (some Game of the Year version at 80% off (about the cost of a single South Park season)) to experience the good parts of this game.
Really South Park: the Fracture But Whole is two parts that are greater there sum: the South Park “Story” part and the “Game” mechanics and systems. For South Park Fans the South Park parts are great, and give you a constant bread crumbs trail of voice lines, character designs, and cut scenes to make you laugh. At the end of the game the story does become less enjoyable when it really becomes a series of “But then this,  and then you need to fight X, and then you need to play with time in X way, etc” but I’d say right to the end of the big Cop battle A+ from a South park Fan.
The game mechanics and systems however aren’t a good fit for the game. The problem is in isolation the grid battles, the level system, the crafting system, and you home screen system are “good” systems and are functional; they just don’t fit the game. I really feels like someone said “Ya Stick of Truth is cute, but this is how you make a modern RPG”.
Artifacts/Leveling – the leveling in FbW is really poor and is the one the key examples of the “this is how you make game now a days”. As the player you gain XP which more or less after Boss battles open artifact slots which you equipment power modifiers into “powering up” your character. It is super indirect and a poor replacement of the character RPG and equipment/weapon Patch system in SoT. Generally you are equipping the right/top 1-2 most artifact (the last two you received) and bumping artifacts down the slots as you get into the 3rd and fourth layer of artifacts and the 60-100 range of artifact powers. This was way less effective as story+game mechanics then weapons, armor and patches in SoT as “these would be the way kids power up in their game”
Crafting – as I said before the system isn’t bad but the result is. I never really felt that the crafting level mattered and for personal preference I liked the artifacts you got from the world better. But the result of the crafting system is you have a constant stream of “crafting items” when you loot stuff; in SoT it felt like its looting gave you one or two references with the “junk” item type; FbW gives you 2-4 crafting items per loot, you just stop looking at the top right after the first multi-loot room because of the noise of the named crafting materials
Costumes – the Change to costumes elements as purely cosmetic is again on its face not that bad and eliminates the “best set/weapon” outcome of the SoT style mechanics but it adds to the overwhelming wave of “new stuff” that fills every menu and map; crafting, shops on map, items you pick up, etc. Yes you can change to be a Viper/Speaker with magnet hands and KISS makeup and change again in two minutes but your picking up one of the 6+ types of costume pieces all the time
Quick time the game: everything in the game is a quick time event, buddy skill = QT, calling your buddy = QT, farting = QT, Attacking = QT, Hit recovery = QT
o	The first time couple of times you encounter the QT abstraction for an action they are quite funny and additive; the fifth time and the third buddy scan/buddy action in a room it is much less fun and slows down the game
It is slow game, very slow: removing the run button means anytime you can’t use fast travel it is 10 seconds to clear a street screen, battle is very slow attacks take 5 seconds, enemy turns each take 5 seconds, supers have a couple of second before and couple of seconds after, it all adds up to a very long time to finish an encounter, and as mentioned the buddy scan /action mechanic just takes a ton of time

For an early access game, it is completely solid and stable. As a big fan of the show from day one episode one I have been following this game since it was on greenlight and I am completely satisfied but that may have something to do with my love for the show. I’ll just talk about what I personally like or dislike so read it if you want detailed information about the game but if you want to short version then I have to say I like the game and I think it’s a great value for money and even greater if you manage to play with a couple of people you know or your just a fan of the show like I am. I do not regret my purchase and am happy to support this game where ever it decides to go.
Combat is solid and enjoyable, not very difficult but not very simple either. You can die very easily if you don’t make use of the dodge button and your skills from which there are a good verity between the current four characters of the show. You have your basic combo attacks and a ranged attack which can mix together for a different combo and each of the characters have their own unique skills which use a portion of your skill bar. You can also upgrade your skills by levelling your character, which add some unique effects or just upgrade general things such as your aura which acts as your health. You gain one skill point per level, at the moment the max level is ten so you have a total of ten points to spend but again that could be only for now and could change later. Picking between which skills you want to upgrade more and focus towards is completely up to you and from what I’ve seen there isn’t a TRINITY between skills at the moment. But then again I only play Ruby and Yang so take my word for a grain of sand :P The game is also four player drop in and drop out co-op so you can have some great fun with friends or random people, enemies do increase in difficulty depending on how many people are with you so it doesn’t make the game easier in a sense. However I must say there is no lock on system which is kind of weird, it makes son skills completely miss the enemy you want to hit and sometimes hits the wrong one. You kind of get use to it as you keep playing but still, adding a lock on will fix this issue. It should also be mentioned that this game supports Xbox One and PS4 controller support surprisingly, the controls on a keyboard and mouse are perfectly fine in my opinion but the option is there for those who want it. I do not own a controller for either console so I can’t fully recommend them as I have no idea if they are a blessing or a curse but again the option is there.
Sound is decent I guess, there is a track what plays through missions and sometimes have these epic tracks playing during large battles and boss fights which puts a smile on your face now and then. Voice acting is also here and for the most part works well, every character sounds like their own and isn’t a pain to listen to but then again I watch allot of anime so maybe that has something to do with it. Sound effects are spot on, you feel like your attacks are connecting and your specials are in fact SPECIAL. Not much else I can really say, I think it’s all great and works just as intended but it is worth mentioning that it does get a bit too loud especially the combat sounds. It just gets ridiculously loud for no reasons but again its nothing game breaking so…YOLO I guess.
Graphics are just as they are in the show which is a very and I mean VERY GOOD THING. It all looks right by nature and stays true to its origin. If you aren’t a fan of a cartoony style with an anime flare then walk away now because it is not getting any better than it is. The character models are perfect and represent the player characters and the enemy NPC’s perfectly. I personally love Yang’s hair as it’s the best thing to look at while laying the beat down on grimm :P
Levels are a hit and miss for me, they serve their function with flying colours and there is nothing wrong with them in a sense. The problem is that there are way TOO many invisible walls for no real reason. For example during the first two missions where you play in large fields, you can see large open areas which you can’t get to because there’s an inviable force stopping you. It makes levels feel like a straight line, a corridor not allowing the players to explore these good looking areas in a large and interesting world. That said there are a good amount of secrets on each map which grant extra EXP which are very easy to miss but worth getting if you can so for that I will thank the designer, it does give the players a reason to actually explore the area than just go on with the objective. Also some missions have these “defend the objective” goal which isn’t bad for me since I like the combat enough but I can see if people start to get annoyed by this so mixing up the objective would be nice. That’s not to say that’s the only thing you do because it’s not.
Animations are a mixed bag here, for the characters you control they are spot on. Each character feels unique and has a unique play style which makes you want to main a charter over the others which is always a good thing as you feel connect to these charter especially if you watch the show, I personally absolutely love Yang but will defiantly play Raven if she gets added. It’s the enemy NPCs who have issues now and then, for example Weiss can freeze an enemy in place with one of her upgrades but for some reason the enemy still attacks and even move around despite being frozen in ice. What the hell? It happens a hand full of times but way more common as you play more and more so hopefully that can get fixed.
Skills for some characters are clearly better than others, for example Yang’s third ability “Blastwave” is completely worthless and unreliable as you miss your targets five out of ten times. Making the upgrades for that ability a complete waste. Another example is Ruby’s general upgrade “Armor piercing rounds” which increases the damage of your range attacks, why? This is a game where you have to combo enemy’s to even use your skills, range attacks are nice to have but don’t even get close to the same damage as your melee attacks do. So why have an upgrade for something you barely use? It may not be bad as I’m making it out to be but it does make you scratch your head now and then especially since you can currently only getting a total of ten points to spend, so you want to be sure your making you right decisions. It just when you have a good damaging ability you should have other good options which are comparably not a liability.
It’s a very solid game to play and enjoy especially if you have friends so if you’re a fan of the show then show your support and pick this up. Get some friends and you will have some great fun as I have with my friends. Really excited to see how this game will grow and hopefully it will be for the better. All in all I have not regretted my purchase at all.
More characters. (Please add Raven! I’ll pay whatever the price)
More levels because why not?
Remove the invisible walls or at least make then less noticeable.
Change some of the skills so they make more sense.
A character creator.
If possible, a PvP mode. It would be awesome putting a team like RWBY vs JNPR.

This is a fantastic Early Access game in it's own right. It has great fighting, flawless controller support, and awesome voice acting. That being said, there are some bad things too. 1)The Grimm (the enemies) spam their abilities just like a player would, but they aren't limited to 4 or 6 charges like players are; they are invincible while using those abilities, so you can see why this would be a problem. 2)Knowing the show doesn't really do anything for anybody except know what the creatures are called beforehand and know what weapons the characters use (awesome weapons btw). That being said, not knowing the show isn't very different except you wonder why all the characters are girls... 3)This game is difficult. That is just a fact at this stage. Right now it's not very easy to deal with 15,000 monsters at a time with how they fight and how we, as players, are limited while the Grimm are not. This game is in great shape for being in early access for less than a week, though. Lots of things can happen with this game and lots of things WILL happen for this game. It's just not quite ready to be called fantastic, but it's almost there.

For those who don't know much about the series, they might not understand a lot about what's going on as this takes place after season 2 and before season 3. I would probably recommend something in the option that can give the player a short re-cap of what happened between seasons 1 & 2, this can allow players who got this game without watching the series to get a basic summarization of what happened and possibly allow them to look into the series more themselves through the game.
Aside from that, really fun game with beautiful graphics. I've only played as Blake and Ruby right now but I personally like how each character's skills and playing style fits with how they are in the series. Using RPG class terms, Blake is similar to the Ninja that attacks quickly and is better at at a distance as well as reviving her team mates, while Yang is similar to a Monk class that just tanks and deals damage. Most of the errors in this game have already been mentioned, but my only thing that I'd recommend is check the audio files in the game before releasing updates. There was one point I saw Yang's picture but heard Ruby's voice, and Ruby wasn't even around. So mistakes like that do need to be corrected as it is something that does bug me. Other thing I can recommend is saving LV progress, because in reality with how much Grimm can swarm you at some points and the amount of abilities you have being small in number makes keeping LVs not a big deal as recklessness can lead to you getting surrounded. Using this idea, if people wanted to start from LV 1 they can play a different character and level them up,, which in turn will go well if more characters are added like say members from Team JNPR or even Team CFVY.
Overall, for an Early Access, this game is great and I liked it a lot. Looking forward to seeing what will be in there later on in the story, what new characters will be in the game, what they'll do for the other Grimm (Like the Nevermore and the Death Stalkers) and much more. RWBY fans will certainly enjoy this, and I'm hoping eventually gamers who aren't familiar with the series will eventually look into it.

Welp, I've been pushed over the edge into writing this review in lieu of recent events which can be read in any other review posted recently. This review will cover actual issues the game has instead of chewing out take2 (though they do deserve to be chewed out, but, at this point I feel anything I'd say has already been said).
I will begin by saying this game was entertaining for a short while. It has nice graphics, pretty fluid gameplay, and they like to keep online updated which they've done for free instead of having you pay for dlc so I commend them for doing that. Unfortunately that's all the praise I have for this game.
I will begin ripping this thing apart with single-player mode. Unlike other GTA games I've played (mostly Vice City and San Andreas, which are arguably the best 2 in the series) the game is a cakewalk. When I play GTA I want to be challenged to the point of rage-quitting then coming back to it a short while later (anyone remember Demolition Man from VC? or what about the damn RC plane mission in SA?). Not to mention this game feels smaller than SA with only 1 city and the countryside. The story is decent, some of the characters are great, but all of that is overshadowed by how easily one breezes through the story. This isn't a GTA game, it's got the look and some of the humor of a GTA game, but it lacks the soul-crushingly difficult mission(s) that gives each of the other GTA's I've played their unique charm.
Now on to the real killer for me: online mode. Online mode is a great concept, but, horribly executed. It's nice to be able to play with others and progress from having your first vehicle you stole to having a few houses, a business, multiple full garages full of customized cars, etc. It would also be nice if that were possible in a reasonable amount of time. Unfortunately, it's not. If you're like me and refuse to do any microtransactions so you end up grinding the resourses, online takes eons. They price things so exorbitantly high that most players just end up buying the shark cards, making it one of the cardinal sins of gaming: pay-to-win. Online, at this point has become just a money grab. Additionally, online mode is riddled with players who bend the rules. Some of these people are nice, but most I've come across are just trolls. Then there's the seemingly endless supply of rule-abiding trolls. Those who don't circumvent the rules with additional tools, but rather use their equipment to wreak havoc on honest players. I understand that some of this is fine, fun even, but when it's every server then it makes it unbearable. Also, you can forget about acomplishing anything in your own private server, the freeroam events are disabled, thus forcing you to play in a troll-riddled hellhole of a place just trying to accomplish anything to make some decent cash so you don't have to spend real money on those damn shark cards. As far as running the MC or CEO stuff, most people don't want to bother with it unless they get the highest cut, so everyone runs their own stuff rather than working together. So many of the practices with online mode are very anti-cooperative play, which is in direct contrast to the real world of crime where you have people working together to achieve things. So even as a crime simulator this game fails.
Now to break my own rule I gave myself at the beginning of this... talking about the Take 2 legal action against a certain modding tool.
Mods are what made single-player mode bearable. You could make it difficult, quirky, grimey, and downright weird. But that's the beauty of mods in games. Companies like Take 2 think of mods as ways to break rules and ruin their games, but that's not what modding, real modding, is. Modding, for all intents and purposes, is a way for people to enjoy the product that the company has released long past its vanilla playability allows. Furthermore, it's a form of creative expression allowing people to view the game as a wonderfully built canvas to unleash their creative desires and share with others. Modding brings me back to the good 'ol days of gaming; before all the extreme budgets, corporate buyouts, playing it safe with releases (which this game is... dumbed down to appeal to the widest audience). All gaming is nowadays, seems like it's about making the most money rather than providing quality entertainment. I remember a time when games used to be innovative, groundbreaking even, people used to push the limits, take risks, succeed and fail. But that was the beauty of it. If a game failed it was because it was a bad game, not because they didn't spend enough on marketing (in the beginning anyway... this did eventually become the reason many games do fail). Modding allows people to do what those crazy fools did back in the day: push the limits, cause paradigm shifts, and create quality entertainment. Many of the games which have brought massive loads of cash in for some of these companies began as mods for other games, so it's sickening to see companies doing things like Take2 has done to the modding community. Basically what they're saying is: "Your ideas are trash, allow us to give you what we say you want" rather than being a decent company and providing us with what we actually want. We get the same 15 games every year because it reaches the widest audience, mods are there to make the more nuanced alterations that fit smaller segments within the market, allowing us to turn the game into what we want. Some may claim that it sullies the original work, my response to them is to wake up and realize that it's just a money game now when it comes to the big companies.
Back on topic a bit: Take2's legal action against a certain modding tool is appalling. They claim it's to prevent modders online, which would be fine since it's their servers, people may have conflicting mods, there's no way to manage them all, among other issues. However, this particular tool doesn't allow for any sort of online modding (not to mention the modders who are online are rarely punished anyway). So why is it they claim it's to prevent online modding when clearly it's not? The answer is simple, long ago they said that they'll allow modding in offline mode, it's your game so you should be able to turn it into something you enjoy playing. They say it's to prevent online modding so they don't have to go back on their original promise, though actions speak louder than words and it's clear they have indeed gone back on their word. Why do they want to eliminate offline modding? Well that's a simple question to answer. As stated earlier, mods allow players to enjoy games long past their original playability value. In the case of GTA5 once you beat the story and quests there's nothing left to do so naturally you head online. Mods allowed peole to continue to play offline long after the story ended which was no good for Take2. Once you remove the Mods, the playability factor is gone thus forcing people to play online. Once online, they realize the exorbitant prices for most things and either quit playing the game altogether, attempt to grind it out, or in the case of most people, buy the shark cards.
This kind of anti-consumer behavior cannot stand. Not to mention the game isn't even that spectacular and is riddled with issues that they don't appear to care enough about to fix. So no, I do not recommend this game.

This is less a game and more an interactive story. The rewards are not just watching the story unfold at your fingertips but viewing the stunning visuals along the way. Using creative gameplay that challenges your hand/eye coordination, the developers set you on a path that forces you to be observant in order to conquer the journey ahead. Each small quest is a parable to life and its merciless double edge that all too often reminds us of how fragile we truly are. The story is told primarily by visuals, no discernable dialogue, no captions, and while the characters use body language and grunts to convey general emotion, this I feel, preserves the viewers need to use their imagination to unfold the story details in their own mind. As a player of this interactive story, you can expect linear path selection and camera control, limited exploration opportunities that unlock hidden game achievments, minor scenes of gore and blood but most importantly, a refreshing journey that steals you away from the grind of repetitive games that obliterate the scene today. It can be played in one evening with a low replay factor due primarily to the hidden achievments that can be discovered. Certainly an unforgettable journey.

Hey whoo boy! Who doesn't like to be a sniper? I suggest you start on the 'Cadet" mode first to get the feel of it. I did and had a tendency to snap off shots at times that caused what seemed like the entire Afrika Corps and Italian army come down on me like a ton of bricks. However second time around using stealth and background noise to mask my shots I had a much more enjoyable time.
I think the graphics are outstanding and the AI is pretty smart. I mean at least to a degree. If your shot is heard the enemy starts searching for you so best thing to do is skeedaddle from the area until the indicator in the HUD indicates things have cooled down. Use trucks, fuel barrels and 88 ammo to cause large scale destruction and wipe out a few of the enemy at a time. In fact the "X-Ray" mode where you can watch your shot either enter a gas tank of a truck, Halftrack or tank and blow it to kingdom come or in the case of human flesh, bone and internal organs is just good, plain fun and addictive as hell.
The story line is okay but the area s you have to transverse are terrific and large. Sunlight in your eyes, getting into the right position for a shot is sometimes an effort in and of itself. My only wish is that when you are moving around in stealth there could be a 'up against your cover' position. By that I mean unlike GTA IV or Mafia II or II you can press up against your cover instead of just crouching behind it. I would think it would help make those stealth kills much more easy.
But I recommend this game to anyone who enjoys sneaking around, taking your time, thinking out your plan of action and then execution of your plan by sending a Garand's .30 caliber copper jacketed round into someones vital parts or wreaking havoc to the engine or gas tank of a vehicle.

The maps are so detailed (and in-depth) that players who have 2000+ hours on tha game (played for 2+years) still find new features daily (NOTE: one of recent game-changing updates remodeled all maps to help spawn-camping issue so that reference is pre-Garmon update)
There is a large Twitch Streaming community that provides the only real TEAM-WIDE coordination in battles.
There is now a way to report abuse in-game
There is a universal way to quickly ask for a ride - "F" - whistle - when whistling outdoors most vehicles stop to let you hop on.  Indoors it's used to relay info such as "Point Clear" or "The area by me is clear"
Lastly any and all headshots, even by the weakest weapon in the game, is instant death.
IMPORTANT NOTES FOR THE NEW PLAYERS!!!
any explosives will cause repair costs to skyrocket.
First weapon you try to buy should be the T1 SMG for your faction
anti-tank weapons are especially expensive per use
first new soldier you buy should be a Tank crewman - Killing tanks with a tank is the most practical way to get credits for average skilled players
DO NOT BUY A PILOT!!  The price per spawn is more than anything else in the game (500 each)!!  Also the flight controls are abnormal so first time flying you'll be lucky with just 10 suicides via collision (5k creds lost)
Be mindful of upgrades to weapons (like high-damage high-precision rifle rounds) to increase Rate of Fire and Damage
Be sure that when the rest of your team pushes to the next point, you stay behind to defend.  It's not uncommon to have 12 people (2/3 team) capturing the next point and have your push stopped by "Ghost cappers" that capture the previous point while your team is traveling/capturing the next point.

ChuSingura46+1 is a visual novel about the 47 ronin, if those ronin would (almost) all be women and if there would be one man amongst them from the future, trapped in feudal Japan after a mysterious curse that somehow involves a solar eclipse and fortune cards put him there. So not really a realistic depiction of this historical event.
If you want to know if this VN is one for you, answer the following questions:
-Do you like slice-of-life elements and silly trope characters? Because that will be most of the story for the first half.
-Do you like loooooong VN stories? Because this is one of those.
-Do you like harem stories? And I mean the kind where every woman is attracted to you for no apparent reason once you give them even the slightest hint of attention or affection.
If your answer to any of these questions isn't a solid no, you have a fair chance of liking this game.
Pros:
-The shojo elements of the story are surprisingly good for a VN; the protagonist's choice to pick up the sword again, his training and the enemies he fights all feel natural and good. It would have been really easy for them to screw this up by making him overcome his adversity to swordfighting too abrupt or forced but they didn't.
-Some characters are good or likable and the roles that are too trope are either small enough for this to be understandable or not taken serious to begin with. This with the exeption of the daylight lamp.
-There are a lot more sprites than a free-to-play VN player like me is used to. Various outfits, little details, lots of expressions, and most of all the small roles. For not only the roles so small that they could've easily been written out completely, but also the insignificant characters like the Kira servants to get their own sprites is quite unique for the $0 VN's.
Cons:
-This is a completely kinetic story, no choices at all. I wouldn't mind this so much if they hadn't picked such an unusual choice to be your romantic interest, but they did.
-While I praised the shojo elements before, the actual action scenes are not really good. In between the sword fights that are pretty much just still frames with a vpunch effect and the sprites that are being moved around a little too much for too long, the action scenes actually felt like the slowest scenes in the story sometimes.
-This is more a minus to Japanese story telling in general, but the freaking flashbacks. If you're giving me a flashback of something they said literally just one minute ago, you're giving me the idea you see me as a 5-year old. The explaining of things isn't actually as bad here as it can be in other Japanese stories, but they give so many unneccesary flashbacks and repetition of dialogue.

First of all a disclaimer about my hours on record. I put in a lot of hours on Xbox 360 on this game when it came out. I received it for PC as part of a humble bundle and decided to revisit it.
Right from the start of the intro you will find Brutal Legend to be a funny, quirky game with great humour and good music. This is even more true if you have even an inkling of Hard Rock, Metal or Heavy Metal in your bones. The jokes are still funny and relevant even today, and the metal world you are presented with in the game is full of witty references and well thought out re-imaginings of what a metal world would look like.
The gameplay itself is a mix of hack-&-slash and strategy game, depending on what's going on. The main part of the game is a third person adventure where you cut down enemies and explore a sandbox world. There are boss battle type encounters later on that go over to the strategy gaming side. Both are executed well and do what you'd expect. A third component of the game is your car, which provides an easy way to travel in the game world and also allows for driving over stuff as you go which is amusing.
The game has a very metal soundtrack which, depending on your taste, should set the tone quite well and provides you with an enjoyable backdrop to the carnage. Besides the excellent voice acting of Jack Black as the main protagonist, there are some good guest appearances in the form of Ozzy Osbourne and Lemmy Kilmister.
Despite everything it has going for it, I have to admit that Brutal Legend's ultimate downfall is repetition. As fun as it is to drive around a well imagined metal world in your cool car with metal blazing, it just doesn't keep the game alive. The hacking and slashing becomes tiringly repetitive eventually, and eventually the only things that keep you playing are the funny cut-scenes and strategy battles.
Still, Brutal Legend has a lot to offer before it becomes repetitive. If you love metal and you are a fan of Jack Black, I don't know how you could've passed on this title.

Brutal Legend is a mash up of a couple different genres, Action Adventure Open World RTS...yes, that many...
I'll start out with the graphics, it is a nice art style however the graphics really show the three years difference, even on higher resolutions the game doesn't look as crisp as others. There is hardly any customization in the options menu to try get a bit more beef out the graphics which is almost a must for PC ports.
The actual game play is nicely done though, as I said to begin with, there are four different genres mashed up here, Action Adventure is done very well, the hack and slash mechanics are basic, but the addition of guitar solos brings a whole new way of playing, allowing you to buff up your characters or deal damage to your foes.  The open world aspect is also done very well, the world seems huge, there are plenty of side quests to keep you busy throughout the story, however these aren't crucial for story or game progress elements, and they are purely there as additional things to do.  Finally, the RTS element, throughout the course of the game, you will take part in a number of grand scale battles, in which you have to manage your resources (fans in this case) and build an army in which you command using basic squad game controls, so follow, defend and attack. To me this seemed like the worst of the four though, it seemed a little clunky and out of place, I would much rather have played it without the strategy side.
The sound track and music in Brutal Legend is obviously going to be amazing. The game features 107 metal tracks from 75 different bands, ranging from Motörhead, Ozzy Osbourne, Kiss to Tenacious D as well as many more.  The main character is also voiced and based on Jack Black which also adds the comical side of things in too.
There isn't much difficulty in playing Brutal Legends, as long as you get to grips with the basics of the RTS elements, you won't find yourself having too many issues. The hack and slash parts are too easy at times, so the only challenge comes from the RTS, which is a shame, because I would of liked to have got a little more stuck into the combat and maybe the addition of extra combos.
The game length is very respectable, I normally try to complete as many of the side missions I can in these types of games, so it took me almost thirty five hours to complete it fully, so it is a pretty chunky game, time wise.
I had a few minor technical issues, even though the game was running at a smooth 60 fps most of the time, it almost felt as if I was still playing at 30, not sure whether that was an issue with my rig or not though, I turned on v-sync and that seemed to make a little better, but not by much. I also wanted to play in windowed mode for a while because I had the wiki page open on my second screen, and this gave me numerous issues with the cursor in game, I would all of a sudden just get my desktop background because my mouse had wandered off screen into my task bar, or I would start to get hover-over tooltips for other shortcuts on my windows task bar randomly, all small issues that could of quite easily of been fixed.
My final recommendation for Brutal Legend is definitely give it a try, it might not be everyone's cup of tea, but I did have a lot of fun playing it, I mean, I did plunge thirty five hours of my life playing it...there is plenty of content and even just the sound track is worth some of your time, you can get the game at regular price for £10,99, but expect this to drop to as low as £2 in sales, and then you have yourself a real bargain.

Well, for an early access game, this is certainly a polished game in some regards. I wouldn't recommend buying the game unless you're either a RWBY fan or simply want to have early access to the game.
-Voice acting pays homage to the characters and isn't annoying.
-Combat is pretty fluid apart from a few animation bugs here and there.
-Characters remain true to RWBY.
-Music and environments are beautiful.
-Abilities and leveling up system is a nice factor to add to the game.
-Some of the subtitles are not able to keep up with later dialogue.
-Players who get the kill are the only one who get the EXP. It's a bit frustrating to do all the work only to get kill-stealed at the very end.
-There's no real sense of progression since the character level is dropped to 1 each time. You may be able to unlock some of the abilities in the skill tree for future playthroughs, but that really doesn't feel like a permanent change.
-Shooting projectiles with anyone other than Weiss is wonky and tends to miss.
Overall, it's a well put together game for early access. I'd like to see more levels, more abilities, actual character progression, and more difficulty to make the game truly enjoyable and immersive. As a RWBY fan, this is a game that I really do love despite the issues, and thus I will continue playing.

To start, it's an RWBY game.  If you like RWBY, you'll definitely appreciate that they have access to the real voices, that it seems aware of its own cult following, and that each character feels quite different and plays differently.
At the moment, it's really small, but it's got a lot of replayability, as long as you have a friend to play with.  They've said there will be more enemies and levels to come, and I definitely look forward to it.
The Skills system keeps things fresh by having a steady unlock system, that doesn't seem too grindy, and as the game grows larger, it will become even less of a grind.
My only complaint about the game is that monsters grant experience points based on last hitting, which means that the team can wind up with a huge variance in experience, and not from anything the player did wrong.  Yang's abilities makes this a lot harsher, as she tends to hit things for a truckload of damage in a wide area, while the rest of the crew is whittling it down; it lead to me being nearly a level behind Yang at the end of the game, despite having frequently done most of the damage as Ruby.
I would really appreciate an option that splits experience, or rewards assists at all.

TL;DR: Great potential, rough around the edges because early access.
It's a tactical realtime strategy where you control a squad of four soldiers. Each side has multiple players in charge of a squad each. The goal of each round is either to eliminate all enemy soldiers or to capture and hold victory points long enough to achieve victory.
The game reminded me of Close Combat series. There is no base building. Each round your commanding officer makes extra equipment available to you for a bit of customization, but beyond that there is not much you can do to customize your squad. The game is fairly tactical where the winner is determined by who is better at flanking the enemy and by grenades. Seriously, the grenades have played a very decisive role in every battle I've fought so far.
There is definitely great potential here, but the game is an early access game, no doubt about that. There is a lot polish missing, there are bugs with the camera system, matches not ending when they should, crashes, etc.
As of today there are also not many concurrent users. I've been able to find a game every time I played, but there seems to be just enough people to populate one North America server at any given time. One little gripe I have is the time it takes to play again after your squad gets wiped out (and this will happen a lot when you first start). You go into spectator mode when that happens and wait until the round is resolved. Maybe if you could join another game while waiting, it would feel better but 1) there usually is not another populated game room as mentioned above, and 2) the game crashed every single time on me when trying to leave the game room.
So all in all it's good fun when you're on a good run. Patience is advised at other times.

I love the very detailed map of this game, the amount of units it offers and the ability to play from 1936 into the future.
there are however some gamebreaking bugs, most notably the game becomes a crawl after about 10 years ingame, which makes further progression extremely slow at upwards of 20 seconds per ingame day.
Also, the game does not offer a realistic diplomatic AI in my opinion, in the cold war scenario you can declare war on a NATO member without the rest of NATO declaring war on you in turn. Alliances in general dont mean much.
A third problem I have with the game is the very inactive industrial AI, that makes it possible for the player to economically outgrow AI nations easily without much effort.
Due to these major problems, I originally gave the game a thumbs down, but as the dev hints in his response here, that might have been slightly unfair considering I spent well over 300 hours ingame at the time, and have spent over 400 by now. I do see how it is unfair of me to give the game a thumbs down after 400 hours of enjoying it, so I change it to a thumbs up at this point. If you want to support a passionate small Developer team, consider buying this game, but be aware that it is by no means flawless.
Since Battlegoat has a new game in the making (Supreme Ruler Great War), I hope that these major issues will be adressed, so we can have an even greater Supreme Ruler game, and I am looking forward to spending hundreds of hours in it again.

Ok, so after completing the game once, and halfway through new game+ mode I can clearly review the game. First of all, they did not stray far from the human revolution formula. They chose the city of prague (Czech Republic) for the main city hub where you get all of your side quests from.
The distopian society of a plausable near future prague is something anyone can imagine and probably what would happen when augmentation becomes a reality in the near future.
There are microtransactions but they really dont matter. I see many people whining about them, and the day 1 dlc that can only be used on one game... New Game+ keeps all of your praxis kits and inventory from the previous game, and gives you more praxis kits (praxis kits are levels for those that have never played deus ex human revolution). So buying the microtransactions is not only optional, but a waste of money. Just play through the game once, and you are golden for the next playthrough.
They further increased the skills/abilities Adam has, this time. They integrated the peps from human revolution into his arm, for this game, so only the ammo takes up inventory space. They added a blade cannon arm, and taser arm, as well as a quick dash/blink to a targeted location for further stealth options. They also increased the challenge with the enemies by introducing new ammo types for weapons. Armor piercing rounds strip armor but normal rounds do more damage to flesh targets. Emp rounds can disable robots/cameras/exosuits, etc. But the tranq rifle has armor piercing capabilities if you hit the helmet.
It doesnt seem like they added as many weapon customization options, as they did in human revolution, which is a shame as I enjoyed upgrading my guns to become twice as powerful, but they did add a few new weapons and I did come across unique weapons as well. A unique sniper rifle and unique shotgun that you cannot get anywhere but the places I found them, meaning its worth exploring what does exist.
They further increased the stealth elements by allowing you to throw objects to distract a guard or lure the guards into a trap. This means you can play stealth a bit more tactically instead of just sneaking around and waiting till an enemy is isolated.
My biggest complaint is the game feels small and short, not a lot of areas to explore, etc. Prague, the thick russian/czech accents, and the distopian society of the czechs republic gets tiring and old, fairly quickly.
It does not have multiplayer, I am not sure what the other reviewers are speaking of. It has a steam leaderboard but is solely a single player experience. It gets old and tiresome quite quickly. Its mostly just time trials and challenges. I would rather have had the developers work on another city hub or more single player quests but who knows, maybe it was a second design team that did the darknet areas.

First of all a disclaimer about my hours on record. I put in a lot of hours on Xbox 360 on this game when it came out. I received it for PC as part of a humble bundle and decided to revisit it.
Right from the start of the intro you will find Brutal Legend to be a funny, quirky game with great humour and good music. This is even more true if you have even an inkling of Hard Rock, Metal or Heavy Metal in your bones. The jokes are still funny and relevant even today, and the metal world you are presented with in the game is full of witty references and well thought out re-imaginings of what a metal world would look like.
The gameplay itself is a mix of hack-&-slash and strategy game, depending on what's going on. The main part of the game is a third person adventure where you cut down enemies and explore a sandbox world. There are boss battle type encounters later on that go over to the strategy gaming side. Both are executed well and do what you'd expect. A third component of the game is your car, which provides an easy way to travel in the game world and also allows for driving over stuff as you go which is amusing.
The game has a very metal soundtrack which, depending on your taste, should set the tone quite well and provides you with an enjoyable backdrop to the carnage. Besides the excellent voice acting of Jack Black as the main protagonist, there are some good guest appearances in the form of Ozzy Osbourne and Lemmy Kilmister.
Despite everything it has going for it, I have to admit that Brutal Legend's ultimate downfall is repetition. As fun as it is to drive around a well imagined metal world in your cool car with metal blazing, it just doesn't keep the game alive. The hacking and slashing becomes tiringly repetitive eventually, and eventually the only things that keep you playing are the funny cut-scenes and strategy battles.
Still, Brutal Legend has a lot to offer before it becomes repetitive. If you love metal and you are a fan of Jack Black, I don't know how you could've passed on this title.

Brutal Legend is a mash up of a couple different genres, Action Adventure Open World RTS...yes, that many...
I'll start out with the graphics, it is a nice art style however the graphics really show the three years difference, even on higher resolutions the game doesn't look as crisp as others. There is hardly any customization in the options menu to try get a bit more beef out the graphics which is almost a must for PC ports.
The actual game play is nicely done though, as I said to begin with, there are four different genres mashed up here, Action Adventure is done very well, the hack and slash mechanics are basic, but the addition of guitar solos brings a whole new way of playing, allowing you to buff up your characters or deal damage to your foes.  The open world aspect is also done very well, the world seems huge, there are plenty of side quests to keep you busy throughout the story, however these aren't crucial for story or game progress elements, and they are purely there as additional things to do.  Finally, the RTS element, throughout the course of the game, you will take part in a number of grand scale battles, in which you have to manage your resources (fans in this case) and build an army in which you command using basic squad game controls, so follow, defend and attack. To me this seemed like the worst of the four though, it seemed a little clunky and out of place, I would much rather have played it without the strategy side.
The sound track and music in Brutal Legend is obviously going to be amazing. The game features 107 metal tracks from 75 different bands, ranging from Motörhead, Ozzy Osbourne, Kiss to Tenacious D as well as many more.  The main character is also voiced and based on Jack Black which also adds the comical side of things in too.
There isn't much difficulty in playing Brutal Legends, as long as you get to grips with the basics of the RTS elements, you won't find yourself having too many issues. The hack and slash parts are too easy at times, so the only challenge comes from the RTS, which is a shame, because I would of liked to have got a little more stuck into the combat and maybe the addition of extra combos.
The game length is very respectable, I normally try to complete as many of the side missions I can in these types of games, so it took me almost thirty five hours to complete it fully, so it is a pretty chunky game, time wise.
I had a few minor technical issues, even though the game was running at a smooth 60 fps most of the time, it almost felt as if I was still playing at 30, not sure whether that was an issue with my rig or not though, I turned on v-sync and that seemed to make a little better, but not by much. I also wanted to play in windowed mode for a while because I had the wiki page open on my second screen, and this gave me numerous issues with the cursor in game, I would all of a sudden just get my desktop background because my mouse had wandered off screen into my task bar, or I would start to get hover-over tooltips for other shortcuts on my windows task bar randomly, all small issues that could of quite easily of been fixed.
My final recommendation for Brutal Legend is definitely give it a try, it might not be everyone's cup of tea, but I did have a lot of fun playing it, I mean, I did plunge thirty five hours of my life playing it...there is plenty of content and even just the sound track is worth some of your time, you can get the game at regular price for £10,99, but expect this to drop to as low as £2 in sales, and then you have yourself a real bargain.

I'd like to be clear on something first: as of right now, the game is nigh unplayable(edit: with the most recent patch, framerate is up to playable on all settings, which vastly improves playability and experience) on my computer due to framrate issues. Even on potato settings, the game is jittery as hell, and I have a GTX 860M which should be able to run a game of this graphical quality with ease (with fast paced combat, a good framerate really improves the experience). Also, the game is very early in development and lacks any real polish either in the UI or the combat. So why the recommendation, you ask? Well, I'm a huge fan of the series, and in particular I think they've done a fantastic job setting up a universe where a game like this has the potential to be INCREDIBLE. The show delivers each character with a unique weapon and combat style, which would make for a perfect cooperative game with players that take on different roles and mesh with each other to balance out strengths and weaknesses. The only thing that the devs need is the time and money to create it. Should you buy the game right now if you've never heard of RWBY? Probably not (unless you are very interested in the final product and think you'll buy the game eventually). Should you buy the game if you're a fan of the show and want to support the game, whether or not the final product meets expectations? Yes. I 100% encourage you to throw money at the things you love.

This game is deceptively good, with "deceptive" being the operative word. I say that because the game really does not try to entice you with its UI or presentation, but underneath is a wonderful simulation that takes a while to fully appreciate.
My first game was about 15  hours. Typical stuff - build up the economy, go to war, easy win, get bored, uninstall after a few weeks in your steam library. That was over an year ago. This week, I had an itch to play the game again for some reason and started a longer campaign. I did the same things - build up the economy, build some resource buildings, annex some neighbors etc. But then I did something I almost never do - continue playing after you think you have won.
This was when I discovered how much this game really has to offer. I started to understand the tech tree and gun for specific techs, I started to understand how the game models inflation and GDP growth, I started to fight wars in the supply map-mode, I started to build different unit types rather than just spamming tanks.
The more I play, the more I fall in love with it. Most AAA titles last for around 30 hours. With SR, I am just beginning to appreciate the game at that mark. Of course, this game is not for everyone - it's a grand strategy title. But if you are the kind of person who likes to play Paradox games, or thought that Civ 4 was the best Civ, or still plays Capitalism 2 or any of the Railroad Tycoon titles, or loves Factorio, then you WILL love this.

2: Multiplayer loads players in order, So the 1st and 2nd players generally load in pretty quickly, However the 3rd and 4th players can take upto 5 minutes before they can load the fully.
3: On atleast 2 levels, we had door blocks just randomly stop working in dungeons for every player, - work around, Mine them.

This game sits at about a 6 / 10 in execution and 8/10 in concept for me, but there are a few things that really make me hesitant to recommend this game.
The look and feel of the game is pretty spot-on with a nice mix of interface, simple combat mechanics, and easy building with extended reach, but the combat is a little too simple. It's only a step above standard Minecraft button-mashing, with a bit of dodging thrown in.
The world-size is another big drawback for me. The game is set on islands, rather than a continuous world, and each island only varies slightly in appearance, with a couple tiers of the same dirt-sand-rock base materials and a few different ores / gems in each tier. Like many other people have noted, the appearance of most of these blocks depends on the world you're in when you place them, not when you picked them up, so a jungle-skinned dirt block will revert to simple grassland if you bring it back to an early-tier world, and vice-versa. Loading screens are a bit of a pain if you world-hop frequently.
This game could have been something more than just another build-craft clone, but the lack of depth and almost pointless exploration of worlds beyond that of getting to one of the few new tiers makes it feel grindy and quite boring. It's like progressing through a mediocre RPG only to get stuck with a few trinkets and a set of Mega-Blocks, instead of either intriguing end-game worldbuilding. It's easy to compare it negatively to Minecraft in its current state, but if you remember the struggles that game had at first alpha release, Portal Knights is still a cut above.
I hope this game will get some of the ongoing-dev and modding that made Minecraft into a fun time-waster, but I fear it will get neglected as just another clone.

Welp, I've been pushed over the edge into writing this review in lieu of recent events which can be read in any other review posted recently. This review will cover actual issues the game has instead of chewing out take2 (though they do deserve to be chewed out, but, at this point I feel anything I'd say has already been said).
I will begin by saying this game was entertaining for a short while. It has nice graphics, pretty fluid gameplay, and they like to keep online updated which they've done for free instead of having you pay for dlc so I commend them for doing that. Unfortunately that's all the praise I have for this game.
I will begin ripping this thing apart with single-player mode. Unlike other GTA games I've played (mostly Vice City and San Andreas, which are arguably the best 2 in the series) the game is a cakewalk. When I play GTA I want to be challenged to the point of rage-quitting then coming back to it a short while later (anyone remember Demolition Man from VC? or what about the damn RC plane mission in SA?). Not to mention this game feels smaller than SA with only 1 city and the countryside. The story is decent, some of the characters are great, but all of that is overshadowed by how easily one breezes through the story. This isn't a GTA game, it's got the look and some of the humor of a GTA game, but it lacks the soul-crushingly difficult mission(s) that gives each of the other GTA's I've played their unique charm.
Now on to the real killer for me: online mode. Online mode is a great concept, but, horribly executed. It's nice to be able to play with others and progress from having your first vehicle you stole to having a few houses, a business, multiple full garages full of customized cars, etc. It would also be nice if that were possible in a reasonable amount of time. Unfortunately, it's not. If you're like me and refuse to do any microtransactions so you end up grinding the resourses, online takes eons. They price things so exorbitantly high that most players just end up buying the shark cards, making it one of the cardinal sins of gaming: pay-to-win. Online, at this point has become just a money grab. Additionally, online mode is riddled with players who bend the rules. Some of these people are nice, but most I've come across are just trolls. Then there's the seemingly endless supply of rule-abiding trolls. Those who don't circumvent the rules with additional tools, but rather use their equipment to wreak havoc on honest players. I understand that some of this is fine, fun even, but when it's every server then it makes it unbearable. Also, you can forget about acomplishing anything in your own private server, the freeroam events are disabled, thus forcing you to play in a troll-riddled hellhole of a place just trying to accomplish anything to make some decent cash so you don't have to spend real money on those damn shark cards. As far as running the MC or CEO stuff, most people don't want to bother with it unless they get the highest cut, so everyone runs their own stuff rather than working together. So many of the practices with online mode are very anti-cooperative play, which is in direct contrast to the real world of crime where you have people working together to achieve things. So even as a crime simulator this game fails.
Now to break my own rule I gave myself at the beginning of this... talking about the Take 2 legal action against a certain modding tool.
Mods are what made single-player mode bearable. You could make it difficult, quirky, grimey, and downright weird. But that's the beauty of mods in games. Companies like Take 2 think of mods as ways to break rules and ruin their games, but that's not what modding, real modding, is. Modding, for all intents and purposes, is a way for people to enjoy the product that the company has released long past its vanilla playability allows. Furthermore, it's a form of creative expression allowing people to view the game as a wonderfully built canvas to unleash their creative desires and share with others. Modding brings me back to the good 'ol days of gaming; before all the extreme budgets, corporate buyouts, playing it safe with releases (which this game is... dumbed down to appeal to the widest audience). All gaming is nowadays, seems like it's about making the most money rather than providing quality entertainment. I remember a time when games used to be innovative, groundbreaking even, people used to push the limits, take risks, succeed and fail. But that was the beauty of it. If a game failed it was because it was a bad game, not because they didn't spend enough on marketing (in the beginning anyway... this did eventually become the reason many games do fail). Modding allows people to do what those crazy fools did back in the day: push the limits, cause paradigm shifts, and create quality entertainment. Many of the games which have brought massive loads of cash in for some of these companies began as mods for other games, so it's sickening to see companies doing things like Take2 has done to the modding community. Basically what they're saying is: "Your ideas are trash, allow us to give you what we say you want" rather than being a decent company and providing us with what we actually want. We get the same 15 games every year because it reaches the widest audience, mods are there to make the more nuanced alterations that fit smaller segments within the market, allowing us to turn the game into what we want. Some may claim that it sullies the original work, my response to them is to wake up and realize that it's just a money game now when it comes to the big companies.
Back on topic a bit: Take2's legal action against a certain modding tool is appalling. They claim it's to prevent modders online, which would be fine since it's their servers, people may have conflicting mods, there's no way to manage them all, among other issues. However, this particular tool doesn't allow for any sort of online modding (not to mention the modders who are online are rarely punished anyway). So why is it they claim it's to prevent online modding when clearly it's not? The answer is simple, long ago they said that they'll allow modding in offline mode, it's your game so you should be able to turn it into something you enjoy playing. They say it's to prevent online modding so they don't have to go back on their original promise, though actions speak louder than words and it's clear they have indeed gone back on their word. Why do they want to eliminate offline modding? Well that's a simple question to answer. As stated earlier, mods allow players to enjoy games long past their original playability value. In the case of GTA5 once you beat the story and quests there's nothing left to do so naturally you head online. Mods allowed peole to continue to play offline long after the story ended which was no good for Take2. Once you remove the Mods, the playability factor is gone thus forcing people to play online. Once online, they realize the exorbitant prices for most things and either quit playing the game altogether, attempt to grind it out, or in the case of most people, buy the shark cards.
This kind of anti-consumer behavior cannot stand. Not to mention the game isn't even that spectacular and is riddled with issues that they don't appear to care enough about to fix. So no, I do not recommend this game.

I am a huge Diablo fan and I've never played this game. I've always rejected it as a cheap diablo clone.
I picked it up because it was on sale for like nothing. I had it over a year and never played it. But once Diablo 3 turned out to be a huge disappointment, I gave this game a try. And oh boy is it awesome.
It surpassed my expectation by far! I couldn't stop playing it.
It does almost everything better than Diablo 3.
The game just plays and feels great.
I really love the free skilltree and character development, you can do whatever you want.
You can choose every difficulty right from the start.
The Elite difficulty offers a great challenge, right  from level 1 and it wont get easy until very very late into the game.
The game world itself is huge and feels alive.
The towns are full of merchants, gambler, enchanters and other NPCS.
The over world and dungeons are filled with hordes of monsters and many bosses that offer a great challenge.
The Mapworks offer a unlimited amount of random generated dungeons. Which is just awesome.
And the best thing. The loot system. Every player gets his OWN loot. There are hundreds of items with 5 quality tiers
And set items.
Enough with the good stuff, the game lacks story. If you don't watch out you miss the story. And the story is also pretty short you can get through the game in 20h or even less. But it has a New Game+ feature so its no that bad.
The multiplayer loading time can  get really really REALLY long. I don't know why but sometimes it takes like 5~10 minutes! to move from  map A to B.
The game saves on your local hard drive so you run  into a lot of cheater when playing multiplayer.
Only 4 character classes. That's always a letdown for me but...

New mods are coming out almost everyday and you even get the developer kit to create your own mods.

Synergies is the best Mod  for TL2. Its an overhaul mod that changes almsot everything.
Salan, the mods creator put alot of work into this awesome mod.

I recommend this game to everyone that like RPG, mod and co-op/multiplayer games.
