- I never felt as if assets were repeated too much
- The game never felt super repetitive which is really good considering all you do is crawl and shoot
- The AI is surprsingly good and has very few issues
- There is a lot to do in each mission
- Each mission is pretty long
- There is a lot of content
- Relocation mechanic makes it seem realistic and does a good job immersing you
Things I didn't like:
- Way too many tanks
- On the highest difficulty the AI can hear your steps from probably about 40 feet away
- If you're spotted on the highest difficulty you're ♥♥♥♥ed
- The enemy has laser aim and never misses
- Somehow MP40s are better than Sniper Rifles when in the hands of everyone but you
- All SMGs you touch dissolve into♥♥♥♥♥♥and the bullets hit everything but your target
- Sometimes my deaths were complete horse♥♥♥♥♥♥br>- The character moves and handles like a tank

- Some missions are way too long and seem to drag on (It took me 2.5 hours to beat one level on max difficulty)
- The last mission is just impossible to go undetected unless you want to spend 3 hours dicking around

I gave it a shot because of the low price, but it's a bit unpolished. I feel like it was worth the price to give it a go, but Steam asks if I recommend it or not and I have to say no.
It has an interesting art style and concept, but everything about the gameplay feels slippery and unrefined. Movement feels like you're on ice, the player character keeps moving after you let go of a key which is frustrating, especially when you fall off a cliff (there's no fall damage, but you have to jump back up again). Levels are uninspired, there's no value to the verticality and not much to reward exploration, levels being too small to really explore anyway.
Attacks are fiddly, it's the sort of game that queues up commands so if you spam attack it will sit there and do as many attacks as you clicked the mouse for before you can do anything, which you can get used to but sometimes the game just doesn't seem to register commands. Pressing a key to turn and face an enemy often wont, why I couldn't say. I've read from the developer that attacks will hit when you have stamina, and you swing the weapon and the blade passes through the hitbox of an enemy, but I have witnessed on multiple occasions attacks with full stamina making contact and doing ... nothing.
I found no real way of healing, it says in the control scheme to press R to eat corpses and I spammed the♥♥♥♥♥♥of the R key and ... nothing. Corpses lay on the ground uneaten and my health unrestored. I got one pickup which regens health at 3 points every ten seconds you don't get hit, which makes for mind numbingly boring gameplay waiting for your health to crawl back up. I fail to see how you can get through more than a few levels of this game with the glitchy attack animations and no heals.
So what you have here is a good concept that I don't exactly regret trying, but I wouldn't recommend buying it.

First of all a disclaimer about my hours on record. I put in a lot of hours on Xbox 360 on this game when it came out. I received it for PC as part of a humble bundle and decided to revisit it.
Right from the start of the intro you will find Brutal Legend to be a funny, quirky game with great humour and good music. This is even more true if you have even an inkling of Hard Rock, Metal or Heavy Metal in your bones. The jokes are still funny and relevant even today, and the metal world you are presented with in the game is full of witty references and well thought out re-imaginings of what a metal world would look like.
The gameplay itself is a mix of hack-&-slash and strategy game, depending on what's going on. The main part of the game is a third person adventure where you cut down enemies and explore a sandbox world. There are boss battle type encounters later on that go over to the strategy gaming side. Both are executed well and do what you'd expect. A third component of the game is your car, which provides an easy way to travel in the game world and also allows for driving over stuff as you go which is amusing.
The game has a very metal soundtrack which, depending on your taste, should set the tone quite well and provides you with an enjoyable backdrop to the carnage. Besides the excellent voice acting of Jack Black as the main protagonist, there are some good guest appearances in the form of Ozzy Osbourne and Lemmy Kilmister.
Despite everything it has going for it, I have to admit that Brutal Legend's ultimate downfall is repetition. As fun as it is to drive around a well imagined metal world in your cool car with metal blazing, it just doesn't keep the game alive. The hacking and slashing becomes tiringly repetitive eventually, and eventually the only things that keep you playing are the funny cut-scenes and strategy battles.
Still, Brutal Legend has a lot to offer before it becomes repetitive. If you love metal and you are a fan of Jack Black, I don't know how you could've passed on this title.

Brutal Legend is a mash up of a couple different genres, Action Adventure Open World RTS...yes, that many...
I'll start out with the graphics, it is a nice art style however the graphics really show the three years difference, even on higher resolutions the game doesn't look as crisp as others. There is hardly any customization in the options menu to try get a bit more beef out the graphics which is almost a must for PC ports.
The actual game play is nicely done though, as I said to begin with, there are four different genres mashed up here, Action Adventure is done very well, the hack and slash mechanics are basic, but the addition of guitar solos brings a whole new way of playing, allowing you to buff up your characters or deal damage to your foes.  The open world aspect is also done very well, the world seems huge, there are plenty of side quests to keep you busy throughout the story, however these aren't crucial for story or game progress elements, and they are purely there as additional things to do.  Finally, the RTS element, throughout the course of the game, you will take part in a number of grand scale battles, in which you have to manage your resources (fans in this case) and build an army in which you command using basic squad game controls, so follow, defend and attack. To me this seemed like the worst of the four though, it seemed a little clunky and out of place, I would much rather have played it without the strategy side.
The sound track and music in Brutal Legend is obviously going to be amazing. The game features 107 metal tracks from 75 different bands, ranging from Motörhead, Ozzy Osbourne, Kiss to Tenacious D as well as many more.  The main character is also voiced and based on Jack Black which also adds the comical side of things in too.
There isn't much difficulty in playing Brutal Legends, as long as you get to grips with the basics of the RTS elements, you won't find yourself having too many issues. The hack and slash parts are too easy at times, so the only challenge comes from the RTS, which is a shame, because I would of liked to have got a little more stuck into the combat and maybe the addition of extra combos.
The game length is very respectable, I normally try to complete as many of the side missions I can in these types of games, so it took me almost thirty five hours to complete it fully, so it is a pretty chunky game, time wise.
I had a few minor technical issues, even though the game was running at a smooth 60 fps most of the time, it almost felt as if I was still playing at 30, not sure whether that was an issue with my rig or not though, I turned on v-sync and that seemed to make a little better, but not by much. I also wanted to play in windowed mode for a while because I had the wiki page open on my second screen, and this gave me numerous issues with the cursor in game, I would all of a sudden just get my desktop background because my mouse had wandered off screen into my task bar, or I would start to get hover-over tooltips for other shortcuts on my windows task bar randomly, all small issues that could of quite easily of been fixed.
My final recommendation for Brutal Legend is definitely give it a try, it might not be everyone's cup of tea, but I did have a lot of fun playing it, I mean, I did plunge thirty five hours of my life playing it...there is plenty of content and even just the sound track is worth some of your time, you can get the game at regular price for £10,99, but expect this to drop to as low as £2 in sales, and then you have yourself a real bargain.

Yes, yes, there are lot of problems with the game, its the early access, calm yourselves :) But it's still great and if you are a fan, which is probably 95% of the people who bought this game, you'll definitely enjoy it.
Grimm Eclipse is a beat 'em up/hack and slash game, so the main goal in the game(at the moment) is just beating up grimm(monsters)  and complete the mission that they have right now. That means that there is a lot of spam clicking involved(which sounds like a beat after clicking a bunch of times XD), and if that doesn't suit you, probably should not get this game then. It's based on the show RWBY which is sponsored and produced by Rooster Teeth. If you want to know about all the characters and why the hell they are killing these monster I suggest you watch the show on the Rooster Teeth site or on their YouTube channel.
Currently you can only play 4 characters, Ruby, Weiss, Blake, and Yang(team RWBY all the way!) but I am pretty sure they will add more characters like team JNPR later as they keep developing the game as well as more missions. The character models and animation is pretty good and the moves so far are almost on the same level as the show. The weapons too match the show, as you know the epic weapons are one of the things that makes RWBY amazing(a scythe and a rifle gun? BRILLIANT!!! Gloves that are also a shotgun? GENUIS!!!!)
Since this game is early access, it is 100% understandable that there are bugs and crashes. (I keep getting crashes for some reason) I also think the requirement for the game is a little high as the game kinda lags a big (I don't know if I just have a bad computer or what, but it is slightly laggy.) Also guns are kinda useless in this version because they do not do a lot of damage and are extremely hard to aim. Some other drawbacks to this game is the fact that it gets repetative, well I mean IT IS a beat 'em up grinding type of ordeal, but I feel like it has a lot of potential, for example maybe a story mode or arena mode that possibly might be implemented into the game. That would be AWESOME if there were multiplayer PVP battle modes.  I am looking forward to the next updates :D
Overall, I still think this game is great and has a lot of potential to get even better. As for buying it right now, I would say no because it is still in early access. Buy it when there is more content. If you are a extreme fan of RWBY, I would say buy it to help support the team who is creating this game, or just because you need to the see the bae Ruby, Weiss, Blake or Yang or anyone else in the show, whoever your bae is in this show.  I'm not judging you :)
Basically don't buy yet if you are not a fan, buy if you are a fan and bae is in the game right now :) Or if you want to support the developers, that too.

Divided We Fall (2016) is the spiritual successor of Chain of Command (1999) by 2AM Games, Call of Combat v1 (2002) and Call of Combat v2 (2008) by KAVA Game Studio. The game takes place during World War II. DWF is a real-time strategy game in which each player controls 4 soldiers with the same basic loadout in battles between Axis and Allies.
The gameplay is advanced and requires some learning as it depends quite heavily on the usage of hotkeys. There are plenty of tactical opportunities for each map, which makes it difficult to master the game completely.
The chain of command plays a large role in the game as the Commanding Officer (CO) for each team is the only player who shares all teammates field of view, while the rest only share the lower ranking players field of view. The CO is also the only person who can issue orders and hand out special weapons such as machine guns and snipers.
The ranks are not only determined by the PPS (experience) you've collected during battles, but also your efficiency, which includes kill/death rate, assists, captures and so on.
The army groups are the clans or regiments of the game. There's a dedicated system for communities who wants to become established in-game. The AGs can participate in the monthly competitions to earn points and officer ranks to hand out to their members.

As many of you may know, Surgeon Simulator has been around for a while. But, with the release of the Inside Donald Trump update, I feel like I should make a review, so f**k it, i'm doing a review.
I will look at the game in it's own merits, ignoring anything else about the online community or the people who made the game, so I can get a clear picture.
SURGEON SIMULATOR 2013
This game is a surgery simulation game. Before you play the game, hoping to learn how to do brain transplants IRL, this game is NOT to be taken seriously.
The game puts you in the shoes of a surgeon named Nigel Burke, who must perform life-saving surgeries on various patients, including: Bob, The Heavy, Gworb and Donald Trump. You control the game using the A W E R and Space keys, controlling all the fingers on the hand. You move the hand with your mouse, you press left click to lower the hand and you press right click to rotate the hand. Alright, now that that's out the way, time for an overview of the game!
The game includes 3 surgeries: Heart Transplant, Double Kidney Transplant and Brain Transplant. Each surgery can be played under certain scenarios, including in the operating theatre, in the back of an ambulance and in space. The A&E DLC adds 2 more surgeries, Eye and Teeth transplants and allows you to perform surgery while running down a hospital corridor.
SURGERIES:
Heart Transplant: Take the old heart out and put a new one in. What happens to the other organs doesn't matter.
Double Kidney Transplant: Take the old kidneys out and put new ones in. Again, what happens to the other organs doesn't matter. NOTE: Both kindeys need to be present. If you accidentally lose one of the kidneys out the back of the ambulance, you're f**ked.
Brain Transplant: Take the old brain out and put a new one in. Note: If you're using the circular saw or the drill to break the skull, DON'T HIT THE BRAIN. It will cause severe blood loss.
Eye Transplant(A&E ONLY): Take the old eyes out and put new ones in. You have more breathing room in terms of donor organs, as there are 2 containers, each with 6 eyes. You can give Bob brown eyes, blue eyes or even a smiley face or an 8 ball.
Teeth Transplant(A&E ONLY): Take the rotten teeth out and put new ones in. You have a large number of teeth to put in, so losing the teeth is no big deal. Note: You should only knock out the rotten teeth, as for every good tooth you knock out, you will have to replace it.
SCENARIOS:
Operating Theatre: Standard. Nothing's crazy here.
Corridor(A&E ONLY): You're running down the hospital corridor. You start with no tools or donor organs, but as you run down the corridor, small trolleys with assorted tools, donor organs and other things will come and go. You can get multiple donor organs in this mode, so losing the donor organs is no big deal. However, you might want to hold onto things, as there have been many times when I have waited 3 minutes for a donor organ to appear on one of the trolleys.
Ambulance: You're in the back of a MOVING ambulance. This mode is the msot crazy, as when the ambulance steers and goes over bumps, your tools will go flying everywhere. Sometimes, the doors on the back of the ambulance will open, allowing things to fall out onto the road. Make sure you don't lose the donor organs!
Space: You're operating in SPAAAAAAAAAAACE! Everything floats around, as you would expect. Make sure you don't bump too many things around, as those objects tend to collide with other objects, which will then bump into other objects, causing everything in the theatre to go flying everywhere.
SPECIAL SURGERIES:
Meet the Medic: You are the Medic operating on the Heavy, like in the TF2 Meet the Medic promotional video! You must perform an Uber Heart Transplant. All the tools have been replaced with TF2 items too.
Alien Surgery: You're operating on an alien named Gworb! Everything floats around like in Space mode. When you start the surgery, you must perform one of 6 transplants: Gobbleshaft, Gavichal, Pewdsball, Birgirspallex, Robbaloraz or a Cubed Trangrifier. All of these organs(not the Gobbleshaft) are named after YouTubers that have played the game.
Gavichal: Gavin and Micheal from Rooster Teeth
Pewdsball: PewDiePie
Birgirspallex: Birgirpall
Robbaloraz: Robbaz
Cubed Trangrifier: NerdCubed
Inside Donald Trump(A&E ONLY): You must perform a heart transplant on Donald Trump! Many of the tools are absent and some have been replaced by gold versions. There are exclusive items, such as the Trump Steak, Trump Vodka and the Trump Tower. There is also a Medical Bill. The more you hurt Trump, the higher the bill goes. Instead of giving him a normal heart, you can give him a heart of gold or a heart of stone. It's your choice.
Final Thoughts: The game can be very hard to get into at first, due to the difficult control scheme. Once you get used to the controls, the game is actually quite fun. Beating all the surgeries, earning all the achievements and getting A++ rating on all the surgeries can be quite challenging. The music is great too. If you download the game, you can listen to the soundtrack in the music player. One thing I didn't like is how some of the achievements are glitched. For some of them, you must disable the A&E DLC, earn the achievement and then enable the DLC again. Some of the achievements are REALLY frustrating too. One achievement needs you to drug yourself(jab yourself with the green syringe, this will f**k up your vision) and jam a scalpel into the electrical socket(inverts the controls) and then complete the surgery. It's ridiculously furstrating.
Final Score: The game does many things right, but still fails with a few things, so I give Surgeon Simulator 2013 8.6/10. The DLC is worth it too, so pick up both if you can.

I understand why there are mixed reviews, but this game is brilliant on several levels.  If you understand what you are getting with this game then there is no disappointment.  Everyone expects what you get in most other games.  They expect to play all aspects of the game and access everything.  This game is not designed that way on purpose.  If you are expecting to grind for every weapon and vehicle imaginable then yes, it does take forever without actually spending money.  I have spent $10 dollars and I have everything I want.  This is because I choose to specialize only a couple characters and I don't mind grinding a lot to earn the rest of what I want.  This brings me to my points about why this game is great.
1. Specialization.  Making it difficult to obtain weapons and vehicles means that players are forced to specialize in a certain area.  For example, I had to make specific decisions about what kind of player I want to be instead of just getting every piece of equipment.  This is an excellent aspect of the game, because it means that strategy is incorporated into the game play.  If I only choose to be mobile and support infantry with a light tank then I am not going to go charging into a line of enemy tank destroyers.  This is the first game that I have experienced that has this level of planning required.
2. Front lines.  The use of tactics on each battlefield is always critical and ever changing.  You can witness "front lines" develop on every battle map and many times there is more than one.  Being able to shape the enemies formations on the battlefield with well coordinated fire or witness your own line crumble on one flank is so interesting.  Also, not everyone is the main effort.  Support efforts are just as important.  Team members assist with repairing, supplies, and transporation efforts as one great effort to achieving the goals of the battle and the overall war campaign.
3.  Campaign strategy.  I have never seen a game that incorporates such a large scale war where every battle helps to determine the outcome.  Once you start purchasing your own assault teams with credits you have earned makes you more invested in the outcome of the war.  This level of higher strategy mixed with the lower level tactics needed at each battle truly makes the overall experience seem truly bigger than an individual soldier, but at the same time you know that the indivudual actions help to shape that outcome.
The bottom line is this:  Yes there have been issues with crashing and I have experienced the occasional hacker, but the overall concept and execuation of this game is great.  This is not a game for those that just like to run and gun.  This game requires time, planning, and patience, but I think that this is why it is great.  There are plenty of other games out there for deathmatch style run and gun, so if that's what you are looking for then look elsewhere

I've enjoyed this game overall so far, yet definitely see room for improvement. One minor technical issue that turns me off is the lack of true full-screen, another is the sometimes too-narrow spaces in levels that one can fall through, yet not jump back up. Pretty good overall, though.
First, the pros:
Combat is paced well, and on reading the dev's responses in other reviews, is made in a logical fashion.
The cave painting style looks pretty cool, though it would be nice if the borders/terrain looked more natural, like the curve of an actual cave. Perhaps in that vein, some set spawn points could be larger groups of paintings in the background/foreground that enter the arena and diminish as you kill them off?
The money management system increases the difficulty in a good way.
Bonfires.
Now the cons:
The music isn't bad, but it gets repetitive. More variety (not outside the genre, mind. I mean more death metal) would be nice.
The endurance bar is hard to keep track of during combat, at least for me.
The spawns of the enemies are unintuitive, but since they are meant to be reactionary, that makes more sense. Doesn't mean I particularly like have one taking a swing at me as it spawns, though...
I'll add more to this review after I've done a few more runs, just to work out whether I suck (probably) or the game needs more tweaking (what game doesn't?).

It's a pretty average game. The Graphics and world building are top notch. The combat and balancing was unique but not fully engaging. It became monotonous and I just ran past most of the fights towards the end. I suggest this game to people who really like RPGs. If you don't like RPGs, I don't think there's much here you'll enjoy.
The story and writing is a bit inconsistent. The sidequests are written brilliantly while the main story is rather dry. The combat isn't bad, but it's not good. It was never balanced properly. So your character will be OP for about 90% of the game no matter what you pick. Combat is more of a pacing mechanic than a  meaty gameplay element. You'll find yourself simply running past enemies to fulfill quests since enemies become time sinks rather than challenges.
It was the quintessential mediocre RPG. Not too good, not too bad, with proper pacing so you never get stuck doing something you don't want to do.

Its pretty much Oblivion + WoW. The world is huge, especially with the DLCs, and I think the killmoves are awesome. Basically, the graphics are more fantasy-like than Skyrim, which was based on realism. This is totally like Oblivion except... bigger and better!
As a matter of fact, I think it's more like Fable than Oblivion. Since it's a 3rd person RPG based in a fantasy world with non-realistic graphics.

I am extremely impressed with this game, in spite of it's one major flaw which is that it can be easy to "Overlevel" your character quickly. I am somewhat disappointed that there is a level cap, unlike Skyrim, but I believe this could be remedied if any new DLC decided to scale enemies to the character's level, rather than hard lock them by regions explored. At that point, a level cap becomes moot, since enemies would always scale to the character's level and thus keep the challenge high (or at least higher than what is current.
The game reminds me of Skyrim in it's use of combat and quests, but the story is deep and complex, and there are literally hours of exploration for those who take the time to do so.
It is the story and the versatility of character development which really drew me in. The parallels to Skyrim are quite high, and I believe that Amalur actually was developed concurrently but released about eight months prior to that other great game.
All in all, you cannot go wrong with this game. Especially at $20.00 or even lower during weekend or mid-week madness specials. (I picked up Amalur and all DLC content for $9.99 during one such special). It is easily work twice as much in terms of content and play time. (Heck, just look at my hours played! :) )
If you haven't seen the hundred+ other positive reviews and decided to buy this one, the let this review be your impetus! BUY THIS GAME! It's awesome :)

Short Review: Tekken 7 is one of the Best Tekkens to be released, if not, the Best Tekken. Is Kind of short on game modes, but does everything else almost perfectly (Online Play, Gameplay, Visuals, etc).  Rating: 9.5/10
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Detailed Review: Lets get this out of the way first.. I go as far back as Tekken 3 regarding experience with this Series. Although, I never got the chance to really get into 4 and 5, but have really been playing it every since Tekken 6. So when I say that this is potentially the BEST Tekken to be released to date, take my word for it.
As a Tekken game, it gives you Almost everything that you could want! It gives you some of the most balanced GAMEPLAY that I have seen in years regarding a fighting game (There is no "OMG so and so is broken"). They brought in a good balance of both new and returning characters that will for sure make you spend hours in the Lab trying to understand the ins and outs of them, at the same time still feeling as home if youve played previous games. The STORY is kind of short (Which is made up with small side stories) but it had me glued to my chair until the very end. and the last fight is one that I was ALWAYS remember! SO INTENSE... ONLINE PLAY could be looked at as having few game modes (Personally "Player Matches" and "Ranked" Matches isnt a small list to me at all. I think we have been spoiled with games like Injustice 2, but thats my opinion), but the netcode is one of the best that I have ever used in a fighting game. and it also adds in a mode called "Tournament mode" where you actually get placed withing a tourney bracket to try and win in game prizes (Which i think is AWESOME). Practice mode has had some small additions added to it, which just adds to the game's polished feel. and last but not least, the one thing that long time tekken fans will probably complain about it the fact that this game lacks in having a variety of offline game modes, along with Arcade endings. Personally, when I play offline, its only to practice or play against people, so it doesnt really effect me. and yes, there isnt a TRUE tutorial mode but they actually go through things generally in story mode so I dont see what the complaints are about. But I will say this... regarding the arcade endings, that really shouldnt be a big deal. There are small side stories (granted it doenst touch on everyone) that will give you "endings." I think people are really overreacting when in response to "Character endings." and Music is CRAZY GOOD!!
Overall, GREAT Story (Kind of short but again is made up with character endings), gameplay is near perfect that makes you want to come back to play, online is near perfect (Gives you exactly what a fighting game should) Offline can be looked at as having very few modes, but for me its just fine. Visuals are stunning and the best by far in any Tekken game. Music is, again, some of the most enjoyable music that I have heard from a Tekken game.
Rating: 9.5/10

I greatly enjoy this game, but it's certainly not for everyone. The skill tree and classes are simple, easy to use, and you can change your skills on a dime without having to do anything.
I've seen a lot of people compare this game to minecraft but I would honestly compare it more closely to Terraria. The reason being there's a very clear set path for you to go down, despite it seeming so open, and once you beat a boss you willll unlock the next tier of materials to upgrade your equipment further. If there's ever a material you don't have or need in order to make better equipment and can't find it, then its not that the game is dumb and didn't spawn any for you, it's simply because you haven't gotten far enough to see that material.
Going off of that, the islands that you visit are procedurally generated, meaning you will always run into the same materials or the same flora as your first run through of the game, but the layout will more than likely be massively different, with the exception of a few set pieces.
I would talk about the multiplayer aspect, but honestly I haven't tried it. Reason being I've heard the multiplayer needs some work, and honestly, multiplayer isn't the reason I picked up this game. I was looking for a single player creative combat game that I could play casually and that's exactly what I got from this game, and I couldn't be happier.
Below I will put some bugs that I have found, but it could be simply that my computer needs a hardware update (which I'm currently saving money to do)
-- When I go into the steam overlay (for me I have to press tab+shift) I can no longer scroll through my equipment bar and I can't switch items from my inventory to my euipment bar. I've noticed that if I press shift one or two times it usually fixes it.
-- The other day there was an event with some spores roaming the place, I was playing a mage character, but because of the way that the targeting system was working for the spores it would target an area that wasn't actually in the spore's hit box, and because I was low level and the event was in a low level area, I basically could not progress further on that island (luckily I had a side path I could take on a different island) because the portal was somewhere in that spore cluster.
-- There was one instance where my game crashed and when I reloaded the game the frame was so bad that it left the game unplayable. I fixed the problem by restarting my computer, but it was really weird. The frame rate drop was not only noticable in game, but also in the start menu and on the loading screen, which even with my not so up to par computer would normally run smooth as water.
-- Enemy healing is acting weird. So I'm assuming, from what I've seen, that this game uses a mechanic for enemies that is "whent the enemy is no longer in combat, restore the enemy's health to 100%" but there are times when I'm shooting an enemy and he's just... not going after me for no reason. He's just standing still, staring at a door, or something passed me and he just doesn't move. And I'm like "well whatever. That's an easy kill." and then as soon as I get the enemy to have health he is suddenly back at 100%. and if I keep attacking him he keeps getting restored to 100%. I've also had this happen to enemies who are agroed and running towards me, but this is far less often. If it's the programing I mentioned above, then it's probably just the enemy is for some reason not registering the fact that its in combat.
Some questions and concerns I have:
-- Why does the ranger have a skill that is entirely focused on standing still to do more damage? Because of the armour, the other skills, as well as the ranger's core abilities are heavily focused on movement it just seems like a very odd choice to have as a skill. I mean you could use it as a sniper type of ability, but because of the way combat works in this game sniping isn't really a viable option.
-- I'm also confused on the point of staves for mages. They don't hit much harder than a wand, and a wand can hit an enemy three times before the staff can hit an enemy once. Plus the staff shoots such a slow moving projectile that if often misses if the enemy is moving slightly to the right.
-- For character customization I was wondering if there would be a way to have more makeup options. Right now there's only two or three "makeup options" with the lips, with three mouths having noticable lips, one being purple, one being more normal in colour, and one giving an odd smirk. A (assumedly) simple solution would be having one lip that looks like the basic lip (or more lips that are different in shape) but being able to colour the mouth, with it applying to the colour of the lips.
Some final notes:
I really enjoy this game, it's pretty much exactly what I was looking to play. There's a variety of tools to use, some are just kinda nifty like the mirror of teleportation and others are huge game changers like the compass that can show you the direction of the nearest portal. it's a great and beautiful game and I highly reccomend anyone who likes the building of Minecraft, the combat of Terraria, loves exploring, but might not be into all of the red stone buisness that minecraft has (since this game's building mechanics are really basic and don't have anything that resembles redstone).

I have bought every one of the supreme ruler games since the original 2020. I have mentioned in a review for another SR game that I am unhappy with the way Battlegoat has handled new versions of the game (selling them as whole new games) because this game is basically just an updated version of SR 2020, SR CW, SR 1936, combined into one.
That said, If you have played any of the older versions, then you will certainly find this one to be the better experience. Anyone new to the series would also want to pick this one up too as there is little point in buying any of the older games in the SR series.
I have found this game to be a very good Geopolitical/Military (more focus on military) simulator. It does have a steep learning curve, but when you figure it out, it is an amazing game for its scope and scale.
You can simulate yourself into the leadership position of any country in the world. You manage military, economics, research, and diplomacy.
The version of the game has many new and very much needed features from prior versions added. Being able to delete all the pop ups from one catagory in a single click rather then tediously one by one, as well as being able to easily select which units you want from a stack by simply holding left ctrl and clicking. Renaming your county, units and even cities new or old is a nice touch as well.
They Ai is seemingly much more intelligent in this version. They are actually reserving units they are not using and actively invading by sea, aggressivly and effectively this time.
Politics is hit or miss. The Ai seems to be doing a much better job making wars and alliances regional and relevant, rather then across the globe and logistically infeasible. I have also seen them make a cease fire agreement. Which I cannot recall happing much if ever in prior games. Aliiances are still a odd ball in the series. The AI wants a ton of them for some reason, but they do not include mutual defense like you would think.
The game does still have some issues, but it is a fun game either way. The worst issue I have noticed that hasnt been fixed yet is the merchant marines just willy nilly floating to their deaths. The Ai should recognize when its military is being sunk to the bottom of the ocean, but they dont seem to mind sending their entire army to its death.
If planning invasions and military operations on land or sea or across oceans is your thing, as well as organizing and commanding the operations, then you will probably enjoy this game. It has ministers to help you out while you get started, but I find the true fun to be in doing it myself.
I picked it up on sale cheap for less then 10 bucks. At that price it is a good deal. If you dont want to pay full price, keep an eye on it for a good sale downt he road.

I will look at the game in it's own merits, ignoring anything else about the online community or the people who made the game, so I can get a clear picture.
SURGEON SIMULATOR 2013
This game is a surgery simulation game. Before you play the game, hoping to learn how to do brain transplants IRL, this game is NOT to be taken seriously.
The game puts you in the shoes of a surgeon named Nigel Burke, who must perform life-saving surgeries on various patients, including: Bob, The Heavy, Gworb and Donald Trump. You control the game using the A W E R and Space keys, controlling all the fingers on the hand. You move the hand with your mouse, you press left click to lower the hand and you press right click to rotate the hand. Alright, now that that's out the way, time for an overview of the game!
The game includes 3 surgeries: Heart Transplant, Double Kidney Transplant and Brain Transplant. Each surgery can be played under certain scenarios, including in the operating theatre, in the back of an ambulance and in space. The A&E DLC adds 2 more surgeries, Eye and Teeth transplants and allows you to perform surgery while running down a hospital corridor.
SURGERIES:
Heart Transplant: Take the old heart out and put a new one in. What happens to the other organs doesn't matter.
Double Kidney Transplant: Take the old kidneys out and put new ones in. Again, what happens to the other organs doesn't matter. NOTE: Both kindeys need to be present. If you accidentally lose one of the kidneys out the back of the ambulance, you're f**ked.
Brain Transplant: Take the old brain out and put a new one in. Note: If you're using the circular saw or the drill to break the skull, DON'T HIT THE BRAIN. It will cause severe blood loss.
Eye Transplant(A&E ONLY): Take the old eyes out and put new ones in. You have more breathing room in terms of donor organs, as there are 2 containers, each with 6 eyes. You can give Bob brown eyes, blue eyes or even a smiley face or an 8 ball.
Teeth Transplant(A&E ONLY): Take the rotten teeth out and put new ones in. You have a large number of teeth to put in, so losing the teeth is no big deal. Note: You should only knock out the rotten teeth, as for every good tooth you knock out, you will have to replace it.
SCENARIOS:
Operating Theatre: Standard. Nothing's crazy here.
Corridor(A&E ONLY): You're running down the hospital corridor. You start with no tools or donor organs, but as you run down the corridor, small trolleys with assorted tools, donor organs and other things will come and go. You can get multiple donor organs in this mode, so losing the donor organs is no big deal. However, you might want to hold onto things, as there have been many times when I have waited 3 minutes for a donor organ to appear on one of the trolleys.
Ambulance: You're in the back of a MOVING ambulance. This mode is the msot crazy, as when the ambulance steers and goes over bumps, your tools will go flying everywhere. Sometimes, the doors on the back of the ambulance will open, allowing things to fall out onto the road. Make sure you don't lose the donor organs!
Space: You're operating in SPAAAAAAAAAAACE! Everything floats around, as you would expect. Make sure you don't bump too many things around, as those objects tend to collide with other objects, which will then bump into other objects, causing everything in the theatre to go flying everywhere.
SPECIAL SURGERIES:
Meet the Medic: You are the Medic operating on the Heavy, like in the TF2 Meet the Medic promotional video! You must perform an Uber Heart Transplant. All the tools have been replaced with TF2 items too.
Alien Surgery: You're operating on an alien named Gworb! Everything floats around like in Space mode. When you start the surgery, you must perform one of 6 transplants: Gobbleshaft, Gavichal, Pewdsball, Birgirspallex, Robbaloraz or a Cubed Trangrifier. All of these organs(not the Gobbleshaft) are named after YouTubers that have played the game.
Gavichal: Gavin and Micheal from Rooster Teeth
Pewdsball: PewDiePie
Birgirspallex: Birgirpall
Robbaloraz: Robbaz
Cubed Trangrifier: NerdCubed
Inside Donald Trump(A&E ONLY): You must perform a heart transplant on Donald Trump! Many of the tools are absent and some have been replaced by gold versions. There are exclusive items, such as the Trump Steak, Trump Vodka and the Trump Tower. There is also a Medical Bill. The more you hurt Trump, the higher the bill goes. Instead of giving him a normal heart, you can give him a heart of gold or a heart of stone. It's your choice.
Final Thoughts: The game can be very hard to get into at first, due to the difficult control scheme. Once you get used to the controls, the game is actually quite fun. Beating all the surgeries, earning all the achievements and getting A++ rating on all the surgeries can be quite challenging. The music is great too. If you download the game, you can listen to the soundtrack in the music player. One thing I didn't like is how some of the achievements are glitched. For some of them, you must disable the A&E DLC, earn the achievement and then enable the DLC again. Some of the achievements are REALLY frustrating too. One achievement needs you to drug yourself(jab yourself with the green syringe, this will f**k up your vision) and jam a scalpel into the electrical socket(inverts the controls) and then complete the surgery. It's ridiculously furstrating.
Final Score: The game does many things right, but still fails with a few things, so I give Surgeon Simulator 2013 8.6/10. The DLC is worth it too, so pick up both if you can.

This game is broken and/or just♥♥♥♥♥♥
If it was polished - er, not even polished, but actually... built instead of slapped together as it seems to have been - it could be great, maybe even rival Apotheon.
Instead, the game abides by its own rules, which are separate from the ones you are given/told.
You will do the actions you input only when your character feels like it.
You can sometimes double-jump and you can sometimes jump until you hit the roof; it seems you have to have the apex of your initial jump be right beside a wal for multiple jumps to be possible (i.e. literally bounding up the wall), but this, too, is finnicky and thus only a guess on my part.
It seems there is a legit delay in when you hit the attack button and when the attack is executed; this could be attributed to the weapons being heavy - for some sort of immersion - but due to the overall quality of the game, I'd just as soon assume it's because of... shoddy coding(?)
The pause menu has different options such as "Blood" and "Corpses." Whatever option you select just boots you out of the game.
There is a "View Map" button, which just zooms out so you can get a better feel FOR the arena. Sometimes this works, sometimes it doesn't, sometimes you have to hit it again if you want to zoom back in, sometimes it does so on its own.
There is a "Dodge." It does nothing for defense.
Enemies spawn out of nowhere, frequently right on top of you.
There are bonfires to "Rest"/Level-up at (ya); don't seem to really help much - no option for to actually rest (as in regaining some health).
The game seems an impossible grind - mainly due to how poor the quality is/how little you can trust the game to do what you intend/did on the controller. Cited as "Partial Controller Support," so I may try with KB+M but...
To level-up doesn't really cost a significant amount, but neither do you get a decent amount of Gold (and zero Health Crates).
When you die, you have the option to buy perks; the cheapest is 3500 - I accrued 3495 after having collected every bit of Gold in the first two maps and from killing all but the last enemy. Too bad the combat is broken.
You can scroll through every perk except the last two, because why not?
The cave walls are a single painting repeated in a tile format.
The music is a grungy, garbled orgy of grotesque.
I feel like the dev might be Swedish; if so, I can't really fault the music.
I definitely find fault in the game as a whole.
There is enough of a violent, chaotic cacophony in the soundtrack; Dear Dev Pohlak, please forgive my harsh words. I want to like this game. There's no way that I can right now, nor would I be able to recommend it. I can't speak on how much effort was put into the game, and I do not wish to disrespect you... but I call for mechanic and all-encompassing tweaks/rebuilding. With such rough music, the gameplay doesn't need to be as; streamline it and Stones of Sorrow could become something great.
P.S. The low price doesn't excuse the quality.

250 hours deep and Spelunky is still a wonderful and entrancing game.
Admittedly I now play in shorter spells but for a while there It was a game I just could not put down.

I don't like platformers, and I don't generally like roguelites (give me the full mystery and suspense Rogue experience, not some watered-down version with only a handful of unlockables...)
But I love Spelunky. It's not a game that can be easily pigeon-holed into one of those two genres, it takes something from both and remixes the experience with procedural level generation that's geniunely challenging (in a "I really have to pay attention and think about this" way, not a "lol there's a lava pit and a spike pit together I can't jump across both" kind of way), a handlful of different paths to attempt (so if you miss one of the early "quest" items you can still achieve a different kind of success), varied enemies, brutal trap combos, and a huge skill depth.
This is a game honed to the keenest edge between fun and challenge, and it works brilliantly for that. It's more than just the sum of its genres, it's a well-oiled machine.
I throuroughly reccommend Spelunky, just be warned that you won't be coming out of the cave for a while.

The Lobby is nothing like the the first Gunz: The Duel. Gone is the "Join open game" and the option to create private games (again, this is Beta, it might change later in the stages). A game can only be a max of 4 v 4 which is really strange as you can invite 5 of your friends to a party. When you enter a room, there is no option at the moment to leave the room which is bad because as of writing, if one person in the room does not ready up, the entire room gets stuck in frozen room hell. This means there's no leaving the room and no game starting, and the only way out is by quitting the application which brings us to the login issue mentioned earlier.
Actual gameplay has been dramatically changed as well. There is no more "K-style" which is what made the original Gunz so popular. And other styles have pretty much been removed as well. So Veterans to the original game, this is NOT the same. Then again, I haven't played the original Gunz for maybe 3 years now. As mentioned before, there are 4 character classes, Gunslinger, Slient Avenger, Shadow Dancer (new to NA from what I hear), and Shield Trooper. You can kinda guess what each class does if you haven't seen any gameplay videos before. I played Rena, the Shadow Dancer, who is a fast paced dual wield character. The game, when it works smoothly, plays fantastically and feels polished. But if you have a ping of over 200, you'll struggle, and anything over 500 is just a walking dummy. Prepare to die. A lot. I don't know if it's because I'm low level, but it looks like they removed health and armor packs, and grenades from the game. Kinda disappointed by that change.
There's also a new Campaign mode which tries to tell a story, but being as it's so new, we (my friends and I) jumped right into the action to test out the gameplay. The first mission is made up of a lot of mini rounds, and can get quite difficult if you like to use melee weapons. Try to space out your weapons or else you'll find yourself out of ammo a lot when facing a big mob. Be wary of the red barrels because if your teammate blows them up, you can get damaged as well, and they hurt. Note that when you first start an account, you are given 3 revival coins for use in the campaign. These coins allow you to revive when you are KO'ed during the mission, but these coins are also $2.50 in the shop. Real money, not in game currency, use those coin sparingly if you're cheap. Speaking of the shop, it's pretty brutal. Comparing to other games, the items are a lot of money. Accessaries start at $10, up to $15, and these are PER item. Being F2P, it's understandable that you want to charge money for perks and asthetics, but that is a lot when comparing to say PSN or XBLive that charge maybe $5 per item.
Music is very true to it's predecessor, and quite enjoyable. Everything starts out quite loud, esspecially if you are wearing headphones, so headphone users, be sure to set it to a likable volume. Sound effects are pretty much the same from the old game as well. Overall, I found the music the best part so far in the game.
Pros:
Gameplay when there is little to no lag
Everyone at the moment is on equal footing (No k-style means no "noob hunting")
Music is wonderful
Campaign is a fresh new element
Cons:
Frozen Room Hell
Beginning beta mode means huge server lags that happen frequently for now
No private rooms, and a max party of 4 even though the room can host up to 8 (4 v 4)
Again, this review is based on opening day beta and these critiques can be subjected to change by Maiet (please change for the better). I personally think the game has a lot of potential, and can outshine the original Gunz given time, but at the moment, the game is a bit unbearable due to the stockpile of mini issues. For now 6/10, and I'm sure I'm missing elements to nitpick on.

Short Review: Tekken 7 is one of the Best Tekkens to be released, if not, the Best Tekken. Is Kind of short on game modes, but does everything else almost perfectly (Online Play, Gameplay, Visuals, etc).  Rating: 9.5/10
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Detailed Review: Lets get this out of the way first.. I go as far back as Tekken 3 regarding experience with this Series. Although, I never got the chance to really get into 4 and 5, but have really been playing it every since Tekken 6. So when I say that this is potentially the BEST Tekken to be released to date, take my word for it.
As a Tekken game, it gives you Almost everything that you could want! It gives you some of the most balanced GAMEPLAY that I have seen in years regarding a fighting game (There is no "OMG so and so is broken"). They brought in a good balance of both new and returning characters that will for sure make you spend hours in the Lab trying to understand the ins and outs of them, at the same time still feeling as home if youve played previous games. The STORY is kind of short (Which is made up with small side stories) but it had me glued to my chair until the very end. and the last fight is one that I was ALWAYS remember! SO INTENSE... ONLINE PLAY could be looked at as having few game modes (Personally "Player Matches" and "Ranked" Matches isnt a small list to me at all. I think we have been spoiled with games like Injustice 2, but thats my opinion), but the netcode is one of the best that I have ever used in a fighting game. and it also adds in a mode called "Tournament mode" where you actually get placed withing a tourney bracket to try and win in game prizes (Which i think is AWESOME). Practice mode has had some small additions added to it, which just adds to the game's polished feel. and last but not least, the one thing that long time tekken fans will probably complain about it the fact that this game lacks in having a variety of offline game modes, along with Arcade endings. Personally, when I play offline, its only to practice or play against people, so it doesnt really effect me. and yes, there isnt a TRUE tutorial mode but they actually go through things generally in story mode so I dont see what the complaints are about. But I will say this... regarding the arcade endings, that really shouldnt be a big deal. There are small side stories (granted it doenst touch on everyone) that will give you "endings." I think people are really overreacting when in response to "Character endings." and Music is CRAZY GOOD!!
Overall, GREAT Story (Kind of short but again is made up with character endings), gameplay is near perfect that makes you want to come back to play, online is near perfect (Gives you exactly what a fighting game should) Offline can be looked at as having very few modes, but for me its just fine. Visuals are stunning and the best by far in any Tekken game. Music is, again, some of the most enjoyable music that I have heard from a Tekken game.
Rating: 9.5/10

Before the review I must say that I do greatly enjoy RWBY.  I don't feel that would change my view of the gameplay, but it is worth mentioning.
This game is a simple yet enjoyable hack 'n' slash game that allows for up to four-player co-op.  I have seen people compare it to the Warriors games, and I feel that isn't a particularly apt comparison.  While you do fight large hordes of enemies, this game is very focused on special moves, which each character has three of.  Proper application of these special moves, as well as management of the special meter, is the key to success.
Besides the special moves, each character has a melee and ranged attack.  Repeatedly using the melee attack will lead to a combo, which a player can either do all the way to the end, or use the ranged attack button to do a different combo ender.
Since this is early access, they're only focusing on one section of gameplay at a time, and as of the time of writing that section of gameplay is only about one-two hours.  While there will be more, and I do think there is plenty of reason to replay what there is, for many that just isn't enough, and I understand that, and suggest you check back in later.  That said, the full release of the game will be more expensive, as they wish to have it be a lower price for early adopters.
If you enjoy some fun hack 'n' slash gameplay, a fun co-op time with friends, or just like the show RWBY, I think this will be a good purchase for you.

All this one is, is just a combination of all the Supreme Ruler games. It really doesn't add anything new. Pre-Steam, I have hundreds hours into the Supreme Ruler games (mostly 2020), so don't let my 12 hrs fool you.
The game is designed for you to play a more advanced country. If you play a smaller one, then all you'll get is a couple of different unit types and some tech and that's it. And eventually you get overrun by far more advanced units or get bored, more so the latter.
Diplomacy is crap in this game. If the dislike you in the beginning, they'll always dislike you. Condeming or supporting an action makes no difference. Other thing I didn't like about the game is the Casus Belli. If you attack a country, every country gets a higher Casus against you, but if another country does the same thing, you don't get anything against them. Also countries will just attack you out of the blue for no reason other then that you share borders or not or it's a random event, like one of your units accidently attacked theirs.
You can conduct covert actions against countries. Most of the choices seem utterly pointless. Like funding opposing factions or supplying weapons. I have yet to actually get anything to work in this. Tested this a few times, funding countries for over 5 years at max resulted in nothing, just makes for a money sink. Spies are really only good for seeing what units are around in the area, I've never been able to sabatoge anything with them ever or anything else. If a spy gets caught, it'll automatically start a war every time.
The Devs couldn't figure out how to program the AI to load units onto transports, so you get merchant marines. They can land anywhere where theres a port and aren't affected by fuel, unlike your ships.
Best to play with the AI controlling everything, since you can't be everywhere at the same time. Drawback to this is if you give a unit orders to go somewhere, the AI will countermand this order and if you remove the option for the AI to control the unit, I'll you'll have to remember where every single unit is. Good luck with that!
The AI will also make really stupid desisions for you. Like for ranged units, instead of positioning the unit just withing striking range, it'll move it right up to front lines to be destroyed. However it's funny that AI doesn't do the same for non-human controlled players. It also has a tendacy to move ships outside of their fuel range. So there's all your ships, stuck in the ocean, can't move, unless you manually move a supply ship on top of every each one. Talked about excitement there. Oh and don't forget to take your supply ship off of AI control unless you never want it to get there.
If you have planes, you have to constantly remember to move them always closer to the borders, the AI will never redeploy them, even if there are just too many at a base. Also if the base you're redeploying/moving them is out of fuel range, the only way you'll know that is if you see them crash. With the exception of radar planes, when you give them orders and they're out of range, they'll turn around, refuel, try again and again.......
The game has a weird bug that if you have too much in storage of a resource or you get too much money on hand, your cash will all of a sudden go into negatives (it's a memory issue). Populations will jump into unreasonalble levels and you'll stop producing everything. And at this point all you can do is try loading a save if you have one or start over. This has been ongoing since Supreme Ruler 2020 (pre-Steam).
Unlike the original 2020 (pre-Steam), you have no control over bonds and repaying them back (amongst other things). It's at the whim of the AI, so most likely you'll always be paying interest on them, even if you have plenty of cash on hand, the AI simply does not repay them back so you can be debt free. I find this method really frustrating as hell. I feel I should be able to have control over everything for my country, not just certain things, what then is the point of being a ruler in the first place.
As you play, you'll find out that you're always out of Industry Goods. This is the games way of keeping you from over building/expanding. Of all the games I've played, I've never been able to get excess to stockpile regardless of how many building material building I've had or stockpiles. And if you forget to take it off from AI control, it'll sell it all and you'll never be able to build anything.
Thoughout the game, you'll get messages that some resources you're selling internally are priced too high and you need to reduce it. I found this message to be utterly pointless. I've had internal prices in the negatives and I still get these messages that the population is complaining about the prices. So in other words, you're making negative profit selling internally and yet the price is still too high, WTF!
You also have to keep a close eye on what the AI is doing. For instance it'll keep cranking the taxes up to well over 90%, which will cause your populatiry to go down and you'll get kicked out of office and have to do a military coup (if you can), and then at that point you have to keep the military happy. If not, game over, you lose.
Thre's also too much randomness for income, one days you'll be making profit and then the next day you'll be in the negatives and you'll never be able to figure out why.
Frankly the UI for 2020 way out shines what you're left with here. I had a hell of a time trying to find everything and figure it all out (it's like going from Winxp (very user friendly) to win8 (WTF). Another game that's gone from good to terrible.
Time to uninstall permanantly and never buy another game from these guys ever again.

Initially I disliked this game - the camera was instantly annoying.  As one reviewer put it "Your biggest fight in this game is with the camera". I found myself doing 360 degree spins just trying to view enemies. The auto aim with ranged weapons was unsettling and took some getting used to. I also found multiple clicks to navigate through my inventory painful - perhaps there's some shortcuts I'm missing. I found some aspects of the game could have been documented or explained better, like how best to use reckoning mode.
However, I persisted through these minor issues and have ended up enjoying the game. Things like the auto aim that I initially found unsettling turns out to be quite useful when attacking multiple enemies. I've gotten used to the camera. There is reasonable graphics and music. Some of the game areas remind me of areas within World of Warcraft - there is a fair amount of scenic detail in the game world.
The story and quest lines are quite in depth. There's plenty of equipment, spell and ability upgrades to keep one interested, plus crafting. You can choose to pursue the main quest line or build experience via various side quests.
I've found the combination moves with fights are interesting and entertaining. Sneaking up and backstabbing opponents is a quick and easy way to take down an opponent.
There's enough variety in this game to keep any gamer interested. I'm changing my initial opinion to thumbs up.

This review could go either way, so I hit "Do Not Recommend" to balance out the average a little more toward the 7/10 or so this game deserves.
While elegantly made, with great environments and some great humour, the Brutal Legend really falls flat in a few areas. If you enjoy Jack Black and his movies, this game will probably feel like a good length. To me, it felt like they could have cut a third to a half of the game and no one would have noticed. In particular, the lengthy time needed to unlock units, progress the story, or get enough fire for the upgrades takes forever. The story seemed good, but stretched too far out. Unless you roll straight from story mission to story mission, you're likely to have forgotten the plot or why you ever cared in the first place because of all the filler missions in between.
If Double Fine had instead focused on EITHER an RTS or a third-person brawler/adventure/sandbox, the game would feel so much better. Instead, you find yourself repeating the same moves with the same character, rolling into a terribly designed RTS where your immediate objective is to get out as fast as possible to hop back in your car, summoned with the same boring chord that you'll use fifty billion times. Oh, and your car remains the same; some upgrades, but don't go looking for even a bike (except for 2 minutes in one mission), because that car is it. I'd enjoy at least a little variety. Given the strength of the third-person adventuring, Double Fine could have cut the RTS sections totally, shortened the game considerably, and still had an awesome title.
Finally, if you don't enjoy Jack Black, his voice will make you want to murder him. The intro to the game has no bearing on the game itself (why is Black in a record store? Why is this record there? Why are we watching this dumb video whenever you start the game? And best of all, why should we care?), and Black could only be arsed to record some lines, which means you'll hear many Riggs' lines over and over and over. There's only so much self-depreciating "hurr hurr look at me I'm just a roadie in the background but you're hot wanna bang oh no ok that's cool I'm still better than anyone else but I'm in the background" that you can take before wanting to garrote yourself with guitar strings.
In summary:
PROS:
Good humour (the first time you hear it), great environment, great art, killer soundtrack, some excellent sections and bosses.
CONS:
Stretched far beyond reasonable game length, the repetitious missions and humour ("Hey, who we ambushing?" "BAD GUYS!" x200), the half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥game setup split between combat and RTS, graphical glitches that screw up any hair (in particular LionWhyte's, which is sad, as it's his only real feature), predictable and trite storyline, Black's humour gets old really fast. Multiplayer is a crappy port of the RTS section, with all of its weaknesses. WHERE'S THE GODDAMN MINIMAP? No real reason to upgrade beyond the basics (machine guns for the car, more combos if you want them, the mountain man look).

Spelunky is a masterclass in game design. You learn by doing, with every pitfall and mistake made just another stepping stone on your pathway to greatness. You'll die a lot, so be warned, but each death will be meaningful as you take in the game's systems and find cheeky tricks you can perform to survive that little bit longer. It isn't over-complicated like some Rogue-lites, the essence of the thing is very pure and concise, the complexity here is in tackling difficult situations and thinking on your feet. Despite the simplicity of the core gameplay loop, it has surprising depth and replayability. I'm 200 hours in and I keep coming back, pushing that little bit further, getting those final few achievements.
Spelunky deserves your time and respect. You needn't delve deep into your pockets either, but this cave sure isn't shallow!

I've been thinking of making this review for some time, and thought about writing a funny comment. I changed my mind and decided to try and make people who are on the edge of buying this game a worthy review, which might make the decision for you. At the point of writing this review I have 490 hours in the game. At the moment this means it is my most played game. Obviously that means it has some value.
I first saw this game being played by my little brother, and remember thinking "This looks terrible". None the less I liked the setting. After lots of doubting I decided to get it in sale for 10 euro. I started playing the singleplayer campaign and I loved it. There is a line between the dialogue aspect, and the battle aspect. The first one I never understood, even after playing for so long, the battle aspect is why this game is so amazing. THE BATTLES ARE GREAT. Chaotic, but controlled at the same time. The longer you fight the more blood will be on you and your guys. This is the story for singleplayer.
After that I tried multiplayer. Damn, if you like some medival battles, they won't get better then this. It's amazing, I cant describe how they did it. It actually feels like you're a soldier in a battle, and
the MVP. Your life does not matter, it's the amount of people that help which matters. It does not matter if you are good or not, you will die by a unexpected blow or arrow. If you want to survive, stick together and use shields, swords, bows and siege towers wisely, and you might survive.
. If you like medival battles you just want to try again and again. It does not matter if you lost of won, it's always fun.
This is where I got most of my hours. All of the fun gameplay in medival times, now recreated in the Napoleonic times. There is cannons, boats, horses and ♥♥♥♥ING TRUMPETS. YOU CAN MAKE MUSIC. YOU CAN WIELD FLAGS, YOU CAN BLOW UP WALLS, YOU SHOOT ONCE, RELOAD FOR AGES. YOU CAN STICK A KNIFE IN PEOPLE.
I swear. The athmosphere is there. Do not buy this game unless you plan to spend the extra 5 euro on this DLC. You can thank me later.

This game is a work of art. And I don't just mean that from a visual perspective, I mean that from the perspective of a game. In every respect, from graphics to gameplay, Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons is a work of art.
The gameplay is simple conceptually. You play as two brothers simultaneously, and overcome obstacles with each brother's unique strengths. A Tale of Two Sons pushes that concept as far as it can without being overly difficult. The more you experience it, the more you realize how perfect the execution is.
The story is perfect. It's also something all its own. The characters speak in an unknown language, but there are no subtitles. Instead, the story is expressed through actions. You can't understand a word they're saying, yet you can understand their situation perfectly. The two brothers are on a quest to save their father's life. The focus is on the two brothers and their journey, the influence they have on the individuals they meet, and the impact those individuals ultimately have on them.
Graphically and musically, this game is beautiful, with its own unique style. The graphics seem like a secondary thing in comparison to gameplay and story, but the choice of these particular graphics in this particular style is in perfect harmony with the rest of the game. Same with the music. Displace one note and there would be diminishment... The graphics really shine when you encounter some of the grand architecture that this game has to offer.
Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons is as close to perfect as may be possible. It is fresh and innovative, and a truly powerful experience. Recommended. Period.

When trying to describe the Portal Knights, Terraria in 3D comes in mind.
PK is a wonderful mix of procedurally generated worlds (with some pre-determined values), and elements of RPG’s, character progression, base building, and boss enemy fights.
Despite the similarities to some other games in the genre however, it carries enough uniqueness and charm to stand strong amongst other games like Minecraft, Terraria, Starbound and so on.
The game mechanics feel intuitive, with sleek UI, simple (yet rich) building aspects of the game, good combat system, charming graphics, beautiful music and plenty of content for the price it’s asking.

I'm a long time fan of the series ever since the first game in 1991, but this is a major, major, disappointment on the technical side. Let me begin with the BAD things first. NetherRealm Studios somehow broke this game. I have over 1600 games in my library and absolutely NO OTHER GAME crashes as much as MK X. MK 9 for example runs flawlessly.
THE BAD:
In the first week of the release it had massive bugs, and also had massive patches to fix some of the issues, with updates over 15gb. The game *still* suffers from a bad memory leak problem which happens every so often, after 2-3 hours of gameplay. That is a bit upsetting but I managed to finish the game story and it was all fine, Krypt mode was fine, local versus was fine.
The really BAD thing is when you start to play online and try to have fun with friends, or perfect your fighting skills. All the recent patches the game received so far did nothing to help as well. I absolutely CAN'T complete a single online fight, either on KOTH mode, any rooms or single online versus. Crashes happen every time, and sometimes on character select screen or a few seconds into the fight, either with a black screen or simply the game freezing and not responding. And yes, I've tried a clean reboot, rolling back Nvidia drivers, rolling back PhysX drivers, reinstalling DX versions and everything else from scratch. Absolutely nothing I've done worked.
I will change this review at a later time when NetherRealm fixes this mess. Some friends report problems, others do not. It's really a hit and miss, depending on your system. Then again, an AAA game of this magnitude shouldn't have these issues, not by a long shot. As reference, I'm using a very good setup, i7, 16gb ram, gtx 980.
THE GOOD:
The story of the game is a retelling (with a bit of retconning) following the demise of Shao Khan a few years later and the plot that follows sometime after MK3. Graphics are very well done, gameplay is improved but still familiar for those coming from MK 9 / Injustice, and the game has a lot to offer for both old and new players. Story is a bit shorter than MK 9 but satisfying, and sets up a few twists and questions for future games.
Each fighter has 3 different styles, and as a general rule the variations cover rushdown/turtling/zoning. It's down to what style you like the best, and which one best counters the opponent's. You'll spend quite some time exploring the Krypt and unlocking some content for the game, while the rest you'll acquire playing the game, using each character many times and on the special hourly/daily/weekly towers, living towers and other future Invasion / Boss events.
CONCLUSION:
With all this said, I would recommend you to get the game if you really like the series, and see where the story goes, but it's not yet perfectly optimized for online play and you could have problems depending on your setup, with known bugs which have yet to be fixed. It pains me really as a fan to say this, but I will not recommend it at this time if you like a solid and smooth online experience.

First to address many of the terrible "reviews". I'm not sure what most people are talking about with this being a "bad" port. Any port will undoubtedly run slower on PC. Those are just the facts of life. Just like using an emulator, you will need a more powerful machine than it was originally designed for the get the same performance due to changes made for optimization. This being said, those using dual-GPU cards (295x2, HD 7990, etc.) should expect even MORE problems since the game is originally designed for consoles which use a single GPU. Most games are not optimized for dual-GPU cards or setups already and may have issues with them such as: Not working at all, using a single card in a dual/triple/quad card build, or major artifacts and graphical glitches.
I am running this game on two computers right now with zero problems and 60fps @1080. First build is an i7 4770k, R9 290, 2x8GB dual channel 2333, and a WD 7200RPM HDD. My other buid is an i5 4460, r9 280x, 2x8GB dual channel 1866, WD 7200RPM HDD. I was also able to stream over wifi at 60fps from my first build to my second one using a Netgear AC1200 adapter and Belkin AC1200 router over 5ghz channel in an office across the house.
My second issue is with reviewing the developer in the game section. Got it, the developers messed up and wiped a bunch of save games. This does not affect the quality of the game! These reviews are unnecessary, take up valuable space, and bring down the overall outlook of the game without actually giving a fair opinion.
Rant aside, this game looks fantastic. I had been playing Mortal Kombat Komplete Edition for a while before I purchased this game and the visual improvements are vast. It is a very beautiful game to look at and extremely satisfying watching fatalities and X-Rays. This is the way Mortal Kombat is supposed to look. Not the dumbed down, kid friendly versions made in the past like DC vs Mortal Kombat.
I feel the overall level of competency for fighting games is mid to low. I wasn't sure about getting this game after reading so many poor reviews, but I made the leap anyway and I'm glad I did. It's a very satisfying game with plenty of hours of content, great visuals, good audio, and it's well worth it's value.

South Park: The Fractured But Whole is the sequel to the critically acclaimed South Park: The Stick of Truth. As this is a South Park game and the sequel you can expect many of the same gags and crass humor found in the first game. Whereas Stick of Truth parodied turn based fantasy roleplaying games. Fractured But Whole parodies superheroes and particularly the Marvel and DC cinematic shared universes.
There are a number of jokes that any comic book fan will appreciate. In addition to the jokes, you will find a number of easter eggs in costumes that have been directly inspired by comic book characters.
You get some greater customization options creating your character. But the customization also extends to various artifacts that you can slot along with perks, classes, and abilities. You even get to choose your 'kryptonite' or weakness from a variety of things like ninjas and crab people.
Mechanically the game is still turn based, however it's added some new twists that make for a deeper layer of strategy and tactics. Now you will find a grid where you can move your characters about in various lanes. These lanes can set up new opportunities to knock enemies into one another for knockback damage and more.
The map of south park itself is largely the same but there are a variety of quests, and other activities to keep you occupied. Fractured But Whole is not without it's faults however.
During my playtime it seems like battles can take a bit to initiate when you enter an encounter. It just seems to pause for a bit with the characters standing there idle until you finally can give any commands.
Finally Ubisoft once again stubbornly has inserted Denuvo DRM into the game. That makes three forms of DRM just to run one game and it's pretty damned ridiculous to have Steam, Uplay and Denuvo all in one game.
All in all South Park: the Fractured But Whole is a worthwhile followup to it's predecessor, especially if your a fan of the tv show. However it's also worth checking out if you love super heroes and comic books.
