I really want to love this game, I do... But I can't.
The title is what you get; it got the sniping right but everything else was meh.
The mechanics when it comes to sniping are decent. Obviously we all love the bullet cam. Sometimes, however, if you use the aim assist that tells you where your bullet will land, it will turn red (meaning your shot is unobstructed) yet when you fire the bullet simply doesn't hit the enemy and actually just alerts them instead. Whether the bullet is hitting the cover in front of you or the indicator is bugged, I'm not sure but regardless it has robbed me of my stealthy sniping and instead forced me to play loud. Also, sometimes I line up the perfect shot and I can't shoot. Yes, I have rounds in my rifle but it simply refuses to fire.
The story is terrible but let's face it, we didn't come for the story, we came to shoot Hitler in the nuts. The characters had little to no development and *spoiler alert, for as little as it's worth* I didn't give a♥♥♥♥♥♥when Brauer died. He was a♥♥♥♥♥♥poor character. Moving swiftly on...
Stealth. My god this game butchers it. Compare it to Metal Gear Solid: Phantom Pain for example. Guard sees a body, they run and ring the alarm. Base goes on alert for a while, settle when they don't find anything. Sure, it's not amazingly realistic, but at least it gives a slightly realistic feeling of everyone panicking because their people are dropping dead. Yet when a soldier in Sniper Elite III discovers a body, he stands there for a minute, then shrugs and walks off.
I mean... Really? You can overhear dialogue between two soldiers and one mentions he's afraid of "The Desert Ghost" (Which sounds like something an edgy 13 year old names their Youtube channel) and is worried he'll get popped in the skull. Yet when said scenario happens and his buddy's grey matter is sprayed all over his face, he doesn't give a rat's♥♥♥♥♥♥ That's just straight up ridiculous.
Not to mention it's a very clunky, clumsy game. Which, in case you haven't noticed, is very bad for a game that dabbles so heavily in stealth. Of course, you don't have to be stealthy, but it certainly helps on the hardest difficulty since the enemies, rightly so, turn you into swiss cheese with their MP40s when they get hold of you. On one mission, I dropped a body and he fell through the floor. Next thing I know 3 other soldiers see this corpse and come up to investigate (and then decide it's not worth caring about). It feels very gritty and unpolished.
Tl:Dr sniping is fun, everything else is pretty bad. I'm only recommending that you get it on sale for about $5 or so, but don't waste any more money than that. Hopefully SE4 isn't as big a failure as this one.

Let’s celebrate the first Tekken game on PC in 22 years!
Tekken 7 has been a rock solid performer from launch day. It’s an impressive arcade port with "Ultra" smooth gameplay running at 60 frames per second.
Controller support on the PC version is excellent. At home I have a Hori V3, Hori RAP4, Mad Catz WWE and one homemade fight stick. All of them work flawlessly with Tekken.

Fun action RPG that does have its flaws but is entertaining none the less.  Combat is fun although gets to be a bit repetative.  Might help to switch classes/fate part way through but I stuck with my hybrid rogue/mage the entire time.  Progression is fun gaining new skills and trying new things althogh with the DLC at least, it's easy to hit max level way before reaching the end of the game.
Some of the crafting skills are interesting but in my experience never seemed to be worth very much.  I was rarely able to make anything better than what I could find (again, might be a product of the DLC) so I ended up carrying around a bunch of stuff I didn't really need or breaking down items I could have sold for gold.  Gold is hard to come by at the early stages of the game but later on I had all I needed/wanted with plenty to spare.  What does become a larger annoyance with this is the inventory management sucks plus has a few glitches.  There are only a few categories of inventory and vendor loot (stuff with the only purpose of selling for gold) gets mixed in with the large volume of crafting materials and quest goods.  This makes it hard to even find the stuff you want to sell and get rid of.  This wouldn't be a big deal excet for the inventory limits that are constantly a problem.  Many quest items cant be removed from inventory even well after the quests are completed which bloats the list of items to scroll through even more.
Beyond those issues, there are a few sound and camera issues here and there but nothing overly frustrating or game breaking. I would't mention them at all except that with the studio going out of business, there is no chance of them ever being fixed with an official patch.
On the positive side, the game looks great and has a similar colorful and slightly comic/cartoonish look of Blizzard games like the Warcraft series.  The voice acting is good and the music, while fairly generic, does a good job setting the mood and complements the visuals.  Gameplay is also fun and while there are a ton of fetch quests like every other RPG in the world, travel to various locations tends to be quick (you can fast travel from any outdoor area to any specific location you have visited before) and the quests tend to be farily quick.
If you do all the sidequests including the 2 DLC campaigns, this game will take a long time to finish.  I have over 110 hours invested in this game and that is on a single playthrough.  I did enjoy the game and would be tempted to play again as a different class but I'm not sure that 110 hours was enjoyable enough for a 2nd go around.

Once you've collected what you need you can move onto a new world through a portal that you'll have to locate in the world. This is one of those times I started playing a game and was mad I hadn't heard of it before. It really does deserve a much larger fanbase. Anyway, it is an awesome game with a very small, but dedicated team.
Pros
-Much larger unit base than any other comparable game. You know how Civ gives you a few units for each era? Well, this gives you hundreds, if not thousands.
-Intensive combat system. Models many of the intricacies of war, inclusing missiles, a detailed supply system, and many more things missed in other grand strategy games.
-Detailed economy. Models a decent variety of resources, all with profitabilities that fluctuate as supply and demand change, as well as your own country's internal economic factors such as inflation, unemployment, and infrastructure,
-Large amount of researchable techs. This game offers a very large and detailed tech tree that has a wide variety of effects on your nation.
-AI allocation. While this game has a steep learning curve, the game offers AI advisors that can pretty much run your nation for you. Their actions are hardly ever ideal, but it really helps when you are still learning.
-AI military difficulty settings. This is really something I have to applaud them for, as it is the ideal for how such a system should work. When you change the difficulty up a level, you are not giving the AI units a stat boost, instead you unlock more tactics for the AI to use. On easy, they do little besides charge your positions. However, on the harder difficulty levels, the AI can pull off challenging strategic manuevers.
-And many more awesome things!
Cons:
-With the huge variety of units, there is a noticable amount that use ill-fitting models. For instance, the US marines will use AKs and Strykers use the LAV model.
-Some military aspects are imperfect. Aircraft squadrons receive aircraft to replace lost ones, and since destroying an entire squadron in one go is difficult, you will occasionally run into situations where the enemy army is destroyed, but you cannot move up due to the concentration of enemy aircraft. This also occurs with artillery, but to a lesser degree and for a different reason.
-The biggest gripe I have is the diplomacy system. My biggest problem with the system is that when a coup happens in a country you previously liked, your populace continues to like it. While you might want to attack it and reinstate the old government, you cannot without taking huge amounts of grief from your populace. The problem extends to when you liberate a country. You can rarely seek treaties with them because all of the civilians in both countries still hate the other.
Ultimately, while the game has quite a few bugs, I am willing to forgive it. The (sometimes serious) problems are simply a side effect of having a detailed and complex game.
It is flipping awesome, and if you like EU4 like games, then you will most likely love this.

As a fan of hack and slash games RWBY encapsulates exactly what a hack and slash is;
Grimm Eclipse is a fun fast paced hack and slash with a massive amounts of room for growth. The combat is by no means bad but it's simple, this simplicity seperates players. To the untrained eye there are zero combos however this is untrue.
Animation cancelling is what makes a combo in this right now.
Ruby; Right before her slam attack at the end of her ground combo you can shoot, this stops yourself from being knocked up and resets your attack chain allowing you to continue a onslaught of ground based melee damage.
Another example with ruby is on her third melee swing you dodge, you should get off 4 attacks because of this, your dodge is an Iframe making it so monsters have a harder time targeting you accuratly and making it so when you should potentially get hurt you take no damage.
I would however like to see a lot more;
More melee attacks. I would like to see at least 2-3 melee attack types that you can combo and chain together
The ability to animation cancel with attack variants will greatly improve the current combat system and allow mastery over the game to those who invest time
More characters; I understand people are all over the idea of playing Ruby and the gang but with only 4 playable characters this does limit playstyle as there are not many variants to attacks other than animation cancelling and picking the strongest special ability your character has to offer.
Allowing more characters like Juane into the fray gives a massive boost in what could be done and considered possible to the developers. The addition of a new weapon and combat style in a character like Juane allows a focus on a defensive or possible protective playstyle, this however does not mean he would not dish out damage. Rather than evasion with a dodge you can be encouraged to block damage or intercept attacks with dash based specials.
The current special attack limitations are a but rough, ruby and yang having the best methods to get past this through less hits required and aura failure charging to full special respectively.
Specials should charge over time, slowly, as well as or being limited to being charged minimally by every attack rather than chaining a combo without getting struck.

Do you like shooting people's heads with a sniper rifle or do you like stabbing people with a knife? Either way you may like doing both. Want to hunt down that Hitler guy who has one part of that men usually have two of (DLC)? Like blowing up vehicles? Well then this is a game for you!
Pros:
(1.) Great graphics. This game does not require such high graphics card requirements. Turn it up to max if you can to see better graphics. Don't see how people don't like the graphics, but ehh I would judge you it's your opinion.
(2.) Different difficulties to choose from. Want to go into the fight careless, shooting everyone in the open... or do you want to be more forced to stay silent and kill quietly? Your choice.
(3.) A reasonable amount of missions to play considering the price of this game. Including the 8 story missions and a survival mode either solo or multiplayer. The main missions do have a reason for you to come back, such as finding collectibles you missed on your first time through or for the thrill.
(4.) Great slow motion X-ray kill cams for kills done with a sniper rifle. Some people may find this annoying, but you can simply turn this off in the settings of the game.
(5.) Multiplayer is fun to test your skills against other players, but remember that people will not go easy on you. Jumping into your first online match, you may find yourself fighting against very experienced players.
(6.) The downloadable content for seperate purchase for the game is great. Loads of new weapons and weapon styles (8 weapon packs and 1 outfit pack) and 4 missions. You can get these if you are willing to throw in some extra cash for the game.
(7.) Lots of achievement for you to get on PC or console. Great for the achievement hunters out there.
Cons:
(1.) The price of this game is a bit high when it is not on sale. If you can wait, I would wait until this game is on sale. Your choice.
(2.) The price for the DLC is also a bit high, but previously stated you can wait if you want or buy it at the regular price.
(3.) The game may crash or freeze at certain parts in the game depending on how good your computer is, so if you have a  PC that does not come within range of the system requirements prepare for it. The game does have minor glitches/bugs, but not too severe to make you not like the game. One glitch is the red reticle when using a sniper rifle, but this does not happen often it occurs rarely.
(4.) The game's campaign mode (story mode) is in my opinion a bit shorter than I expected, but hey I'm not the developer. The game can be completed within a day or two if you know what you are doing. The game can last a bit longer if you are going for finding all the collectibles and doing all the optional objectives. The campaign mode is still great and fun to play.
Information:
(1.) If you simply did not find this game fun or did not like the game, you can get a refund. Check Steam refund policies here:
(2.) Buy the Season Pass if you want a great deal on the DLC in this game. Buy it while it's on sale or buy it now your choice.
(3.) Before you buy the game, check your computer specs to make sure it can even run the game.
Overall great game to play! :)

I'm a newcomer to the Tekken series, but comparing this game to Street Fighter 5, its so much better. Firstly, it's more fun to watch and play then Street Fighter. No more fire ball spamming, for the most part, and no more wake up dps that make you want to punch your computer screen. Some characters have them, but due to Tekken's 3D mechanics, I think that even characters like Akuma are pretty balanced. The game looks nice, and runs on my rig on high just fine, consistent 60 fps. The launch content is far more substantial than SFV. There is story mode, arcade mode, treasure mode, and loads more characters. Additionally, I like the combos system in Tekken much more than in Street Fighter 5. Tekken combos are mostly button strings with directional imputs thrown in. Critical arts are usually just two buttons, and sometimes a direction. You also have the option of just pushing R1. I don't know about other people, but the hardest thing in Street Fighter 5 for me was canceling a special into a critical art. Double quarter motions after the short window of a special move connecting was just too hard for me to pull off consistently. Having access to a super with a touch of a button is makes it way easier to combo into. Tekken 7 is more accessible, but still has great depth to it's fighting mechanics.  The online isn't as great as some reviewers made it ought to be. I found myself struggling to find a match with a good connection, and waiting for a good amount of time before I got into a match. Connections dropped more often than I'd like. It's ok, but it needs some work. In terms of all the fighting games I played, including Street Fighter, MK, Injustice, KOF, Blazblue, and Soul Calibur. Tekken  takes the cake, hands down.

Salutations, first off let me say that when I first downloaded this game I knew it was a demo but I only expected a few hours of gameplay like similar other demo. What you get is a lot more than that. Great story...check, well fleshed out characters...check, (excuse me for my french) A ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that made me almost punch my computer...check. ChuSingura 46+1 S is so far a great Demo but there are a few cons as well.
First let start off with the few cons of the game before I begin singing praises. As stated this is only a demo with only the first chapter available and so that you know it is a kinetic novel as you won't have to make any decisions at all. Where I thought I could make decisions there was no choices to be made. The game gives you that feeling quite a bit at certain parts. There are a few typoes in the text so you have to guess what was said. Especially when there's only one word written, but you hear the characters speaking out whole sentences.
Now for the Pros of the game. Though this is a demo don't expect to finish it in one sitting for me it took about 30 hours of reading on auto and very little sleep.The story at first reminded me of the koihime series with a slight twist, but quickly steps out on it own. With some excellent foreshadowing and a few well placed twists and turns here and there the story draws you in. At times there are sad parts and tradegies that tug at your heart and make you cry. I did and I'm proud to admit it cause that's how immersed I was in the story. Not to say there aren't times of cuteness and silliness cause there is especially when it comes to Kuranosuke in her loli form and even Tsunayoshi on the rare occasion.
Characters are well fleshed out and draw you in with their individuality as well. The main villain in my P.O.V. is well done any time you want to punch your screen cause of how mad the villain gets you is a definite plus. The music is good and helps set the mood for you.
All in all this great game and I hope for more soon though to make it an all ages edition might take some time to do. Especially compared to the uncut original version even the opening is slightly different for obvious reasons. Thank you for taking your time read this and all hail Kuranosuke!!!!

*spoilers ahead* A unique game. You take control of the two brothers represented individually by the analog sticks on your controller. Basically, it's a little like a co-op game for single player. You'll need the brothers to work together to progress through the chapters.
The puzzles are pretty straightforward and won't have you scratching your head to figure them out (hey, not even me). There's virtually no threat to you either (okay, so the wolves killed me a few times) but you can still get a sense of the journey and the risk the boys are taking in order to save their father.
It's a short game but that's okay. The game is worth it for how beautiful it looks and the storytelling. The fact that there's no narrative but a Sim-like language spoken between the characters it's a nice touch. The story is told through its visuals.
The world you progress through is mysterious and full of otherworldly creatures, adding to the experience. There's more to this place than meets the eye.
The ending? Hm, *obvious spoilers here* is morbid and bleak. It won't leave you feeling uplifted but instead leave you feeling, dare I say, depressed? If you're already feeling down I'd steer clear but otherwise this is absolutely recommended.

This is the Citizen Kane of games. It's so brutal and rage inducing at first, but your self-genocidal deaths count for something in this game. Picture yourselves as Bill Murray and Tom Cruise reliving the day over and over but being skilled and knowledgably after each and every death. This is the quintessential rogue-like.
Controller or keyboard you say? Tomatoes ,Tomatos. Apples, Oranges. It’s always about your preference. No kills during your run? Sure why not! No gold till the end game? Of course! Try doing both in one speed run? It’s achievable. Point is, your playstyle will fit to anything in this game.
This game along with Binding of Isaac are the quintessential “podcast” games. Do you constantly listen to audiobooks, podcasts, or John Bonham’s drum solo from Moby♥♥♥♥♥♥ Then this is the perfect tag along game for you. While the music is perfect for this game, I just love the combo of podcast and Spelunky.
Another good way to look at this as the quintessential platformer is almost how it makes you paranoid. In Mario, you see a stack of coins leading up into the sky and you jump impulsively to catch the coins. Now in Spelunky, if you didn’t look up before hand or even down to get some gold, who knows if an arrows or spikes will meet your fate. You are constantly memorizing how the enemies and level layouts work. As much as you’re running left and right, you need to be careful going up and down. You know when the first level can either give you 8900 gold or 30000. Or even when you praise the RNG gods when they give you a jetpack in a crate and two pick axes in each subsequent levels.
Now if I would have to give this game constructive criticism, I would say simple one thing: I do not know whether it’s the teleporter’s fault or my own. I keep teleporting into walls and structures. Also when you’re running and whipping a crate, and you somehow get climbing gloves. It just hurts.
Lastly, I want to share this quote from the creator Derek Yu, “Make sure the core mechanics are fun. It should be fun to execute the most basic interactions, because that’s what players will be doing the most when they play your game. Ultimately, you want this core to drive your development.” That’s what drives insane people like your humble friend and reviewer to replay this over and over and over. It’s not insanity, it’s just Spelunky.
Tl;dr: Buy this game. You will know the jetpack, and the jetpack will set you free

===
Portal Knights is a sandbox action game with RPG and crafting elements, in which the player's objective will be to travel through various portals to different areas, to defeat the Portal Guardians, powerful creatures that exist in remote and dangerous areas of the world. This title is heavily inspired by the now all-time classic Minecraft, in fact many elements of its gameplay are taken out straight from it, while some others are entirely new and make it more than just another Minecraft clone.
===
Portal Knights follows the general gameplay of sandbox, block-based games, which is explore, loot, craft, fight. In this game you will be able to reactivate portals all over the world and use them to get to other areas with different climate, loot, enemies and quests. As you progress, the areas will contain better materials but also stronger enemies and more elaborate dungeons. Your character gains experience both from fighting and also looting materials and containers, when an experience level is achieved, you will be able to assign statistic points such as Strenght, Dexterity, Intelligence and so on, other than, also, unique Traits that vary for each of the three available classes, which are Warrior, Mage and Scout. Levels are very important but so is equipment, and to craft better stuff you'll have an array of facilities at your disposal, such as Anvils, Workbenches and Furnaces, each upgradeable various times to unlock new, more powerful blueprints to create. You have the possibility of building a base anywhere you want, as there is a teleportation pad you can place in any world anytime where you can return at your command. Also many other useful tools for base building are present, such as magic anti-enemy barriers to prevent mobs from spawning inside your fortress. The overall gameplay is quite classic for this type of game but has some elements that make it unique and involving, not just another copy-paste of Minecraft. The game can be player both solo or with co-op (local and online), and is enjoyable in both ways. This game also has an Event system, which basically makes special events happen in a random World on the map, these events often include unique enemies or special locations, and offer unique rewards aswell, so better check them out.
Combat in Portal Knights is based upon dodging at the right time and studying the attack patterns of each unique enemy you will face. enemies of your same level are generally quite tough and failing in avoiding their attacks multiple times will end up in your quick death, as healing items have a cooldown and generally, especially with non-durable classes such as the Mage, dodging and keeping your distance becomes very important. There is a quite good array of skills you can create at specialized workbenches and then learn, each skill will cost Mana which can be restored with items or slowly over-time. There also are various types of weapons for each class, for example Mage has Heavy Staff and Wand, the first is more damaging but slower, while the other is quicker but weaker. A system of elemental strenghts and weaknesses is present and is important to understand which element is weak to what other one in order to inflict maximum damage to each enemy. Items has a series of bonuses and statistics such as Critical Chance, More Health, Critical Mutliplier and so on, so there is also a RPG element to the equipment which adds some depth and build customization to the game.
There is quite a lot of content in Portal Knights. If you want to explore everything, and set the maximum size of environments to Large which is actually an option and gives you more stuff to do and explore, it will take you about 25-30 hours to do everything. The absence of a Creative mode for just building and design enthusiasts is quite missed and would give content a boost for sure. Still, for the price we're talking about, the content / price ratio is more than decent.
Basically the balacing of Portal Knights can be divided in three segments: whenever you start a new tier of worlds, you will have the worst stuff and enemies will be very difficult to kill, so focusing on harvesting and crafting is recommended, then you will get mid-level stuff and enemies will be quite tough but beatabale, and then you get the best stuff at that point in the game and almost all enemies become easy to kill unless they are special ones or bosses. A more refined balance of higher tier gear would have made the challenge tougher but not overly so, this is the only dent in an otherwise good overall balancing.
The challenge rating for this game is Medium-Low, since it is 50/50Level and Gear / Skill based and grinding will mostly be the key to overcome more powerful foes where skill cannot, sure personal skill in combat and dodging matters to a degree but also equipment does, especially later in the game.
===
Graphics, for this kind of game, are very good. Especially dynamic illumination and shadows are done well. Textures are of good quality as enemy and player models are. Animations are decent. Overall the graphical and art style is pleasant, colorful, rich and well done. Graphically is above average for a sandbox, block-based game.
Average sound effects and soundtracks, nothing either special or bad to mention.
Voxel based games of this type matched with a above-average graphical engine result often in being heavy, but in this case optimization is quite good and this game will run even on older systems with a few adjustments. Pelase not this game is mostly RAM and CPU intensive than it is GPU intensive, mind that.
No stability problems to report.
Enemy AI is a simple attack-pattern and follow based AI, common in this type of games and Portal Knights makes no exception in this field. Average, nothing more or less.
Quality of life aspects of this game are by FAR the worst part, seriously this game almost got a downvote just for this so read CAREFULLY. Containers for items cannot be labeled in any way and have minuscule space compared to the quantity of items you find. Also character inventory is very small, this leads to building massive quantities of chests in your base and returning often to deposit materials. Too often. Combat is decent but the whole lock-on system is quite bad and will lead you to death in more than one occasion. You cannot cast healing spells on your teammates if your health is full, this is frustrating for support mage classes ans also quite stupid. Your entire party has to teleport with any of you if one decides to leave a world and go to another. This leads to massive quantities of times to farm materials and stuff because only ONE world at a time can be farmed. Events give no rewards.
World generation can sometimes lead to strange environments and dungeon placements, other than this, one only major bug was found: when a player interacts with a door opened by another player in the exact moment it is opening, the player whi did not open the door but interacted with it, will not be able to attack or use any item for a few minutes, then the bug will vanish. Nothing else to report.
===
Portal Knights is more than a Minecraft clone for sure, some ideas are good but some things feel unfinished, like the sparse and little quantity of quests from NPCs or the absence of dedicated Controller and Keyboard UIs. quality of life is borderline A JOKE and seriously cripples a game that could have been much better.
Glad take-two really cares about the community that keeps its games fun /s

I have read a few reviews on the store page so i thought, even though i have still invested just a couple of hours into the game, I'd write a few lines to point other potential buyers in (what it think is) the right direction.
When you go for Mortal Kombat you really already know what to expect. The game mechanics are tried and tested and there is really no way for you not to have fun.
Want fast paced fights? Check!
Want ninjas, monsters, necromancers, shaolin monks and whatnot? Step right over here!
Want Fatalites? We gotcha!
Developers brought a few new ideas into the mix this time though, first the brought back brutalities which are simply finishing moves much like fatalities only triggered by combos. Second, they decided to make every character unique by differentiating it with three combat styles that gives the character access to a particular moveset. It might seem like a stupid thing, but having access to a specific set of inputs really changes the whole game.
Take Scorpion for example: The ninjutsu style gives him pretty much the same moveset as MK9. A second style instead, gives him access to his two swords that make it easier for him to launch enemies into the air and start juggle combos.
Besides this the game also has multiple modes to keep you entertained. If you want offline play you can meddle with the story mode or try out single matches, the kript, the towers.. really a lot of things to keep you busy here.
Online mode is no less, you have faction war (you basically choose a faction and every win in the online mode adds point to you team) with particular events like invasions.
The true weak point of the game is poor optimization. Besides the large game size and the huge patches, the game keeps on running sluggishly. I understand that I am playing this on a portable PC but i'm quite sure the game can definitely run on medium settings at least. Instead i'm stuck on running it with all Visual effects off and at minimum resolution (800x600) just to enjoy it properly. Even with this configuration though, the game has some hiccups at times.
As for DLC's i don't really see the point in whining. One may consider these to be a major or minor weak point, but i just don't care. If you think DLC's are not worthy of your money, the only thing you have to do is not buy them. They don't really cut off any extra parts of the story but just add a handful of fighters... I don't really see what the fuss is all about.
In the end, I think the game itself is worth the price, given that there are interesting ideas and the gameplay is fun. I can see how the optimization will throw off a lot of people but i think it'll get sorted over time.

"What is it"? Silly question... It's Mortal Kombat! It's Sub-Zero, it's fatalities, it's "GET OVER HERE!", it's gallons of blood and gore etc. etc.
This is the tenth installment in the main line of Mortal Kombat fighting games, hailing from the first release in '92. The franchise has stood out for it's focus on "realistic" violence.
My history with MK goes way back. I was not old enough to play them but did anyway and I've loved them ever since. I'd like to say I've played 'em all but I know there are some releases I never played. Much to my dismay these also seem to be the best games :(
When playing the older games (1,2,3) as a kid you'd maybe wonder "Oh man, what if this was like real?". Well with MKX arrives the answer to that question! I'm not saying that MKX looks very "realistic" per se but the technical graphics are impressive. From the crevices in Ermacs face to the wet-effects when fighting in the Sky Temple to the blood effects.
They've kept the art style intact. Of course the costumes have been updated but you've never at a loss for who's who. Raiden's still sporting his asian-style straw hat, Kano's still the guy with the half-robot face and Mileena's still the source of nightmares!
Oh and speaking of the visual style for the lady kombatans: The females of MK have never been known for wearing much clothing, and even if they did it would be pretty damned pornographic in nature! While not completely untrue in MKX, I must say that their original attires are generally more clothed and battle-appropriate.
So I mentioned I wouldn't do this bit. Half true. I'm writing explaining why I'm not:
I don't generally have much interest in fighting online. That's just how I am. However I did try to match up for singles-fights online but I never found any :S I could sit looking for ten minutes and nothing. Bug or just few people online? Beats me.
However the few online interactions I've had is with the faction war feature. Upon entering the game you've prompted to enter a faction. You can earn so called War-Points for your faction by completing certain challenges and these points determine which faction wins that week. All factions get bonuses for participating but the winning faction obviously gets larger bonuses.
So there's a couple of modes available in SP mostly composed of a variety of towers, including endless, survival etc.
The modes that stand out I suppose are the Living towers. They require an internet connection and are updated every hour, day and week. They're generally themed and feature a variety of modifiers.
The roster is pretty much what you would've expect from a MK game - The veterans are mostly there, Scorpion, Sub-Zero, Liu Kang, Raiden and so on. But there's also a couple of new ones visiting. I'd say they're not spectacular but there's some interesting additions such as the new ruler of Outworld and some of his underlings, there's also the offspring of certain returning characters.
Some interesting choices were made for the roster. Some characters were cut, among them some which you can understand and some which are just so much connected with the franchise that I don't understand how they coul've excluded them (if not for future DLC). I mean Stryker is a forgivable exclusion but Baraka? Nightwolf? Like I said - interesting.
The krypt also makes a return, this time with an interactive twist to it. It used to be just the "area where you unlock stuff". It still is but now it's also the area which you explore and experience in first person. There's timed chests, there's puzzles and jump scares. These damned spiders and wolves always manage to scare me outta my chair. As you gasp for air, you're asked to press buttons to defeat your surprise attacker. I often fail at these challenges...
Right so to conclude this review I'd say the latest entry into the MK franchise is a good one. I look forward to eventually seeing more characters coming to the game. I have had a blast with this game so far and I'd recommend this game to anyone with an interest in fighting games.

I'm a newcomer to the Tekken series, but comparing this game to Street Fighter 5, its so much better. Firstly, it's more fun to watch and play then Street Fighter. No more fire ball spamming, for the most part, and no more wake up dps that make you want to punch your computer screen. Some characters have them, but due to Tekken's 3D mechanics, I think that even characters like Akuma are pretty balanced. The game looks nice, and runs on my rig on high just fine, consistent 60 fps. The launch content is far more substantial than SFV. There is story mode, arcade mode, treasure mode, and loads more characters. Additionally, I like the combos system in Tekken much more than in Street Fighter 5. Tekken combos are mostly button strings with directional imputs thrown in. Critical arts are usually just two buttons, and sometimes a direction. You also have the option of just pushing R1. I don't know about other people, but the hardest thing in Street Fighter 5 for me was canceling a special into a critical art. Double quarter motions after the short window of a special move connecting was just too hard for me to pull off consistently. Having access to a super with a touch of a button is makes it way easier to combo into. Tekken 7 is more accessible, but still has great depth to it's fighting mechanics.  The online isn't as great as some reviewers made it ought to be. I found myself struggling to find a match with a good connection, and waiting for a good amount of time before I got into a match. Connections dropped more often than I'd like. It's ok, but it needs some work. In terms of all the fighting games I played, including Street Fighter, MK, Injustice, KOF, Blazblue, and Soul Calibur. Tekken  takes the cake, hands down.

EXP share. As Weiss, The AOE blast killed quite a few mobs that my team members were attacking. They got no EXP, so I had to really work at not immediately killing everything with it so the rest of the team got EXP, and it still didnt help much.
Semblances. In the series, they all a special ability unique to them. Ruby's speed, Weiss' glyphs, Blake's shadow clone. and Yang's power increase when injured.
Special points. I understand that the special attacks are powerful, but if you get hit in the middle of a combo, or stop, your special gauge resets. I've played this before for the xbox but then saw it was on offer on steam, with its DLC and thought i'd pick it up. I wasnt dissappointed. The character creation in terms of the physical appearance of your face is rather simplistic in that there's only a few presets to choose from. Four diffference races to choose from determines the apperance of your character with each giving a starting bonus to some skills. From there you go to change hair, skin colour, eyeshadow, lipstick shade, tattoo and body jewelry.
The leveling up system is simplistic too. There are base skills like lock picking and blacksmithing which let you interact with the world better and the combat system is split into three sections, finesse, might and sorcery with players being allowed to invest in each one if they wish which really allows you to customise your playthrough; something which alot of RPG's tend to overlook, either you're an archer or a mage... you cant be both.
The open world means you can do as you wish, or not do as is my case sometimes. Each area is populated with monsters at specific levels so be careful to not wander too far out early on but then again, why not?
The controls are little fiddly to get a hang on first off and I would definitely recommend setting the "run" key to toggle rather than hold.

I deleted my old review because I wanted to REALLY review it.
This game is incredible. Absolutely mind-blowing. It will make you puke rainbows for days.
The atmosphere of the game is great! No matter where you are, you've still got just enough content to really take in your environment even from the top-down perspective. Each act, in itself, is a different environment and even in those acts, you explore all different lands and experience a smooth looking game.
Each class is unique is lots of ways. There's the Charge system, which holds unique benefits depending on what class you are. All the classes have their own benefits but all in all, no matter what class you are, you can always use any weapon you want.  For example, want to be a Embermage wielding a pistol in one hand and donning a shield in the other? Be my guest. However, not every skill each class has will be compatible with every weapon.
Unfortunately, a lot of the quests are quite bland and are pretty much the same every act. It's usually getting you to travel to a dungeon, complete the dungeon and kill the boss at the end to progress. Side quests range from collecting an item to also going to a dungeon and killing its boss.
Once you finish the game, you can proceed into New Game+, holding harder monsters with higher rewards (it starts at your level, too), or you can complete a few maps, which are basically dungeons in themselves, but sometimes hold strange benefits or disadvantages. Alternatively, though, you can check out the Steam Workshop for user-created content -- some of it is amazing!
All in all, Torchlight II is a magnificant game, and I feel it was worth the wait (I pre-ordered it then waited months 'till it finally released). I've finished it twice already on an Engineer and Embermage, but already started my third playthrough on an Outlander. I recommend picking this up if you're a Dungeon Crawler fan! It'll be well worth your time. Thank you for reading, and have a good day/night.

Short but very inspired game. VIsuals truly set the atmosphere of this game, there really are a lot of different settings you happen to play in. There's a nice care for detail, you might notice some basic sort of side-activities, not literally sidequests but just a few things you can do (usually to help around, or communicate) that make the game world feel a bit less tight.
PC keyboard controls work, maybe the the hard part about playing with two characters aren't the controls, but finding the exact spot that's supposed to trigger the event or the action you're supposed to work for.
Dialogue wise, it's funny that the game is labelled as "English language" on the store page! All of the voice over is made in a fantasy language, and that's a bit of a shame because using a *real* english voice user could've add a layer that would have made for much more empathy towards the characters. Brothers is a game where two brothers embark on a quest to bring back water from a giant tree far away from home to cure their father. I didn't really expect anything when I bought and played this game, and boy I was in for a treat. The cinematography in this game is amazing, there are many times you would have that urge to just stop for a moment and take a screenshot of where you are.
In this game, you have to rely on what you see to understand what is happening. The characters do speak, but you won't really understand much since they speak a fictional language. This does raise a few questions here and there, but overall they do a fantastic job at painting the tone of the world. The gameplay is unique, and I recommend using the controller for the best experience.
Storywise? Amazing. There are several memorable moments, some of joy while others of somber and they sure know how to hit them feels. During my initial playthrough I had mixed feelings about the story. But upon rethinking I can appreciate how they did the story. This is a story of two brothers, travelling in a beautiful but harsh world. They live in a world where there is love and kindness, but they must also be cautious and prepared for the dangers hiding in every corner.
The only thing I would complain is that the playtime is a bit short, but other than that it's a 10/10 to me. Highly recommended game.

This is the Citizen Kane of games. It's so brutal and rage inducing at first, but your self-genocidal deaths count for something in this game. Picture yourselves as Bill Murray and Tom Cruise reliving the day over and over but being skilled and knowledgably after each and every death. This is the quintessential rogue-like.
Controller or keyboard you say? Tomatoes ,Tomatos. Apples, Oranges. It’s always about your preference. No kills during your run? Sure why not! No gold till the end game? Of course! Try doing both in one speed run? It’s achievable. Point is, your playstyle will fit to anything in this game.
This game along with Binding of Isaac are the quintessential “podcast” games. Do you constantly listen to audiobooks, podcasts, or John Bonham’s drum solo from Moby♥♥♥♥♥♥ Then this is the perfect tag along game for you. While the music is perfect for this game, I just love the combo of podcast and Spelunky.
Another good way to look at this as the quintessential platformer is almost how it makes you paranoid. In Mario, you see a stack of coins leading up into the sky and you jump impulsively to catch the coins. Now in Spelunky, if you didn’t look up before hand or even down to get some gold, who knows if an arrows or spikes will meet your fate. You are constantly memorizing how the enemies and level layouts work. As much as you’re running left and right, you need to be careful going up and down. You know when the first level can either give you 8900 gold or 30000. Or even when you praise the RNG gods when they give you a jetpack in a crate and two pick axes in each subsequent levels.
Now if I would have to give this game constructive criticism, I would say simple one thing: I do not know whether it’s the teleporter’s fault or my own. I keep teleporting into walls and structures. Also when you’re running and whipping a crate, and you somehow get climbing gloves. It just hurts.
Lastly, I want to share this quote from the creator Derek Yu, “Make sure the core mechanics are fun. It should be fun to execute the most basic interactions, because that’s what players will be doing the most when they play your game. Ultimately, you want this core to drive your development.” That’s what drives insane people like your humble friend and reviewer to replay this over and over and over. It’s not insanity, it’s just Spelunky.
Tl;dr: Buy this game. You will know the jetpack, and the jetpack will set you free

I love this game:) The newest installment of the Mortal Kombat franchise futuring old and some new characters. Sadly favorites like Noob Saibot, Smoke and many others from the last game are not present. Gladly most of the important classic characters are included. This may or may not be a turnoff for some.
The game is noticably darker looking than the last game and goes for a more realistic look compared to the last one. No more bright colors and huge boobies. I think the art direction is mostly positive..
The story mode is a bit shorter, but not as short as some people say. I still have my old runthough video from the last game and it took me 4 hours and 22 minutes after the credit roll. This new game took me 3 hours and 43 minutes.
The story continues from the last game, in the new timeline set by Raiden. If you loved the older Mortal Kombat games from the 90s and for some reason did not play the last game, I would highly recommend that you play through that story first. It feels very nostalgic with a few twists, as Raiden has knowledge of the future.
Since this story is a continuation it does not have the same nostalgic effect, but is still worth playing through.
Thankfully even if some "important" characters died or somehow "changed" in the last story mode, this have not prevented Netherrealm from including them in this game. There were some characters that I would have surely missed if they had not been included. And even if they may or may not be a huge part in the new story there are some very much enjoyable arcade endings for theese characters as well.
Every characters have 3 variations that adds different special attacks and often alters their move set a bit. If you look closely every variation also changes that characters appearance. Which variation you choose will also affect each costume.
The new Mortal Kombat is just as gory as it always have been (if you discount the Nintendo censored version of the first game, hehe). The X-Ray system from the last game is still present and there are Fatalities, Brutalities and the new Faction kills.
The faction kills are unlocked as you level up your faction, they are easy to perform, can be used on every character and are unique for each faction. If you play regularly, leveling up a faction is relatively fast. There is even a achivement for leveling all factions up. Keep in mind that you will loose all your faction progress if you leave.
For some reason they dropped the Stage Fatalities from the last game and seems unwilling to give us Friendships and Bablities.. If you play online and your opponent rage quits you get a Quitality!
In case you are wondering, this game is not ment for kids.
The gameplay is as you might expect from a Mortal Kombat game. Two opponents beat each other to death, best of three rounds, fatality!
It is worth mentioning that the 2 player Tag mode have been removed. Instead we have group fights, these requires 3 or 4 people teams. If you only have 1 friend who is about your level in fighting games, you will have to do with single matches against each other or if you both feel like it "king of the hill" mode. There are no way for 2 friends to play together on a team against other players online and I think that is a shame.
There are a few negative things that I feel is worth mentioning:
- 15 GB patches! Patches for this game comes in the awesome sizes of about 15GB.. If you have a slow internet connection or your internet provider limits the amount you can download, this will probably be more than a minor annoyance,..
- Performance problems for many people. I have not personally witnessed this but the forums are full of people crying for their high end rigs and low fps (frames per secound)...
- The online play suffers because of theese problems as the game uses peer to peer. If you are to fight someone with low or unstable fps, the game will slow down or lag for you too. There is also alot of talk about the bad netcode beeing better on the consoles, could be related to some pcs not running at 60fps...
- Requires iOs/android app to unlock some awesome (I think must have) costumes. This is horribly bad because the mobile game is of the now sadly common "pay to win" type. It has gameplay even worse than thoose old "Tiger handheld LCD games" from the 80s and mid 90s.  This modern mobile game does not require any skill, only money or lots of time grinding. Tap, tap finger slide is a perfect description of the gameplay, and wait for energy to come back. The graphics are prettier than toose older inferior mobile ports though. But like mentioned, even worse gameplay. Put your phone in the R-Zone and you will probably suffer the ultimate low of gaming possible.

EXP share. As Weiss, The AOE blast killed quite a few mobs that my team members were attacking. They got no EXP, so I had to really work at not immediately killing everything with it so the rest of the team got EXP, and it still didnt help much.
Semblances. In the series, they all a special ability unique to them. Ruby's speed, Weiss' glyphs, Blake's shadow clone. and Yang's power increase when injured.
Special points. I understand that the special attacks are powerful, but if you get hit in the middle of a combo, or stop, your special gauge resets. Let's Review...RWBY: Grimm Eclipse.
If somehow you didn't know, RWBY: Grimm Eclipse is a hack-and-slash game by RoosterTeeth Games. As far as i'm aware, this would be their second game and it is pretty well-off for early access.
The Menu:
Yeah, sure; The menu isn't super technical and may not be as flashy as other games, but it does carry itself with the font and color. I know it's probably not noticable, but it does make a visual difference.
The Settings:
Just looking at face value, the settings seem to be very bare-bones and simplistic. Now, one could argue that the enjoyment is really more gated towards gameplay instead of having you fiddle around in the resolution and graphical differences. But on the other hand, getting the best possible qualtiy from your equipment or visual enjoyment is what some people strive for. It's a mixed bag for me.
Now the main part, The Gameplay:
There isn't a single-player campaign mode, but you can access a sort of pseudo-single player by establishing a private lobby and just hopping in to the carnage by yourself. The online mode is more focused on. You can join in a Quick Match, create a new lobby with New Game, the previously mentioned Play with Friends, and lastly just straight up leave like you never wanted to be there anyway (Exiting highly un-recommended).
The player models are intact and are retty close to what you would see in the show. The animations are pretty good and very fluid. Since it IS in developement, there was maybe one or two hiccups for me, but they corrected themselves. There is a respawn and revive system, but it leans more towards having you get revived rather than respawning.
The combat is very hack-and-slash, reminiscent of almost Devil May Cry or even Dynasty Warriors. The abilities are super helpful when crowded by Grimm, but you only get to a cerain level so not all upgrades can be unlocked, so choose carefully. There about 3 abilities to choose from and are quite similar between characters (Weiss' Nova and Yang's Quake) are both AoE attackes and the difference is just the effect it has...which could mean they're different?
The environment are scenic and pretty, but they do have a sort of Tales of feel. You know, where the plains are absurdely large and there are only enough monsters for about an eighth of the filed, that's how RWBY: GRimm Eclipse plays it and it's not so bad when you playing with four people (The fieds flood with darkness), but by anything less than 2, the field is just to big. Other than that, it works well.
My suggestions and Thoughts:
This are all open to discussion from you all (Players of RWBY: GRimm Eclipse and/or  others). Don't get me wrong, RWBY: Grimm Eclipse is a great game and good starting point to further developement, but it's far from complete.
I'm not to miffed at the menues or the settings. Could they be improved upon, but not in any need for a complete overhaul. The lobby system the game uses is also fine. Within point, Nothing technical needs to change.
The combat works as is, but tere should be more skills to choose from or implement semblances as a 4 skill that uses all special at once. The skill trees fit their purpose, however I feel as though if they maybe implemented the passive skills in with active skills it would look more like a tree, or even include more specific passive skills that increase damage, range etc. of the active skills.
In regard to the environment, although lovely and battle spacious, in my mind it feels like there is hidden potential in it. Maybe, have class assignments that fall like dead-drops and add more challenges or specific condition for bonus EXP. You could also add a mini boss, beside Alpha Beowolves and Ursas.
And just for kicks (Kinda serious) there is only one thing that I can think that may just be fan service and not really the best choice for overall developement. But what if there was an option to model and script you own character into the game. Now, I understand some people could easily turn this into a bad thing, but there are also good things that could come from it. I don't know, just food for thought.
Although this review may have came off as strangely negative, I hold nothing but the highest regards and faith in RooserTeeth Games in making RWBY: Grimm Eclipse one of the greats. So to you, The Members of the RoosterTeeth Games crew, Keep up the Great work.

Pros:
-Excellent combat: It takes a bit of getting used to; because the game LOOKS so much like an MMO, you expect to just be able to hold down M1 and swish around. This is not the case. Combat takes a bit more skill than that, and honestly reminds me a bit of Dark Souls, just cleaned up around the edges a bit. You get several "encounter powers" that use mana, and these come with every class. The ability to slip into "Fate mode" is an awesome addition, basically everything slows down and the last thing you kill is smote in an epic slow-mo QTE.
-Great art style: The graphics kind of remind me of Torchlight, but if you could zoom waaay in on Torchlight and see all the little details. It's overall smooth, and, once again, reminiscent of your typical MMO. Overall the landscape is bright and colorful, and there's never a lack of things to look at even in the darkest, gloomiest caverns.
-Good animations: Overall the game flows. I suppose this ties mostly into combat, but I hardly ever see things chopping around. It's not exactly the best in show for animation, but only the occasional buggy-eyed townie and jump to another stance while in combat break the immersion, and the physics hardly ever seem out of place.
Cons:
Crafting: My biggest bone to pick with this game is the crafting system. I personally have had a difficult time figuring it out, and it really doesn't seem worth it. There are Smithing, Alchemy, and "Sagecraft," each representing weapon/armor crafting, potion crafting, and enchantment crafting respectively. Sagecraft is a bit like Torchlight's enchantment system, where you can upgrade gem shards into enchantments for your weapons. My problem is, I can seldom find weapons that are better than my starter (from a DLC I'm assuming) hammer, The Mountain, which lacks an enchantment slot. So I'm brought to wonder what the point of that even is. I haven't focused on Alchemy at all seeing as I can just buy potions, and am brought back to my Sagecraft problem when it comes to Smithing. Nothing I can fabricate is better than The Mountain thus far. Furthermore, the crafting skills all level with you, assuming you've put your one skill point per level into a crafting skill. There's no way to level them up besides this, which is probably just as good considering they seem to be fairly useless entities.
Music and Sounds: The music is fitting in most circumstances, but the sounds could have been done a lot better. In particular the grunts/squeals of the various characters and fauna; the action noises and other sound effects are just fine. Right off the bat though, you're met with strange grunting noises that seem out of place and repetative as your character decends from a pile of dead bodies. You can replicate this awkward, way-too-long performance at any time by repeatedly smashing the sprint button; if this is done right, the player character will take on the posture and personality of a large ape as he lopes towards his next objective, making strange gutteral noises while he does so. I also found the animals to have similarly small sound banks that tend to repeat themselves a tad too often.
Overall the pros certainly outweigh the cons, and for such a low sale price you'll get many hours of quality gameplay.

If you run around trying to find a reason to not play it despite already owning it, I really don't know what to say.
Sure, it's one of the highest ALL TIME community rated games on Steam, but it's also notorious for it's difficulty.
An average of 9/10 approval rating doesn't express itself properly... A game which often goes out of it's way to remove any possibility of escape, any possibility of success, boxes you into a corner or abyss without tools to leave should you make one poor choice. A game which might spawn you in a location where the lack of bombs forces you to jump headlong into a triple dart trap, without any bait whatsoever, likely killing you if you were already low on health, possibly knocking you waywards into that spike pit 50 yards away, or the spider. Or the bat. Or the snake. Or off a cliff. The game doesn't care.
The controls? Simple.
The premise? Leave the level, preferably short of two and a half minutes.
The reward? Maybe some sense of accomplishment knowing you didn't mess up this time. This time.
The only flaw this game really has is your poor choices. Like choosing to jump down without checking first. Or killing a pacified NPC. Or making dumb decisions that will blow up the shop. Oh, right. Poor choices, not flaws.
And like I said... maybe the poorest choice of all was not touching the game despite having owned it for nearly two years, or three months, or 3 weeks. What're ya waiting for. An invitation?
Maybe the scariest thing is, for once... it's not that a difficult game is well acclaimed by the majority, but that IGN managed to write an accurate review.

Gonna get into the meat of this right away: If you are planning on buying this to play with your friends - don't. The multiplayer system this game uses is very bad. Any time anyone in your game wants to move to another island to gather materials for crafting - YOUR ENTIRE party has to come too. You can't set up a base and build because your entire party has to leave the island when someone needs to make a run to get building supplies. Does someone need to travel to another island quickly to get a few gems to make something? EVERYONE COMES WITH YOU. There isn't even any affirmation or anything... every single player is suddenly forced into a loading screen if anyone in the server initiates a load.
This single issue nearly completely breaks the game if you wish to play with other people. You end up just lugging your crafting tables with you and crafting on the spot instead of doing any actual building.

- Loot is just generic potions and crafting bricks.
- It took me 4 hours before I finally was able to make a new weapon due to shortage of materials. That is way too long.

- The islands don't really hide any secrets or treasures. Just really short dungeons (if you can call them that) which contain a chest containing generic potions.

I played it for a considerable time and some time before writing this review.  The game has tremedous POTENTIAL.
Tech;  The game has a tremendously extensive tech tree.  Unfortunately too many of the techs only lead to other techs and yielded nothing in an of themselves.
Command and control of units;  While you're able to build battalions of ground units which is fine, there is no good command and control system.  For a world wide game battalions need to be in divisions with some command control structure.  HOI3 has a good system.  At least ships can be put into battlegroups which can represent fleets fairly well.  There are issues with the handling of air units as well.
Economy;  The game has an extensive economic system.  You have many tools to tweak your economy. Many cities are in the game with populations listed.  Here the game misses a golden opportunity.  Rather than use popuation to limit facilities built in a city, the game uses an arbitrary limit of 6 facilities per hex.  I'm sorry, but my home town which is in the game has no business having potentially as many facilities as the core hex of a major metropolis like NYC.
The game also has a very simple minded low unemployment rate equals high inflation rate. The economic system has many questionable aspects, but I don't consider those a game stopper.
Diplomacy; There are many different things you can do, but there are a couple things that bothered me.  One is there is only 5 levels of relationships.  It needs more than that.  Trading goods is limited to 90 day maximum trades which to me makes no sense for a game that can theoretically go for over 100 years. HOI3 system of being able to establish the trade and keep it going until someone cancels it is far superior.
The developers seem to be responsive, but they may be biting off more than they can chew.

This is one of the few Mortal Kombat games that interested me in the last decade, and boy, IS THIS GARBAGE. Its unacceptable for a fighting game to run at 10-20 FPS, it makes it downright impossible to play, and changing the graphic options doesn't help anything. The game is locked at a resolution of 1600x900 at the moment (which is fine by me, that's my size anyways, but maybe not for other people), the fighting UI is way too squished in, there's barely any room for the health bar, let alone the special meter before they sandwich the fighters. Hell, even the tutorial was♥♥♥♥♥♥poor, the choice of font and colour scheme makes it incredibly hard to learn, instead of utilizing a gamepad's directional and button inputs, they simply use basic letters, such as L+X, Y, LR + B on a white thin font with a black background. Why not use directional arrows and coloured buttons? It'll make learning combos much easier and faster, rather than sitting down and trying to decipher it and them memorize to heart before you even try it. Hell, even the universal fighting game language of 214C or 623B and 632146D is easier to understand than this.
You cannot even play this game offline, let alone online, the poor FPS makes it impossible to convert a hit confirm into a proper combo, as the game lags so much that it doesn't read all your inputs at the correct time, giving the opponent time to recouver and both of you going "wat". You basically have to YOLO combo in one fluid motion without any assurance if its a safe move or an unsafe move, doesn't matter how many frames are for this attack, it doesn't matter! YOLO!
Seriously, this is just unacceptable for a fighting game where frames matter ALOT for the game to function at all. Especially if your netcode is gonna suck as well, as if they didn't learn their lesson from Injustice's PC version. I'll admit, the game looks terrific to play (minus some grips on the stamina bar feature), and it does! On the PS4 and Xbox One version. What's that? One of the three platforms our game is on is having problems? Doesn't matter, we got their money. SEE YA!
Until they take the time to sit down, hire a QA team, and actually listen to them, this game is definitely a no-buy-can't-play list. This was just pushed out the door with little to no polish.
Now if you'll excuse me, I'll go play a good fighting game, like Guilty Gear, Street Fighter, Blazblue, Skullgirls, or even Persona 4 Arena. You heard me, an RPG turned fighting game does better than this.

I would much rather    prefer stunlock until your target finds a way out of it. Max is a fine example of that, a good melee    stunlock until his opponent finally turns around and blocks.

   The sword and blunt weapon and daggers and shield ALL can flip

   I understand that they don't want people to die in an instant from any distance but the Coffin and    Striker are just unusable at mid range.

   There is no variety here, another thing that irritates me. Each class is limited to 2 different    weapons, and you cannot have 2 of the same or one that belongs to a different class (With the    exception for Ivan and Rena's SMGs). No standard revolvers or pistols for anyone to share.

The game is pretty for being an Early Access Game. With that being said there are some things it needs to change and add. There are only 4 characters which are Ruby, Weiss, Blake, and Yang. Within the characters there are skills you can have, some take time to unlock but it is not that hard to unlock them after a few games.
There is only 3 different types of maps so far and it is all in one semi-long story line. The maps tend to have a one path way only kind of feel. So over all the game is Early Access for these reasons but it is good. If you like the show and want to kick some grimms' butts then this is the game for you. I like this game alot. its fun to play, and you can see the set up for an amazing story (its early access and the story is far from finished, as far as i can tell). now for with my quick praise time for pros, cons, and things i would like to see.
Pros-
The voice acting is pretty well made and actually sounds like the character, with yang making puns and ruby being excited over your first beowolf encounter.
The enemies are fun to fight, and it auto balances it depending on how many players you have.
The characters play like you would expect them to for the most part. yang carries a lot of force and knockback, ruby is good at constantly hitting and chaining, weiss is light and fast, and blake strikes fast and has many evasive based attacks.
Everything looks like the show. the animation is admittedly choppy, but the whole world and characters look like the show to a very good extent.
Cons-
As i just said, the animation is pretty choppy, if you run downhill expect to be stuck in one shape of the running animation, so you look like you are floating in the sky.
This isnt a con for me, but it might be for others. this is meant to be played multiplayer. you dont get ai teammates. this isnt a problem for me, but some people may dislike this feature.
some of the unlockable abilities might take a little while. some are pretty easy, like kill 100 enemies with your aoe attack. but some are hard, like kill 200 with your ranged attack (which generally does very little damage)
The little image things that show the person who is talking is sometimes super low quality. this just bothered me personally, but wont change the game.
Personal wants-
i want to see more characters. as awesome as it is to play as team RWBY, i would like to play as teams JNPR and SSSN. this is just me wanting more characters, as that would be fun.
more skills, because right now every character only 3 attacks that follow a pattern. AOE attack. Heavy damage attack that needs careful setup to hit more than one. And a ranged attack.
to sum it up, its fun, but flawed. as an early access game i would recommend it as it is fun. the controls work well with the keyboard or a controller. i would reccomend this game, but keep in mind it is flawed, as any early access game would be.

Great game. There aren't that many campaign missions, but the variety in difficulty makes up for that. You can go in Cadet mode with aim assist on and shoot your way through like Rambo and Deadshot combined...
or you can go full authentic mode where you can't tag any enemies and know you have a 99% chance of dying after pulling the trigger on your first enemy (and missing your shot thanks to the wind and gravity and the movement of your target).
or any variant in difficulty in between. The game gives you many choices of how you want to approach a mission target and I love that. Gun variety is decent but not fantastic. Would ahve loved a silenced sniper rifle, even if it wasn't real world realistic.
Multiplayer mode is pretty challenging too. It's hard to see your enemies so the game does force you to stay still and observe. But at the risk of being observed yourself. So you're also thinking about whether your skin blends into the background and where in the map you're hiding. Hide well, can't see well. Want to see in the open, also means you're exposed. Finding that balance is just part of the challenge. Then comes hitting your target.
Overall, great challenging game. Not for those that expect CSGO type AWP sniper. Nono... this one is going to make you breath slowly and make sure your mouse click trigger pull really counts. Satisfying when you complete a mission on a diffucult setting. Very very very satisying.

I find this very difficult to recommend,
The game itself is very well done and you can find yourself losing hours upon hours into it all the combat is fun and awesome to get into and the quests are interesting and have their own storyline and aren't usually fetch quests like stuff out of other open world games. Additionally the world looks very good. Not as good as a lot of other games granted. But pretty in it's own right, it has multiple locations showing different weathers with different botany.
The skill tree is incredible. It has a lot of skills and it is highly probable that you will find the way you like to fight on there as every weapon has it's own feel.
Lastly I can't recommend the faction quests enough (outside of the seemingly weird attraction fae have to you in spite of most fae completely despising/ignoring humans). The quests provided are interesting the stories are very good. and you will find yourself emmersed completely in the stories, at the end you feel like you have done something incredible and you will get something incredible for completing them.
However. Outside of the enjoyable combat and the incredible quests is a hopelessly big world, now usually that isn't a bad thing. When you here about a large world in any other games it would be a major selling point. However at least those games find ways of getting from point A to point B. In this game you have two options run, or roll (teleport dependant on your specialization). Some locations allow you a teleport locale (such as towns and dungeons) however it still requires you to run and get there. Now if the game was smaller that isn't a problem. But a large amount of your time will be spent doing that. take  10 minutes or so to do a side quest. Now double that. That is how long it takes to get to the objective. Half of your time will be spent travelling and running into additional groups of enemies that you have fought a large amount of times before. Game feels made for consoles but the port works fine. Controles are simplifed with buttons having multiple uses and the character draw distance being tiny.
Game is no longer being developed.
------------------------------
Overall it is a very enjoyable experiance just don't expect anything earthshattering.

This is one of the few Mortal Kombat games that interested me in the last decade, and boy, IS THIS GARBAGE. Its unacceptable for a fighting game to run at 10-20 FPS, it makes it downright impossible to play, and changing the graphic options doesn't help anything. The game is locked at a resolution of 1600x900 at the moment (which is fine by me, that's my size anyways, but maybe not for other people), the fighting UI is way too squished in, there's barely any room for the health bar, let alone the special meter before they sandwich the fighters. Hell, even the tutorial was♥♥♥♥♥♥poor, the choice of font and colour scheme makes it incredibly hard to learn, instead of utilizing a gamepad's directional and button inputs, they simply use basic letters, such as L+X, Y, LR + B on a white thin font with a black background. Why not use directional arrows and coloured buttons? It'll make learning combos much easier and faster, rather than sitting down and trying to decipher it and them memorize to heart before you even try it. Hell, even the universal fighting game language of 214C or 623B and 632146D is easier to understand than this.
You cannot even play this game offline, let alone online, the poor FPS makes it impossible to convert a hit confirm into a proper combo, as the game lags so much that it doesn't read all your inputs at the correct time, giving the opponent time to recouver and both of you going "wat". You basically have to YOLO combo in one fluid motion without any assurance if its a safe move or an unsafe move, doesn't matter how many frames are for this attack, it doesn't matter! YOLO!
Seriously, this is just unacceptable for a fighting game where frames matter ALOT for the game to function at all. Especially if your netcode is gonna suck as well, as if they didn't learn their lesson from Injustice's PC version. I'll admit, the game looks terrific to play (minus some grips on the stamina bar feature), and it does! On the PS4 and Xbox One version. What's that? One of the three platforms our game is on is having problems? Doesn't matter, we got their money. SEE YA!
Until they take the time to sit down, hire a QA team, and actually listen to them, this game is definitely a no-buy-can't-play list. This was just pushed out the door with little to no polish.
Now if you'll excuse me, I'll go play a good fighting game, like Guilty Gear, Street Fighter, Blazblue, Skullgirls, or even Persona 4 Arena. You heard me, an RPG turned fighting game does better than this.
