The game became a close memory that many of us hold close to our hearts, bringing a unique game from the wave of free-to-play gaming from korea in the 2000's. It provided Fast-Paced gameplay, with a high skill curve due to a glitch in the game that allowed players to execute complex inputs. Mainly known as K-style, it truely provided a "hardcore" expirience due to it's difficulty in execution and strict timing. For those who are unfamiliar with K-style below is a example along with the inputs (There is music so beware),

Below is a quick bit/review from my expiriences of trying both the Taiwan server and US server.
One main factor is
. For many this is a
deal, it was the sole reason why alot of players loved the first game so much. As the game strayed away from it's original intent, Maiet already adressed the issue in interviews regarding the decision on removing k-style. I understand many of you are upset, i was bummed too but im not going to let a crucial change for the better ruin my view on a franchise, if i really want to expirience K-style again there is allways private servers.
The playstyle of the game is now a tense, fast paced TPS more reliant on using firearms compared to what many were used to advanced attacks with melee weapons. Melee now is very situational.  Another is
.  Although it is a different game, it still preserves the freedom of mobility the first game offered which made it unique. The gameplay is much more focused on run and gun, but it can still be great fun. Simular to another TPS, S4 league, the game's insane pace is still here, with a shiny coat of paint. Getting the timing down and using the enviroment to your advantage still provided great key-mashing fun, such as when chaining dashes while in combat. It is still very easy to die if you make yourself a easy target by just aiming while on the ground, you will just get taken down quickly by easy head shots.
Most games were pretty great to run about and kick♥♥♥♥♥ but when played as a team it can be great fun. Deathmatch sort of reminded me of the good ol days of Quake-styled arena FPS, hectic as hell as you mow foes down and rush for Armor/Ammo spread about the place to sustain your rampage. There is slight inbalances among the game, but for the most part the classes do a great job of seperating playstyles, weaknesses and strengths, and many approches to gameplay.
The maps are very well designed, balanced with team-tactics in mind with each map having it's own unique feel. There are symetrical maps such as the mansion, big maps to even small closed enviroments that result in a chaotic brawl. But the most striking joy comes from using the map itself to your advantage, which is one of the key hooks of this game that make it unique. Thinking on the fly about every wall to climb, piece of cover, vantage point, object or area to decimate your enemies.
Although there is no K-style, there is some "techniques" players have discovered such as Melee animation canceling via jumping to create a stun-lock melee combo or cancelling dash frames by jumping to dash quickly again to move faster than running.
In terms of how it runs, so far ive had no graphical issues and it runs fine without my FPS dropping below 120(cap) on Max.
I do have one issue with the game's host system, if you have a ping above 80,
. If the host is close to you however there are no issues. Dedicated servers may be nice for ranked play later on for a
.
The class system is intresting, you can't try out the others on a single account without purchase.
So make sure you research abit on your class of choice. (Kind of a bummer here, i will admit)
After trying out multiple classes on different accounts, each has great pros and cons and your role plays a big part in engagement decisions. For example, a shield trooper(Max) going rampant and simply burning whoever gets close enough to him, while you stay back and just cleanly engage or harass from a distance giving a easy kill. None of the classes really stuck out to me as "OP",
Another new feature related to classes are unique Active/Passive skills that run off a meter gained from drops and actions. It works sort of like a fighter in the sense of a "Super Meter", however when full you enter a powered up stage that allows you to use any of your abilities that drains at a moderate pace over time.
Just like in the first game, there is a PvE mode with a actual story now. While the story isn't gripping it's decent and the art is great. It still retains the same harsh difficulty like the first game in the later stages, but even in the first few missions enemies can cut you down very fast. It almost forces you to play the game in a entirely different style seperate from PvP, staying beheind cover and picking off enemies.
The overall game itself has a simple yet clean interface, and the game loads quite fast.
a
nice feature is, the game contains a Host-selection option in the game, so if there is lag you can pass the host to another player who can improve latency for everyone. There is one big change, the game uses a match-making service based on levels simular to league of legends instead of a server browser. With this, they also added a ranked mode for serious players above level 20. I would very much love to see a custom game option, for battles with friends or for practice or the return of GunZ CTF.
For players new to this genre, this game is MUCH easier to pick up compared to the first. You just need to get down the idea of thinking outside the box, be unpredictable. Get off the ground and on the walls, and choose your engagements wisely, don't bite more than what you can chew. The first thing to get down is
, practice with wall running, bouncing, dashing. View the map like it's your own playground to freely move how you want, you have the ability to use any surface to your advantage,
Don't forget to aim for the head, you do significantly more damage.
If you ever wanted to play a game as some badass armed with guns and blades while you run on the walls and mow players down, you might want to try this out.
At this moment it is in Open Beta for western audiences via steam, there is bound to be many issues but i have high hopes for the team to pull this game to greatness. So far they have adressed a severe gamebreaking issue immediatley and provided a solution along with communicating with the community to help polish the game.
Of course since this is in Beta, i will update this once it is out in full-detail.
Will this live up to the legend of the first game?, It's very different but I will say it has ALOT of potential.

As a big fan of RWBY and an avid player of the original Grimm Eclipse game, I was pretty excited to see this come up on Early Access. I was even more excited when it turned out that the game is really, really fun.
Stuff I Liked:
- gorgeous art, as we've come to expect from RWBY products
- fast-paced gameplay that never drags
- each character has a distinct and interesting skillset
- shared XP for pickups from crates/trophies, not all games do this but I think it's a good idea
- last level mixed up gameplay in an interesting way that kept me from getting bored with doing the same thing over again
Stuff I Didn't:
- I still can't get the hang of Boarbatusks (the boars). Might help if we were able to dodge sideways, as opposed to only the direction we're facing? Especially difficult in big crowds of enemies.
- sorry, Arryn, but Blake sounds like she just rolled out of bed and hasn't woken up yet
- a very specific one: I'm not a big fan of how the camera gets yoinked out of your grasp when you meet the Boarbatusks, even if you're on the other side of the map. At the end of levels, okay, that's fine, but in the middle of one it's a bit annoying.
- refilling your special gets really, really hard late in the game because of how swarmed with enemies you get. It might help if it refilled veeeeery slowly based on time.
- the last level was really the only one that introduced anything NEW in terms of game mechanics, aside from new enemy types. It made the last level quite fun, but it also kind of made the previous levels more boring in retrospect.
- framerate/lag issues when there's a ton of enemies
For anyone who's played the original Grimm Eclipse--I mean the REALLY original one in the snowy landscape, based on the Red Trailer--it's got some of that same feel that I enjoyed so much from that, the feeling of blasting through hordes of enemies, the MOBA-like leveling that you can do differently every time, all of that. The ammo mechanic is totally gone, but this is a good thing, because while ammo was used interestingly in the original, it was also a MASSIVE PAIN to run around scavenging ammo and trying to make sure you always had enough.
I think the current game length is a great length for a single set of missions, and I hope they don't add anymore missions to the chapter--I can put in 45 minutes to an hour at a time, but I can't necessarily dedicate two or three hours.
All in all, a lot more polished than I expected for an Early Access game. About the only thing keeping me from considering it a finished game is that there's only one chapter!

If you're a fan of hacking up mobs, like I am, then this is shaping up to be the game for you. I feel the combat system could use some more variety and hopefully we'll see some additions in the future.
Pros;
*Smooth combat, most of the time anyways.
*The difficulty curve is gradual enough for beginners but still challenging enough to make defeating each mob of Grimm feel rewarding.
*The voice acting is well done, AND spread out enough that you're not dealing with voice spam while playing.
*Graphics are on par with what I expect for an early access game.
*The dash ability is smooth, immediate, has no cooldown, and can be used infinitely...all of which is very useful in a game that requires you to keep mobile.
*The feel of the show was definitely there. Could use more, though.
Cons;
*The game gets laggy with more enemies on the screen. This held true for everyone in our session.
*The combat needs more variety. I spent much of my time just spamming the attack button and occassionally using a special.
*Speaking of the specials, having more options per character would be nice instead of each character just having three abilities that you get right away. I'd like to be able to pick and choose which specials I get.
*The settings menu is very sparse. There's no ability to customize your graphic settings, or change your control scheme.

First, the negatives of the game: It's quite short, and I clocked in at 4 hours on the first, unguided playthrough. A chapter select menu to help go back and get achievements further reduces play time, instead of being forced to play through a second time (which, arguably, can be just as bad). The second main negative is that the game is very easy, requiring very little agility or puzzle solving skills. Controlling two avatars at once does need some practice,  but becomes second nature very quickly. It's really more of a walking simulator; you're there for the sights and experiences rather than the "gameyness."
With that out of the way, I can't recommend this game enough. If you have 4 hours to spare, there's very little in terms of entertainment that would be better than playing through this game. The environments are awe-inspiring and very, forgive the hackneyed term, epic. There's a sense of grandness in what you do in the game, despite being very straightforward. If you want a challenge and proper game, then you might be disappointed with Brothers. If you can appreciate a touching experience, and some fantastic sights, then Brothers is a definite must-play.

I bought this game while on sale for less than $2. I was looking for a story driven game, and this seemed promising with the "overwhelming positive" reviews....and of course the price.
As almost every other review states, the game is short. I finished it in less than 3 hours (that is without going out of the way to get all the achievements tho). I wish it was longer but I wont knock it down for that.
In Short:
The technical parts of the game, like controls were good, but story-wise....eh.
I was dissapointed in the story and the feels aspect of the game.
Its not a bad game, I just didn't think it lived up to the hype.
But maybe its just me tho, I am not really the kind that looks very deeply into art.
I would say that this is an experimental game. Not in a bad way but its kind of a niche in my eyes.
Can't say I would really recommend it unless its on sale. This game is a hit or miss....it was a miss for me sadly.
I wanted to like it.
In Long (that makes sense right? lol):
Graphics are fine, nothing to complain or praise about. (as long as the graphics are decent it really doesnt affect me).
Controls are a bit weird, basically, the right side of the controller controls the younger brother, and the left side controls the older brother. And often you have to control them at the same time, so it can get confusing. BUT they did a good job  so that during important parts its easier to control and not confusing, they did this by either having you control one brother at a time or by force aligning the brothers so that they are on the same side that their controls are on (Older brother will be on the left side, which matches his left side controls). So basically dont worry about raging due to the controls.  I give them credit because the amount of controls is low; 1 analog stick for each brother and 1 button for each brother, 2 buttons for camera movement, and the start/pause button. So 7 in total, but you'll mainly just use 4 lol.
But even with the simplistic controls you do a large range of activities, so it doesnt feel like your input to the characters is limited.
This game consists of puzzles, none of which I really found that challenging though. And there were a couple times where I'm thinking "why dont they just do this instead, and just avoid this problem all together?" or "how come that person doesnt just help us by doing exactly what they will do later but just do it NOW!!". Some things i also just found silly, or some things they did just would never work. Some of the puzzles can get a bit repetitive. But thats me being picky. The game is for really casual play.
There is no understandable dialogue. The characters speak to each other, but its some language not known to our world. Which is a cool idea that i respect, and one reason i find this to be an experimental kind of game. BUT i feel that the lack of dialogue made it so i didn't connect to the characters as well and I felt it left out the details of the story. The overall story is easy to follow and understand without the dialogue, but i would have liked some more detail, personally.
The environments you go through are quite nice and i like some of them a lot. As well as interesting creatures.
Replay value: Low
Honestly, I'm mixed on whether to press the thumbs up or thumbs down for this. I wish their was a sideways thumb option. lol
Conclusion:
Its an experimental game that, in my opinion, does some things right and some things wrong. Its unique and i give it a lot of credit for that. But i guess it just didn't live up to the hype for me storywise, i didnt get all the feels most people seem to be talking about. If you are curious, like experiment games, like real casual games, or want to be a game dev, then get Brothers while its on sale. Otherwise...look somewhere else.

It's not Mortal Kombat. I'm not saying that's a bad thing either. I'll do different categories so this review is easier to navigate.
GAMEPLAY:
The base is the same, slap a bunch of buttons and look really cool (or hot in Scorpian's case) doing it. HERE'S THE CHANGE! I gotta say wow, the controls have gotten even more fluid. I no longer feel like I'm punished if I haven't studied a character's move list.  Most of the combo's go in a pattern like so: (Xbox One controller) X,X,Y. OR X,Y,X. OR A,B,B. Obviously there are longer more complicated combo's that will appeal to people who want to really learn a character from the ground up but now this appeals to someone like me who likes the idea of playing as everyone and not just a couple characters. The special moves usually fallow the same idea like they used to: DOWN, RIGHT, X. LEFT, RIGHT, X. You get the idea. Overall the gameplay is so fun to do now, which is good considering it's a video game.
END OF GAMEPLAY
STORY:
So we all know by now that MK's past stories have been mostly bad or confusing. That's not to say that there haven't been really good stories (I'm looking at you Deadly Alliance, HIGH FIVE) I'm just saying that I wasn't really expecting to be blown away by the story. I WASN'T BLOWN AWAY BY THE STORY. BUT. BUT BUT BUT. IT WAS REALLY GOOD. Just in case you're afraid of SPOILERS, you may want to skip to the next section. Story time! So we start off pretty much being a general badass and kicking the tar out of Shinnok which in turn makes you feel like a badass. You go through the game in MK9 fashion. You see different characters points of view while playing as them. Mostly near the end of the game the story scrolls over to the new kids. (I.E all the main characters children) You fight as them, you get to see the world come to the brink of destruction because Scorpion really needed to get revenge (I mean, fate of the world or feeling like you avenged your clan? Clan>Earthrealm every time) So Shinnok comes back and you're thinking "Oh no big deal, I kicked his butt the first time" WRONG. Shinnok gains Earthrealm's power source which in turn makes him crazily strong.  You do end up kicking his butt (or end up crying in fetal as he fondles your butt) and afterwards everything is great cause you know, you saved Earthrealm for like the 16th time. BUT WAIT, WHAT'S THAT THING?? OH MY GAHD NO. It's a cliffhanger and honestly if you didn't expect it then you haven't played Mortal Kombat enough. *Side note, Shinnok is spammy but he will never reach the spam level of some other bosses (IF YOU SHOULDER SLAM ME ONE MORE TIME SHAO KAHN I WILL EAT YOUR BABIES)
END OF STORY.
KRYPT:
Wow. We upgraded from 2D sprites jump scaring us to having spiders humping out faces with all of their polygonal beauty. So the Krypt is honestly my favorite Krypt of all time, I would venture to say that this is the best Krypt EVER. (But that's just m opinion.) It's a 3D world that you can walk along little invisible tracks and use your gold you fished off of Sonya's dead corpse to get stuff with. It's so well made that I really can't say too much bad other than performace occasionally falls.
END OF KRYPT
Personal Problems:
This is my favorite Mortal Kombat so it pains me to say that I actually hate something about it, and it's not inherently it's fault. It's becoming common place among new video games to incorporate your extra devices and I'm all for it.  I stop being all for it when the only way to unlock a costume is to have an expensive phone that's Apple or Android.  I have a Nokia Lumia 1520, it's a windows phone. It has a terrible marketplace but it has an awesome camera. Why should I be punished because I didn't choose a more popular phone? Why should someone with not enough money for an expensive new phone get left out of a cool mechanic of the game? I already know what you're thinking because I thought it. "Why are you buying games if you can't afford a phone?" and that makes sense, BUT. But why should a $60 dollar game turn into $60+$100 (lower price for android phones)? That's not fair, I shouldn't have to spend extra money to unlock stuff in a game I already paid for.
OVERALL:
This game is fantastic and I would recommend it 10 times over. Nuff said.

This is an awesome game!
Story: The storytelling is rich and makes some really great commentary on the nature of stories and the roles of NPCs encountered by the hero. Tho some of it stuff is pretty standard fare but it does tend to pull it off with a nice little twist that keeps it refreshing.
Characters: NPCs range from incredibly well written to largely forgettable but while many may be the latter rather than the former this is more down to the absolute shear number of NPCs you encounter rather than them being poorly written (seriously it gets to the point where you can feel a little swamped by the number of NPCs you can strike up a conversation with).
Quests: These range from awesome, large scale and well written affairs to your regular fetch this or kill that numbers that we're all too familar with. What really is praise worthy, however, is that they've seperated the type of quest you can recieve into 4 sections: Main Story, Faction, Side Quests and Tasks and once you catch on to the fact that you don't need to do all of the quests to progress in the game and that Tasks are just repetitive stuff you can do to make some quick cash if your hurting for it you can start to weed out the repeative stuff in favour of the awesomeness with ease.
Combat: It's always fast, it also requires you to think and strategise a bit when it comes to dealing with the various enemies(rather than just button mashin' as most ARPGs do) and it can also pull off some truly epic moments, ie. when a combo pulls off just right exterminating a small group of enemies or when you catch yourself pulling off multiple hits on a mob to had launched into the air. I also love Reckoning mode, that's freakin' brilliant!
Graphics: Even for it's time it doesn't have top range graphics (it was released the same year as Skyrim so you could compare the two and find it wanting) however despite this the game does manage to create some truly beautiful areas and scenery. Quite often when playing games like these one can forget to properly look around when blinded by the persuit of the quest/experience bar/loot, but i really think you should take the time when entering a new area/city to have a good little look at the enviroment cause it can be very pretty (not Skyrim stunning but certainly pretty).
Gameplay: I've heard many people compare the way this game plays to an MMO but for me the gameplay in fact feels most like the FABLE games, which i love so for me it's great. I've also heard complaints about the camera being crap or that it's horrible to play on mouse and keyboard and, yes, i did have to fiddle with my mouse's sensitivity a bit to get it to feel comfortable but once i did that i had absolutely no problems, in fact i rather like the camera, it seems rather intelligent at times pulling back when you're engaging a large group of enemies but not when you're dealing with fewer or smaller (that's smaller in body size) mobs. The only critism i will levy at it is that the interface can be a bit clumbersome to get around, but considering i am using a mouse and keyboard as always that's not much of an issue since a mouse literally can over come any obsticle.
In summery i do recommend this game for all who have a love and passion for RPGs. Don't be put off by it's ARPG look and gameplay (if you're against such a thing) for this game has a lot of depth, a mega ton of NPCs and a whole heap of story telling, all of which makes it an ideal RPG in my book. The DLCs are top notch stuff too, expansion pack worthy imo.
It was a real shame this game was overlooked (largely because of Skyrim's release that same year) and that the devs failed to make any money on it and then closed due to bankruptcy, for this is a game i could've seen turning into a great series (much like TES or DA) and now i'll always feel a little bit of emptiness thanks to the knowledge that'll never be.

I love Deus Ex. I really, really do. I've enjoyed original title enormously, and Human Revolution, despite being quite a different game, gave me a lot of happy gameplay hours too.

Everything.
First thing you notice when you start playing - omfg, why my mouse dashes like Usain Bolt. Okay, turn the sensitivity almost all way down.
Second thing you notice about Mankind Divided - holy crap, why so laggy. Ok, I don't have a top-notch system (GTX 770 video), BUT why the hell not-so-recently released DOOM looks better and runs smoother than this? And - of course you heard it, watched it and know everything about it, but I just can't be silent about it - even Ultra Settings won't give you a wow-effect. It doesn't even look
.
Third thing you notice - you turned almost all graphical settings all the way down and there is still some room for low FPS. So, the optimization really sucks.

To sum up all this stuff - the main feeling I get about new Deus Ex –
. The one I least expected, it's not even about frustration or disappointment - it's all about irritation.

Okay so I have played this "Early Access" game for a while now and so feel I am now in a position to give a fair review. To strart of with, I recommend this game for 3 simple reasons:
1) If you like RWBY, like I do, you will enjoy this game
2) It's a decent price for Early access and shows a lot of promise
3) Any game with a graphic setting of "Potato" really deserves some praise and attention
However... lets be realistic here people. Its not finished, not by a long shot. It is playable, it is fun and if you have 3 friends to play with, its a riot. You can play solo, but here is the thing, its not for that right now. Hopefully it will be down the line.
What it is, simply put, is Space Martine Last Stand. You have different areas to get to and eventually you have to defend wave after wave of enemies. Each enemy gives XP and this gives you the ability to upgrade you characters capabilities. Each enemy is also worth points and so at the end of the mission/level you will have a chart saying how many points/kills you have and so you are placed in a leaderboard with the rest of your party. There are also MVP's for the waves.
This is where the current fun lies because its about friendly competition - the game does have some flaws though. Like any "Early Access" game, you have glitches. Places where you freeze, get stuck, fall through a grate.. not many, but there are some.
It is also currently short lived and a little too linear, so will get repetative. Combos will probably be introduced as currently the Level Cap is 10, but I don't see this being the final level you can obtain. I would also imagine, since there is scope for it, that the "SHIPS" will come into play for special combos that can be made with the viable partner when in range on larger enemies, as there still needs to be that "Massive Boss Fight" to be included.
All in all, its a great game so far and a lot of fun.
Plus seriously, Potato graphic setting, you gotta try it.

An alright action/adventure RPG in the same vein as the Diablo franchise. In fact some of the guys that worked on Diablo 2 had a hand in creating this game. It has a nostalgic sound track and gameplay elements, and some interesting semi-fun loot. After that though it all goes down hill.
Even though there are multiple skill trees to choose for every character almost all of them are boring and revovle around only using two or three of the skills on the whole tree along with the passives. Which presents a large problem, it is VERY easy to mess up your skill points and stats in this game. What hurts even worse, your actual active skills you have control of are very lackluster and boring, even when you power them up all the way, it's usually you just spamming your most powerful skill to clear a larger group of baddies, it gets old FAST, and it's not very dynamic like in other action RPGs where your moves feel as if they have impact, or can be comboed into one another with different effects. No no, none of that. Here your moves feel like you're hitting the enemy with a wet noodle repeatedly until they finally go down after enough mindless spam and auto attack, only to drop a random assortment of garbage items and a handful of gold.
There is a limited reset option for if you make mistakes while distributing your  points while leveling, but it only applies to the last three levels and choices you've made. So if you mess up hard enough, there's no going back. To make things worse, spreading your points into different trees, and even messing up a small amount with distributing stat points can literally make your character worthless later on, to the point of having to start from scratch completely with a new character. This even applies to normal difficulty, which is MUCH more forgiving then the Hard mode. Mess up in Hard mode? Allocate one level to the wrong things, do yourself a favor and restart right there.
Clicking and targeting accurately is a pain, and when trying to back up with a ranged character you'll often take a ton of extra hits or even die while trying to create distance, because your character will simply refuse to move, and instead spam auto attacks. It's even worse for melee characters, they literally get pushed around all over your screen because of their terribly short range, and the fact almost all enemies cause knock back with their attacks.
Don't even bother with the story. If you skip most of the cut-scenes or dialogues it won't even matter. The game does NOTHING to get you invovled in the plot, and it's pretty much a mystery why your character even gives a crap what's happening in the game world. Even if you do watch the animated cutscenes and scroll through the dialogue options available to you it does little to make you care about your quest, or what you're doing in general. Do yourself a favor, keep your head down and keep swinging, it's actually beneficial to ignore the bland story so you can move quickly on to the next area, since no one you talk to has anything worth listening to in the first place.
It's a shame the mechanics and leveling system are so terrible, because there are alot of quests and interesting areas to explore, and a wide variety of enemies to fight. Including bosses, which sometimes have a neat mechanic you have to play along with to defgeat them. It's just the fact of if you actually want to invest the time in actually forcing yourself through the terrible gameplay to get that far.
Do yourself a favor and only pick this up if it's on sale, and you have a friend or two to play through it with. It makes the terrible leveling system more bearable and the action a little bit more interesting.

Other than this the developers added many things that was absent in previous titles like unit trading with allies a must have future also caused me to stop playing earlier titles. On the other hand I must confess that this game is not for everyone.
This game has its own economical model that is quite different from modern theories although basics are same namely supply and demand is still major part of the economical side of the game but classical economical approaches may not help you a lot. This game has a very long learning curve that may discourage many but if you try you can have your own style. For example my strategy is same for any country I play with 1st Product self suffieciency, 2nd enough researching to get some good army technology and other useful civil ones, 3rd modernized small but elite army and finally after I have enough stockpiled war materials that in game they are petroleum and military goods used by your army in war. After that it is finally the world is yours. Many may say other but I prefer colonizing the world not annexing because if you keep annexing you cannot handle if your goverment is democracy no matter how experienced you are.
I advice not to hurry on conquest but develop earlier then fight and if you are new avoid modern maps try WW II maps.

Short:
You might like this game if you like to basicly not do anything while the game plays itself.
You will probably not like this game if you like to think and and want failure is a possibility.
Nothing in this game will be of even the slightest difficulty for any person of any age.
Long:
I had read about this game a while back. I didnt have too high hopes but I was kinda hoping for a short game with decent graphics and a good story. But how terribly wrong I was. The graphics is allright. Story is quite random but I guess it could do. The thing that struck me though, was the lack of challenge. And Im not against easy games, even though I do like the challenge. And if it wasnt for the "gore" here and there, this game would be suited from 5 years and up, in my opinion.
Gameplay!
You only have 1 button to use, besides the camera buttons, and you spend your time running forward, mindlessly jumping up rocks, and pressing your button in front of stuff.
Now the gamplay is where this game just dies in my opinion. I got fooled a couple of times thinking, "yay, heres a puzzle", only to realize you only have a press a button, or move a lever. The unique way of controlling both brothers at the same time isnt there. It requires no thinking, and no skills. The only challenge I ever had was to try to make the boys run different directions and keeping track of both characters movement. However, this is just cosmetica and doesnt impact the gameplay at all. The idea is nice but the implementation is terrible. I have to give it a 1.
Graphics!
When I saw it I thought "Fable". It does look decent most of the time so I give this game a 7 in graphics. Occasionally its quite beautiful, but then you might turn the camera the other way and it looks terrible. I get the feeling that this game was created quickly.
Audio!
Audio seems very much inspired by the classic swedish movie "Ronja Robbersdaughter". Otherwise dont have too much to say about it except for the fairly annoying sounds these boys will make when they are having fun, flying or similar. Ill give it a 6.
Story!
Story starts out kind of standard and even though the places you travel to look good, they seem very random and the ways you get there seems just like a big cut and paste job to me. The world is kind of a mix of childs stories, from towns and mountains to trolls and giants. The dialogues are in a fake language without subtitles. I felt that the characters acted quite weird during cinematics or dialogues and no matter how hard I try, I cant sympathize even the slightest with any of the characters.  I give it a 5
How this game has recieved such good criticism is beyond me and my brother, with whom I played it together.
Simply put. This game might be great for someone who has never played a video game before. Personally I felt it was pointless playing it. Kind of like a movie where you have to constanly hold down two buttons for it to play. It wasnt fun, the graphics were ok but that doesnt make it a good game, and the music felt like a straight up rip-off from Ronja Robbersdaughter.
But since it has gotten such tremendous reviews there might be something Im missing. No game is for everyone and this game is certainly not for me, as I have trouble even calling it a game.

My recommending this game is one with a big BUT...
I love Tekken; I have played T2, T3, a bit of T5, A LOT of TTT2 and now I'm playing T7 - I will try T6 soon, too.
If you just want a solid fighting game on PC, then this is a really good buy. I'm serious. However, if I - and I do - compare it to Tekken Tag Tournament 2/TTT2 I played on the Xbox 360, I feel like I would have been A LOT happier with a PC port for that game, with the new characters as (even paid) DLC for said port.
- The fighting is excellent, except for some cheap battles I will not spoil. You will need to get better than my noob level to breeze through those
- There is more to customize, but most of it is useless or ridiculous-looking stuff. I had hoped T7 would be better at customization than TTT2, but it is not, in my opinion. There are no mid-length, or long hairstyles, no separate hairstyle categories and somehow I feel like colors are harder to fine-tune then before. Also, you earn battle money to buy customzations with, but most of it is locked only to be obtained with Treasure Battle now, which is ridiculous, because in the previous game you were able to decide yourself what to get when. Now you cannot, for many things. You get money, but for what purpose, I wonder? This is coming from a guy who had bought all customizations in TTT2 for his mains and secondary characters after a while. But at least I was able to decide what I bought when. And I was able to give proper, good-looking hairstyles.
- The graphics are supposed to be a step up. In some cases, that's true, but I find hair on many characters to look more like plastic than before, they messed up some faces - like Lili's, my previous main - and the graphics WERE already good. I see no reason why they changed it like this; there are engine limitations, but they wanted to show off the graphics system. Then why have plastic hair, very, very few hair customizations and worse looking faces (even though not in all cases)?
- There is almost no offline mode to speak of anymore to me. I'm an offline player, I'm mad. I don't like lag and spammers. I don't want to be halfway forced to play online. There is no survival mode, which I always immensely enjoyed, there is no team battle, which was always fun with friends, there is no time attack (frankly I don't care about that one), the arcade had been reduced from 10 to 8 stages in TTT2, now it's only 5, with no cinematic ending when you beat it. There is 0 incentive to play it. Treasure Battle has some nice mixup battles, but limits customization unlike TTT2's Ghost Battle. 1 Plus about it is that it now saves your winstreak. It just doesn't get saved in a list, so it's no real replacement for Survival and you will still fight ridiculously customized characters 90% of the time, like in TTT2, which started to annoy me even in that gem of a game.
- I have the season pass and I regret it. In no way, shape or form, do I think this game can compete with TTT2.
- The story is nice to play through once, maybe twice, then you're done and the character episodes are only 1 measly fight each time - at least for the 3 characters I tried it out with.
- Many characters are missing. Angel (my 2nd main in TTT2 and T2) would've been a perfect fit and high time to include her and give us answers, but she is not in, instead there is some weird exorcist I give 0 things about.
- Lili does not act like, play like, sound like, or look like her old self, nor can you customize her like you could in the past. I'm disappointed. She's become even more exaggerated, less pretty, important moves were changed and all previous cute moments she had are completely gone (yes this is a thing for me, sorry).
- Yoshimitsu looks like he came straight out of a tentacle hent** to r**e the girls. His most ridiculous look yet.
- Guest character Akuma sticks out like a sore thumb, unlike Gon did in the past. I never played a SF game for more than 5 minutes before and I did not know a guest character would appear. Once I saw Akuma's design and stance in the game I immediately knew he didn't belong. I won't spoil anything, so I'll stop there.
All in all I'm very disappointed, but I still recommend it for those who want to try the new characters, want to play Tekken on PC and for those who don't care about any of my negatives. At least I'm having fun with Kazumi and Eliza, but I wonder for how long.

We did it folks, we finally got a Tekken on PC!
The story mode is fairly short, on the standard difficulty it took me somewhere between 3-4 hours to beat it. Still, if you're new to the fighting game genre, be aware that exceptionally few fighting games have big campaigns. Most campaigns in fighting games are a series of fights strung together with a loose notion of plot, the only real exception I can think of is Mortal Kombat/Injustice.
Tekken looks prettier than ever on the UE4 engine, visually it's a gorgeous game. The hair on the characters doesn't look fantastic but speaking as someone who has spent three years failing to get hair to work in UE4, trust me, it's really difficult. I can't blame the developers for it if I can't manage it myself either.
The combat feels absolutely incredible to play. The hitboxes on the characters are eerily 1:1 with their models, meaning that timing is now more crucial than ever. You can't get away with barely missing, if your punch doesn't connect, you won't get off on a technicality any more.
At present, the season pass gets you a bunch of cosmetic items in a metallic tint (you can get the non-metallic variants without the pass) and two new characters that haven't been announced yet. I'm not sure if the pass with get you Eliza or if she was just a pre-order bonus. Still, I feel the need to bring this up:
THERE ARE NO MIRCROTRANSACTIONS!
With the exception of the metallic stuff, everything you can unlock for your characters, you do so by playing the game. Beating the campaign and participating in battles online gives you Fighting Coins which you can spend on cosmetic stuff for characters. You don't need any of it, it's all just for aesthetics only. There is one item which does effect gameplay called the Mirror, but it's free. All it does is stops your opponent from moving when the fight is over, so if you're the type of person who doesn't like getting BM'd at the end of the fight, you can stop your opponent from doing it by equipping the mirror. But again, it's free.
TL;DR
Game is optomised exceptionally well, had a great launch, no outstanding bugs or glitches, the online works gloriously, the game looks beautiful and there are no microtransactions in it. On top of that it's incredibly fun. This is what games should aspire to be.

[UPDATED REVIEW v2]
Tekken 7 is a rich, complex fighter played by a tight community where many players have more than 10 years of experience. The game offers several rather specific mechanics, tons and tons of moves and a rather large roster. The gameplay is as polished as it gets, characters are rather balanced (despite what some people complain about, there's no 'cheap moves' once you learn how to counter them).
On the negative site, the online experience can at times be cringe worthy. The online Ux is simply not good; it currently seems like finding an opponent (let alone an opponent at your level) can be difficult and up to neigh impossible depending on your time zone and whether or not you're one of these unlucky players who experiences 'The Limbo'.
Some of the soundtracks are going to make you mute your sound, too. Not all of them, some.
Now, your experience will vary greatly depending on how much you're invested in the franchise/fighting games. If you're looking for single player experience, there is none except a bad story more and basic survival and arcade. If you're looking for online fun though, you'll find a lot of people willing to fight you. Warning: Tekken is HARD and getting really good is going to take time.
I can't recommend it as a first fighter experience right now (not until the single player modes receive some content and tutorials), but I will recommend it if you are the dedicated, competitive type.

TL;DR: While there's a lot of bad to the game, it's still an entertaining experience and worth checking out.
I've been playing Heroes & Generals since the Quesada update (circa July 2014).  I have over 2000 Steam hours on the game, and plenty more using the browser version.  I've also streamed this game for well over a year.  After all that time, I can honestly say, this is the game that you will love to hate.  It is not a bad game, but there's so many things that have changed over the years that have brought down the quality while increasing the cash-grab aspect that I feel people need to take a good, hard look at whether they want to invest the time (and money) into this game or not.
There are so many things mismanaged with this game, and far too many issues with modeling.  Reto Moto utilizes its own engine, rather than an off-the-shelf engine with more capabilities.  Consequently, you will see a noticeable drop in FPS compared to other games with similar requirements.  The engine has not receiving an update in over 2 years.  We only recently received significant updates to the maps, and those updates consisted of questionable spawn locations, more rehashes of the same tired old buildings, and some color differences.  Destructible terrain is non-existent, and you'll find that glass is bullet-proof for the first shot in addition to improper edge modeling of buildings and objects.
Everything in this game can be ground out, but the cost of doing such has steadily increased over the years.  Most recently, the latest patch decreased the credits earned per hour while slightly increasing the cost of some highly-purchased items.  This, along with a slight increase in the cost of gold, has pushed the game to more real-money purchase of gold.  There is no doubt that Reto Moto is doing this to reinforce its dwindling coffers.  Make no mistake, Reto Moto is an indie studio with a small budget trying to pull off a AAA gaming experience.  Therefore, the cash shop is their sole source of income to keep their doors open.  The more use there is, the better for them.
My last bit of bad review is centered on the development team, and especially the game director (RedBjarne). Priorities for this team are sorely mismanaged.  I say this as a developer myself, and shudder every time I see a decision to go after cash-grab opportunities (such as adding new tanks/guns) instead of fixing long-standing bugs (double-shot glitch has existed for 2 years with no resolution).  I personally feel that RedBjarne is harming the development of the game rather than helping, and is known for his egotistical attitude towards others.
Despite all of the bad, I still recommend this game.  Why?  Frankly, there's only 2 WWII infantry-based MMOs still in existence, and this one has the larger community.  I've met some tremendous people through this game, and the Twitch-streaming community is the most tight-knit group I've seen.  We all support each other, and you'll never lack for an entertaining long-time player within that community.  If you have several years (or deep pockets), the higher-end weapons and tanks are awesome, and you'll definitely have a lot of fun.  Cheating, despite what most people think, is still relatively minor compared to the AAA titles out there (it does exist, though).  If you find a good group to work with, you'll be amazed by how different the game is versus just running solo.
I'd highly recommend that you check the game out and hop in a few streams.  You'll find plenty of us (myself included) that are willing to show new players the ropes.  If you stick around, maybe you'll be in this place 2 years from now talking about the game you love to hate.

Brutal Legend was some of the most fun I've had in a while. Enter a world based on the mythology of metal - demons, beasts, flowing hair, and music that reshapes reality. The most notable thing about BL is its world design. Few games have this level of creativity on display in every inch of every piece of their world. It's in the characters and the archetypes they play with, the use of guitar solos and chord progressions to cast magic, the monsters that are half-vehicle/half nightmare beast, and the landscape itself, with its ancient statues of fists and guitars, chrome-tipped trees, Beerhenge, and cracked freeways. The way the Double Fine team has taken all the most fun and fist-pumping elements of classic metal and rock music and infused them into every square inch of this game made it feel unique and refreshing. I left the game wishing I could keep playing more in this world, seeing the characters continue to grow and keep on rocking.
The gameplay is simple but engaging; a light action/adventure style with a lot of axe-swinging and guitar playing. You'll spend as much time in your hot-rod "The Deuce" as you will on foot, and that's a mixed bag. Controlling the car can be pretty squirrely, and it'll be a while before you're doing more than careening uncontrollably from one rock outcropping to the next. Once you get the hang of it, driving can be pretty fun - the landscape is designed for your car, and filled with ramps to jump, twisting roads to navigate, and critters to splat.
It's an adventure game through-and-through, but occasionally BL tries its hand at RTS gameplay. You're a roadie trying to turn ragtag freedom fighters into a genuine rebellion army, and at certain points you will get to lead that army into battle. It's... another mixed bag, honestly. There's a lot that's good about it; giving orders works pretty well and easily, and watching all these troops you've freed and brought to your cause charge into the fray lends a weight to the story and your actions throughout. But years of games like Starcraft and the like have conditioned me to expect a top-down view that allows me a wide survey of the battlefield. BL sticks with its third-person view during the big battles, and it can sometimes be hard to tell where the enemy is and whay they're doing beyond a vague directional guide. I kept wanting more fine control than I had, and to be able to see more than I could.
Further complicating the RTS sections, I rarely knew just what my objectives were. Eventually, tips would start popping up, but they're easy to miss if you aren't looking for them. More than a couple times I spent a long time waiting around in the big battles waiting for something to happen, not realizing I had to do some specific thing. Several of these times, the battle would suddenly end in victory and I had no idea how I'd won. These segments add gravitas to the game, but they never quite stand up to the level I wanted, and I'm left unsure how I felt about them.
What sold BL to me and really brought out the fun were the cast of characters and the performance of their actors. Jack Black is an endlessly entertaining guy, and in BL he's paired with Jennifer Hale as the female lead. It's worth the pricetag on this game just to watch JB and FemShep lead a metal army against demons and hair-rockers. Guest appearances from Ozzy Ozbourne, Lemmy Killmeister, and Rob Halford buoy the rock cred, and are really entertaining. Lita Ford isn't quite as adept in her small part, but the performance of Tim Curry as the demonic Emperor Doviculus is as operatically theatrical as you could possibly want.
I loved almost every moment of playing this game. I enjoyed the story, I enjoyed exploring the world, and once I could get my head and hands wrapped around controlling the Deuce, I even enjoyed driving across the countryside like a bat out of hell. Brutal Legend comes highly recommended from me, an overlooked gem that will leave you wishing for more.

Before anything is said, this is another kinetic novel (Subject to change at a whim). There are no choices, as far as I have seen in the first chapter but may change, or any sort of gameplay to that extent. Thus, this is a kinetic novel with a preset story but it is still very, very good.
Opening Thoughts:
For a kinetic novel that is basically a free demo of the full release, I would have never pegged this as a demo. The art and proportions are a bit off. But the story is amazing. It captures your attention and makes you really feel for these characters. I hated Suguha at first due to his cowardly nature but I grew to like him as he matured and gained a backbone. The development is pretty good as I really felt emotion and depth with the characters.
Small Censorship Rant:
The 'demo' is hardly a demo. Yes, it is censored but so what? You are missing a few h-scenes that despite causing a bit of context loss, hardly mean anything. I've seen a fair few people complaining in the forums and in the reviews of this game about an uncensored version or patch(<-- This might be out when the full thing releases, as for an uncensored version just buy it somewhere that isn't steam.) I followed along the story well despite people saying that the censorship of certain parts cause portions to be hidden away.
The Verdict:
Anyways, back to the point at hand, this game is hardly a demo. With close to 10 hours of content, ChuSingura 46+1 S takes you on rollercoaster ride. You will laugh, hate, and cry alongside an ordinary Japanese student that took some kendo as he is transported 300 years into the past. Its story is captivating and truly interesting as he slowly sees the "inner workings" (as loosely as you can call this entire alternate history inner workings) of the 47 Ronin as they work to avenge their disgraced lord and family. I cannot wait for the full release as I will fully support the developers as they port the series into the PC realm. In all, this 'demo' is amazing and I suggest it to anybody looking for a well-written and captivating kinetic novel.

Okay so I have played this "Early Access" game for a while now and so feel I am now in a position to give a fair review. To strart of with, I recommend this game for 3 simple reasons:
1) If you like RWBY, like I do, you will enjoy this game
2) It's a decent price for Early access and shows a lot of promise
3) Any game with a graphic setting of "Potato" really deserves some praise and attention
However... lets be realistic here people. Its not finished, not by a long shot. It is playable, it is fun and if you have 3 friends to play with, its a riot. You can play solo, but here is the thing, its not for that right now. Hopefully it will be down the line.
What it is, simply put, is Space Martine Last Stand. You have different areas to get to and eventually you have to defend wave after wave of enemies. Each enemy gives XP and this gives you the ability to upgrade you characters capabilities. Each enemy is also worth points and so at the end of the mission/level you will have a chart saying how many points/kills you have and so you are placed in a leaderboard with the rest of your party. There are also MVP's for the waves.
This is where the current fun lies because its about friendly competition - the game does have some flaws though. Like any "Early Access" game, you have glitches. Places where you freeze, get stuck, fall through a grate.. not many, but there are some.
It is also currently short lived and a little too linear, so will get repetative. Combos will probably be introduced as currently the Level Cap is 10, but I don't see this being the final level you can obtain. I would also imagine, since there is scope for it, that the "SHIPS" will come into play for special combos that can be made with the viable partner when in range on larger enemies, as there still needs to be that "Massive Boss Fight" to be included.
All in all, its a great game so far and a lot of fun.
Plus seriously, Potato graphic setting, you gotta try it.

It's not Mortal Kombat. I'm not saying that's a bad thing either. I'll do different categories so this review is easier to navigate.
GAMEPLAY:
The base is the same, slap a bunch of buttons and look really cool (or hot in Scorpian's case) doing it. HERE'S THE CHANGE! I gotta say wow, the controls have gotten even more fluid. I no longer feel like I'm punished if I haven't studied a character's move list.  Most of the combo's go in a pattern like so: (Xbox One controller) X,X,Y. OR X,Y,X. OR A,B,B. Obviously there are longer more complicated combo's that will appeal to people who want to really learn a character from the ground up but now this appeals to someone like me who likes the idea of playing as everyone and not just a couple characters. The special moves usually fallow the same idea like they used to: DOWN, RIGHT, X. LEFT, RIGHT, X. You get the idea. Overall the gameplay is so fun to do now, which is good considering it's a video game.
END OF GAMEPLAY
STORY:
So we all know by now that MK's past stories have been mostly bad or confusing. That's not to say that there haven't been really good stories (I'm looking at you Deadly Alliance, HIGH FIVE) I'm just saying that I wasn't really expecting to be blown away by the story. I WASN'T BLOWN AWAY BY THE STORY. BUT. BUT BUT BUT. IT WAS REALLY GOOD. Just in case you're afraid of SPOILERS, you may want to skip to the next section. Story time! So we start off pretty much being a general badass and kicking the tar out of Shinnok which in turn makes you feel like a badass. You go through the game in MK9 fashion. You see different characters points of view while playing as them. Mostly near the end of the game the story scrolls over to the new kids. (I.E all the main characters children) You fight as them, you get to see the world come to the brink of destruction because Scorpion really needed to get revenge (I mean, fate of the world or feeling like you avenged your clan? Clan>Earthrealm every time) So Shinnok comes back and you're thinking "Oh no big deal, I kicked his butt the first time" WRONG. Shinnok gains Earthrealm's power source which in turn makes him crazily strong.  You do end up kicking his butt (or end up crying in fetal as he fondles your butt) and afterwards everything is great cause you know, you saved Earthrealm for like the 16th time. BUT WAIT, WHAT'S THAT THING?? OH MY GAHD NO. It's a cliffhanger and honestly if you didn't expect it then you haven't played Mortal Kombat enough. *Side note, Shinnok is spammy but he will never reach the spam level of some other bosses (IF YOU SHOULDER SLAM ME ONE MORE TIME SHAO KAHN I WILL EAT YOUR BABIES)
END OF STORY.
KRYPT:
Wow. We upgraded from 2D sprites jump scaring us to having spiders humping out faces with all of their polygonal beauty. So the Krypt is honestly my favorite Krypt of all time, I would venture to say that this is the best Krypt EVER. (But that's just m opinion.) It's a 3D world that you can walk along little invisible tracks and use your gold you fished off of Sonya's dead corpse to get stuff with. It's so well made that I really can't say too much bad other than performace occasionally falls.
END OF KRYPT
Personal Problems:
This is my favorite Mortal Kombat so it pains me to say that I actually hate something about it, and it's not inherently it's fault. It's becoming common place among new video games to incorporate your extra devices and I'm all for it.  I stop being all for it when the only way to unlock a costume is to have an expensive phone that's Apple or Android.  I have a Nokia Lumia 1520, it's a windows phone. It has a terrible marketplace but it has an awesome camera. Why should I be punished because I didn't choose a more popular phone? Why should someone with not enough money for an expensive new phone get left out of a cool mechanic of the game? I already know what you're thinking because I thought it. "Why are you buying games if you can't afford a phone?" and that makes sense, BUT. But why should a $60 dollar game turn into $60+$100 (lower price for android phones)? That's not fair, I shouldn't have to spend extra money to unlock stuff in a game I already paid for.
OVERALL:
This game is fantastic and I would recommend it 10 times over. Nuff said.

GunZ: The Duel was a game I spent 8 years on when I first became a PC gamer. It was an innovative, past-paced, purely skill-based slasher/shooter that separated the boys from the men. This was all made possible by a series of move cancellations that were placed in the game by a programming error. That single error spawned a vastly devout following of jaded shooter fans who were looking for a serious challenge. You could break the rules of gravity as you bounced off walls and engaged enemies in visceral dogfights on levels most people only fantasize about. GunZ was as close to perfect as you could get, with only a small problem of hacker prevention.
GunZ 2 is a slow, clunky, severely limiting shooter that makes its predecessor want to crawl out of the grave it's rolling in, and devour it. The move cancellations have been "fixed", and with it goes their loyal following. Every game should have a single aspect that grants that game its individuality. GunZ didn't just have the move cancellations, it embraced them. The fans embraced it lovingly, and it brought so much character to a world that was no longer just running around firing the same tiresome weapons at one another.
With these moves gone, and strict timing in place, you're forced to move at the pace they deem reasonable. Gone are the days of being able to skillfully double-butterfly an enemy into slices of shame. No more slash-shooting opponents from across the map with a rocket launcher. Never again will an opponent be launched airborne just to fall back down into a full metal jacket by way of meteor. This game is NOT a worthy successor. It shouldn't even bear the title of the game it dares to tread on. GunZ 2 is just another third person shooter, and while many of us were excited for a return to glory within its arena walls- it was a fleeting sense of nostalgia that kept us interested as this game progressed.
The graphics are semi-pretty, the sound is about the same as the first, the class system is hilariously crippling, and the movement system single-handedly buries the game.

Obviously this game is a Diablo clone so if you like action RPGs then this is already worth your time.  However, what really distinguishes this game is that it came out shortly after Diablo 3 but managed to hit all the sweet spots that Diablo 3 missed.  Playing online is certainly effortless although it does take getting familiar with the interface for online joining.  Once you figure it out though, you'll be good to go and will have no more problems after that.
Additionally however, it's completely able to be played offline which is something that's not possible for Diablo 3.  It doesn't need to make up for a lack of offline play by trying to overextend itself with superfluous features an auction house (which I think has now been terminated) and a spam saturated friending system.  Add to that the fact that this game was literally 1/3 the price of Diablo 3 at launch with probably 50% more content to it.  As if that wasn't enough, the game's system requirements are very minimal yet it manages to look and feel just right for a top notch ARPG.
If I think of more things to write I'll update but I think that hits all the essentials -Sorry to do so at the expense of Diablo 3 but that was supposed to be the benchmark for these kinds of games at the time.  If you like Diablo 3 (or games like it) definitely -DEFINITELY- pick this up, especially if it goes on sale.  It's about as good of a value as you're ever going to get for a video game.

Okay, let's get this out of the way first - I wholeheartedly recommend this game for any south park fan.
Now, here's the review itself:
I guess the weirdest thing about this game, is that although it's a sequel to the "Stick of truth" (I'll be writing Stick from now on, to save time) - it truly feels like a prequel in most ways. And what do I mean by that?
- The story, although one that still sits beautifully with the franchise and has some intense moments, feels less cohesive then the one presented in Stick. It just doesn't have that same edge or diversity that it had, and although it tries to portray a more serious tone - sometimes, it just takes itself way too seriously. Especially for a series such as south park.
- The battle system is different, and takes some getting use to. I'll admit that at first, after the first half an hour of the game, I found myself quitting just because it reminded me nothing of Stick, and I expected something else. Like the Stick system being taken to the next level. But once I came back, and gave it a shot, it presented a whole new challenge for me. It is much more complex, especially with movement involved, which can lead to some epic strikes, but at the same time - to some very frustrating moments. I'm not saying it's either better or worse than the one presented in Stick - it's just different, and might repel players who loved Stick's combat style (although, I do encourage you to give it a chance).
- The difficulty is imbalanced. I play on the hardest setting, and I must say it offers quite a challenge (which is excellent, and somewhat lacked of in Stick, at least for me). But some battles are just imbalanced, when taking the players level and skill in the game into account, at that moment. This can lead to you winning some battles with ease, while losing in a later fight that just seems to be "more of the same". Granted, this didn't happen alot - but at the times it did, it just felt unjust. I know that some people might say it has everything to do with strategy, resource management or the right equipment and abilities being equipped - but I still say that with a little more tweaking, the experience could've been a much more balanced one.
- The town itself feels.. less alive, somehow. I really don't know how to put this in writing - but when you walk around the town, the atmosphere feels wrong. Most NPC's are bland, main characters behavior just feels a little off, the quests mostly consist of the same missions in repetiting order, and even the interactions between the kids lack some of the humor and sophistication that the show brings, and that Stick actually nailed. This, I believe, is one of the main issues I have with the game in general, and why it feels more of a prequel in my eyes to that amazing feeling Stick brought along with it.
Now, considering all of this - it seems a little weird that I recommend this game, right?
Well.. no. Not really.
The game still has some great rythem to it. The styling is fantastic and fits with the theme perfectly. The writing has some clever moments that you can't help but find yourself giggling to. The inner jokes are some of the best I've seen in a while, and fit perfectly with the narrative of the show. It's a good RPG for all you RPG lovers out there, with grinding, crafting, a good leveling up system, challenging bosses and decent storyline...
And it's SOUTH PARK, for crying out loud.
So, in conclusion...
Is it better than the "Stick of truth"?
Well, when it comes to me - the answer is no.
But is it a worthy sequel, and one that's fitting with the series' overall theme?
Hell yes.

Portal Knights was a game I purchased one night because my best friend and I had been looking for a fun co-op game to jump into. What can I say about supreme ruler ultimate.
It's such an awesome idea that combines some of the best mechanics from other games and crams it into a massive bundle of awesome customisable in depth detailed and destructive fun.  I have always like grand strategy within the modern eras of warfare.  Commanding soldiers has always been fun but with previous games I found them very restrictive.  Normally just giving you command of a squad or a putting you in one battle was just too restricting.  I want to command my nation send it off to wars I plan for.  Go against nations I want to fight and do it through the 30s to 2000s.  Well that game is this one.
First off if your a fan of say total war but it now.  The map follows a very similar feel to total war with supply lines, economy maniging and building production.  There's even research that unlocks units although it's not a tree which would have been better to know what you should research when.  Unlike total war though the map is larger and it takes place within real time.  Politics in the game is fun when all nations hate you for building your empire.  Hell if you wanted you could play the game without any war but what fun is that.  Seeing hour defences on borders and battle lines is Aldo a lot of fun and there is a ton of opportunity for strategy.  Planning invasions is crucial, you need to know the land you plan to take and where best to fight, assault and land.  It's such an immersive game.
But does it have its problems. Well yes.  For example the game can sometimes grind to a slow pace as you build up more troops for a new invasion or if you plan to go peacefully for a while it can get little dull. Even on fastest game speed (which I highly recommend you play on once you knows what your doing) the game can be a little slow I'll sometimes just let it play while I go off and make lunch waiting for my new marines to be ready.  Also some problems occur with amphibious units disembarking on island and getting stuck there forever which is a huge pain in the♥♥♥♥♥  Also there is quite a learning curve and the tutorial is not as detailed as it should be.
However for all the bad the game shines on.  I highly recommend getting this game it is such a fun experience being the command on high over a nation building it up to be the next superpower.  Oh and before I forget.  All nations from 1936 are playable.  Enjoy

My favorite aspect is the economy.  Lots of people toss this game because they act like Democrats.  They spend tons of money on infrastructure.  They don't have industry goods to produce any of the facilities.  Therefore they import them driving the world market price through the roof.  They go broke.  Taxes eventually reach 99% as you run a full on socialist state.  Inflation goes through the roof as your government spends and borrows wildly at the whims of the rulers.  And because you.... the user.... has total control (ie big government) your complete mismanagement wrecks the entire nation for a generation.
Instead..... focus the economy on GDP.  It's everything IMO.  Higher GDP equals more tax revenue.  You want the people to be prosperous.  I've tried many economic models and found most to be somewhat realistic.  I've use the common flat tax.  It's fairly effective.  The "fair tax" ie sales tax is an excellent model.  The citizens only pay taxes on goods consumed.  In a perfect world you produce most of what you consume..... and consume a lot.  Domestic profits are much higher than exports.  If you keep a healthy balance of supply and demand with a national sales tax of roughly 30%..... you're good.  GDP will go up.  You'll gain tax revenue everytime goods are sold to the populace.  And you get general revenue from the sale.  In the real world..... this is essentially a free market with a national sales tax (as the only source of income.)  People scoff at the idea because they think THEY would end up paying everything at the counter while the rich walk away unscathed.  Anyone with a brain knows that's what happens anyway.  Raise taxes on corporations and they simply raise prices to match.  A healthy business will always maintain a steady profit line.  Taxes are nothing more than a business expese.  Either way it goes taxes are always paid by the little guy.  Even now..... your employer is responsible for a large portion of your taxes.  People think....  "Great... the company pays that."  Except for the reality that it's simply a business expense considered under "labor."  Which means you.  Therefore you are more expensive to the company and get paid less.  Therefore you actually pay ALL taxes.  Because if they did not exist.... then a healthy competitive market would drive wages up to the current line anyway.  It doesn't matter who gets the money from the companies perspective.  Either the government.... or you.... cost X amount of dollars for one employee per year.
Anyway if you choose to run a socialist economic model.... your goal is to export.  You want to drive GDP down.  In lamens terms.... you want the people poor.  Poor people work for nothing.  The end result of all socialist nations is poverty.  Poverty keeps you in business.  Look at China.  When their people become to prosperous they print a ton of money and devalue their currency by half...... essentially making the people 50% poorer.  The easiest way to make everyone poor.... is to jack taxes through the roof.  You can simultaneously raise services to maintain public order.  But the people will still be poor.  The lower their GDP.... the cheaper you can produce goods (ie China).... the less people of your own country can afford goods like electricity and water..... and you'll have a ton of cheap goods available on the market.  If they pile up.... simply do bulk sales with a minimal profit.  Technologies can also reduce the cost of production.  But GDP is a huge factor and you can crash it quickly.  As a socialist nation you will make tons of money off consumer goods.  They are always in demand.  They fetch a nice profit.  And the poorer your people are.... the richer you get.  ....  Gee.... isn't socialism great.
Overall don't be afraid to raise and lower taxes.  The economy should be flexible.  Don't build it around one strategy.  Grow it in all directions.  Don't be afraid to shut factories down if you can import goods cheaper than you can make them.  Why pay your own people more money when another country can produce it cheaper?  Unemployment isn't that difficult to control.  (Higher unemployement also means less competition for workers.... which means lower wages... whicih means you can produce goods cheaper and drop GDP.)  You want a healthy balance of everything.  I typically start the game by building a few industrial goods complexes.  I want enough to sustain a war.  Then I identify the particular countries trade imbalance.  Try to produce goods rather than import them (unless producing them is more expensive.)  And eventually create a small surplus of various commodities for export.  I try to run about a 20% overall tax rate usually focussing on the sales tax.  You want the people rich and prosperous.  Make sure you maintain a healthy budget surplus.  And you'll be fine.  The game is not about massively overhauling countries.  It's about managing them over time with minor tweaks.

I have been playing this game since its early beta release and have been holding out on this review for quite some time. The reason for that is because I felt this game had a lot of potential, and offered something unique to the RTS gamer. However, after release, and a second release (Supreme Ruler Ultimate) the game still lacks logical or sensable content. AI constantly remain idol, or stuck in one time period, and lack any sort of diplomatic logic. The game uses a UN system, who's rating can never be changed or influenced but the rating effects all diplomacy and your economy. The Research system is full of dead ends and techs with absolutely no description/purpose. The challenge isn't even here. Starting at China in 1936 I have the military and economic might of 1990s China by the 1950s while other countries like the USA remain in a downward spin of debt, or research 1 new tech every decade. This game is a great trick, it looks very promising, but lacks the right content to allow the game to function. The game is still loaded with bugs, glitches, and crashes regardless of your system. Updates come once every month 1/2 or 2 and the content is to fix what you'd expect would have been done before release. To conclude this rant, don't buy this game for another 4 years, it will take them that long to add content and fix the bugs at their rate.

Having originally played a lot of Supreme Ruler 2020 I was very excited to play this Ultimate Version. It did initially feel a bit of a cheeky move releasing it so soon after 1936 (and to be honest before 1936 had been properly finished) but I appreciated the discounted price as compensation. To be fair I never really got into 1936 as I prefered the future setting of 2020. This version lets you play the 1936, cold war and 2020 games with the added benefit that the tech tree in a 1936 start will go all the way through to the end of the 2020 tech tree. To be honest in a normal game stretching the gameplay out that far would be pretty difficult, I have never managed it.
As it is my faveourite game mode the review is mainly based on a 2020 starting date. I found the 1936 game pretty tough due to supply shortages which I know are realistic but still it makes for a tough game for a lot of countries. I do on the whole enjoy this version however I find that at this stage of its development I honestly prefer how a game played out in the original 2020 version. My major complaint with this version so far is that the computer is far too free with alliances. After a couple of years the world becomes such a tangled mess of alliances that wars do not seem to break out that much between AI countries.  Unless you play as say China or Russia you will probably find most countries are friendly to you and probably have pretty similar allies making conquest a bit of a headache. It makes rampant warmongoring with the UK for example a lot more difficult than in the original 2020. As a lesser note some of the AI combat provides odd outcomes, in one go I played through South Korea conquered the whole of China and Pakistan conquered India. After that there were hardly any hostile enemies for me to target. You can fiddle around with the game settings to provide a different gameplay experience, at the moment I prefer Shattered World with very high volitility (no units can help to prevent some counter intuitive outcomes from wars) as a sanbox go.
On the plus side there has been a lot of incremental improvements to the game with a lot of issues I had on release being ironed out through patches so I am hopeful the game is only going to get better going forward.  Undoutedly the graphics are better and the tech tree has been improved so it is not simply just a nicer looking version of 2020.
I do recommend giving the game a try, particularly if you do not have all of the versions included in Ultimate but I can't help thinking that in its current state I did used to have a lot more fun playing the original 2020.
