One of the biggest points of this game is Heavy Metal and its imagery: Long-haired head bangers (with comically -unless you are a F1 pilot- sized necks), cool and sexy (In the eighties sense of sexy) biker girls, huge metal-themed statues bursting out of the ground, giganitc anvils with lava rives flowing, riffs, demons, epic battles, motorcycles speeding, and beer and horns everywhere. Is one of those games made by someone who enjoyed the medium it references and which grow in it. This is not a "let's push some random generic references to heavy metal" (as so many games have done before with the eighties), but a truly unique and well crafted journey through the perspective of actual metal fans of what the "Land of Metal" is.
Thus, if you know who Rob Halford is, or if you use (or used) to headbang with Ronnie James Dio, you will feel here at home, laugh with (almost) every joke and smile at every single reference, and really enjoy how the world of metal and some of its sub genres is represented, all glued together with one of the best licensed OST's lawyers and money can put together. You got no idea about classic heavy metal? Then lookup "Brütal Legend Soundtrack playlist" and choose the playlist with MORE THAN 100 LICENSED SONGS. Titanic effort to please your ears while riding through the land of metal.
The mandatory horns are here -> \m/, so we can keep going.
This is a classic Double fine game in what background and history refeers: Its ♥♥♥♥ing great. At every single level. Characters are funny and well developed (Voiced in the original version by people like Jack Black or Lemmy Kilmister), the artistic side of the game is impressive at almost every single level, with different zones of the map following different substyles of heavy music, huge creatures which seems to have just escaped from a Judas Priest cover roaming the land... visually everything is in its place and ready to rock, achieving a weird mixture between some of the best designs for both creatures and landscape I've seen, alsoo imbued with a classic spirit straight from the beginning of the eighties. Also, the (epic) history, filled with demons, vikings, gods of metal and a "as subtle as an atom bomb" reference to Motörhead would fit without problem in a conceptual album from Manowar or Dio.
The main problem with the game is that it tries to cover way too much features. You got a car which you can use to roam the Land of Metal listening to the different heavy metal songs mentioned earlier. You can fight with axe and guitar (yeah and guitar, HELL YEAH!) against multiple enemies. And you can direct battles in a simple-RTS style, in which it seems to be the main focus of the game. Everything can be upgraded, everything has combos, but almost nothing is deeply explored.
You never got to a smart designed melee fight past the first level, nor you get more activities than racing with your car, and the RTS battles aren't exactly food for fans of the genre, as most of them are really simple "go ahead with everyone until you destroy the enemy base" missions, something that, on the other hand, is to be grateful for as the RTS controls (designed to use a console pad) are improvable, if I had to be polite.
The crappy thing about all of this is that I'm not complaining about the game being bad (besides the poor RTS controls), but because I WANT MORE AND BETTER. The hack and slash deserves levels playing together with Ofelia (The female companion of the main character), the open world deserves to be bigger and more detailed, the RTS deserves to have proper mouse + keyboard controls so I can actually think on performing more complex strategies, like banding together with some infantry and attack in a mosh pit while a squad of bikers from hell cover our asses.
I liked the game. A lot. I enjoyed every reference, listened to every song (Even discovered some groups that have gone under my radar), laughed at every joke and enjoyed a ride in a world I want to go back to. But I have serious doubts as if someone who wouldn't enjoy the background of the game would enjoy the gameplay itself, with its cool things, but also with its many flaws.

My recommending this game is one with a big BUT...
I love Tekken; I have played T2, T3, a bit of T5, A LOT of TTT2 and now I'm playing T7 - I will try T6 soon, too.
If you just want a solid fighting game on PC, then this is a really good buy. I'm serious. However, if I - and I do - compare it to Tekken Tag Tournament 2/TTT2 I played on the Xbox 360, I feel like I would have been A LOT happier with a PC port for that game, with the new characters as (even paid) DLC for said port.
- The fighting is excellent, except for some cheap battles I will not spoil. You will need to get better than my noob level to breeze through those
- There is more to customize, but most of it is useless or ridiculous-looking stuff. I had hoped T7 would be better at customization than TTT2, but it is not, in my opinion. There are no mid-length, or long hairstyles, no separate hairstyle categories and somehow I feel like colors are harder to fine-tune then before. Also, you earn battle money to buy customzations with, but most of it is locked only to be obtained with Treasure Battle now, which is ridiculous, because in the previous game you were able to decide yourself what to get when. Now you cannot, for many things. You get money, but for what purpose, I wonder? This is coming from a guy who had bought all customizations in TTT2 for his mains and secondary characters after a while. But at least I was able to decide what I bought when. And I was able to give proper, good-looking hairstyles.
- The graphics are supposed to be a step up. In some cases, that's true, but I find hair on many characters to look more like plastic than before, they messed up some faces - like Lili's, my previous main - and the graphics WERE already good. I see no reason why they changed it like this; there are engine limitations, but they wanted to show off the graphics system. Then why have plastic hair, very, very few hair customizations and worse looking faces (even though not in all cases)?
- There is almost no offline mode to speak of anymore to me. I'm an offline player, I'm mad. I don't like lag and spammers. I don't want to be halfway forced to play online. There is no survival mode, which I always immensely enjoyed, there is no team battle, which was always fun with friends, there is no time attack (frankly I don't care about that one), the arcade had been reduced from 10 to 8 stages in TTT2, now it's only 5, with no cinematic ending when you beat it. There is 0 incentive to play it. Treasure Battle has some nice mixup battles, but limits customization unlike TTT2's Ghost Battle. 1 Plus about it is that it now saves your winstreak. It just doesn't get saved in a list, so it's no real replacement for Survival and you will still fight ridiculously customized characters 90% of the time, like in TTT2, which started to annoy me even in that gem of a game.
- I have the season pass and I regret it. In no way, shape or form, do I think this game can compete with TTT2.
- The story is nice to play through once, maybe twice, then you're done and the character episodes are only 1 measly fight each time - at least for the 3 characters I tried it out with.
- Many characters are missing. Angel (my 2nd main in TTT2 and T2) would've been a perfect fit and high time to include her and give us answers, but she is not in, instead there is some weird exorcist I give 0 things about.
- Lili does not act like, play like, sound like, or look like her old self, nor can you customize her like you could in the past. I'm disappointed. She's become even more exaggerated, less pretty, important moves were changed and all previous cute moments she had are completely gone (yes this is a thing for me, sorry).
- Yoshimitsu looks like he came straight out of a tentacle hent** to r**e the girls. His most ridiculous look yet.
- Guest character Akuma sticks out like a sore thumb, unlike Gon did in the past. I never played a SF game for more than 5 minutes before and I did not know a guest character would appear. Once I saw Akuma's design and stance in the game I immediately knew he didn't belong. I won't spoil anything, so I'll stop there.
All in all I'm very disappointed, but I still recommend it for those who want to try the new characters, want to play Tekken on PC and for those who don't care about any of my negatives. At least I'm having fun with Kazumi and Eliza, but I wonder for how long.

We did it folks, we finally got a Tekken on PC!
The story mode is fairly short, on the standard difficulty it took me somewhere between 3-4 hours to beat it. Still, if you're new to the fighting game genre, be aware that exceptionally few fighting games have big campaigns. Most campaigns in fighting games are a series of fights strung together with a loose notion of plot, the only real exception I can think of is Mortal Kombat/Injustice.
Tekken looks prettier than ever on the UE4 engine, visually it's a gorgeous game. The hair on the characters doesn't look fantastic but speaking as someone who has spent three years failing to get hair to work in UE4, trust me, it's really difficult. I can't blame the developers for it if I can't manage it myself either.
The combat feels absolutely incredible to play. The hitboxes on the characters are eerily 1:1 with their models, meaning that timing is now more crucial than ever. You can't get away with barely missing, if your punch doesn't connect, you won't get off on a technicality any more.
At present, the season pass gets you a bunch of cosmetic items in a metallic tint (you can get the non-metallic variants without the pass) and two new characters that haven't been announced yet. I'm not sure if the pass with get you Eliza or if she was just a pre-order bonus. Still, I feel the need to bring this up:
THERE ARE NO MIRCROTRANSACTIONS!
With the exception of the metallic stuff, everything you can unlock for your characters, you do so by playing the game. Beating the campaign and participating in battles online gives you Fighting Coins which you can spend on cosmetic stuff for characters. You don't need any of it, it's all just for aesthetics only. There is one item which does effect gameplay called the Mirror, but it's free. All it does is stops your opponent from moving when the fight is over, so if you're the type of person who doesn't like getting BM'd at the end of the fight, you can stop your opponent from doing it by equipping the mirror. But again, it's free.
TL;DR
Game is optomised exceptionally well, had a great launch, no outstanding bugs or glitches, the online works gloriously, the game looks beautiful and there are no microtransactions in it. On top of that it's incredibly fun. This is what games should aspire to be.

[UPDATED REVIEW v2]
Tekken 7 is a rich, complex fighter played by a tight community where many players have more than 10 years of experience. The game offers several rather specific mechanics, tons and tons of moves and a rather large roster. The gameplay is as polished as it gets, characters are rather balanced (despite what some people complain about, there's no 'cheap moves' once you learn how to counter them).
On the negative site, the online experience can at times be cringe worthy. The online Ux is simply not good; it currently seems like finding an opponent (let alone an opponent at your level) can be difficult and up to neigh impossible depending on your time zone and whether or not you're one of these unlucky players who experiences 'The Limbo'.
Some of the soundtracks are going to make you mute your sound, too. Not all of them, some.
Now, your experience will vary greatly depending on how much you're invested in the franchise/fighting games. If you're looking for single player experience, there is none except a bad story more and basic survival and arcade. If you're looking for online fun though, you'll find a lot of people willing to fight you. Warning: Tekken is HARD and getting really good is going to take time.
I can't recommend it as a first fighter experience right now (not until the single player modes receive some content and tutorials), but I will recommend it if you are the dedicated, competitive type.

<CSG-46+1> is an excellent anime visual novel {VN} derived from the renowned Japanese
legend.  It is offered as "free-to-play" on Steam, so the price is hard to beat !  Essentially,
is an introduction to the full VN which includes 4 additional chapters.  Be aware that this is a mature tale with limited nudity, but there is no "hentai" in the Steam version.
Whereas
is an all male Samurai story,
is written from the perspective of a young male Protagonist who is transported from 21st Century Tokyo to Edo Period {circa 1700} Ako domain Japan.  He finds himself among a largely female Samurai society.  This is Chapter 1 of 5 of the VN and focuses on
relationship with the Chamberlain {senior administrative and war leader} for the noble Asano family based in Ako in southwestern Honshu.  The following chapters develop alternate "realities" for the Protagonist in the Edo Period as he struggles to counter the tides of history.
delivers a gripping, sometimes emotional, tale with voice acting in Japanese accompanied by available English or Japanese subtitles.  While the subtitle "messages" could stand some editing, they do not significantly detract from the story-line.  An especially nice feature is an appendix of Character profiles providing biographical details.  This is needed during game-play to help keep track of the inter-relationships among the extensive list of characters and the Protagonist.
I strongly recommend that any gamer interested in Visual Novels {or who just would like to read a good tale} try the "free-to-play" first chapter of
.  Personally, I enjoyed the "demo" sufficiently to buy all the follow-on Chapters.

While I'm still early on, I am very much impressed by the game (Ill revise this review if that changes) On the performance front, there are a lot of complaints of poor optimization. While I can't speak for the claims of others, I'm running it at 60 FPS 1920x1080 without many problems after a small bit of tweaking the GFX settings (Apparently, nVidia users, its encouraged to disable contact hard shadows ((I think thats what its labelled)) and MSAA. After that and some other settings I don't care for like Bloom, no problems with a Gigabyte GeForce GTX 980 3X OC, 16 GB RAM, and a i7 6700K)
On to the Graphics, it's very much an impressive step up after Human Revolution (which still looks good imo. Except for the hair. Oh god the hair) I don't have too much to say that hasn't been said already, it looks amazing, especially the lighting. The detail on the faces (And the hair, thank christ) are much improved over their HR counterparts.
Gameplay I haven't had much of a chance to really appraise yet, since I've been coming through everything carefully. The cover movement has changed a bit from HR, and it'll take some getting used to, such as hitting F instead of RMB to enter cover.
I would wholly recommend picking it up when you can. So far it's fun, the story has that same sense of mystery that I've come to expect out of a Deus Ex game with some big names in the lore making appearances very early on in the game, which pleases the fanboy in me on some level.
==Game Completion update==
Alright so I finally completed the game. I'm very sad to see the reputation of such a great game being tarnished by the silly reviews being spat out by everyone and their mother. In terms of optimization, I thankfully never had any issues with the game other than a consistent freezing here and there while running about Prague. I'd move, it'd lock up for a second or two, then I'd be back on my way. Why that happens I don't know, but it never really got in my way.
Microtransactions - Not a whole lot to say in this regard. I don't need them, and the fact that some people do need them has had no impact on my enjoyment of the game. Don't like them? Don't use them.
Ending - I will not spoil it, but the ending is the one BIG issue I have with this game. Boss fight, followed by end of the game cutscene with Alex. They have a small conversation about things I won't talk about for the readers sake, but it's very unfufilling as to what we've been fighting and bleeding for in this journey of a story. That being said, I still have yet to play the first "Jensen's Stories" so that might have some more conclusion on Mankind Divided for me.
Overall - I stand by my original post. Get this game. If you're a fan of this the Deus Ex franchise, get it. If you're nervous about all the people going on endlessly about bad optimization and bugs, maybe wait a bit for more than 2 patches to come out.

7.3/10 and Yes but with a large grain of salt. Was this game as great as the first no, was it still a good game yes and I did enjoy it. I know that many people have had a large amount of game breaking bugs and after reading some of them in the discussion threads, I pray for your fixes to come. I thankfully did not have any massive bugs but a host of small annoying ones. I would recommed this game to anyone interested once it hits atleast 40% off. The dlc are not currently neccessary (Towliee provides some funny dialogue hints, if they were free and while I don't have the relics of zaron I can't image they are strong enough to warrant buying them).
Now lets break some of it down-
- The story overall was good, had some very funny parts and enjoyable side quests but the first game definately outshines it. The fist half of the game was great, started going downhill halfway through and I found the ending to be very ehhhhhh.
- The new combat system I found highly enjoyable, however it was also were I had all of the bugs issues I experienced. Which mainfested themselves in random pauses in combat where no characters either myself, ally or enemy would move or do any actions for anywhere between 10-30 seconds. This would happen when an enemy was knocked down, an ally was knocked down, any enemy or ally moved on top of a knocked down enemy or when an ally was revived. Now this didn't happen during every combat sometimes I would have 6-7 fights where it would all go smoothly and then I would have a fight last an extra 5-10 minutes because nobody would be able to do anything. While this isn't nearly as bad as other bugs it could definately test your patience.
My largest problem with the game ***THIS INCLUDES SOME SPOLIERS READ AHEAD AT YOUR OWN PERIL, YOU HAVE BEEN WARNED***
When Timmy gives you access to all the powers in the game.
Now many of you were probably overjoyed when that happened but I found it completely unneccesary. When given the ability to multiclass by Cartman you get to look at all the classes and choose a new one to add for more abilities, which I thought was a very cool idea, giving you access to more abilities helped make the character more customizable. You could select from 1st & 2nd tier heroes the first time and all 3 teirs the second time. This all seemed like natural character progession to me and you were picking classes that fit together and ignoring classes and abilities that you weren't going to use cause they didn't fit your character. So when Timmy gives you access to everything, I was like I didn't want these before why would I want them now. To be fair I did screw around with some the of abilities I got access to against random fights, but once I started back into the story I went back to how my artifacts and DNA were built to the abilities I had been using. The game is an RPG, your picking these roles specifically cause thats what you had in mind for your character, why would you want access to a bunch of ranged/magic abilities if your playing a punch people in the face hero. I think a better idea for what Timmy could have given you to progess your character futher would have mabye been to empower one of your 3 classes picked so that those abilities maybe did more damage or had extra effects. Or maybe he gave you access to a 4th normal ability slot, giving you one more ability then anyones else plus your ultimate. I'm prefectly fine if an RPG wants to give you the keys to the kingdom at the start of the game (Skyrim, Fallout 4) and allow to progress and change as you see fit, but to have you pick classes specifically making a kind of character in mind only to half way through say "O now you can have whatever you want" is just lazy and boring.

The South Park part of it is funny. The Ubisoft part of it is also funny.
It's like they took every bad video game design trend and mashed them all into a pot:
An unnessicary crafting system?
Constant nagging for going off the beaten path?
Condescening help immediatly after encountering simple puzzles?
A metagame based entierly on collectables?
They're all checked off. God help you if you felt like having a thought on your own.
But I think I'm still going to trudge through it. South Park is just too damn good. This may be too, even in spite of the cynicial, focus-tested design choices. But I certainly wouldn't recommend it to anyone that wasn't already going to get it.
*Update after finishing*
On the hardest difficulty  the combat system in the game is really solid-- using your allies to heal, overshield, damage and tank with you allows for a surprisingly nuanced battle system-- all of which is ultimately undermined by the ability to buy a trove of healing items at no real cost.
But if you force yourself not to abuse the items (say, by using only the ones you find in treasure boxes, like I did) you can have a really good time with it.
Further I might add that the game seems to have a problem ending. It looks like it's coming to a close 5 or 6 times, and each time it just seems to keep going on afterward. Strangely, it's not like their doubling down each time, either. Not all the endings are bigger and bolder than the ones that came before them.
A last note: as funny as it was at times, I'm disappointed in the big time wimpiness I saw from the jokes in the game. South Park's good ol' humor persists toward mexicans, rednecks, christians and asians but is deeply reverent of and flinching toward alternate genders, sexualities, religions and black people.
This game pulled back from going after all of today's hot button issues but kept on with the usual tirade against people who aren't a big deal in the news these days. Which is weak as hell. Because when a comedian selectivly pulls punches it makes the ones they actually decide to throw turn into *actual* blows.
Maybe that's Ubisoft's doing too? Maybe they weren't willing to touch issues that were so hot with so much money on the line? But so what? That wouldn't Parker and Stone less culpible. It would only mean that their price was met.

This is a really solid hack n slash, or action RPG as they seem to be called now. I personally enjoyed Diablo 3 but I think this is a better game overall.
The way the classes work is a bit different to how Diablo 3 does it, I think I would say it works better but you could argue it is different. Essentially instead of just having a modular system of skills that you can quick swap like in Diablo 3 what you get is a set of 3 skills trees per class which allow for a lot of variety. You also get to increase your stat points every level, which was available in Diablo 2 but not 3 for some reason.
Another nice touch is the pet system: You can choose the look of your pet on character creation whether you want a Wolf, Bulldog or a number of other choices. This is aesthetic but you can obtain fish, surprisingly by fishing and these transform your pet into other creatures with new abilities or increased stats for a limited time. The pets can also be loaded up with gear you intend to sell, plus you can make a shopping list(indentify scrolls, portals and potions) and send them back to pick them up plus sell all the junk you've acquired. It is a nice system as it saves constantly going back to town to restock and clear bag space.
The thing that really makes it though is the modding community, even just counting Synergies which adds tons of new monsters through the campaign, new classes plus an endgame. What this means is once you hit around level 50 and complete the original game you can find a vendor that sells portals to tons of different dungeons from around level 50+
Basically that mod alone adds a silly amount of content and you could quite easily get a couple hundred hours worth of play time, either solo or with friends.
The only criticism I could level at this game is the online multiplayer seems a bit flakey, my friend and I would randomly find the lobby saw the other person as offline when they were hosting a game. It still worked, it just ocassionally required a couple of minutes of refreshing and relogging.

The gameplay is acceptable but dull after awhile. Level requirements on abilities you can "refund" for in game currency lends itself to slower character progression. There are lateral character progression elements with the ability to invest into learned skills and occasionally unlock surprisingly fun combinations.
The story is original enough as these click fests tend to go, but it's neither overtly grim nor tongue in check, it plays the setting straight and has voice acting but it doesn't compell as well as the grim (and often grisly) settings of it's competitors. Having played the first two Dungeon sieges I'm not blown away by the blocky landscapes, although the ambient sound effects and bug activity are a good touch.

While useful, there's no skill tree, or interaction between your character, nor is it's presence acknowledged by any of the npcs, and it has no involvement in the cutscenes. Your pet is basically a slave (of a skin you find aesthically pleasing).

Now to the good things, which there is a lot of. Amazing fun, a level up system that really makes you feel the progression, dynamic gameplay, moderate skill required, problem solving, unique characters, so much fun to play with friends. I can go on but I think all I really need to say is that the good things heavily outweigh the bad.
As far as the not worth $15, yes, it alone is not worth it, but it is important to remember that you're not just buying the early access, you're supporting RoosterTeeth to continue to refine this game and make it blossom in to something AMAZING, even more than it already is. Look at it as thanks to RoosterTeeth for making an amazing game to come, thanks for making an amazing series and story universe, and an investment made to help them continue to develop this title and a way to show your support for what is truly a worthy game, and a worthy developer.

So this is one of my favorite games of all time.
Setting:
Imagine a game based on what it would be like to interact and inhabit the world that's depicted on Heavy Metal albums from the 70-80's.
Imagine seeing a creature like the one depicted on Judas Priest's 'Screaming for Vengeance' or better yet, to be able to travel to the great pyramid and temples of Iron Maiden's 'Power Slave' album.
Only the journey doesn't end there...imagine if this metal world was separated into different regions based on the different styles of music. An example region, Mashlands covered in a dense fog that's the home of emo-nightmare before Christmas creatures and people.
Another example, imagine Amazon jungles with panthers that shoot lazers out of their eyes while being road by warrior women from KISS' album 'Love Gun'.
Gameplay:
The game starts out as a 3rd person hack and slash with driving and overall RPG- Action/Adventure where the hero explore this amazing world I talked about above. You soon assemble an army, from this point you become a commander and a warrior...the game then becomes a RTS. It's a very interesting shift in gameplay.
Story:
The story honestly reminds of something from a Black Sabbath or RUSH album. I can't put it into words without spoiling it.
I think the best way to play this is jump in head first.
Soundtrack:
One of the greatest soundtracks out there. If you want to cut your teeth on metal, rock, or just something new for those of you who don't normally listen to heavy stuff, look no further. The soundtrack that comes with the game for $19.99 is the OST written for the game (Not the one with Ozzy, Iron Maiden, and so on) . Which I also highly recommend.
Does this game have it's issues? of course but, I highly recommend it to anyone and everyone thanks to the game world, music, and it's great story.

This is a well-crafted game with great visuals, sound and music.
I didn't find the story particularly interesting or moving, but the real fun is to be had in exploring the 'world' of the game.  The characters move through different environments, from village to forest to underground caves and so on – so there's a good variation in these environments, each have something of a unique, enchanting atmosphere of  their own.
I see a lot of complaints about the keyboard controls.  They are a little annoying, several times I found myself confusing which set of controls were for which character, but this is only a minor issue – the player can still manage to get through without too much trouble, and the good parts of this game definitely outweigh the issue of controls.  There are too many video segments interrupting gameplay, and gameplay often involves something a simple as moving foward, and when these two issues come together, you start to feel like you're having little real influence on the game.
For some reason, the game reminded me of 'From Dust', another game with great visuals, sound and music – and especially atmosphere, so if you liked that – you'll probably enjoy 'Brothers'.  I think a younger audience would appreciate 'Brothers' more, because younger minds can really get absorbed by the world and its atmosphere, the puzzles are pretty easy, and the story is very simple.
You certainly won't regret buying this game on sale.

As a DeusEx Fan, I was really looking forward Mankind Divided and after around 4 Hours with the game I’m in a very positive mood about it. I also read through quite some reviews on here and I’m not sure why so many people here give negative reviews.

Personally I only had very small problems with the controls in the beginning that were resolved after a few minutes of calibrating my mouse. The other controls are fine and easy to learn and master.


It’s true that the game wants some good hardware to play on the Very High and Ultra settings. I’m playing on High myself and in my opinion the game still looks great.
I have a Geforce GTX680 with 4gb ram and an i7 3770k@3,50ghz, also the game is installed on a normal HDD and the loading times are amazingly quick.
In my first 4 Hours with Mankind Divided I had constant frames, no stuttering’s or a crash. It ran smooth in any given moment. Thumps up for that. I can’t tell yet if there will be any technically problems later, if so, I’ll update my review.

*edit* As a little update note. I’ve played now for over 60h and I still had no crash or anything. The only technical problem I had so far was that the screen froze for 2seconds. That’s happened two times. Nothing else. The game still runs smooth at any given moment. I’m still playing on the standard High settings. I’m totally happy with that. The game looks awesome!

For the Gameplay, if you played Human Revolution you won’t have any problems to get into the game. It plays pretty much the same.  I felt like "I'm home" the first time I took control over Adam.
And if this is your first DeusEx Game, you won’t have much trouble either. There are playable tutorials in the first Level, which will teach you the gameplay and what you can do in the game.
*edit* As you would expect it from a DeusEx game, you have multiple ways to solve every mission in a lot of ways, the areas welcome you to explore. There are also areas again that you can access only with certain perks, what is a good reason to visit places later again and find their last hidden secret. As a person that needs to search every inch of an area, that really suits me. And the game rewards you for exploring. It’s always worth it, may it be items, side missions, infomations. But if you don’t want to do that, I’m sure you’re still fine. But you’ll definitely miss a lot of details :)
If you play the game on German, like I do, the voices, in the well made cutscenes, aren’t always lip-sync what’s a bit annoying but nothing too bad. The translation is very good and the Voice Actors are doing a good job overall.
What I really like is that you can switch between English and the language in which you play the game. So you can choose to hear the original voices if you like to and have the subtitles in your local language. A really nice feature for people that aren’t fluent enough in English, but would still like to listen the original voices.

The atmosphere is great from what I’ve seen so far. You feel that the world is divided into two classes of humans. Naturals and Augs are separated from each other. Everywhere is police that controls the Augs and dare you if you don’t have your papers with you. The social pressure and oppression is in every corner of the town. Augs only talk with each other, if you talk to “naturals” they mostly react in a unfriendly way to you. Posters on the walls, security posts. Stuff you see on TV or hear over the Radio. I would give the atmosphere an A+ so far.
Now after I've done some missions, I can say that the atmosphere in the mission is great aswell. I’m doing a stealth/no kills playthough. Don’t know how different it is when you just gun everything down. But I would guess it’s great aswell. :)
If you haven’t played Human Revolution (You should. It’s amazing) you can watch a 12minute Video before you start playing that will inform you about everything that happened so far.
Overall, I can fully recommend DeusEx: Mankind Divided to any DeusEx fan, and to anyone that likes Stealth/Action Games with an amazing Story..

So after 25 hours of gameplay I can say that this game is truly a fantastic purchase for 15 bucks! But be warned, ahead is an HONEST review!
Graphics: 9/10 Charming and bright in most of the worlds.  I like the graphics alot acutally. They inspire and relax me at the same time and I like that feeling.  With smooth edges, no blockiness, and the game running very smooth with no visible chopping it lends itself to a great gaming experience!
Sound: 6/10 Sound effects are busted! After mining for a few minutes, 20mins or so, the sound effects just stop working! The music is lovely and very peaceful when it should be and exciting/suspenseful when you enter underground caves or mines, almost Metroid like.  Sound would be a 10/10 but with problems of this magnitude...gotta dock 4 points at least.
Gameplay: 9/10 So far the game plays like Minecraft when you are building, and plays like Zelda (any 3d version) when in combat.  The spell/magic system is more than enough to defeat baddies while maintaining proper balance to the Mage's melee counterparts.  The crafting is decent and keeps my interest for hours.  It doesn't take long to craft anything, but you will have to do some grinding and portal hopping to obtain the resources you need.  This isn't like certain mining games where you walk into a cave and 10 types of minerals/metals are there.  This feature kind of forces you to explore the new areas and keeps the game progressing, if you so choose to do so.  I would love it if every world/island had it's own miniboss as this game lost 1 gameplay point for not having enough challenging bosses.  I do like the boss fights but there just aren't enough of them.  Single player, LAN play, and Steam Friends are all options for gameplay so go it alone or with up to 3 other friends!
Storyline: 7/10 This is pretty basic.  There isn't much of a storyline other than you somehow are a portal knight that is tasked with opening up portals and defending them from the incoming baddies.  There are semi-random NPCs that talk to you, ignore you, or on occassion you will find one that is a trader.  There needs to be more NPCs on each island, a trader for sure!  Other mining sandbox games have villagers in a village...why not add a similar feature to this game so there is a way to get rid of unwanted items instead of just trashing them. In all honesty, this game doesn't need much of a storyline.  It is a sandbox game/Arpg but a strong(er) storyline would definitely help the younger, unfocused, or players that are not as interested in the sandbox aspect.
Value: 9/10 Even though this game is still in early access and has a few flaws, mainly sound effects quitting out, I would still highly recommend this game to anyone who enjoys a sandbox environment with almost complete freedom to do as you please.  For $15 this is a family friendly game I can stream with my kids and still have fun as an adult.  Portal Knights throws me back to the days of my youth playing console ARPG games. I do wish the game devs would add a 2 or 4 pack in the steam store with a slight discount as this is a coop game and benefits greatly from the multiplayer experience.
Overall score: 8/10 This game is above average in fun, great graphics, super fun multiplayer, family friendly, and runs smoothly on a normal pc/low end gaming rig.  Again I have only 25 hours into this game and have only scratched the surface.  After I have played more I will leave an update and let everyone know if and how things have changed.  Cheers!

There's just something about being able to freely run amok and fight and explore without having the normal linear experience that follows with combat RPG games. Often I tell myself why they wasted the time crafting gear you have to blindly swap out for the next best things. (Or rip my hair out because of games that have 6 armor sets but enough quests to make you take a hiatus) If you feel that way about the typical Crawler experience, and games like dungeon siege, dungeon hunter, fable, God of war, and many other games on that front, this is worth your money.
The major selling point to this game for me is the perspective of gameplay. It's just you and monsters almost all of the time, someone who wants a quest, and a bunch of dead travellers everywhere. It's pretty much saying No one is strong enough to leave the city but the bandits or a few scarce soldiers around the game that want you recruited. It is extremely hard to explain without a video. So you should go watch a video review. And even with the reviewers saying, hey, it's easy, it's boring, I see the action And the exploration And it just became a sure buy in my opinion.
As for the difficulty. I started hard mode and felt right at home, I think you can change the difficulty at any time, but I didn't bother because the twists and turns are the same as Skyrim on adept. Though you'll probably die more here because they're more blatant on using combos to pressure you. You can do the same to enemies provided you have a weapon or spell that does enough raw damage.
Speaking of raw damage. There are disciplines. Might, finesse and sorcery I think... Or wisdom. Basically it's warrior assassin and mage. BUT these disciplines are based on ability point distribution. And the general number of the points spent in each one dictate the type of armor you can wear. Also, those points Also unlock a destiny card system that offers you all cards your points accumulate into. So if you had every discipline at 100 you can select one of any of the perk setups in the game. It is very rewarding to all play styles and I would have loved to see more of it. Some skills even come with evasion modifiers that help balance gameplay for you.
The quests in this game are very well done. Not in the skyrim sense of, there's a right way to do anything that isn't daedric, but in more of a, why would I help you steal something for what I think is No reason?, kind of way. If you're supporting a specific role in the game, it shows a lot of promise as you can easily find a few quests that have some odd bad alignment turns, though to the same event, it does lack motivation in how it doesn't explain why they want you to necessarily do these things, however I would think the game will feature the same dissatisfaction if you don't assume the role of being someone who has the power to change fate. And in that sense it may be entirely up to you to shape people and their, it was written so it is done, attitude. It's a very nice way to get you on your own two feet without direction.
I don't think I have done one story quest. I basically just help the people that appeal to me and move on. And it still manages to be enough for me as a game to recommend without knowing anything of the story. The game is just good looking. The combat is simple, yet fun, the skills and quests are very cut and dry, but remain relevant because they can be improved.
I personally think a lot of love went into the game. I don't see too many games that meet most of the expectations most people want and don't get out of games, essentially making them jump between several games to name a justifiable experience. With this game, you get combat, self implied story, open world, skills, magic, you can say it was supposed to be an mmo, and it does feel that way at times. You can even rag on the story, or repetitive quests that everyone seems to complain at. I guess they never played a real mmo. It's really not that bad, and I would have gotten the game during the summer had I known that. And I'm glad they made this game an offline game, so that even though they're gone, people can still experience it fully. Because it is really well made and quality driven. It's definitely not a purchase to regret. Unless you have a game just like it, and if you do, tell me so I can get that too.

Portal Knights completely lacks scope and depth. There is pretty much no reason to play this game.
In theory, Portal Knights is a Minecraft clone with the addition of (boring) fetch quests. You travel through a series of worlds by finding portals. Each world has different resources for you to harvest, so you'll often need to travel among several worlds to collect everything you need. You can setup a base in any or all worlds you travel to, but it makes the most sense to declare one world as your Home world and setup a single base there.  Either way, you'll still be travelling back and forth between several worlds to collect the specific resources you need for the next tier of items.
The whole point of the game, from what I can tell, is to collect items in order to craft better items which help you collect more items faster and craft even more items... It's just an endless cycle of resource harvesting and crafting with no meaningful end goal.  If the resource harvesting were enjoyable, then the means would be acceptable, but turns out harvesting for the sake of harvesting is dreadfully boring.  The 3+ boss fights are made easier if you have higher-level gear, but who cares!? The bosses are just meaningless fights you must encounter at specific points before you can advance. Plus, the penalty for dying is the loss of some coins (which serve no useful purpose), so nothing is lost if you face a boss too soon and die a lot in the process.
Very few NPCs serve any purpose, but occasionally you will find one that runs a store or offers a quest. I have yet to see a point to the coins you collect as all shopkeepers sell useless garbage (like seeds or pets) that you can easily collect in any number of worlds. The handful of random quests you encounter periodically throughout the various worlds nearly all require you to find or craft a certain item and bring it back to the NPC. A few will have you kill X number of an enemy type. The easiest way to finish the item quests is to just warp back to your home base, craft the item, and bring it back to the NPC... but there's a problem. The Universe map doesn't tell you which quests you have active in each world, so it's impossible to track your quest status in game unless you travel to each and every world to manually check for a quest. Once you're in the right world you then need to hunt down the NPC who gave you the quest, because there is no indication to tell you where to go.
The game is downright boring in solo, so multiplayer is a must, but it has a terrible multiplayer setup. The Universe map is linked to a player's character, so if you join someone else's multiplayer game, the only progress you will retain is your character's level and current inventory. Any portals you open in another player's Universe will not transfer back to your character's Universe. This means if you start a game with friends, you will never be able to play solo without them unless you want to restart the exploration process.  Considering the worlds fail to offer anything unique, therefore providing no reason to ever revisit them (except resource gathering), the idea of having to restart is unacceptable.  This game desperately needs a way to setup a dedicated server, otherwise the multiplayer likely won't survive.
Mechanically, I think the game is okay. There are 3 different classes, each with its own specialty and gear.  The graphics are gorgeous, the audio tracks are fantastic, the combat is more or less good, but the complete lack of meaningful activities is unforgivable.  What activities are present are so shallow that they really don't offer anything fun to come back to.  This game may actually be redeemable if the developers decide to add any meaningful content, but I doubt that will happen anytime soon. At a minimum, the following must be addressed:
* There are not enough boss fights.
* There are not enough enemy varieties (though I am thankful to see that while enemies are repeated, they do at least have different strengths/weaknesses in each world.)
* There are not enough quest-granting NPCs.
* There are too many crafting quests (those that just require you to build a weapon and give it to the NPC).
* Active quests need to be visible from the Universe map, not just within the world that has the quest.
* There are not enough merchant NPCs.
* Merchants and coins are useless (the few Merchants I encounter never have anything worth purchasing).
* Inventory size should be expandable.
* Each world should be distinctly unique in one or more noteworthy aspects.

I'm going to begin this review by saying what a lot of people are saying, if you are getting this for multiplayer don't buy it. Sometimes it can work well and be fun, but it will take you hours to get a game going...
However, this game is like no other game out there. There are hundreds if not thousands of different unit designs to choose from, from 1936 - 2020 and beyond. Its a great war simulator if you choose to use it that way, you can drag and click with mobs of troops or you can play tactically.
The AI in SRU is better than in the rest of the Supreme Ruler series, but it still leaves some to be desired. While the AI can be challenging to the player, generally unless they are a huge country with hundreds or thousands of units to send at you, you don't have much to worry about. The naval invasions are easily stopped by placing ships at your port because they don't send naval escorts. There isn't much of a naval AI, but I believe I have seen improvments in this.
The economy is fairly detailed, the world market reacts to how much resources there are in the world and the demand. So they generally represent the world economy, but i'm not sure what else to really say about it.
The world doesn't really seem to interact with the player in any real way, I often find myself just siting there not knowing really what to do but let time go by and then end up just going to war for the heck of it. If you are new to the game I recommend large countries to start but to really feel like you're in the game and to be actually doing something I recommend smaller countries as they actually need more attention.
Overall the game is great and I recommend it, I have had a lot of fun playing multiplayer (And a lot of stress and wasted time) and I have a lot of time in Singleplayer. If you are looking for a good political simnulator, look somewhere else, if you're looking for decent economics and great warfare than you found the right game.

Let me preface this review by saying that I have been a huge fan of the SR games and have played all of them with the exception of 2010. I really want to be able to recommend this game but, sadly, I cannot. Not in its current shape at least. It is just way too buggy at this point for anyone to spend $30 on it. I did so in early access because I really enjoy the series and wanted to support the development of this game. However, I now feel somewhat betrayed by the lack of progress that has been made between then and now. The economic simulator in the game, which has always been the shining feature of the previous titles, is still utterly broken. In my last play though, I spent $98 million on a bulk purchase of electricity, only to have zero of it show up in my inventory.
On top of the general game play issues, and despite comments to the contrary I've seen from others, I find this to be the most poorly optimized offering in the series. My games often ground to a halt a couple of game months in, making the game completely unplayable.
I am holding out hope that the developers are still intent on making this game into a workable, finished product. They have demonstrated great fidelity to their fans in the past by frequently updating and improving the other iterations in the series. If they do so here, I will gladly change this review. Until then, I can only advise you to go buy SR 2020 Gold. It's a heck of a lot cheaper and still one of the best (and most under appreciated) grand strategy games of all time.

This game has some obvious problems. It has been in full release for some time, but there are some campaign mechanics and events missing like the civil war in China which leads to Japan's rapid defeat before the second world war proper begins. That said, the devs are very responsive to these issues and release regular updates.
So why is this a yes rather than no? Unfortunatley very few grand strategy games of this scope and nature are made. Other than Paradox (who published previous Supreme Rulers), Battle Goat are the only company active in this genre other than even smaller companies making smaller and more focused titles.
In terms of mechanics, the military units are well researched and there are many hundreds of designs to develop. Research stetches from the 1930s and past hypothetical future technoligies. Politics and diplomacy have been fleshed out with the ability to diplomatically annex colonies as well as liberating dead regions (unfortunately you can't liberate them as a colony). A faction system has also been introduced to model the Axis and Allies as well as NATO and Warsaw Pact. Economics is largely the same as previous titles, except water has been replaced with rubber with adds another strategic consideration which will become apparent during large scale warfare.
One final warning is that you need a decent rig to run it. I only have one computer to test it on but I believe you need a decent amount of RAM and pretty powerful CPU to handle the thousands of simultaneous calculations done by the AI. The devs have improved game speed since the last games but with my i7 2.7Ghz quad core (admittedly six odd years old now) the game slows down noticably after a decade. Still playable but requires patience. If your CPU is any less powerful I would do more research before buying.

I'm not going to lie. I had high hopes for this game because I like what RWBY managed to start with. When they announced there would be a game, I thought it might actually be good.
... And then the game actually came out.
Visually, the game looks pretty similar to the animated series its based off of. It's essentially a 3D anime. It looks decent. Nothing too noteworthy and nothing that deserves too much scorn... Until something moves. The animations are... unnatural. I get that it's supposed to be anime, but the running animations by themselves are awful. Given that the animation in the source material isn't completely stellar either, I suppose it's possible to give this a pass, though I personally wouldn't.
Gameplaywise, there's not much to do. You just mash your normal attack and then press your counter button when you see a prompt. Heavy attacks and Ultimates aren't necessary. If you take damage, back off and wait for your Aura to regenerate. It's not a good system for what this game is, because it ultimately causes flow to break in almost every case. It's not fun, especially for players who enjoy aggressive play.
You gain EXP (which grows far too slowly, in my opinion) and you level up to get new skills... which aren't that useful.
Soundwise, the game is mediocre. Music is not too great, but not really grating either. The voicework is the same quality as the webseries, so that should be your judge on it.
Ultimately, the game feels like an overpriced fan game that feels like it's still in progress or, worse even, still a proof of concept. While this normally wouldn't be that big a deal, it has a price point of 19.99 USD and the creation was helped by Rooster Teeth does not help this game at all.
I could not recommend this game. It's too expensive for something far too dull. You're better off spending the 19.99 USD for something more fun or saving up for a better game of this genre.

EDIT: New Review for 12/19/2015 @ 2:29 PM EST
The Game may still be a very early access version of a much greater dream but I highly reccomend it still for those who are fans of the show or new arrivals to Rooster Teeth. (Not much new has occurred except for new visuals and info from the dev team during the livestream. Review has not changed)
[PROS/CONS]
+Beautiful graphical design. very similar to the actual show's design which adds to the immersion
+Voice acting, while limited, is high quality. The girls, Ryan, and Joel all did fantastic work
+Diversity. Yes there may only be four levels and an equal number of Grimm types but let's remeber where the roots of this game were with one level and one type of enemy based on the older concept of the Beowolf.
+Online connectivity. practically seemless ability to connect to matches and lobbies and no lag if a player drops mid game
-limited worlds/levels. As stated before, there are only four levels and those four levels are also highly restricted to a linear path. Hopefully the Game Dev team at Rooster Teeth will expand upon the limits of the levels they have (Can be forgiven thanks to the announced forever fall map in early 2016)
-Skill menu is too small. The choices in what to spend your skill points are still in the early stages so there aren't many things to put your points towards as many are locked away behind challenges
-Combat needs to be worked on. This goes as the most urgent of gameplay updates to me. there is only a dodge, no blocking and enemies gain both invincibility and speed during attacks making it tough to counter if at all. The addition of Lock on is also a must as ranged attacks are a real crapshoot for if you're gonna hit
-Only four characters. Yes I know, Team RWBY is the lead group but I would love to see the ability to play as JNPR, CFVY or even non Beacon affilitated teams like SSSN.
-More grimm are needed. Bring on swarms of Nevermores or giant Deathstalkers
-No boss fights. I want the "Defend the control point" system to include a major boss at the end of each wave defense segment (4 waves of normal enemies/pack leaders and then one fight against a Giant Grimm or equivilant boss)
-Difficulty based lobbies. As of right now, difficulty adjusts to player count. i would love to see specific chosen difficulty (from easy or trainee, to Very hard or True Huntsman or something)
[RECENT CHANGES]
Two patches have come out since My review of the game. These mostly adress preformance issues and don't work towards the combat system or the skill menus of the characters but they do make the game feel a bit smoother. Which is always an added bonus. There are also more breakable objects to find xp orbs in and while I didn't ask for it I'll welcome it all the same.
[WHAT I WOULD WANT UPDATED IMMEDIATELY]
First off, Fix the ranged attacks, if nothing else. Blake's ranged attack is too quick and overpowered. Ruby can only do three shot bursts and count your lucky stars for hitting something all three shots in a row (Saving grace is her personal armor piercing upgrade which allows you to damage the tougher enemies like Borbatusks and Ursa). Yang fires shots with a cone shape animated blast but from what I've seen the bullets still fire in straight lines. Weiss' attack is too slow compared to everyone else in the ranged catagory.
Secondly, Lock on would be a godsend especially for challenge related skill use since it is very easy to miss an attack or do a combo straight out of the field of enemies.
Third. Larger level scale, the number of invisible walls are too damn high!
Still, after a week and only two patches the game in my opinion is worth the time and money, now if you excuse me, I have challenges to complete and skills to unlock. Happy hunting, students.

I just finished the early relese stuff with both Ruby and Yang and I can honestly say, this is definitely looking like it's shaped up for some high hopes from me. With the fluid combat system and skill tree possibilities, this could easily be a long and rewarding game. Though I know there's still a lot of development going on, here are a few things that I feel could be done better.
1. The running animations are fine, however, shen running downhill or from a ledge it seems to freeze the legs in an awkward "floating" position, sure it's comical, but it's a little distracting.
2. A more expansive skill tree that incorporates the character's "semblance" in a more refined manner would be fun and entertaining.
3. There seems to be quite a bit of connectivity issues, what with a consistent string of disconnects among players. Not sure if this has to do with the players just quitting, or if the servers themselveas are flawed.
4. The lack of character level save function that would make it a little more rewarding to play through the game.
That being said, I see a huge amount of pros that outweigh the cons of the game immensely. Here is a short list of things that I found to be enjoyable.
1. The difficulty is great, forcing you tou be a little more tactical and conservative with your aura as you are forced to dodge and fight as necessary to make it through the areas.
2. The incorporation of objectives gives a sense of purpose behind the reason you are fighting or fleeing the hordes of grimm and makes you prioritize your tasks based on what will or will not be most beneficial to the completion of your objectives.
3.The fluid and uninterrupted combat system allows you to meld your regular attacks with your specials exteremely well, making the fancy combos look all the more beautiful when you finish them with a big resounding "YANG".... er "BANG"
4.As much as I would like to see other characters such as Nora and Pyrrah, It's still nice to be able to choose whichever character you like as opposed to be forced into using a character that is unused, in the end it allows the player to choose the specific play style that they are most comfortable with.
5. The art comes together nicely and makes the world of RWBY come to life in the most colorful and intricate way. Being able to explore the places that you saw on the show as well as new places in the world of Remnant.
6. Although the running is a little glitched the animations are great, the hair and clothing moving fluidly with the character makes for an enjoyable p visual experience.
For those reasons and more, I am glad to have paid out for the early access and I am excited to watch the game as the development progresses.

Fun adventure game, where you play as Jack Black, using the power of metal to overcome evil.

One of the biggest points of this game is Heavy Metal and its imagery: Long-haired head bangers (with comically -unless you are a F1 pilot- sized necks), cool and sexy (In the eighties sense of sexy) biker girls, huge metal-themed statues bursting out of the ground, giganitc anvils with lava rives flowing, riffs, demons, epic battles, motorcycles speeding, and beer and horns everywhere. Is one of those games made by someone who enjoyed the medium it references and which grow in it. This is not a "let's push some random generic references to heavy metal" (as so many games have done before with the eighties), but a truly unique and well crafted journey through the perspective of actual metal fans of what the "Land of Metal" is.
Thus, if you know who Rob Halford is, or if you use (or used) to headbang with Ronnie James Dio, you will feel here at home, laugh with (almost) every joke and smile at every single reference, and really enjoy how the world of metal and some of its sub genres is represented, all glued together with one of the best licensed OST's lawyers and money can put together. You got no idea about classic heavy metal? Then lookup "Brütal Legend Soundtrack playlist" and choose the playlist with MORE THAN 100 LICENSED SONGS. Titanic effort to please your ears while riding through the land of metal.
The mandatory horns are here -> \m/, so we can keep going.
This is a classic Double fine game in what background and history refeers: Its ♥♥♥♥ing great. At every single level. Characters are funny and well developed (Voiced in the original version by people like Jack Black or Lemmy Kilmister), the artistic side of the game is impressive at almost every single level, with different zones of the map following different substyles of heavy music, huge creatures which seems to have just escaped from a Judas Priest cover roaming the land... visually everything is in its place and ready to rock, achieving a weird mixture between some of the best designs for both creatures and landscape I've seen, alsoo imbued with a classic spirit straight from the beginning of the eighties. Also, the (epic) history, filled with demons, vikings, gods of metal and a "as subtle as an atom bomb" reference to Motörhead would fit without problem in a conceptual album from Manowar or Dio.
The main problem with the game is that it tries to cover way too much features. You got a car which you can use to roam the Land of Metal listening to the different heavy metal songs mentioned earlier. You can fight with axe and guitar (yeah and guitar, HELL YEAH!) against multiple enemies. And you can direct battles in a simple-RTS style, in which it seems to be the main focus of the game. Everything can be upgraded, everything has combos, but almost nothing is deeply explored.
You never got to a smart designed melee fight past the first level, nor you get more activities than racing with your car, and the RTS battles aren't exactly food for fans of the genre, as most of them are really simple "go ahead with everyone until you destroy the enemy base" missions, something that, on the other hand, is to be grateful for as the RTS controls (designed to use a console pad) are improvable, if I had to be polite.
The crappy thing about all of this is that I'm not complaining about the game being bad (besides the poor RTS controls), but because I WANT MORE AND BETTER. The hack and slash deserves levels playing together with Ofelia (The female companion of the main character), the open world deserves to be bigger and more detailed, the RTS deserves to have proper mouse + keyboard controls so I can actually think on performing more complex strategies, like banding together with some infantry and attack in a mosh pit while a squad of bikers from hell cover our asses.
I liked the game. A lot. I enjoyed every reference, listened to every song (Even discovered some groups that have gone under my radar), laughed at every joke and enjoyed a ride in a world I want to go back to. But I have serious doubts as if someone who wouldn't enjoy the background of the game would enjoy the gameplay itself, with its cool things, but also with its many flaws.

I have been a fan of fighting games most of my life, and especially have some fond memories of Tekken 3 on playstation.
I am a tad bias thus but even when I look at the comparison objectively, this feels like a replacement for all fighting games.
To start, let me give my opinion on other fighting games I played:
- I love comics and especially Batman, but while injustice has more lore to put its story in, the gameplay and controls often feels frustrating.
- Dead or Alive took a giant chunk of my free time, I mean, boobs and bikinis, but it wesn't on the same technical combat level as a tekken or mortal kombat, but it was still superbly fun.
- Speaking of Mortal Kombat, Mortal Kombat X was great, it kinda felt like the Dark Souls of fighting games, even on Easy, but that was mostly thanks to the same control limitations that injustice suffered from.
- Street fighter was... well... I didn't enjoy it as much as the rest, but I saw the appeal and cannot fault anyone for liking it.
Tekken 7 ticks all the boxes positively in one way or another but is not without it's faults too.
Pros:
- Tekken 7 is one of few games that is released completely at launch and doesn't suffer from massive technical issues.
- The animations make the martial arts come to life.
- The animations are smoothe due to the game being very well optomised.
- The controls are so easy to learn that new-comers can face regulars after a few short practice matches. If you aren't sure how something works or what it does, play the campaign and visit the practice match section to view your fighter's move set in action and see the effects of a chosen combo in motion.
- The story is simple and short and can be used to easily get the groove of the game, and since very few fighting games really do stories well, that's a plus.
- Characters can be customised to a large extent, and some of the customisable options include previous outfits. Don't like Jin's padded getup? Put the flame pants back and take that shirt off for the classic look.
- All the cutscenes from the first tekken game through to the latest, including Tag Tournament. can be unlocked and viewed in case you ever felt you missed something.
- Overall It just feels more polished than most gmaes, especially fighting games, out there.
- I linked up my two wireless xbox controllers to my PC, invited my uncle (whom is also my long time tekken rival) over, and had my♥♥♥♥♥solidly handed to be until midnight, fun and frustration that can happily put any friendship to the test.
Cons:
- As with any tekken, your boss characters feel a tad gimmicky and love to spam unblockable attacks when reaching higher ranked matches in arcade or endless treasure hunt mode.
- The character episodes are basically one match played with each character to unlock their ending, which used to be something you earned after several grueling matches in arcade.
- It's the first tekken to come to PC, why did it take so long Banda Namco?!
- There is no "Send help, I am addicted and can't seperate from the game long enough to sleep, eat or go to work" button.
Short Verdict:
- If you enjoy fighting games, then why are you reading and not trying to win the King of Iron Fist Tournament?! Buy the game, its a knock-out!

Torchlight II is an isometric action Role-Playing Game developed and published by Runic Games who's composed of developers from popular titles such as Fate and the Diablo (1 and 2). This game was designed to resurrect the old school dungeon crawler genre adding to it a fresh coat of paint and an attempt to quench the thirst for the classical isometric experience. True to the formula on what made the first Torchlight great, Torchlight 2 is one of the better Dungeon Crawler / Top-Down Action RPG available in the market.
The game takes place several years after the first game. The Alchemist, one of the three original heroes, gets corrupted by the Heart of Odrak, the monster that was the source of evil that plagued the small town of Torchlight. The Alchemist, wearing new power armor and wielding the Heart of Odrak, destroys the town and sets out on a mysterious quest that would, if not stopped, eventually disrupt the flow of nature and interrupt the delicate balance of power in the world.
+ Classic gameplay with nice little tweaks to fit the modern age of gaming
+ Colorful Graphics
+ Good level variation and environment design
+ New classes and a much more varied choices for pets
+ Much more complex skill tree: This is a good new addition from the first game. More complex and more specialized player builds are sure to come up.
+ Good re-playability: Lots of characters, lots of builds and lots of loot.
+ Multiplayer option that was absent in the first game
+ Better end game content
+ PC hardware friendly
+ Steam Workshop Support
+ Does not require 24 hour internet connection to play.
- Inferior voice acting: -Unlike Diablo II who had very good dialogue and memorable quotes.
- Inconsistent volume levels on dialogue: -background music can sometimes drown NPC voices.
- Confusing Story: -The story isn't immersive enough to keep you interested. Story is also very difficult to comprehend without paying close attention and references.
- Inconsistent Difficulty: -Normal is extremely easy that you will probably get bored the moment you get some of your more powerful skills/spells. Hard and Elite however are extremely difficult that it would make a frustrating experience to the casual gamer. I would recommend playing at Hard since I believe that getting a better challenge is much more acceptable than getting bored.
- Connecting to multiplayer can sometimes be difficult

This is gonna get complicated. Ok, let's get this out of the way: the game is quite good. I've played 75 hours, Steam tells me, and I did enjoy them - at least modded. Unmodded, the record would probably be more like 6. There are some great mods that hugely improve what's already a solid base. The reasons I can't recommend it, though, are complex.
First off, it's the feel. I do not like the game's aesthetic. It's very cartoonish and detracts from the feel I'd want. The story is forgettable at best, a confusing afterthought with no thought put into it whatsoever at worst, which I suppose you could expect from an ARPG, but... why? It's a spiritual successor to Diablo, right? Diablo 2 especially had a really interesting story. The setting was great, with Good and Evil both presented as Bad, some cool ideas and history, and even genuine characters! With personality! It was also very good-looking for the time, with a dark, interesting aesthetic, rather than the goofy one here that I personally dislike. Admittedly, that's a matter of taste, but this isn't meant to be objective. And the characters are just... nonexistant. The most interesting thing about the setting are a race that's left their bodies behind and are now just animated suits of armor, basically. Which are never really explored anyway.
Modded, though, I'd say it's worth the price except for one thing: the existence of Path of Exile.
In a vacuum? Sure, it's fun. $20 of fun, especially if you're looking for a time sink. Compared to Diablo 3? Yeah, certainly buy this. Compared to Path of Exile, which is free, incredibly innovative, gorgeous, dark, actually has an interesting story, and is simply more fun (in my opinion)? Why bother?
And, frankly, even today I'd call it as much fun as Diablo 2: Lord of Destruction at best, at least if you care much about story, atmosphere, or aesthetic. If you don't, and just want gameplay and can seriously ignore all that, go for it. If you do, well there's Path of Exile, or... so how much is Diablo 2: LoD now?
It should also be mentioned I rather resent the game because I preordered it due to the promise of the toolset, GUTS, being made available "soon" (and even, in one instance, "very soon") after release. Not relevent to you, dear reader, but it was not. And so my high-fallutin' plans fell to ruin as interest waned, until by the time it was released I was sitting by myself, eating ice cream, sobbing, and plotting my revenge. In addition, it requires you to make a Runic games account to use the online service. Not a huge deal, but the principle of the thing bugs me as it wasn't disclosed. So those are my biases against it. Grain of salt and all that. Hope it helped.

Before I start, even though I may have a small amount of hours, I have experienced enough of the game mechanics, as I already own SR:CW and SR:2020, and I know how these games work.
I have always had fun with this series in the past. And even now, I can enjoy myself playing Supreme Ruler Ultimate... for a while that is. I would love to support the developers at battlegoat. I really would. However this game has so many large issues that NEED fixing, yet since I discovered this game 2 months ago. Nothing has changed.
First off, the AI is much better than the previous titles. So I will praise Battlegoat for that. However the negatives outweigh the positives in this game.
The economy has always been a massive factor in Supreme Ruler games. And that is why it must be done right. But in this game, the economy is done poorly. Instead of fresh water (which is a necessity for any poputation) they replaced it with rubber. RUBBER! The only natural rubber resources are in 3rd world countries. Perhaps this is supposed to be balance. But it is the worst balancing attempt I have ever seen. Also, the bond system people requested to return from SR:2020, was not brought back despite the communtiy requesting it. (The bond system allowed you to manually take out new bonds or pay off debt) Now, this new debt system works in Supreme Ruler Cold War (not sure about 1936). But not this game. It is SO broken, that when a minister takes out a loan, it translates into free money! NO debt is added! Also, in the start dates, nobody has any debt (but I will not continue this complaint as the debt system does not work)
At times, you can suddenly start losing hundreds of millions a day for no reason. One day you just made 28 mil, and the next you start losing 100+ mil day after day until you take out a "free-money" loan.
I, personally think the research system in this game is better than any SR game, with the tech trees, and the 4 different tech races all in one (Race for the Bomb --> Space Race --> Internet Race (race to develop the internet) --> Race to Mars). And this also combines with the military system, by researching units models. However, the WW2 stuff was rushed during the development of SR1936, and it seems the devs made no effort trying to add to this. (Seriously?! "Tank Designs '39?") The world war 2 tech is extremely shallow in comparison to the time periods of the Cold War and 2020.
And WW2, what a disaster. The Chinese are an unstoppable, filthy rich, military superpower by the time the Japanese invade. (SERIOUSLY?! China wasnt even a country back then!) USSR is weak as hell, and gets annexed by Germany very fast. The USA never joins or trades with the allies, even after they declare war on the axis. Oh, and there is a global shortage of Industry goods. And Consumer Goods get random unexplained shortages as well.
However I can have fun with this game, the many errors ruin the experience and immersion.
Also, this game is FAR from finished. Most of the errors I have listed have been reported as I have seen. And the developers have said time and time again they will look into and fix these issues. However instead of fixing these issues, they took the game out of early access! This is obviously a BETA product and is not at all ready to be released. Yet they did release the game. And what a massive pile of♥♥♥♥♥♥it has turned out to be....

I have mixed feelings about this game. On the one hand it's clear that a lot of effort went into making the game a believable simulation, it plays and feels a lot like Hearts of Iron 3. You can play many nations during various points in history and there are a variety of scenarios and challenges.
On the other hand, the interface could use a lot of work, information is not efficiently communicated to the player and it's not filtered well so players can become overwhelmed with useless and trivial spam. The interface is also overwhelming, and lacks adequate tool tips. The game also has an extremely steep learning curve, and the tutorial isn't user friendly.
So this really awesome game that gets so much right has a prohibitive user interface system, and because of that most (like me) will likely only just scratch the surface.

Ultimate has some good things going for it.  Better optimization of speed for one, and it allows you to play on past WW2.  Despite some nice features, particularly the economy, the game falls flat on its face with game play issues and some terrible design flaws:
- China is extremely overpowered in 1936 and easily steamrolls Japan!  This is because China is united, not broken up into smaller controlling factions.  HOI3 did a good job, SRUltimate is a fail.
- Incompetent economic AI.  Warfare is fought by consuming military goods yet the AI builds almost no military goods.
- Russia is an economic mess and quickly folds.
- The German navy often wipes out the UK navy
- The military AI doesn't garrison Hongkong, India, or most of its Colonies.
- The French AI does not garrison the Magnot Line of fortifications.  The Germans just walk in.
The developers have done nothing to address these issues.  Until they do, it is a waste of money.

I'm not going to lie. I had high hopes for this game because I like what RWBY managed to start with. When they announced there would be a game, I thought it might actually be good.
... And then the game actually came out.
Visually, the game looks pretty similar to the animated series its based off of. It's essentially a 3D anime. It looks decent. Nothing too noteworthy and nothing that deserves too much scorn... Until something moves. The animations are... unnatural. I get that it's supposed to be anime, but the running animations by themselves are awful. Given that the animation in the source material isn't completely stellar either, I suppose it's possible to give this a pass, though I personally wouldn't.
Gameplaywise, there's not much to do. You just mash your normal attack and then press your counter button when you see a prompt. Heavy attacks and Ultimates aren't necessary. If you take damage, back off and wait for your Aura to regenerate. It's not a good system for what this game is, because it ultimately causes flow to break in almost every case. It's not fun, especially for players who enjoy aggressive play.
You gain EXP (which grows far too slowly, in my opinion) and you level up to get new skills... which aren't that useful.
Soundwise, the game is mediocre. Music is not too great, but not really grating either. The voicework is the same quality as the webseries, so that should be your judge on it.
Ultimately, the game feels like an overpriced fan game that feels like it's still in progress or, worse even, still a proof of concept. While this normally wouldn't be that big a deal, it has a price point of 19.99 USD and the creation was helped by Rooster Teeth does not help this game at all.
I could not recommend this game. It's too expensive for something far too dull. You're better off spending the 19.99 USD for something more fun or saving up for a better game of this genre.
