EDIT: New Review for 12/19/2015 @ 2:29 PM EST
The Game may still be a very early access version of a much greater dream but I highly reccomend it still for those who are fans of the show or new arrivals to Rooster Teeth. (Not much new has occurred except for new visuals and info from the dev team during the livestream. Review has not changed)
[PROS/CONS]
+Beautiful graphical design. very similar to the actual show's design which adds to the immersion
+Voice acting, while limited, is high quality. The girls, Ryan, and Joel all did fantastic work
+Diversity. Yes there may only be four levels and an equal number of Grimm types but let's remeber where the roots of this game were with one level and one type of enemy based on the older concept of the Beowolf.
+Online connectivity. practically seemless ability to connect to matches and lobbies and no lag if a player drops mid game
-limited worlds/levels. As stated before, there are only four levels and those four levels are also highly restricted to a linear path. Hopefully the Game Dev team at Rooster Teeth will expand upon the limits of the levels they have (Can be forgiven thanks to the announced forever fall map in early 2016)
-Skill menu is too small. The choices in what to spend your skill points are still in the early stages so there aren't many things to put your points towards as many are locked away behind challenges
-Combat needs to be worked on. This goes as the most urgent of gameplay updates to me. there is only a dodge, no blocking and enemies gain both invincibility and speed during attacks making it tough to counter if at all. The addition of Lock on is also a must as ranged attacks are a real crapshoot for if you're gonna hit
-Only four characters. Yes I know, Team RWBY is the lead group but I would love to see the ability to play as JNPR, CFVY or even non Beacon affilitated teams like SSSN.
-More grimm are needed. Bring on swarms of Nevermores or giant Deathstalkers
-No boss fights. I want the "Defend the control point" system to include a major boss at the end of each wave defense segment (4 waves of normal enemies/pack leaders and then one fight against a Giant Grimm or equivilant boss)
-Difficulty based lobbies. As of right now, difficulty adjusts to player count. i would love to see specific chosen difficulty (from easy or trainee, to Very hard or True Huntsman or something)
[RECENT CHANGES]
Two patches have come out since My review of the game. These mostly adress preformance issues and don't work towards the combat system or the skill menus of the characters but they do make the game feel a bit smoother. Which is always an added bonus. There are also more breakable objects to find xp orbs in and while I didn't ask for it I'll welcome it all the same.
[WHAT I WOULD WANT UPDATED IMMEDIATELY]
First off, Fix the ranged attacks, if nothing else. Blake's ranged attack is too quick and overpowered. Ruby can only do three shot bursts and count your lucky stars for hitting something all three shots in a row (Saving grace is her personal armor piercing upgrade which allows you to damage the tougher enemies like Borbatusks and Ursa). Yang fires shots with a cone shape animated blast but from what I've seen the bullets still fire in straight lines. Weiss' attack is too slow compared to everyone else in the ranged catagory.
Secondly, Lock on would be a godsend especially for challenge related skill use since it is very easy to miss an attack or do a combo straight out of the field of enemies.
Third. Larger level scale, the number of invisible walls are too damn high!
Still, after a week and only two patches the game in my opinion is worth the time and money, now if you excuse me, I have challenges to complete and skills to unlock. Happy hunting, students.

I just finished the early relese stuff with both Ruby and Yang and I can honestly say, this is definitely looking like it's shaped up for some high hopes from me. With the fluid combat system and skill tree possibilities, this could easily be a long and rewarding game. Though I know there's still a lot of development going on, here are a few things that I feel could be done better.
1. The running animations are fine, however, shen running downhill or from a ledge it seems to freeze the legs in an awkward "floating" position, sure it's comical, but it's a little distracting.
2. A more expansive skill tree that incorporates the character's "semblance" in a more refined manner would be fun and entertaining.
3. There seems to be quite a bit of connectivity issues, what with a consistent string of disconnects among players. Not sure if this has to do with the players just quitting, or if the servers themselveas are flawed.
4. The lack of character level save function that would make it a little more rewarding to play through the game.
That being said, I see a huge amount of pros that outweigh the cons of the game immensely. Here is a short list of things that I found to be enjoyable.
1. The difficulty is great, forcing you tou be a little more tactical and conservative with your aura as you are forced to dodge and fight as necessary to make it through the areas.
2. The incorporation of objectives gives a sense of purpose behind the reason you are fighting or fleeing the hordes of grimm and makes you prioritize your tasks based on what will or will not be most beneficial to the completion of your objectives.
3.The fluid and uninterrupted combat system allows you to meld your regular attacks with your specials exteremely well, making the fancy combos look all the more beautiful when you finish them with a big resounding "YANG".... er "BANG"
4.As much as I would like to see other characters such as Nora and Pyrrah, It's still nice to be able to choose whichever character you like as opposed to be forced into using a character that is unused, in the end it allows the player to choose the specific play style that they are most comfortable with.
5. The art comes together nicely and makes the world of RWBY come to life in the most colorful and intricate way. Being able to explore the places that you saw on the show as well as new places in the world of Remnant.
6. Although the running is a little glitched the animations are great, the hair and clothing moving fluidly with the character makes for an enjoyable p visual experience.
For those reasons and more, I am glad to have paid out for the early access and I am excited to watch the game as the development progresses.

I'd like to go into this review by stating I will be comparing this game heavily to my experiences in Terraria; also with the understanding that Terraria has had more time to add more content.
PROS
+Beautiful game. Never fails to catch the eye compared to other games of its type.
+Character customization is pretty good.
+Leveling system adds a feeling of progression.
+Great animations for bosses, enemies and characters.
+Price is right.
+Game has some sick potential.
+Personally I find the music reminiscent of Banjo-Kazooie which brings back many memories.
+I also love their take on the Dark element. If you like games with elemental aspects to it you may find it interesting.
CONS
-Game is incredibly easy, hard mode bosses are also barely a challenge. Though they were intended to be fought with a full party of highly-geared people, they are easily soloable with decent gear. They follow set patterns and only have about 3 moves each.
-The reward for anything considered to be challenging is minor. Loot from hard mode bosses can be incredibly underwhelming, at least as a Warrior.
-Very little variety of enemies.
-Unfortunately many of the pros are standard for today's games.
-Loot pools are incredibly shallow. Not much to see here.
-There is not much to create either.
-Very little reason to explore. You can likely find everything there is in a level within the first few steps. Treasure chests and hidden loot are incredibly worthless. They do not offer anything worthwhile.
-No special mechanics to use, like button systems, teleporters, levers, lights to turn on and off, etc. This cuts into homebuilding immensely.
-Biome restrictions on growing plants. An example of why this is bad is the Ghostlands, where there's seeds of different plants you can gather, but absolutely no reason to collect them because they can only grow there. In addition, the Ghostlands only show up for 2 days, then disappear for who knows how long. There is little reason to even grow them to farm materials because there are tons in the level, and they are used to make a somewhat useless potion.
-On that note Ghostlands is nice to look at, but there's almost no reason to go there beyond getting the achievement.
-Events are rare, and many are simply "kill X enemies." There is no reward for these events at all. Some of them have a higher chance of dropping the insanely-hard-to-come-by Energy Crystals, but that is all.
-Also on Energy Crystals, they are very hard to find, but needed for many end-game things. Many of these things aren't even worth creating, like the Warrior armor sets.
-Many end-game weapons are not worth creating or hunting for in general. Warrior gear seems created with the sole purpose of tanking, which is totally unnecessary in this game. One can easily kill anything with the Archer DPS sets.
-Your character is SLOW.
-Farming takes forever, farming titanium takes longer, and the amount of items you can create with what you've found is very small. Long farming with little pay-off is no bueno.
-Crafting UI is difficult to navigate.
-Currently you can only co-op by having someone on your friends list. What is also a problem is that anyone can loot any of your own chests where you store your goods and take everything you have, or even destroy everything you have. You can say that you need to only trust your friends, but there's a problem that if you invite a friend, and they have a less than trustworthy friend, that person can come into your world if your friend is there, and then do the damage. Doing multiplayer is VERY risky.
-Some things you find during events have no associated recipe to duplicate it. Things like blue lanterns you can only find a couple of. There should at least be a way to farm anything, or create replicas of what you find. This exists, but not for many things.
This game does have a charm. It really does, but what concerns me is how dead the forums are, and how little has actually been added to the game since its "early access" over a year ago. If content is going to be added that slowly then there is going to be very little reason to stick around.
-Money is near useless.
This game is very fun and I would definitely recommend it to anyone. So far I think the best part is the multiplayer and weapons options.

I have been a fan of fighting games most of my life, and especially have some fond memories of Tekken 3 on playstation.
I am a tad bias thus but even when I look at the comparison objectively, this feels like a replacement for all fighting games.
To start, let me give my opinion on other fighting games I played:
- I love comics and especially Batman, but while injustice has more lore to put its story in, the gameplay and controls often feels frustrating.
- Dead or Alive took a giant chunk of my free time, I mean, boobs and bikinis, but it wesn't on the same technical combat level as a tekken or mortal kombat, but it was still superbly fun.
- Speaking of Mortal Kombat, Mortal Kombat X was great, it kinda felt like the Dark Souls of fighting games, even on Easy, but that was mostly thanks to the same control limitations that injustice suffered from.
- Street fighter was... well... I didn't enjoy it as much as the rest, but I saw the appeal and cannot fault anyone for liking it.
Tekken 7 ticks all the boxes positively in one way or another but is not without it's faults too.
Pros:
- Tekken 7 is one of few games that is released completely at launch and doesn't suffer from massive technical issues.
- The animations make the martial arts come to life.
- The animations are smoothe due to the game being very well optomised.
- The controls are so easy to learn that new-comers can face regulars after a few short practice matches. If you aren't sure how something works or what it does, play the campaign and visit the practice match section to view your fighter's move set in action and see the effects of a chosen combo in motion.
- The story is simple and short and can be used to easily get the groove of the game, and since very few fighting games really do stories well, that's a plus.
- Characters can be customised to a large extent, and some of the customisable options include previous outfits. Don't like Jin's padded getup? Put the flame pants back and take that shirt off for the classic look.
- All the cutscenes from the first tekken game through to the latest, including Tag Tournament. can be unlocked and viewed in case you ever felt you missed something.
- Overall It just feels more polished than most gmaes, especially fighting games, out there.
- I linked up my two wireless xbox controllers to my PC, invited my uncle (whom is also my long time tekken rival) over, and had my♥♥♥♥♥solidly handed to be until midnight, fun and frustration that can happily put any friendship to the test.
Cons:
- As with any tekken, your boss characters feel a tad gimmicky and love to spam unblockable attacks when reaching higher ranked matches in arcade or endless treasure hunt mode.
- The character episodes are basically one match played with each character to unlock their ending, which used to be something you earned after several grueling matches in arcade.
- It's the first tekken to come to PC, why did it take so long Banda Namco?!
- There is no "Send help, I am addicted and can't seperate from the game long enough to sleep, eat or go to work" button.
Short Verdict:
- If you enjoy fighting games, then why are you reading and not trying to win the King of Iron Fist Tournament?! Buy the game, its a knock-out!

Okay so, first off - this game has been getting a supreme amount of hate. Yes the Uplay thing is annoying and the in game store is unnecessary, and yes, launching a DLC with the game is a weak move. Well I just finished the game and I have to call out all the haters who said they loved Stick of Truth but hated this game. TFBW is Stick of Truth + - it has everything that made that game great, and more. Yes it recycles several elements, but I don't think that's necessarily a bad thing. I plays similarly to the first game with a couple of major improvements - the combat system is more strategic for one. Think the first game plus Final Fanatsy Tactics. There are classes to deal with and you can actually spec your character in a few different ways.
Stick of Truth was very much a game for South Park superfans and the sequel is the same exact approach. There are great call backs to the last few seasons of the show. Whereas the first game had about 15 seasons to work with, this one is more centered on the last 5 or so. The boss battles are challenging and there is a puzzle element to it that actually made me think a few times.
Last good point - it's bigger than the first. More playable characters, more special moves, and more♥♥♥♥♥♥to collect. If you didn't like Stick of Truth, or generally hate South Park, then obviously don't bother with this game. Otherwise, get it and love it.
$60 felt pricey, but I was too excited to wait for a sale.

The maps are quite large there are countless dungeons that can be revisted all kinds of weapons with equippment sets and socketable items. I like the feature of having a Pet (my outlander has a headcrab which is sick) and how the pet actually can effect gameplay especially if you use those fish that can morph them into other creatures and or give them boosts. Difficulty is perfect for each setting and I love the fact that there is a hardcore mode. The game is fantastic and I fully recommend it. Overall, vastly better when compared to other block games and I feels its worth everyone's time. Built on the PC where it runs smooth and looks good, the characters might make some individuals think its for a younger audience but its not much different than many other cartoonish games. It is definitely worth play for all ages whether you play with your kids or play with your gaming buddies.  Game play is simple to begin with but as you spend time progressing there is much more depth, bosses, tesseract dungeons, events, and then hard mode bosses.  If I were to grade the game overall, I'd give it a 'A++'. It has many positive reviews for a reason, try this game out and actually spend some hours and you will be happy about the purchase.
The game plays smoothly, but like most games on the PC you will rebind keys to your preference.  I suggest removing the lock on target and scatter objects. Island map size changes depending on the random gen so don't be surprised to see smaller maps, or high peak maps, or heavy jungle maps. Character movement speed is an issue for a lot of people but if one desires you can increase that speed. Personally I find the ones with the most speed issues are people with the least patience. The game is colorful and cartoony, but overall it looks very polished. Water was recently added and needs more fine tuning, but is a fun mechanic and adds character to the maps. If you die, you get sent back to the starting pad and you lose some coin though coins have proved to be not needed so far for me.  The end game leaves it open for more content and hopefully this continues to develop an even better game.
Building is great, allows you to see where you place your blocks and a fairly sizable reach to drop them quickly.  You can also walk and place blocks if you time it right.  There are many kinds of building materials through out the game and its always fun to see how your base expands and changes as you reach or loot new materials. There isn't any need to quarry blocks unless your building massive structures, you usually find enough just with regular resource gathering and looting and in some events.
There are three class and that determines your weapon use and end level armor choices.  In beyond the initial starting gear and end level, you are free to mix and match armor depending on what you want to do with your character.  Melee combat seems rough at first to the unfocused, but the warrior can really shine as he adds more health, battle shouts, abilities, and multistrike.  The thrown weapons available to be used by the warrior seem out of place as do the daggers on the ranger.  Flying creatures are easy to take down once you grasp the warrior and I see no reason to stay in melee for a ranger.  The ranger might be the best for newbies but also ends up with a few great builds end game.  The mage also can start slow, but once spells are acquired and mana recovery sorted out, it can be a lot of fun and comparable.  Late game more weapons and damage types are available as well and provide the mage with the needed tools depending on the fight.  Don't give up on a class to early, as they are all fun and have more options if you have the patience to level them.
Multiplayer works great if you have a decent box.  Load time seems a little long but its probably 30 seconds tops and just seems longer with the spinning portal.  A little patience goes a long way.  I have played with my son and also with a few friends, the game adds a lot more with friends.  You do currently have to stay on the same island map as the other players, but the fix for that is supposedly in the works.  If you are a focused team that works well together and has patience then staying on the same island map is only a small annoyance.  There is usually coordinated resource gathering before returning to base.
In conclusion, if you only play this game for less than 10 hours and have zero patience, you probably won't like it.  If you actually give it a shot, build your base, level and progress, you are going to have lots of fun and worth whatever you pay for it.

I've just completed Brutal Legend and it's a wonderful thing. Anyone who worships at the altar of metal will be smiling all the way through - it's worth going back to the forges just because it's Ozzy in there - and the combination of the stylised artwork and impressive soundtrack mean that sometimes you want to drive around just for the sheer hell of it. And because EA (yes, that does say EA, and this may well be the last original game they've produced) went for art over photorealism it's aged well, very well indeed.
However it's not without it's downsides, which are all gameplay related and could easily ruin it were it not for everything else being so much fun. The hand to hand combat is fairly basic, the controls are cluncky, and the longer base capturing missions in the campaign can get very frustrating - although the last one does a bit to make up for this with the usual RTS trick of giving you all your toys and toning down the difficulty a little. The side missions are fairly standard open-world fare, but come in only four flavours, and the upgrade progression could be better balanced - in the later game I frequently went to the forge only to decide I was happy with what I had whilst waiting for some killer new upgrade that never came.
So to be honest, if this was a generic open-worlder, and bear in mind this is open-world 2009-style, it would be mediocre at best, but it's not. It's a heartfelt tribute to the gods of metal. In most open-worlder's the plot is subservient to the game, but in Brutal Legend the plot rules and however frustrating some of the missions get you'll keep going because you'll want to see the next cut sequence - and these are beautiful things.
You will smile, you will laugh, and you may well shed a tear, you will hear some of the greatest music ever made - and you will rock on.

This is the first review I have ever written, because this game is getting such a bad shake.
Yes, Uplay sucks. If you don't like it enough to put up with the tiny inconvenience of having it take 5 seconds to load in the background, don't buy this game.
I never played Stick of Truth, so thanks to the combo deal I was able to play both in quick succession. Whoever says Stick is the better game is wearing a very large pair of nostalgia glasses.
FBW has a better, more interesting combat system. You can have up to three additional party members, and the number of potential party members is much greater than in Stick of Truth. The grid combat keeps things interesting and fresh (warning: It's not Final Fantasy Tactics, but it's good enough). There are a number of boss fights with interesting special mechanics ("gimmicks" for the jaded) that keep things challenging.
You have much more ability to mix and match your character's abilities. You can only have four equipped at once, but there are over a dozen to choose from by the end of the game, so if you are so inclined you can never get bored with combinations. If you feel like roleplaying and sticking with a character concept, you can do that too.
The side quests and collections were similar to those of SoT. If you don't like fetch or collectible quests, they're easy enough to ignore.
The button pressing/mashing, which I found to be extremely annoying in SoT, was much easier to handle in FBW (I play on a keyboard and am not very dexterous). If you want a challenge with those, though, you can still play the optional Toilet minigame.
I found the story much more interesting than Stick of Truth. The humor was more subtle, too (though don't worry, it is a South Park game and there is still plenty of gross out humor). It also seemed a good bit longer.
My only complaint is that I wish there were more genuine choices in the game, which SoT did better.
All in all, I would say that FBW is a fun game on its own merits, and superior to Stick of Truth in almost every way. I probably overpayed for $60, but getting it on sale is worth it.

This is probably my favorite game of all time. It is a relatively short game, but the pacing of the game means you are encouraged to explore and interact with your surroundings (necessary if you want to get all of the achievements). The storyline is compelling, taking full advantage of the whimsical world you play through. The characters speak a made up language which I personally feel only enhances the experience as it means you're forced to pay attention to what the characters are doing, how they interact with others, and the tone of their voices. The game takes you through a series of environmental puzzles which are generally rather simplistic in solution, but the control mechanisms are challenging enough to keep it interesting. As soon as you've mastered the controls in one area you move on to another puzzle which introduces new mechanics.
This game is an emotional journey- you encounter situations which bring the player in touch with feelings such as playfulness, fear, jealousy, joy, and grief.  I personally think that by making the controls so challenging and making them operate in such a way that you really have to pay attention to what you're doing, it makes the storyline all the more powerful and the ending that much more poignant. You don't always realize what you have and how much you rely on it until it is gone, and this game captures that experience beautifully.
Basically, brace yourself for some major feels.

Kingdoms of Amalur is a good game.
It took the direction Fable was suppose to take, and it did it quite well.
The game itself feels like a cousin of Fable, but with more linear story.
Storytelling itself in the game is pleasant. Main story unfolds gradually, with little
twists and turns along the way. That being said main story is the only good quest line

you'll be doing the same thing few times to complete the whole thing. One thing that
really disappoints me about the story part of this game is how unmemorable the characters
are, it's the lack of special features  of the charaters that really blends them all together
and in my opinion, it would've helped the story immensly if there was more variety with the
character skins, and models. (Even humanoid bosses look just the same as any NPC of that race)
Main story line is quite lengthy, and it does offer good replayability value, so even if you were to
skip the side missions entirely, the game still gives you enough for its price.
Dynamic and entertaining combat system which feels rewarding from the very start,
allowing you to execute combo moves with quite a few different weapon kinds, each
kind having their own moveset. It also handles the melee mix with spellcasting very naturally.
Class system is great, it lets you go a standard path of a Warrior, a Mage, or a Rogue, but also
mix two, or even all three together to make some unique classes, and level them up.
If you're a Fable fan, you will most likely find this game enjoyable.

The game isn't bad, but I don't recommend it. Overall, it didn't 'wow' me and I just felt like it wasn't worth my time. The look and feel of the game makes me perceive it as a console port, which has been designed for a younger audience. Gameplay is simple in all aspects, there is not much depth to be found here. If I were to grade the game overall, I'd give it a 'D+'. It passes as a game, but I was surprised it got so many positive reviews.
Gameplay:
The game plays smoothly, but I had to rebind a lot of keys to make it feel right for PC. The maps are very small, even when you select the option to have the largest world sizes. Character movement speed is probably one of the biggest issues for me. Your character just moves slow. There is  a character stat tied to movement speed, but dumping points into it didn't seem to affect anything. I can't help but feel like the game's movement speed is slow by design: to trick the player into coping with the small size of each world. The game is colorful and cartoony, but overall it looks polished. Water is strange, you can't swim but it seems like jumping while underwater gives you more jump height. It's a bandaid fix, being in deep water is a bad time. You can teleport back to the starting pad of each map, which helps. If you die, you get sent back to the starting pad and you lose some coin.
Building:
When considering this game for purchase, I read a lot of comments comparing it to minecraft. After playing it, I would say that it is closer to Trove. The build system was usable, but you are placing blocks one at a time. My gripe with building in this game is: the block placement preview mechanism. In minecraft, block placement is more contextual and allows you to build faster because you can walk while placing blocks in an effective manor. In Portal Knights the game tries to predict where you want to place your block and gives you a preview of where the block will go when you click. This seems like a feature to make building more practical for someone using a controller, but it makes building tedious with mouse & keyboard. Gathering materials is a real grind. In minecraft, you end up with a ton of building materials just by mining and exploring. In Portal Knights, if you want to build a structure out of stone bricks you have to go quarry dirt and stone.
Classes & Combat:
There are 3 classes and essentially your class choice has 2 major affects: natural stat gain and weapons. The classes are unbalanced, with ranger being superior. The ranger class can hit enemies from a distance for massive damage. The warrior class is restricted to melee combat. Melee is a bad time, it's hard to hit enemies (especially when they are in the air). You also have to actively dodge, or you'll take hits. Warriors are tankier to curb the additional damage they take from being up close and they get throwing weapons to compensate for the inability to handle airborn enemies, but these throwning weapons are consume-on-use. This feels like another bandaid. The mage class is dogged by a damage-type system. Your magic weapons deal a damage type (such as fire or earth). The enemies have a weakness to a specific type of magic and a resistance to a specific type. Overall, the mage class doesn't hit as hard as the ranger.
Multiplayer:
I bought this game to play with 2 friends, but I spent a few hours playing solo to figure out what class I wanted to commit to. This was a mistake. If you play this alone, the game seems alright; Portal Knights didn't impress me, but I figured I could use it to hang out with my buddies and have a good time. Multiplayer is where the game-breaking flaws show themselves. Loading screen time is attrocious. It just takes forever, even on good computers with the game installed on SSD's. Every time you go through a portal you have to wait. The worst part is: if one person goes through a portal, it drags EVERYONE with them. These two flaws make multiplayer unbearable. You have limited inventory space and need to use crafting tables to upgrade your items. You also need materials from different worlds. The worlds are small and only contain specific crafting mats. The logical thing to do would be to establish a basecamp on one of the worlds so you can make chests and have your crafting tables all placed down. However, this strategy becomes a logistical nightmare when you can't return to base without dragging everyone along with you through a long loadscreen. If you wanted to craft a new weapon: your team has to endure a load screen, then wait for you to craft it (crafting is not instant on may of these items, it can take minutes), then once you are finished your team has to endure another loadscreen to get back to the map where you were progressing. The variety of different crafting materials makes it impractical to mule your crafting tables along with you, your inventory will fill up.
Conclusion:
To be fair, I only played the game for about 9 hours. I sampled each class, then settled on mage. I played for a few hours by myself before joining up with 2 friends who were playing warrior and ranger. I got a good feel for how the game plays, but I gave up on it before getting too far. I am writing this review because I don't recommend the game, and there aren't enough reviews that fall in line with my opinion. I would say: if you want to pick up Portal Knights to play with friends, buyer beware.

There's a lot to like here.  The graphics and audio are well-done, the whole heavy metal asthetic is burned into the DNA of the game and its world and there are lots of great heavy metal tracks to unlock from a really well-chosen selection of big-name bands and more obscure (but excellent) underground bands.  The characters are okay, not up to the typical Double Fine standard of memorability or amusingness, but most voice acting is great (the worst being the guest voices from rock icons, but hey, it's authentic) and it's mostly lighthearted enough.
What really fails is the game itself.  There's some moderate fun to be had driving around and exploring. but the riff-based 'magic' system isn't as fun as it should be, and the pivotal epic battles are designed as (bizarrely) a sort of real-time strategy game that is clumsy, confusing, and ultimately so damn poor.  The story - a fairly generic tale of good, evil, betrayal and redemption - is merely a skeleton to dress the rest of the game upon, and not enough to keep me playing through an indefinite number of these rough spots.

One of the most exciting and dynamic new methods of keeping a game interesting and relevant that i've seen in modern times. No matter how much i do, accomplish, or unlock in the game, i always find myself coming back to check. Sometimes merely out of curiousity, wondering such things as "Is there a new patch or announcement yet?" "Did they finally improve their netcode?" "Have they solved the 'crashing to windows' problem?" "Have the frames per second finally been improved?" "Have they balanced the audio so that i can hear what's going on in story mode, rather than having to play through it with subtitles on?"
They rarely actually release any patches or fixes, but when they do, it's an entirely new, exciting situation. Will it actually make any improvements? Will it make the game run worse and or wipe all  the progress that you've made so far? Will you be one of the many affected, or will you be one of the lucky few who didn't open steam that day until after the "patch" was pulled down? So much drama and excitement!
There are also many opportunities to engage with other players via this game! After playing (or attempting to play!) this game for a while, you can go to the reviews on the store page, or the comments below any of the announcements regarding the game, patches, etc., to voice your thoughts alongside like-minded gamers!

Very complex for players who want a real challenge in real time strategy games, especially in economics, production, and resource management. Its game mechanics are somewhat fixed. There are a few problems however. Atleast the game speed does not lag whenever 3 years pass.
The AI need some fixing when it comes to combat. For example, South Korea will take over North Korea easily, and then invade China. China will have hundreds of units lying around in forts and cities while Manchuria is completely overrun by probably 30-40 inferior South Korean military units.
However, complaints of people saying the AI are not historically accurate are irrelevant. A main component for this game, and something I personally enjoy, is its alternate history options that YOU can control. When you can turn Haiti, a now poor nation with 80% of its population under the poverty line, into a massive superpower that owns Florida, all of Central America, the Carribean, Northern South America, and parts of Europe, you know this game can be fun. This game has unlimited opportunities. These opportunities can range from you being literally any nation in a time period's existence and doing whatever you want with it, wheither it be an expansionist, fascist Uganda, economic superpower of North Korea, or the USSR Part two, this game can provide for that.
Do not expect this game to be a pulse pounding, call of duty action game, because it isn't. This is a hyper-realistic game on steroids. All factors need to be taken into account for in your economy.
Please remember that BattleGoats Studios is still working on this game to make it better for the players. This may have some annoying bugs, but they are expected to be fixed throughout the patches in the game.

This game is so deep and complex that it took me over 200 hours to figure out some huge flaws with it. It is a good game, but for the most part I do not recommend it, and here is why.
Lack of a real manual. The in game tutorial is badly done, and the manual they give you doesnt explain much. This game is complex and needs to come with at least a 100 page manual. Remember the manual in civ 3? 220 pages? I think the manual with this game is about 50 pages. And this game is more "complex". So you are flying in the dark. Your biggest friends will be forums and google, which don't really address the issues because well... Nobody knows. There is a lot of "Lets try this and see what works". This is the biggest problem with the game. Too much is an unknown. Even after 200 hours. Don't get me wrong. I now know how to play this game to a large degree. But am still unsure about a lot of other things. I have played very hard games with steep learning curves. The learning curve of this game is not the issue. I mean the game doesnt even have a tech tree. WTF! Their are 800 techs and there is no tech tree? Not even on google. It doesnt exist as of 11-12-2014. Their are some little player done tech trees but they dont address most of the techs before age 2020.
I give it a 6/10. This game would be a 8/10 if there was a REAL manual. So infuriating.
Oh yea, I got a response from someone from Battlegoat Studios about why there is no tech tree. His answer is that it would be hard to make..... So there is that....

This is the last time I will purchase from this developer.  I want to support games like this ...because it plays so close to what I like in games.
My preference is sandbox mode and this game is such a non event when you play this setting.  How can I interact with a virtual world that does little if anything to connect me to it.
PRO: This will satisfy your desire to conquer the world.


CONS: Same thing lacking here as in other Supreme Ruler games, there is nothing that invests you into this virtual world.
If you are waiting for your virtual world to make sense, not going to happen.  You are just going to wait until China or Russia attack (ie. If you are a NATO country) and then decide how long before you counter attack.  The AI will make you walk to Moscow or Bejing because it won't know to accept a peace deal at its borders once you have removed them from occupying a foriegn territory.
Esentially the same game you have already in your Steam account .. just some different paint.

Message to developer - Please work on how the AI (other countries) work against or with you.  Never does a player feel connected to this world.  Perhaps more in game messages, maybe International news or something that highlights what is occuring in the virtual world.  Human players are way too disconnected from the rest of the AI to feel connected to the experience that we are ALL hoping for.  How are the players suppose to get a sense of the international community?  Everything a player does is reactive to the virtual environement with no real chance to be proactive.  It would be nice to know that China is focusing on certain countries or regions ... maybe I send over an aircraft carrier to send a message that may influence China ... one way or another.
If you develop any other games (and I hope you do) I will be waiting for reviews before supporting it.
I have bought them all ... but no more.
T.
PS. I am a big fan, I just want more of an experience.

I played this game in Early Access and initially did not recommend the game. I've played it for about 2-3 hours at release, and I will still not recommend the game. It is an enjoyable game for about 15-20 hours, but it lacks the longevity needed to keep players playing... and honestly, I feel bad now for putting so many hours into it. May it change later? Maybe, but the reasons for still not recommending the game are:
1. 90% of the equipment for each class, is junk. My Ranger, is still using primarily Warrior gear, as it is just overall better than most of the Ranger gear. All equipment desperately needs Critical Chance and Critical Damage, otherwise it WILL be considered junk, compared to items that do have it, because the faster you kill something, the less time the enemies have to hit you. And as the enemies at LV 30 can easily 1-2 hit kill my Warrior OR Ranger, killing them faster is the best way to go. The best armor pieces and best weapons have Critical Chance and Critical Damage, and thus that is the items I use.
2. Cannot grow plants in different biomes, and for some reason some plants won't even grow in their own biome. I have made farms in every biome, and oddly enough two types of space mushrooms won't grow in the space biome. I'd understand if a plant grew faster in its native biome and slower in another biome, OR you could craft magical soil to allow growing a plant in a different biome, but you can't. And as every new type of potion requires specific plants from specific biomes, it is a real chore setting up the farms, checking back on the farms, and remembering where your farms are... and its just an overall grindy, farmy, chore.
3. Despite changing the amount of ore needed to make bars, is a nice change and all, but still the number of bars needed to craft items is still too high. 6-8 bars, is 60-80 ore, which takes a significant amount of time to gather... just for 1 item to be crafted. And while we are on the topic of crafting... why does it require metal bars to craft leather (Rangers) or cloth armor (Mages)?
4. Most Quests give terrible rewards, except for those quests that give you an Energy Crystal. Honestly, all quests should give an Energy Crystal, as these only drop occasionally from sarcophagi in the area you get to via the T'Serract. Additionally, the Events that occur, most of them don't give decent rewards. Some that have you destroy a specific thing, will grant Energy Crystals or Astral Hearts, but ones that have you kill X number of creatures often give nothing for completing them... and only occasionally drop a Trophy. Most quests and events are just not worth doing.
5. The end area of the game after defeating the 3rd boss, felt like a slap in the face. This place has like 5-6 quests, but you have to defeat the boss to get here, which is no small feat. So by the time you get here, there won't be a reason to do these quests, so it all feels anticlimatic and a huge let down. In Early Access, the area you go to is called The Gate, and it has the single most, massive Gate you've ever seen and after the final game launched, the gate has crumbled and you teleport to this end area, that just doesn't feel like a good reward either. But the biggest irritant about it is that you see Chilis growing here... Chilis can only grow in the volcanic biomes, but for some reason is growing here... and it drives me crazy that you can't even collect the chilis growing here either. I know I know, wierd thing to get angry about, but it does make me angry.
6. There just isn't anything to do when you hit LV 30. Unless you have a lot of friends who play frequently, there just isn't any point to playing once hitting LV 30. The gear isn't that great, and the only challenges remaining are the T'Serract, to get Energy Crystals... or Hard Mode bosses, that just cannot be soloed; I can solo every other kind of boss on my Ranger, but they one-shot my Ranger with the best gear available.
7. I built a big fortress, with massive underground vaults filled with at least 30 chests per floor, with 3 floors (so 90 chests total), expecting that I'd need it when the final game launched. I was wrong. Most of the stuff will never get used and it is in some ways easier to make a big fortress here than in Minecraft, but at the same time, it is also harder to do so as well, as so many things are recipe-locked, and without the recipe learned, you will have trouble building and furnishing your fortress as you want.
Theres a bunch of other things that I'd like fixed, but until the above things get addressed, I don't see any value in mentioning them.
If you have any questions, shoot them my way and I'll answer them to the best of my ability. I have after all, played the game extensively.

This game has pretty much everything a great game should; great music, fun gameplay, interesting characters. However where the game falls short is the campaign. You see, Brutal Legend was designed with the multiplayer component in mind (despite having broken matchmaking), which means the focus of the game is the stage battle system. The story mode clocks in at four hours, is poorely designed and rushed, littered with unlockables, but otherwise worth playing through atleast once.
What many players seemed to want was just the hack and slash gameplay, but didn't like the stage battles which were essentially just giving you allies and resource points to fight over. Ironically, everybody loves Dawn of War and Company of Heroes yet didn't like Brutal Legend just because you are on the feild yourself. It's litterally the same concept: Grab the resource points and balance between tech advancements and troop production. In fact, DoW2's MP can be thought of as the RTS only version of Brutal Legends MP
Gameplay wise, amazing. Your Stage has defenses and produces troops, and can level up to three. You use your troops to clear Fan Geysers so that you can play a magical guitar solo to build a gathering structure on it. You need to have more of these than your enemy to win; as you will get more resources and thus have more troops of better quality. Your goal is to destroy the enemy Stage with your troopers. Map control is required.
Another strange thing is the cars, each character has one, but can also fly. It's rare to need such a device if you can fly. It's mostly only for the campaign.

What do you do when you are on the game’s store page? You buy it, install it and play it. Once you initiate the third process, you won’t need convincing on keeping on doing it.  The game is entertaining, detailed even where you don’t expect it, the npc’s are loveable, the open world big enough to lose yourself in it. What was a surprise that made me skeptic at first but turned out to be another enjoyable feature was the “casual” RTS, where from the protagonists third person that turns into a flying demon you command your various troops to take out towers and ultimately, the stage, by implementing your tactics. I wasn’t a fan of metal when I started playing this game, but because of it, I have all the metal songs from this game in my playlist.
You are Eddie Riggs, the best roadie in the world, which means you are the one responsible for the stage glamour, but no one will know it. As things get out of control, you find your way into the past, into the age of metal, where people are used against their will by a tyrant which servers Doviculus, the demon responsible for the taint that corrupts all what metal stands for. Since Eddie is good at making things work and gives people purpose, a revolution is started. There will be many great characters that you’ll meet along the way, many of which are based on real life metal stars.  There is always a romantic sub plot where you might find some clichés, but they are the best kind. Since the story takes place in an open world, you can expect a lot of variation in locations and types of allies and enemies.
There are a lot of sidequests and neither are the fetch types, more like ambushing, hunting, racing, keeping the bikers away while a headbanger charms a girl, shooting from a ramped car, placing markers for the guy with no aim to shoot rockets, that sort of stuff. Once I had to clear a cave so that a family of bats could go back in, which earned me kisses and an apology from a bat for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ on my head. There are solos to find, serpents to free and legends to learn. It’s the kind of open world that never fills empty.
In the RTS missions, you’ll use your solos and your cunning, for doing things like melting your enemies faces and send the invisible forces to attack the stage while the shooters and the pyromans defend your stage.  The Deuce(your car) is fun to drive, but the controls may prove to be difficult at first, which makes it even more fun.  You can raise relics, which include Motorfoges, where you will  upgrade your attack, the Deuce, change outfits, enhance your weapons and buy stones to place on a mountain.
If you’re a fan of the RTS system in the game, you can expect a good time in the multiplayer.
I found many of my favorite gaming moments here. While people find some faults in this game, everyone finds the way to play this game and others don’t recognize those faults at all. The end was emotional satisfying, sneaking away, yet finding yourself surrounded by friends that simply ask you to never forget them at which point you’d likely say that you won’t, then driving into the sunset while your girlfriend watches smiling and dropping a tear.  You can free roam afterwards to see what more this game has to offer. I’m not done with it and I don’t want to, not until I hear of a sequel at least. In the end, I find Brütal Legend to do everything right.

Generally, I would say that I am the least qualified to write a review about a fighting game; I'm terrible at them. However I will say that during the last year I've had quite a bit of time improving my humble skills with some of the best fighting games I've seen, one of which was 'KILLER INSTINCT' for the Xbox One. When 'Mortal Kombat' (or MK9 as it's otherwise known as) came out, I jumped at the chance to try what looked like quite a casual, non competitive fighting game.
I was not dissapointed. Now MKX is here, I will contrasting it heavily with the last game since It remains the only MK game I've played before this.
I will also not attempt to comment on the actual fighting mechanics, as figthing game novice, I dont feel as though I would do the system justice if I attempt to explain more than the bare mechanics.
Now onto the review:
The story is both predictably good, and a little dissapointing. The original had, what is unaquivically the best Story in any fighting game ever, by a country mile!. It was well acted, and the plot was fantastic. It really felt like the (Good) MK movie we never got. Even better; the campaign length clocked in at around 9 hours, longer than some normal AAA games out there. This time however, we're looking more around 4 hours, which is a dissapointment.
Netherrealms seems to have taken a "Quality over quantity" approach here, and I would be fine with that, if the original had dragged on and represented just something we had to slog through to unlock the extra characters. This wasn't the case however, and I really would have appriciated a longer story. The acting is about on par with MK9. One definate improvement I noticed was Mo-cap in the cutscenes. Great stuff. All in all; a great effort.
Since the game's story is set around 25 years after the original, we see new faces filling up at least half of the roster. These include 'Cassie Cage', Johny and Sonya's daughter, 'Jacqui Briggs', the daughter of the roided up cyborg JAX; and a few others.
All in all, the new characters are great, and feel right at home with the grizzled ancients of the other games. One thing I dislike however is that the new characters seem to be slightly OP compared with the older roster and, at least in my experience, are easier to handle than the old guard.
There are 25 combatants in total, with one locked behind a paywall; and 4 DLC characters, one of which is the OG badass Predator!
Fighting games are best enjoyed against a human opponent, and solo play is secondary if you're able to find a sparring partner. MKX is full of nice touches that cater to competitive-level players, like comprehensive frame data, the option to include diagonals in your move inputs, and button checks (with push-to-set controls) at the character select screen. But there aren't enough guidelines to help bridge the gap between experts and newcomers. The few tutorials are sparse, with almost zero advice on how to properly utilize each variation; there also aren't any trials to teach players which combos should be their bread-and-butter attack strings.
On the other hand, unlike Injustice, every fighter uses the environment in the same mildly advantageous way, making them just impactful enough to add excitement to a match without swinging it grossly in someone's favor. The same goes for the slow-mo internal organ destruction of the returning X-Ray attacks, which offer a satisfying comeback factor without being automatic 'I win' barrages. All of this crazy gruesome gore is wrapped up in a complete (Except Goro -.- )
fighting package which anyone who has an interest in the genre should pick up.
Conclusion:
• Great Story
• Great combat system
• Krypt is great fun
• Faction system is under represented, and the same people win everytime (Damn you Lin Kuei for being too awsome).
• Kombat Towers are boring
• Bad business practices and money grubbing (Goro, and Fatality Tokens)
If you're not willing to make the commitment to perfecting a fighter and going beyond learning the basics, this game will prove to be a absolute joy to play. The life expectancy of the game however, can be put into question.

Decent game but very unbalanced.  As the description said, it's a co-op hack'n'slash and I think therein is its problem: the repetitive predictability of hacking and slashing.  It reminds me of Dynasty Warriors (although minion enemies are way more active/aggressive) where the gameplay emphasis is overwhelmingly on button-mashing melee with the occasional spice of abilities thrown in.  In fact, the (only?) fastest way to recharge your resource to activate those abilities is to score sequential basic weapon hits without taking a hit in return.  In no way does this game feel like the spirit of the online show RWBY.  In the show, teammates constantly display new and inventive tactics where cooperative synergy is the dominant force and the finishing moves are mind-blowing uber powerful one-off abilities.  In Grimm Eclipse, however, the abilities play a minor role versus the efficacy of basic melee, are embarrassingly underpowered compared to the "real" characters' inventive potency, don't recharge fast enough, are prone to missing or having suboptimal effect if the enemies aren't lined up 'just so', and one player's abilities have no beneficial synergistic effect with any other player's.  The only coop effect I could perceive was that when my character was fighting (in melee of course) near to another, our individual melee hits seemed to do a lot more damage, much like, again, Dynasty Warriors coop mode.  If this game is to do proper homage to the show, the abilities need a massive beefing up with greater complexity, frequency of availability, ease of use, and team-oriented effects.
Some good things:
1, the music.  (Thank you for adding a sound fx volume slider after I wrote this review, but why are character fighting voices applied to sound fx instead of, um... Voices slider?)
2, Although the mayhem of melee feels like button mashing, there is a bit of strategy in it in that you can and should use jump and dodge and, by throwing those into your rotations, your chain attacks change up a little bit.  (I'd like to see more of that.)
3, Every character has their niche and feels distinct, even when doing basic melee animations.  For instance, Yang is great at keeping enemies occupied by kiting them with right-click cone effects, compared to Weiss who can pick off enemies with long range attacks.
4, The MOBA style levelling up works.  Personally, I'd prefer a persistent character whom I could take back to the starting chapter with a friend and power through.  (Think 'The Legend of Korra'.)  But with the MOBA style you're encouraged to stick with your team and help each other keep leveling up and progressing.  You quickly become attached to the power/improvements your character gains.
5, It's a great coop game.  Very easy to pick up and play, no team killing shenanigans, no server/lobby lag, people can drop and join at any point, and the enemy difficulty scales to how many players are in the party.  Oh, and a party can consist of four Blakes, if you really all want to have kitty ears.
Some little things I'd recommend improving:
1, I already said the abilities.
2, Please do balance the volumes.
3, I think it only makes sense to have the crate experience spheres contribute to group xp just like the artifact chess pieces.  No point in making people fight over crates or prioritize them over enemies.
4, Wave fights are good and all, but I sincerely hope later levels will include more coop based mechanics, like simultaneous activation puzzles, or needs to separate enemies and tackle them away from each other, or enemies who are especially vulnerable to flanking maneuvers.
5, I know it's a hack'n'slash MOBAish thing, but please let there be some way to save progress.  This game has the potential to be virtually unending in its maps/chapters, but that'd be ridiculously infuriating to have to leave suddenly or have internet hiccup and disconnect a player when they're 20 chapters in and are forced to start over from Ch 1.
6, There should be a lot more evidence of semblance power.  Ruby should become faster as she gains more sequential hits or by capitalizing upon the recoil from Crescent Rose's sniper fire (as is canon).  Would also be nice if she had an ability to sprint across the map to help teammates.  Weiss should have more glyphs, like being able to freeze at a distance, teleport, speed up teammates while slowing enemies, imbue teammates with power, etc.  Blake should do a lot more teleporting and should be able to deploy a distraction dummy of herself, turning invisible or at least dumping aggro until it's destroyed.  Yang should be able to absorb hits and channel that energy back as extra melee damage.
Overall, a fun game, wonderfully reminscent of the world of Remnant, beautiful canon aesthetics, cute little quips from the characters, smart level design, etc.  Good game.  But can be much better.

South Park: The Fractured But Whole is a double-edged sword for me.  I am no South Park die-hard fan, but do like bizarre and obstruct stories, which this game offers. It has many great things that keep it upright enjoyable, but the downsides are too frequent that sadly tone down the experience.
Combat has improved to a chess-like movement area during a fight, which is good for thinking ahead. Most attacks can only be executed to a parallel axis or require to have space free in front of the enemy, however, which eliminates the purpose of charged offenses. It is also way too slow-paced, which could be thanks to the many unnecessary long animations for just one attack.
The story begins very well and has that little charm to it. It's so weird and unusual. After the first 10 hours about, however, that appeal falls short on its pants and has a lousy change to it with an incredibly disappointing ending.
Writing is a lot weaker than the Stick of Truth, probably because of the vast cast of characters that present themselves. Each has little screen time, and hardly any character development.
Bugs are something I often saw being complained about a lot. I can certainly agree I had to experience multiple delays in combat, sync errors with lips, and even one black screen and this is not acceptable for my point of view if you are asking for 60€. The price tag is way too much for Ubisoft's wanted price because I expected at least something more and better than its successor.
South Park: The Fractured But Whole is not a terrible game by any means, and I had my fun with it. Just wait for the sale if you want to play it, the price tag is not worth it for those only 20 hours and for all the problems described.

I was in the need of something small & lighthearted, after spending a few hundred hours running around in ARK, which however felt like becoming more & more of a drag. That is when I stumbled onto this game while browsing the library, which usually doesn't happen that often, but I thought given the low price and the sci-fi setting it can't hurt to try.
For the bucks spent I got a small little schoot-em-up game which felt well-rounded, and good to kill time during a long pause. Granted, there might be a slew of various titles which all serve the same purpose of providing gameplay experiences compatible to this one, and to each & everyone their own what they might be choosing; here it can be acknowledged that the developers did put thought & effort into it.
The mechanic with differently-coloured weapons and how you deal with them by switching schemes adds a little extra layer of strategic combat you probably won't really expect from a regular shoot-em-up title (but I'm not an expert :) ), and at higher difficulties it can heighten tension as either need to switch more frequently, or bite the apple and choose not to in order to get through safely.
If I had a few gripes then I'd say the music wasn't gripping me, but that also boils down to me having a rather specific taste, so this would probably count more as a personal opinion instead of feeling fully objective.
I got what I expected, and I'm very content with that - it has only been recently that I've grown a bit more of an interest in shoot-em-ups (thx to a few trips to the Science museum), and to start off with this one as part of my personal library wasn't a bad choice.

I rate the game Sky Mercenaries 2.5/5. Not very good, not even okay. A good idea done poorly though it's not total trash either.
This is a Schmup action game wherein you choose a character (each with a different specialization) and over time earn in-game money to upgrade your character's skills and, more importantly, upgrade your little fighter craft's equipment as you play through several missions through to the end of the game.
In theory this game seems like it could be a lot like the good game Raptor: Call of the Shadows or the pretty good game Revolution Ace or even the mediocre game Star Saviors (or merely "Saviors") combined the gameplay color-switching elements of Ikaruga. In practice however, Sky Mercenaries is a bit of a confusing mess despite the fact that it's fairly cheap, runs well and has no bugs.
The main problems with Sky Mercenaries are its confusing interface, obtuse, confusing menus, repetitious/poor sound effects, mediocre graphics and fairly uninteresting/unexciting levels. This game has no real story and characters have nearly no background information. The menus are the worst aspect of this game, particularly when you are trying to upgrade your ship. It's hard to know how much in-game money you have and pretty much impossible to know what items you are even using to upgrade your ship nor can you see any demonstration of what any upgrades will do. The game mostly just fails to explain what's happening and what things are and how anything works.
This game did do a few things right though. There are no bugs/errors. The music is at least adequate. The controls, though odd (it's probably best to control your ship's movement with the mouse while holding down the left mouse button to fire), are fairly responsive. The game can be challenging but is not usually very frustrating (particularly if you play for short periods of time). There are two difficulties and 3 characters/ships to choose from. But none of this has been implemented well enough to make the game very fun.
It's hard to explain but overall I feel like Sky Mercenaries is boring and nonsensical. I play it once in a while but I don't particularly look forward to doing so. After playing through all the levels once with one of the characters it just doesn't seem that fun to try to go through it again. This game feels oddly derivative and tired and the bland levels certainly don't help. I'll give it a thumbs down but I sort of wish I could officially give this game a question mark. Regardless, there are better games out there so play those instead.

I really enjoyed this game a lot. I am not an expert in the "bullet-hell/overhead shooter" genre, but I've played my fair share of them and this one stood out to me mainly because of it's uniqueness. It played with some new ideas that some may like and some may not, but it wasn't afraid to try something new and personally, I enjoyed it.
The most immediate and noticable feature of this game is that enemies shooting at you fire either red or blue bullets, which litter the screen. You can change your space ship to either red or blue at will, which will absorb one color bullet, leaving you susceptible to the other color bullet depending on the color your ship happens to be at contact. When you have a screen full of multi-colored bullets and you have to change your ship color constantly upon impact of a certain color bullet, it can be quite intense, both in action and cognition.
There is also the ability to grind for currency and experience to power up your ship, and there are three different pilots and ships to choose from, each one with different play style. Fortunately, there is a nice balance and I did not have to do too much grinding for my first playthrough; just enough to keep it fun and not be too redundant.  One thing that stood out for me was the soundtrack. There are 8 levels with three stages per level, and each level has a unique theme, both in music and aesthetic. My personal favorite level was level 7 because it had a lush, green, forest feel to it complete with floating mountains and waterfalls. Each level has different music, (I liked some more than others). A few of the levels had ambient and subtle music that reminded me of the original 8-bit NES Metroid, others had a more upbeat musical theme, but all of them unique and interesting.
One more thing that is a very minor detail but stood out to me was that very often, the ships didn't explode when they got shot down. Almost every shooter that I can think of has a small explosion animation when a ship explodes. This is pretty much canon for all shooters that I can remember since the early '80's, (even 1942 where a ship falls from the sky to the ground when shot down and them explodes when it hits the ground). But in this game, it's not uncomon for a ship to just fall to the ground when shot down and just remain on the ground after crash landing. I know it's an insignificant detail, but it just stood out to me because I've never seen it before in a space shooter. In closing, this game was very fun, addictive, and aesthically pleasing with flawless controls and a lot of options. Thank you for reading my review.

i don't say this often but i do now: I'm glad this is over.
i'm no shoot'em up guru but i know what i like and i didn't like this one.
all i want is a good looking and enjoyable game with casual to medium rare difficulty. this game is none of that. i'm not saying it's too difficult because it's not (at regular difficulty at least) but it plays out in a way that's needlessly annoying, frustrating and grindy. and it doesn't even look good.
the main idea is decent: enemies shoot either blue or red bullets at you. you can change the color of your ship accordingly to absorb the bullets of one color making them harmless and charge up your power ups. at the same time you can change the color of your ship to do max damage to enemy ships of the opposite color. the first one seems rather obvious. the second one needs figuring out yourself first since the tutorial in this game is barely worth mentioning. at the same time you don't even realize there are enemies with different colors in the first place since the graphics are rather mushy.
at first the game seems pretty ok and fun but soon after the shortcomings of the game really jump at you.
sound, music and graphics in this game try to be retro (i guess?!) but it's really subpar across the board.
the 'rpg elements' mean there are three pilots with different skills. to get skill points you obviously need to fly missions with them. there are three ships with different offensive / defensive capabilities as well but you are going to pick one and forget the rest. why? because you need to level up your ships (wat?) as well and unlock and install upgrades for them separately! and that would take absolutely forever since earning the xp and credits to upgrade one ship usually ends up in replaying the same missions over and over again untill you can finally afford one upgrade.
and usually you don't even notice that during the next mission. you get like 5% more damage for a ton of credits but at the same time the enemies in the next mission are 4% harder to kill. from start to finish you feel like your ship is undergunned at all times. usually you don't die because you s#ck but just because you can't kill the enemies fast enough. then the screen gets filled with bullets of both colors and since you can't avoid all of them you just get wrecked.
plus your ship and your drones have strangely big hitboxes making it hard to avoid anything in the first place.
i finished the game in about 5 hours. i added another hour for 100% achievements and hit that uninstall button the very blink i got it to 100%. i will never play this again.
oh and you can play other players' custom levels and build your own ones. but why would you want to prolong your suffering?
if you are a die hard shoot'em up lover then maybe pick this game up during sale.
but if you are not that deep into the genre then just get out now.

I have died in Spelunky somewhere in the neighborhood of ten thousand times. When I played the original version in high school, I died five thousand times before the end of the year. And I keep coming back. This game is roguelike action done perfectly. You're rewarded for thinking through the consequences of your actions.
"Will this fall hurt me?"
"Can I kill this shopkeeper before he kills me?"
"How can I save my ropes and bombs and still rescue the damsel?"
In spite of all that, the game will not-so-politely (via an unstoppable murder ghost) nudge you out the door if you take too long. The game moves smoothly without feeling rushed. The only time I get the ghost is if I spend too long gambling or durdling around in the black market.
Spelunky is a good game for good people. The couch multiplayer is enjoyable. The deathmatches are chaotic fun, and the co-op adventure mode takes the Indiana Jones motif the single player has and turns it up. If you've never picked up your friends and swung to safety because you're the only one who can make the jump over the ice chasm, you're missing out.
I'm not the kinda guy who romanticizes going into ancient temples and dusting off artifacts. But I think Indiana Jones is cool, and this game is at least 50 percent an Indiana Jones simulator. You save damsels in distress (and use them to kill enemies sometimes). You collect treasure and whip snakes and bats to death. You rodeo or explode giant spiders into submission. You can pick up the golden idol, but it will set off a booby trap. In the first world, that is a classic Indiana Jones boulder trap.
The only downside to this game is that it doesn't Steam cloud save. I've lost my progress too many times. Fix it, devs!

DISCLAIMER: This review is from the perspective of someone who completely sucks at fighting games and it won't apply to most people.  I would warn anyone who isn't proficient in fighting games away from it, learn or re-learn your skills somewhere else.
Growing up I was into Tekken.  Loved the Tekken games and played the heck out of them.  I haven't messed around w/ Tekken in probably 10 years and in that time I just haven't been playing many fighting games.  I got Tekken 7 because of the nostalgia factor.  I was really interested in seeing how the story ends because I had played all the previous games and I wanted to see if I could get back into fighting games again.
This is not the game to start with if you haven't been around fighting games in a long time.  If you're in my boat, and you just want something chill and easy to get into, this isn't the game.  It is not newb/casual friendly.  The story mode AI will rip your head off even on the easiest diff because the setting doesn't actually change the difficulty.  It just gives the player easy one button push ability on some of the character's moves.  Which actually makes it harder in my opinion because with the easy moves on I couldn't even execute 3-4 hit little combos.  To boot, you will mostly play as Heihachi and if you never played him in any of the previous games you're just S.O.L.
When I initially bought the game I just thought "what the heck, I'll chill out and play the story and maybe do some AI fights and some practice afterward".  WRONG.  Be prepared to put in some time in practice mode w/ potentially a character that you don't even wanna play and have no interest in playing if you want to get through the story.  It's just way more effort up front than I wanted to put in and my experience thus far has been so frustrating that I am not even enjoying the game at this point.
Again, this isn't going to apply to most people, just those who, maybe like myself, grew up w/ the game but haven't kept up with Tekken or fighting games in a long time.  I'm the type who bought Injustice, played through the story, then never picked up the game again.  That's just as far as my interest goes w/ the fighting game genre.  So if that's you, then don't bother with this one cause it's way more effort than you probably want to put in.
Edit: I do feel like I should add that I am not saying this is a bad game or poorly made.  I'm not recommending it for people who are new to fighting games or have not played fighting games in a long time.  Tekken has been around forever and many people like myself probably grew up with it.  This is just a warning to those of you who, like myself, haven't kept up with fighting games or those of you who have never played fighting games and want to get into them.  Start with something easier because Tekken is just not easy to pick up IMO.

Supreme Ruler... ah, where do I even begin? Have you ever wanted to conquer the world? Build an empire to rival the British? Watch your nation prosper (or fail) under your command?
This is as good as it gets folks.
SR is a geopolitical grand strategy game set in the modern era, best described as a unique mix of Civilization and Risk. Play as any nation in six different sandbox campaign maps, or try your luck playing as one of the world superpowers through World War 2 or the Cold War (and beyond!).
You control your nation's military, logistics, finances, resources, infrastructure, diplomacy, and espionage while competing to spread your influence around the globe. If that sounds overwhelming, and trust me it probably is at first, your AI cabinet ministers can help manage some of those aspects for you (or with you).
There are hundreds of real-life units to research and build, and a whole range of futuristic-inspired units and technologies to expand games well beyond the year 2070.
A few minor issues here and there, though nothing game-breaking (and if there is, they're pretty good about patching)... I've found hundreds of hours of enjoyment from this series, and I feel like I've just scratched the surface. That being said, the diplomacy is a bit simplistic, the economy is frustrating (well, that's probably not BG's fault), the AI has momentary fatal lapses of judgment, naval combat and pathing need a bit more work, and some things just generally feel unimportant and neglected (like aircraft carriers, but probably because the AI doesn't know what to do with them)...
All in all, this is an incredible sandbox game. It's extremely moddable (though tedious unless we get some proper mod tools), and there's a ton of settings to play around with and victory conditions to play on.
The choice is up to you, do you want to follow history as closely as possible, or completely rewrite it?
